articles.title: N-able Patches 17 N-central Flaws as Attackers Exploit Earlier Bugs to Deploy Crypto Miners
articles.text:
N-able has released a new security update to address additional critical security flaws impacting N-central.
Describing N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 as a critical security update, the company said it includes a number of security patches and fixes that enhance the security of the Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) and Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform.
"HF3 builds on the protections delivered in HF2 and includes further improvements across authentication and access controls, Agent and Probe communications, file handling, server components, legacy APIs, and user management," the company said.
The improvements relate to authentication and access control; Agent, Probe, and appliance security; file and import handling; server hardening; and user management controls. As part of the change, the configuration option for legacy APIs has been completely removed, permanently blocking them.
As of writing, N-able notes that both Remote control functionality and Intune integration are blocked.
Customers running on-premise N-central deployments should upgrade their servers as soon as possible to keep their environments protected. For Hosted N-central servers, no server-side action is required, as the updates are being automatically applied.
"All customers, hosted and on-premise, must upgrade all of their Agents and Probes to the latest version to be fully protected," N-able cautioned. "Agents and Probes that are not upgraded are susceptible to impersonation."
The complete list of vulnerabilities addressed in the update is listed below -
- CVE-2026-129271 - N-central Patch Management Local Privilege Escalation
- CVE-2026-129272 - MMS3 appliance authentication bypass via predictable passcode
- CVE-2026-129273 - Audit Export syslog injection allows root command execution
- CVE-2026-129274 - ServerMMS2 task result submission missing authentication
- CVE-2026-129275 - repositoryItemGet missing authentication discloses policies
- CVE-2026-129276 - ServerMMS2 asset data submission missing authentication
- CVE-2026-129277 - ServerMMS maintenance action read missing authentication
- CVE-2026-129278 - Take Control audit log tampering without authentication
- CVE-2026-129279 - Password reset response discrepancy allows user enumeration
- CVE-2026-129280 - ServerUI SOAP operations missing authorisation checks
- CVE-2026-129281 - View-only users can set DeviceExecute configuration
- CVE-2026-129282 - Test email sendmail argument injection, missing authorisation
- CVE-2026-129283 - N-central custom service import XML external entity injection
- CVE-2026-129284 - Report Manager and Data Export settings SSRF
- CVE-2026-129285 - XMPP action response origin validation error
- CVE-2026-129286 - SIS GenericFiles version path traversal leads to RCE
- CVE-2026-129287 - SIS repository parser XML external entity injection
The development comes days after N-able began restricting certain N-central features and integrations following the disclosure of a new set of flaws tracked as 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell.
The shortcomings can allow attackers to run arbitrary code as root and gain SYSTEM-level access to Windows systems under specific conditions. Successful exploitation of 4EverAble2Shell hinges on the legacy API mode being enabled. Because the legacy API has been removed from the latest N-central version, it plugs the attack vector.
The 4EverAble2Shell vulnerabilities have since come under active exploitation, with attackers leveraging them to deploy cryptocurrency miners on vulnerable servers.
Independent security researcher Sean Bales, who disclosed the flaws, has published additional details for 24 CVEs, stating "these are patched vulnerabilities and should not work on the latest patch."

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Pro et Ultra : Samsung aurait enfin tranché sur le design de leurs appareils photo
articles.text:
Les fuites s’accordent sur un module photo rectangulaire pour les prochains Galaxy haut de gamme. Un leaker publie aujourd’hui un croquis qu’il présente comme la version définitive.
Le design des futurs Galaxy S27 Pro et Galaxy S27 Ultra commence à se préciser. Alors que plusieurs fuites évoquaient déjà un changement de forme pour leur module photo, les détails de cette nouvelle disposition restaient encore flous. C’est désormais sur ce point qu'Ice Universe affirme apporter des précisions.
Un bloc photo rectangulaire aux capteurs bien séparés
Sur X, le leaker a publié un croquis censé représenter l’apparence finale des deux smartphones. Quelques heures après sa diffusion, il a même insisté sur la fiabilité de son information : « Confirmé à 100 %, il s’agit du design définitif ». Le dessin présente un large bloc rectangulaire accueillant plusieurs éléments circulaires. Deux grands objectifs sont disposés l’un au-dessus de l’autre, tandis qu’un troisième, plus petit, prend place sur le côté. Le flash LED et l’ouverture du microphone apparaissent juste au-dessus de ce dernier.
Une disposition qui écarterait donc les découpes oblongues parfois évoquées dans les précédentes fuites. Chaque élément conserverait son propre contour circulaire, sans être regroupé avec le flash dans une ouverture allongée. Les fabricants de coques pourraient néanmoins reprendre cette forme pour leurs accessoires.
Galaxy S27 Pro et Ultra : quelles caméras sont attendues ?
Au-delà de l’apparence du module, plusieurs indiscrétions ont déjà évoqué les caractéristiques photographiques des deux modèles. Le Galaxy S27 Ultra pourrait ainsi embarquer un capteur principal de 200 mégapixels, accompagné d’un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels et d'un téléobjectif de 50 mégapixels.
Le Galaxy S27 Pro reprendrait les deux premiers capteurs, avec une configuration de 200 + 50 mégapixels. Il ferait toutefois une concession sur le zoom. Son téléobjectif serait en effet limité à 12 mégapixels, avec un grossissement optique de 3x.
Cela va sans dire, ces caractéristiques restent à prendre avec les précautions habituelles en attendant une confirmation de Samsung. Le constructeur n’a d’ailleurs pas encore communiqué de date pour la présentation de cette nouvelle génération. Si la firme étoilée reste fidèle à la tradition instaurée il y a plusieurs années, le prochain événement Unpacked devrait avoir lieu en janvier ou février 2027.
Source : SamMobile

articles.title: "Quiero que la gente tenga mucha RAM, todos deberían poder comprarla para su propia computadora": Sam Altman de OpenAI
articles.text:
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, dijo que quiere que todas las personas puedan comprar mucha memoria RAM para sus computadoras. Lo afirmó en una cumbre de Semafor en San Francisco, donde reconoció que el precio de este componente subió entre cinco y siete veces.
“Quiero ser claro: quiero que la gente tenga mucha RAM, creo que todos deberían poder comprar mucha RAM para su propia computadora”, afirmó Altman, según The Verge. Agregó que “el trabajo casero de experimentación es genial”.
Sobre el aumento de precios, dijo que “los precios de la DRAM, no sé exactamente, quizá subieron cinco veces, siete veces, algo así”. La DRAM es el tipo de memoria que usan las computadoras y los teléfonos para ejecutar programas. Altman admitió que no conocía la cifra exacta.
El ejecutivo sostuvo que desde hace años pide ampliar la cadena de suministro de memoria y que el mundo no construyó suficiente capacidad. También señaló que OpenAI estuvo limitada en distintos momentos por la memoria, el armado de servidores, la capacidad de los centros de datos o “algún componente aleatorio”.
La polémica que Altman intenta cerrar
Todo comenzó en el pódcast Cheeky Pint, conducido por John Collison, cofundador de la empresa de pagos Stripe. En una entrevista publicada el 29 de octubre, según el portal Cognizec, Altman dijo que es “bastante terrible” que cada persona tenga parte del suministro limitado de DRAM en su computadora, usada “el cinco por ciento del tiempo”.
En esa conversación sostuvo que, con la oferta tan ajustada, conviene lograr “máxima utilización en la nube”. Cognizec observó que hablaba de modelos de IA que se ejecutan en el equipo del usuario, no de juegos ni de tareas de oficina, y que la cifra del cinco por ciento no tenía una fuente.
Las críticas llegaron de inmediato. A comienzos de noviembre, Altman cambió su nombre en X a “Ram Altman” y escribió que quiere que “el mundo tenga toneladas de memoria” y que le molestó que sus palabras se sacaran de contexto. A otro usuario le respondió: “Quiero que tengas mucha RAM”.
En la cumbre de Semafor mantuvo una parte de su argumento original. Dijo que, si la escasez continúa, lo óptimo sería compartir la memoria para que trabaje “el 100 por ciento del tiempo”, en lugar de quedar a veces inactiva en un dispositivo personal. Reconoció que hay otras consideraciones, como que la gente ejecute IA en su casa.
Los centros de datos absorben la oferta
Las empresas de inteligencia artificial compran gran parte de la memoria del mundo para sus centros de datos, lo que encarece desde teléfonos hasta consolas, según The Verge. Samsung y SK Hynix firmaron acuerdos de largo plazo con operadores de servicios en la nube y con proyectos como Stargate, de OpenAI, que reservan buena parte de su producción.
La firma de análisis TrendForce proyectó en septiembre que los precios de contrato de la DRAM convencional subirían entre un 10% y un 15% en el cuarto trimestre de 2026, según Cognizec. En diciembre de 2025, el fabricante Micron anunció que dejaría de vender memoria de la marca Crucial a consumidores.
La consultora IDC estimó en junio que los envíos mundiales de computadoras caerán un 11,3% en 2026, con un precio promedio 17% más alto. Según Cognizec, IDC no prevé alivio antes de fines de 2027 y advirtió que los precios probablemente no volverán a los niveles de 2025.
Intel prevé que la escasez dure al menos hasta el año próximo, y SK Hynix estimó que podría extenderse hasta 2030, según The Verge.

articles.title: ‘Just because you can do something, does that mean you should?’: I tested Turtle Beach’s touchscreen-equipped gaming mouse and unfortunately I can’t recommend it — here’s why
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
If you were to simply look at its specs, you’d likely be very impressed with the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7. True 8K polling, a sensor with 30k DPI sensitivity, an essentially infinite battery system, and a 4D scroll wheel. But as great as all of this is, the MC7 is let down by an unnecessary touchscreen, a hefty and awkward build, and a high asking price — which it fails to justify overall.
- 
Design Fairly comfortable in use, but hefty, not great-looking, and the touchscreen feels unnecessary.
- 
Performance Fantastic specs with 8K polling and 30K DPI sensitivity, but some may find it a little unwieldy.
- 
Value The cons of the MC7 feel too great for a mouse that costs this much.
Reasons to buy
- + True 8K polling
- + Impressive sensor with 30k DPI sensitivity
- + Excellent hot-swappable batteries
Reasons to avoid
- - Touchscreen feels unnecessary
- - Hefty and awkward looking
- - Fairly expensive
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review
The Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 gaming mouse left me with one question after testing it: just because you can do something, does that mean you should?
See, the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 comes equipped with a touchscreen — just like the brand's Command Series keyboards. I can understand having a few useful shortcuts and commands available at the tap of a screen on your keyboard — especially if you’re a streamer or competitive gamer. But it just feels straight up unnecessary on a mouse.
First of all, the touchscreen is pretty small and didn’t feel particularly natural to use with my thumb. What’s more, a lot of the features available — like adjusting DPI or polling rate — can just be mapped to the customizable ‘M’ buttons scattered across the mouse. Sure, the touchscreen enables you to launch a gaming overlay or media controls, but again, it feels like these could be tied to button controls or keyboard shortcuts.
Don’t get me wrong, the touchscreen is nice and bright, it’s responsive, and the software is easy to get started with after downloading the Swarm II app, but overall, the interface feels superfluous.
Anyway, let’s look past the touchscreen for now, and assess how the MC7 fares against the best gaming mice in terms of performance. And luckily, it does pretty well in this department.
From the specs alone, you can tell that the MC7 is oriented towards competitive gamers. You’re getting true 8K polling with 0.125ms latency, a 30K DPI ‘Owl-Eye’ optical sensor, and Titan Optical Switches with adjustable debounce and, according to Turtle Beach, “a 150 million-click lifespan”.
But how does that translate into actual use? Well, I tried playing Counter-Strike 2, and had a very good experience overall. While you can get higher sensitivity from mice like the Steelseries Sensei Pro, I found the sensor to be excellent, with impressive speed and tracking.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The 8K polling is another great feature, and helped me aim with great precision, with ultra-smooth movement. The Titan Optical Switches also felt highly satisfying and snappy, with a pleasant mechanical sound to them. The 4D scroll wheel is pretty cool too, and can dynamically snap from small steps to free-spin scrolling — plus you can click it left or right for seamless navigation.
What I would say, though, is that some may find the MC7 to be a little unwieldy. While its sloped design felt pretty comfortable to me, I will say that it's a pretty large mouse — and quite heavy at that. Those with smaller hands may want to steer clear, and if you prefer a lightweight feel, this mouse will likely feel too hefty for you.
On the topic of design, I have to say that the MC7 is one of the less attractive mice I’ve tested in my time at TechRadar. The bronze details feel a little garish alongside the purple touchscreen, black body and LED lighting — it’s all just a bit messy. The mouse also uses a strange combination of boldly angular and rounded segments, giving it an awkward form. That is to say that it feels like the MC7 is having a bit of an identity crisis, and I wish it was at least a bit easier on the eye.
I feel like I’ve bashed this mouse quite a lot, so I want to return to the positives for a moment. The Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 has an absolutely brilliant hot-swappable battery system, which essentially gives you infinite playtime. The wireless transmitter houses a battery that can charge while you use your mouse, and when your battery eventually dies, you can swap the transmitter battery right in. Other than the few seconds you’ll take to switch the batteries, you’ll get unbroken play.
Something else that impressed me was the sheer number of features on offer. You can pick between a 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, or wired connection, providing exceptional versatility. The Swarm II companion software also opens up a lot of options, like button mapping, touchscreen customization, and lighting adjustments. What’s more, it allows you to drill into angle-tuning, debounce time alterations, motion sync options, and even haptics adjustments.
All in all, the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 is a highly customizable, feature-rich gaming mouse. And its infinite battery system, solid performance, and detailed companion software all impressed me overall.
However, the cons are plain to see. The mouse is pretty hefty, it's also quite unattractive, and the touchscreen — which is the MC7’s USP — feels unnecessary.
Add in the fact that this mouse has a steep list price of $159.99 / £139.99 / AU$249.95, and it’s not possible for me to recommend this. If you feel like you’d benefit from the touchscreen, and you don’t mind a heavier feel, then it could be worth grabbing this one on sale, but otherwise, I’d be much more tempted by top-tier rivals like the Steelseries Rival Pro and Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike — both of which are expensive too, but do more to justify that fact.
Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review: price & release date
- Priced at $159.99 / £139.99 / AU$249.95
- Released in July 2026
The Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 was released in July 2026 alongside two other mice, the mid-priced wireless MC5 and the entry-level wired MC3. The MC7 has a list price of $159.99 / £139.99 / AU$249.95, placing it in the premium category, though it is a bit cheaper than leading rivals like the Steelseries Rival Pro ($179.99 / £169.99), and the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike ($179.99 / £159.99 / AU$299.95).
Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review: specs
| Interface | Wireless (2.4GHz), Bluetooth, Wired | 
| Battery life | Up to 15 hours (8K polling with LED and LCD off) | 
| Sensor | Owl‑Eye 30K Optical | 
| Polling rate | 8kHz | 
| Buttons | 11 | 
| DPI | 30,000 | 
| Switches | Optical | 
| Dimensions | 5 x 3.4 x 1.8 inches / 127.7 x 85.3 x 45.9mm | 
| Weight | 4.8oz / 135g | 
Should I buy the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7?
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Design | Fairly comfortable in use, but hefty, not great-looking, and the touchscreen feels unnecessary. | 2.5/5 | 
| Performance | Fantastic specs with 8K polling and 30K DPI sensitivity, but some may find it a little unwieldy. | 4/5 | 
| Value | The cons of the MC7 feel too great for a mouse that costs this much. | 2.5/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want excellent battery life
The MC7 uses a brilliant hot-swappable battery system that essentially gives you unlimited playtime. One battery will slot onto the transmitter and charge up while you’re gaming, and when your mouse eventually dies, you can substitute it right in. Pretty convenient, right?
You’re all in on the touchscreen
For me, the touchscreen on the MC7 is unnecessary — most of the functions it performs could be mapped to a keyboard or physical buttons. But if you disagree, and you think the screen will benefit you greatly, then it might just be worth snapping the MC7 up, though I’d still advise you to hold out for a sale.
Don’t buy it if…
You want something lightweight
At 4.8oz / 135g, the MC7 is a pretty hefty lad, and it's fairly large too. While it feels relatively comfortable to grip, I much prefer the lighter feel of rivals such as the Steelseries Rival Pro, which you can read more about in the ‘also consider’ section.
You want the best value for money
The MC7 is expensive, but as I’ve illustrated throughout this review, it doesn’t do enough to live up to its price. I feel that the two options below — despite being a touch pricier — actually offer you far better bang for your buck, with awesome specs, but also great designs.
Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 review: also consider
Steelseries Rival Pro
The Steelseries Rival Pro is one of the best gaming mice I’ve ever used, and easily among the greatest to come out in 2026. Like the MC7, it also has hot-swappable batteries and true 8K polling, but it also boasts higher 42k DPI sensitivity, an extremely lightweight feel, and top-class ergonomics. Read my full Steelseries Rival Pro review.
Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
Where to begin with the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike? It’s a simply spectacular mouse, with ultra-low click and sensor latency, brilliant switches, and amazing build quality too. Even though it's costly, we feel that it has the performance and luxurious feel to back it up. Read our full Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike review.
How I tested the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7
- Spent a whole week testing
- Used for gaming and general productivity
- Made use of all features on touchscreen and in the Swarm II app
I spent a whole week using the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7, both for gaming and general productivity at work.
The main game I tested this mouse with was Counter-Strike 2, and while playing, I made sure to try out the various touchscreen settings and customizable options in the Swarm II app. I also directly compared it against my go-to mouse, the Steelseries Rival Pro.
More generally, I’ve spent years testing gadgets here at TechRadar, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve reviewed all sorts of tech, from wireless headphones like the Sonos Ace Ultra to phones like the Oppo Reno 16 5G. I’ve also tested a number of mice, including the Steelseries Rival Pro Mini, and other products in the Command Series lineup, including the Turtle Beach Command Series KB7 keyboard.

articles.title: iOS 27.3 : Apple ajoute une reconnaissance faciale inédite à l'iPhone Duo
articles.text:
L’iPhone Duo va bientôt pouvoir se déverrouiller d’un simple regard sans pour autant bénéficier du véritable Face ID. Avec la deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3, Apple introduit aussi une option attendue par certains utilisateurs : le verrouillage automatique du smartphone lorsqu’ils le referment.
Jusqu’ici, les utilisateurs de l'iPhone Duo devaient passer par Touch ID ou saisir leur code pour déverrouiller leur appareil. La deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3 change quelque peu la donne en introduisant une nouvelle méthode d’authentification basée sur la caméra frontale située sur l’écran extérieur.
L’iPhone Duo peut désormais reconnaître le visage de son propriétaire
Une fois l’option activée dans les réglages, depuis le menu « Touch ID et code », le smartphone peut reconnaître le visage de son propriétaire pour autoriser son déverrouillage lorsqu’il est fermé. Apple précise néanmoins qu’une authentification récente par Touch ID ou avec le code reste nécessaire pour activer cette fonction. Les données de reconnaissance faciale restent quant à elles stockées sur l'appareil.
Attention toutefois, il ne s’agit pas d’une arrivée de Face ID sur l’iPhone Duo. Le smartphone ne dispose pas des composants nécessaires au fonctionnement du système de reconnaissance faciale d’Apple. Cette nouveauté repose uniquement sur la caméra frontale et présente donc des restrictions plus importantes.
En effet, la reconnaissance faciale ne sert ici qu’à déverrouiller le téléphone. Pour effectuer un paiement avec Apple Pay, accéder à ses mots de passe ou ouvrir certaines applications nécessitant une authentification, Touch ID ou le code restent indispensables. Autre limite : après 45 minutes sans déverrouiller l’appareil, l’utilisateur doit à nouveau s’identifier avec son empreinte ou son code pour réactiver la reconnaissance faciale. Enfin, cette fonction ne fonctionne pas lorsque le smartphone est déplié.
iOS 27.3 permet aussi de verrouiller l’iPhone Duo en le refermant
L’autre nouveauté concerne directement la manière dont le smartphone pliant se comporte lorsqu’on le referme. Jusqu’à présent, fermer l’iPhone Duo entraînait le transfert de l’affichage vers l’écran extérieur. Avec iOS 27.3, Apple ajoute une option permettant de verrouiller complètement l’appareil à la place.
Il suffit pour cela de se rendre dans les réglages, puis dans « Luminosité et affichage », afin d’activer le verrouillage à la fermeture. Le smartphone ne bascule alors plus automatiquement vers son écran externe lorsque son utilisateur le replie. Ces deux ajouts sont d’ores et déjà disponibles dans la deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3.

articles.title: Google Finds Hackers Using AI Agents to Build and Run Exploits From Software Patches
articles.text:
Google on Monday revealed that adversarial use of artificial intelligence (AI) by threat actors has gone beyond manual prompting to deploying autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks like ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI to execute multi-stage intrusions at greater operational velocity.
In tandem, threat actors are leveraging the power and capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and agentic frameworks to automate the reverse engineering of patches via differential analysis, allowing them to rapidly weaponize newly disclosed vulnerabilities, as observed in the case of PaperCut NG/MF flaws earlier this September.
The abuse of open source, agentic penetration-testing (pentesting) frameworks is seen as a way to "automate discrete phases and specific operational tasks during live intrusions," Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
The tech giant said the adoption represents a paradigm shift in which cyber attacks take place at machine speed, allowing the operations to be scaled significantly by chaining together varied attack paths even if the underlying mechanics remain the same.
A number of threat actors have been observed experimenting with these frameworks and harnesses, including financially motivated and suspected espionage actors aligned with China.
"These observations additionally extend to the use of other tools and services, such as ZeroHollow, an inference service used for exploit development and LLM routing, and Agent Zero, an open source agent framework which features autonomous code execution and dynamic tool generation," Google said.
Another key area of misuse revolves around automating labor-intensive tasks like vulnerability analysis and proof-of-concept (POC) weaponization using LLM-driven pipelines, allowing threat actors to collapse the window between patch disclosure and active exploitation.
"Threat actors may find it more efficient to use LLMs to rapidly weaponize patched n-day vulnerabilities, as they can focus research on a finite set of source materials: comparing source code versions (including from pre-release or preview channels), and examining release notes, security research, and POC code related to specific flaws," Google added.
Simultaneously, threat actors are also targeting AI infrastructure to illicit profit from LLMjacking attacks by stealing LLM credentials and cloud resources from compromised enterprise environments, and then reselling the access through underground proxy services like APIMart and JetNight at discounted prices, otherwise known as LLM mixers.
The findings show that the emergence of open-source frameworks have further lowered the barrier to entry, enabling bad actors to easily integrate new exploits, autonomously scale attacks, and mount convincing phishing campaigns, further compressing attack timelines.
This includes a Chinese-language phishing platform called Jieyou that has integrated an LLM chatbot assistant to allow customers to configure phishing panels and modify existing templates using natural language commands without necessarily having the technical expertise to do so.
"The evolution of the Jieyou platform highlights a growing industry trend where PhaaS providers leverage LLMs as a modular force multiplier," Google said. "Rather than manually editing payloads, low-skilled affiliates can now utilize natural language through the chatbot to dynamically customize pretext lures and phishing interfaces on the fly."

articles.title: Unos 400 centros de datos de Estados Unidos usan casi tanta electricidad como todo el estado de Michigan
articles.text:
Un grupo de 403 centros de datos de gran tamaño en Estados Unidos consumió entre 68 y 99 teravatios-hora de electricidad en un año, una cifra cuyo extremo alto se acerca al consumo anual de estados como Michigan, según un estudio de la Universidad de Harvard publicado el 16 de noviembre en la revista Nature Sustainability.
El equipo, liderado por el investigador Gianluca Guidi, estudió las instalaciones que operaron entre mayo de 2024 y abril de 2025. Son los llamados centros de datos de hiperescala: los más grandes, que pertenecen a las mayores empresas de computación en la nube y de inteligencia artificial. Su capacidad promedio es de unos 40 megavatios.
En su escenario central, estos centros usaron unos 82 teravatios-hora, equivalentes a cerca del 1,8% de toda la electricidad que consume el país. Las emisiones de dióxido de carbono asociadas fueron de unos 25,7 millones de toneladas, de dos a tres veces más que una estimación anterior para 2018, según el comunicado de Harvard.
Más de la mitad de la energía es fósil
Alrededor del 54% de la electricidad que alimenta a estos centros se generó con combustibles fósiles: 38% con gas natural y 15% con carbón. Además, cerca de una cuarta parte de la energía se consumió en regiones cuya red eléctrica emite más carbono que el promedio nacional.
El consumo se concentra en pocos lugares. Virginia, Oregon, Ohio e Iowa reúnen más de la mitad de la electricidad analizada, según los investigadores. Virginia aloja la zona conocida como Data Center Alley, una de las mayores concentraciones de centros de datos del mundo, según señaló Wired.
Para ubicar las instalaciones, el equipo usó imágenes satelitales e investigación de la industria. Después modeló su consumo en distintos escenarios de uso y calculó las emisiones a partir del tipo de centrales que abastecen cada región, con datos de la Agencia de Protección Ambiental de Estados Unidos.
Un consumo que nadie mide de forma oficial
Ni el gobierno federal ni los estados registran el uso eléctrico de los centros de datos como una categoría aparte, informó Wired. Cada operador suele tratar sus cifras como información reservada, y ni ellos ni las compañías eléctricas están obligados a divulgarlas.
Jon Koomey, investigador de energía que no participó en el estudio, valoró que exista una cifra anual verificada. “Los centros de hiperescala venían creciendo rápido incluso antes del auge de la IA”, dijo a Wired. Koomey colabora desde 2007 en un informe periódico del Laboratorio Nacional Lawrence Berkeley sobre el consumo de energía y agua del sector.
Los propios autores reconocen límites. No había datos suficientes para incluir todos los centros del país y no pudieron separar la electricidad usada para IA de la dedicada a otras tareas. Tampoco midieron efectos sobre la salud, algo que planean investigar más adelante.
El estudio tampoco cuenta las centrales eléctricas que algunos desarrolladores construyen dentro de sus propios terrenos. Wired informó que hay hasta 189 gigavatios de ese tipo en proyecto para centros de datos, muchos con turbinas de gas. BloombergNEF estimó la semana pasada que, si se construyeran todas, las emisiones totales de Estados Unidos aumentarían 10%.
Guidi advirtió que el estudio puede haber quedado atrás. Según el investigador de Harvard, algunos campus que se proponen hoy son sustancialmente más grandes que la instalación típica de su muestra. Wired indica que los nuevos proyectos alcanzan cientos o incluso miles de megavatios.
Un cambio en la falta de datos oficiales podría llegar pronto. La Administración de Información Energética, el organismo federal que registra el uso de energía por sector, completó este año tres encuestas piloto en 10 estados. Su portavoz, Lee Tucker, dijo a Wired que la agencia usa esos resultados para diseñar una posible encuesta voluntaria al sector.

articles.title: Russia's FSB-linked Turla hackers just hit a key NATO border nation
articles.text:
Russian hackers target Romanian servers to steal NATO, EU emails
Turla hackers breached Romanian government email servers
- Cereal malware secretly searched Romanian government emails for NATO and EU connections
- ESET discovered previously undocumented software linked to Russia's Turla hacking group
- Hackers exploited Microsoft Exchange systems to conceal their email collection activities
Cyberespionage hackers allegedly linked to Russia infiltrated the Romanian government email servers, seeking correspondence involving NATO and European Union institutions.
The operation relied on previously unseen malicious software ESET researchers named Cereal, according to the cybersecurity company's published investigation.
Rather than sending stolen messages immediately to an outside server, the intruders exploited the victim's own email environment to conceal their activity.
A covert toolset searched institutional correspondence
ESET said the intrusion began on December 23, 2025, after investigators had identified the same software in Kazakhstan the previous month.
The malicious package contained several .NET components capable of receiving instructions, executing code in memory, and examining an infected organization's internal structure.
One module, called CerealBox, searched messages for addresses associated with NATO and European Union bodies, then applied filters to identify selected correspondence.
Emails containing Microsoft Word documents or PDF files were among those selected, after which the software packaged and encrypted copies for collection.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This approach allowed the operators to obtain specific material without indiscriminately copying every message stored within the compromised organization's mail environment.
ESET described the software as unusual because its methods relied on detailed knowledge of Exchange systems and unconventional .NET execution techniques.
The researchers said the malicious code also used legitimate server functions, reducing the need for communications with infrastructure controlled directly by the attackers.
That arrangement could make detection more difficult because security teams might see activity occurring through systems their organizations already depend upon.
For institutions managing sensitive diplomatic correspondence, secure email protections must therefore include scrutiny of internal server activity, not simply suspicious external messages.
ESET links the activity to Russia's Turla group
ESET attributed the operation to Turla with high confidence, pointing to overlapping tools and similarities with malicious programs previously associated with the group.
Turla is widely assessed by cybersecurity researchers as connected to Russia's Federal Security Service, which handles internal security and intelligence operations.
The group has a history of pursuing government organizations, including prominent Ukrainian institutions, and has operated across Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
According to ESET, around 70% of the countries previously affected by Turla were former Soviet republics or former communist states.
Romania's location on NATO's eastern edge makes the discovery particularly significant, given the country's exposure to security tensions.
Romanian authorities have previously faced digital attacks, including a 2025 campaign against defense manufacturers supplying equipment or support to Ukraine.
Shortly after the war in Ukraine started, denial-of-service incidents disrupted websites belonging to Romanian public bodies and financial institutions.
The latest compromise adds another example of espionage activity directed at institutions in a country supporting Ukraine and belonging to NATO.
ESET identified the malware, but the company did not disclose how many emails the hackers managed to steal.
Via Defense News

articles.title: Après le Royaume-Uni, les Big tech s'attaquent au Canada qui veut accéder aux données des utilisateurs
articles.text:
Le Canada examine un projet de loi censé aider la police et les services de renseignement à obtenir des données numériques lors de leurs enquêtes. Apple, Google et Meta tentent de le faire modifier avant son adoption.
Baptisé C-22, le texte est en ce moment devant le Sénat, dernière chance de le changer. Les entreprises s’inquiètent pour la sécurité de leurs services et pour le chiffrement.
Métadonnées, chiffrement, « capacités techniques » : ce qui coince dans C-22
La Chambre des communes a voté C-22 le 18 juin. Un comité du Sénat l’examine maintenant et auditionne ce lundi Meta, Signal et Tailscale. Le Sénat rejette rarement un texte, mais il l’amende souvent, d’où l’offensive des lobbyistes. Sur le fond, le ministre de la Sécurité publique pourrait ordonner à un service en ligne de créer des outils pour extraire des informations auxquelles les enquêteurs ont déjà le droit d’accéder. Chaque ordre devrait être validé par le commissaire au renseignement. Certains fournisseurs pourraient aussi devoir garder des métadonnées jusqu’à six mois. Elles décrivent les connexions des utilisateurs, sans le contenu des messages, l’historique de navigation ni l’activité sur les réseaux sociaux.
Bien entendu, le chiffrement est au cœur des débats. D’après le texte, une entreprise n’est obligée de déchiffrer des données que si elle a elle-même fourni le chiffrement et possède de quoi le lever. Avec le chiffrement de bout en bout, seuls l’expéditeur et le destinataire peuvent lire un message : l’entreprise ne peut rien déchiffrer. Signal et Meta (WhatsApp) craignaient d’être visés. Pour les rassurer, les parlementaires ont aussi ajouté qu’une entreprise n’a pas à obéir à un ordre qui l’obligerait à créer une « vulnérabilité systémique », autrement dit, une faiblesse qui crée un risque crédible que des informations protégées soient consultées sans autorisation.
- storage1 Go de stockage
- securityChiffrement natif par défaut
- alternate_emailPas de domaine personnalisé
- smartphoneApplications iOS, Android
- push_pinJurisdiction Suisse
Mais, les inquiétudes persistent. Pour des défenseurs de la vie privée et des dirigeants du secteur, l’État pourrait toujours imposer la création d’outils d’interception des communications. Les entreprises rappellent qu’on ne peut pas créer une porte dérobée réservée aux enquêteurs sans fragiliser la sécurité de tous les utilisateurs. Rachel Curran, responsable des politiques publiques de Meta au Canada, parle de « ligne rouge » si un ordre rendait les systèmes de l’entreprise plus vulnérables. Apple reconnaît les efforts d’Ottawa, mais estime que le texte limiterait encore sa capacité à proposer des fonctions de confidentialité et de sécurité, dont le chiffrement. Le gouvernement se défend en affirmant que le C-22 n’autorise ni surveillance indiscriminée ni porte dérobée. Le texte a été amendé après les craintes d’Apple au Royaume-Uni et il ne fait qu’aligner le Canada sur ses alliés du Five Eyes et du G7. Des élus américains pensent au contraire que le texte va plus loin que les règles adoptées par ces alliés. Le ministre accuse même certains critiques, dont des géants de la tech, de désinformer.
Apple a déjà vécu ce bras de fer au Royaume-Uni. Nous rapportions en février 2025 qu'Apple cessait de proposer la Protection avancée des données d’iCloud aux nouveaux utilisateurs britanniques, après les exigences de Londres. L’affaire est toujours devant les tribunaux. Selon Rachel Curran, Meta devrait envisager des options comparables face à un ordre similaire. Signal menace de quitter le Canada si le texte est adopté en l’état, et Proton, entreprise suisse, dit qu’elle réexaminerait ses projets d’expansion dans le pays. Ottawa risque aussi de freiner les investissements technologiques et d’aggraver ses tensions avec les États-Unis.
Source : Bloomberg

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: N-able 0-Days, Windows 0-Days, Chrome 0-Days, Fridge 0-Days, and More Bad Days
articles.text:
A default password opened doors it never should have. A trusted update delivered malware. Even a security feature became a way to break in. Different stories, same problem: the things meant to protect us aren't always doing their job.
Meanwhile, AI is making bug hunting faster, old flaws are still paying off, and attackers keep finding easy ways in. Some attacks take real skill. Others barely need any.
This week's stories show both sides. Here's what happened.
⚡ Threat of the Week
N-able 0-Days Exploited for Dropping Crypto Miners — A new set of vulnerabilities tracked as 4EverAble2Shell has come under active exploitation, with attackers exploiting it to deploy cryptocurrency miners on vulnerable servers. According to Huntback, the activity has successfully compromised 21 N-central servers across the U.S., South Africa, Canada, the U.K., Germany, France, and Sweden. Patches for the flaw are expected to be released N-able today.
One Secrets Strategy for Developer and AI Agent Credentials
Developer secrets and AI-agent credentials may look like separate issues, but they introduce the same access risks. Read our guide to see how a shared secrets management framework can secure developer secrets and make sure that AI agents don’t see or store raw credentials.
Read Now ➝
🔔 Top News
- Compromised bee-js and Swarm Desktop Steal Swarm Wallet Keys — Threat actors compromised @ethersphere/bee-js, the JavaScript client for the Swarm storage network, with a new postinstall hook in version 13.3.0 that downloads a second stage responsible for stealing the Swarm node's wallet key and installing a backdoor. "On Linux and macOS, the backdoor is a Go remote shell," SafeDep said. "On Windows, it is a hidden ScreenConnect client that runs as SYSTEM." The same malicious code was subsequently distributed via Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 on GitHub. The activity has since been linked to a campaign called SleepyDuck (EtherDuck), which is known to spread malicious Solidity extensions through Open VSX. "The attacker controlled two Ethersphere GitHub accounts. GitHub activity logs attribute 13 pushes on November 6 to long-time maintainer nugaon," SafeDep added. "That day the attacker injected GitHub Actions workflows to steal CI credentials, and the attempts failed. Two days later, the attacker used the release bot bee-worker to publish the malicious releases. How the attacker got into either account remains unknown."
- Nightmare Eclipse New SignDrop 0-Day — Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (aka Chaotic Eclipse) released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges. Called SignDrop, it has been described as a Windows Common Log FileSystem (CLFS) authentication zero-day local privilege escalation flaw. "The vulnerability turns a defense into an attack surface," Cyderes said. "Microsoft added HMAC-based authentication codes to CLFS log files specifically to block the class of logic bugs caused by improper validation of CLFS data structures, which accounted for 19 of 24 CLFS CVEs over five years. SignDrop abuses the signing mechanism itself: it forces clfs.sys to create a .cnpf signature file as SYSTEM in an attacker-controlled location, producing a privileged file-creation primitive at an attacker-selected path. Because the resulting file retains attacker-accessible security attributes, the exploit reopens it and replaces the CLFS-generated content with an embedded payload DLL." Microsoft said it's investigating the reported vulnerability. In late September, the researcher also released an exploit for BigDiskBuster, a denial-of-service (DoS) flaw impacting Microsoft Defender that's similar to UnDefend and prevents the application from performing platform/signature updates.
- Default Admin Password Lets Researchers Unlock and Start Cars — New research found that it's possible to take over customer accounts at two major automakers, and use them to remotely unlock and start a test car, flash headlights, and sound horns after finding an administration console on the brands' login servers still protected by its default password. Both apps signed customers in through ForgeRock, an identity platform now part of Ping Identity. The carmakers remediated the flaw approximately two hours after responsible disclosure.
- Google Patches Actively Exploited Chrome 0-Day — Google released updates to patch a high-severity vulnerability in Chrome has come under active exploitation in the wild. The flaw, tracked as CVE identifier CVE-2026-125350 (CVSS score: 8.8), has been described as a use-after-free bug in the XML component. The issue has been addressed in 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Apple macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. Google did not disclose how the vulnerability is being exploited and in what context.
- Meta Fined by Italy Over Accessing Android Users' Photos with Facebook App — The Italian Data Protection Authority (IDPA) hit Meta with one of its highest fines to date. According to the Italian data regulatory body, Meta has been fined €805 million for failing to disclose that it had access to user photos, videos, and metadata for those using the Facebook app on Android devices. Meta had access to Android users' photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users' personal galleries that they could post. The feature has been available since 2023. Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately. The company said it would appeal the decision. "This is a simple feature that helps people share photos and videos on Facebook," Meta told Reuters. "Users must grant permission on their device before the feature can operate, and they can change that permission at any time in their settings."

🎥 Cybersecurity Webinars
- Your SOC Has an Identity Blind Spot — Here's How Attackers Exploit It and How to Close It → Your SOC may be tracking threats, but is it missing the identities behind them? As attackers increasingly exploit human, machine, and AI identities, traditional security tools often lack the context needed to detect and contain threats quickly. - Your GitHub Actions May Still Be Vulnerable — Even With SHA Pinning. Here's Why → Think your GitHub Actions are secure because you use SHA pinning? Think again. Attackers can exploit hidden weaknesses in CI/CD workflows, even when standard security measures are in place. Join this expert-led webinar to discover how these attacks work, why SHA pinning alone isn't enough, and what you can do to protect your software supply chain.
📰 Around the Cyber World
- A cybercrime investigation from independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs has linked the administrator of Qilin ransomware to Aleksey Mikhailovich Yakovtsev, a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.
- The TOR project released 0.4.9.17 to include denial-of-service (DoS) defenses related to IPv6 handling. "This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators," the maintainers said. "This is not an easy problem to address, as relays across the network are being overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits. We are actively evaluating additional defenses and so expect further releases in the near future."
- As many as six pre-authentication remote code execution 0-day vulnerabilities have been uncovered in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A fridge controllers. The flaws, identified by Midnight Blue within the span of an hour, allow full device take-over, persistent access (possibly after reset), and persistent denial-of-service, rendering the device inoperable. Additional technical details are currently withheld. "Through remote code execution, an unauthenticated attacker can remotely run arbitrary code at the operating system level of the AK-SM800A controller," Midnight Blue said. "Due to the lack of secure boot, an attacker with RCE could push malicious firmware that simply renders the device inoperable and irrecoverable without specialized hardware intervention (e.g. by wiping flash memory and/or causing an infinite boot loop). Such a 'bricking' or wiper approach would require full device replacement." The findings unfold against the backdrop of two waves of cyber attacks targeting internet-exposed fridge controllers by Danfoss and Copeland across Europe.
- Cruciferra has been revealed as a rebrand of the long-running KGB cryptor. It has been sold to cybercriminals since October 2025. ESET said it has prevented over 700,000 compromise attempts from Cruciferra since January 2026, most of them targeting Türkiye, Greece, and Spain. It has been used to deliver payloads like Formbook and PureLogs. "In mid-October the cryptor's domain was seized, and the service went dark," ESET said. "Days later, the same operator resurfaced with a new offering – exclusive $5K-per-build cryptors, pitched against enterprise EDRs and advertised with a claimed bundled kernel 0-day. Seized infrastructure ≠ a dead service."
- Using AI models on a limited budget and running it against 10 popular TCP/IP stacks has led to the discovery of 99 vulnerabilities in 90 hours. Of these, 66 are new vulnerabilities, 52% of them critical or high severity. This also includes seven vulnerabilities specific to the firmware of a discontinued wireless access point, such as buffer overflow via firmware upload and hard-coded administrator credentials that cannot be changed for web and shell management. "AI cut the analysis time from 9 months to 90 hours and the research cost by 100x when compared to our previous analysis," Forescout said. "It rediscovered 40% of the vulnerabilities we had previously disclosed on those stacks. Total static analysis cost was $935, an average of $2.58 per finding."
- Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a "90 + 30" vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to address a vulnerability, plus an extra 30 days "soak time" for patch rollout. That's changing now with the emergence of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Going forward, Google Project Zero will disclose vulnerabilities 90 days after they are reported to the vendor, regardless of whether they are fixed. The deadline drops to 60 days on February 2, 2027, and to 30 days on January 3, 2028.
- ClickFix-style lures are being used to deliver a macOS-focused, modular information stealer called Phexia. The malware is also capable of deploying an XMRig miner. "The most recent and notable change in Phexia occurred in May 2026, when the threat actor started testing smart contracts on the Polygon blockchain as a command-and-control (C2) dead-drop resolver (DDR)," WithSecure said. "The abuse of smart contracts by threat actors as part of their attack chain is generally known as EtherHiding. The malware previously relied on hardcoded C2 domains as well as Telegram channels and Steam profiles as its C2 DDR. The threat actor was observed actively weaponizing the Polygon smart contracts since late May to early June 2026."
- The threat actors behind WeedHack have been linked to another cybercriminal operation called Marsalek that expands beyond using Minecraft lures to disguise malicious software as popular gaming tools, cheats, and utilities for games including Roblox, Fortnite, and Counter-Strike 2. "Active from approximately December 2025 through May 2026, Marsalek offered free access to sophisticated information-stealing malware through a publicly accessible platform, complete with a dashboard that allowed users to create malicious files, track victims, and access stolen information," McAfee Labs said. The cybersecurity company identified more than 1,560 registered accounts, over 400 malicious files, and more than 29 distribution URLs associated with the campaign. Marsalek also deploys a second information stealer called PureLog to steal sensitive data and exfiltrate it to another server. "This means that while someone using Marsalek may believe they're collecting stolen passwords and other personal information for themselves, the malware operator could also gain access to that information without their knowledge," McAfee Labs. This tactic is called double theft or a dual-hook infection.
- New findings from SOCRadar show that ransomware operators have started handing the attack to AI agents, leading to the rise of agentic ransomware attacks. "Agentic ransomware is ransomware where AI agents do the hands-on work: choosing techniques, running tools and writing code, within limits a human sets," SOCRadar said. "In less than a year, AI agents moved from building access for ransomware brands to running live encryption and extortion campaigns."
- An active campaign discovered in early October 2026 is targeting internet-facing Microsoft SQL Server instances and using Transact-SQL (T-SQL) commands to deliver malware such as XMRig miner and Gh0st RAT. The attacks employ predefined username and password lists to brute-force into the servers and exploit their administrative capabilities to execute commands on the underlying Windows systems. "The malware scans IP ranges for exposed SQL Servers and attempts to log in using supplied credentials," Fortinet said. "After a successful login, it remotely executes malicious T-SQL commands on the compromised server to download and run additional malware." It's not known how many servers were compromised or who was behind the campaign.
- A Europol operation, in collaboration with law enforcement agencies from 14 countries across the globe, has successfully identified vendors and buyers from major dark marketplaces as part of Operation TorNado, a coordinated international effort targeting cybercrime, drug trafficking, and firearms offenses. "The operation, which spanned from May 2025 to October 2026, resulted in 354 arrests and hundreds of house searches worldwide," Europol said. "This effort included a follow-up action focused on the identification of suspects after the takedown of five major dark marketplaces: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom, [and] Tor2Door." The U.S. led with 132 arrests, followed by the U.K. (59). Authorities also seized more than 5.7 metric tonnes of illicit drugs, 209 firearms, and over $234 million in both cash and virtual currencies.
- Threat actors have been observed using a "convincing device-code phishing attack" that involves a Microsoft Teams calendar invite booking flow to target a company in the construction sector. The attack was observed in mid-October 2026. "While many device code phishing lures leverage a generic Microsoft sign-in form, this attack crafted an email with a believable social engineering lure that impersonated a legitimate senior vice president of another company in the construction sector, complete with a typosquatted email domain," Huntress said. "A link in the message to the victim began a 'Microsoft Teams Meeting Scheduler' booking flow, which included prompts to pick a duration of the call, as well as a date and a time. On the backend, these prompts kicked off the Microsoft device code sign-in process and returned a user code, and when the target clicked the 'Confirm Meeting' prompt on the lure page, they were unknowingly copying the code to their clipboard. Then a pop-up prompt opened to Microsoft's real device sign-in page, asking the target to submit the code, which completed the device-code phishing attempt."
- Threat actors are probing two of 14 vulnerabilities newly disclosed in XWEB EVO, the Dixell refrigeration supervisor now sold under the Copeland name. According to VulnCheck, the flaws in question are CVE-2026-124014 (an unauthenticated write of the system configuration file via config.lua) and CVE-2026-124010 (an unauthenticated root command execution flaw). These two flaws, along with seven others, only affect firmware builds that predate a 2021 rewrite, while the remaining five also impact the latest firmware, 5.8.8, which has reached end-of-support and won't be patched.. As of March 2026, Copeland ended software support for the XWEB EVO family, and has advised customers to move to XWEB Pro models.
- Microsoft has warned of a phishing campaign exploiting the widespread outage on November 12, 2026, that affected access to business email and other cloud services across multiple regions. "The messages impersonate Microsoft 365 service health notifications and reference the legitimate Exchange Online incident EX1550543," Microsoft said. "The activity is consistent with credential phishing, although credential collection and malware delivery have not been confirmed." The outage has since been attributed to a software defect introduced in a July 2026 update for network gateway servers.
- Threat actors are exploiting unpatched GeoVision camera software to deploy an XMRig cryptocurrency miner across 13 organizations. "All malicious activity stemmed from GeoStartupAgentService.exe; across many endpoints, the activity was run under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM account," Huntress said, adding the bulk of the attacks occurred between November 8 and November 10, 2026. The attack employs the Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) technique to tamper with antivirus protections like Microsoft Defender by making use of "wsftprm.sys." Also deployed as part of the intrusion chain is a PowerShell script that drops a custom Golang loader that uses BitTorrent DHT and PKARR for C2 server discovery for added resilience and to make it possible to move to new infrastructure without losing access to the infected machines. In the final stage, the loader sets up a scheduled task to execute itself every 15 minutes and ultimately deploys the miner.
Conclusion
The strange part isn't how clever some of these attacks have become. It's how many still work because of things nobody checked, fixed, or thought twice about.
And with finding flaws getting cheaper and exploiting them getting easier, that gap is only becoming harder to ignore. Plenty to unpack this week.

articles.title: The smart-heating, auto-leveling Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K 3D printer gets a $250 discount
articles.text:
The smart-heating, auto-leveling Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K 3D printer gets a $250 discount
If you’re after highly detailed 3D prints, this model has dropped to $399 in Elegoo’s Black Friday sale
The Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K resin 3D printer has dropped from $649.99 to $399 in the Black Friday sale. That’s a hefty saving - around 39% - on a printer that’s been built to churn out highly detailed models, so it’s ideal if you want to print miniatures and other intricate prints.
Today’s best Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K deal
The US Elegoo store is offering the printer for $399 as part of its Black Friday sale. This offer applies to the standalone printer, not bundles that include washing and curing equipment.
Don’t fret if you want a bundle or accessories, though: Elegoo’s extensive Black Friday sale also includes discounts on bundles that include post-processing machines and resin, and discounts are also available on accessories like build plates and PFA film.
Why we recommend the Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K
The Saturn 4 Ultra 16K’s headline feature is a 10-inch monochrome LCD with 16K resolution, which means that you get an impressive XY resolution of 14 x 19 microns.
The unit also has a generous 211.68 x 118.37 x 220mm build volume and print speeds of up to 150mm/h. It also serves up automated bed leveling, a heated resin tank, and an AI camera to monitor your prints.
Price context and historical value
The Saturn’s $399 price is a hefty 39% discount from the original $649.99. It’s a substantial discount if you’ve been considering a high-resolution resin printer.
That’s a great start, and we’d also point interested buyers to the variety of bundle and accessory deals available with this model. They may enable you to put together a purchase that better suits your needs.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K if… you want detailed resin prints for your models and miniatures - alongside generous build volume and useful automation
❌ Skip the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K if… you want your next 3D printer to be a low-maintenance model. Resin printing needs more handling, cleaning, curing, and ventilation than filament.

articles.title: ChatGPT suspenderá por 24 horas a quien busque material de abuso sexual infantil
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció que ChatGPT mostrará una advertencia a quien intente encontrar material de abuso sexual infantil, borrará la conversación y pausará el acceso a la cuenta durante 24 horas. La empresa también lanzó una herramienta que detecta imágenes de ese tipo, incluidas las generadas con IA.
Según el anuncio de la empresa, la advertencia explica que sexualizar a menores causa daño, también cuando el material pedido es artificial. Además del aviso, ChatGPT ofrece apoyo especializado para ayudar a la persona a dejar esa conducta.
Las sanciones aumentan si el comportamiento se repite. OpenAI indicó que las infracciones reiteradas pueden derivar en suspensiones más largas, en el cierre definitivo de la cuenta o en un reporte a las autoridades.
La página de ayuda de la compañía precisa el alcance. Las intervenciones rigen en los modos de chat y de trabajo, en la web y en el móvil, para cuentas personales. También puede verlas quien usa ChatGPT sin iniciar sesión.
Qué cuentas y funciones quedan fuera
Por ahora la medida no se aplica a los espacios de ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu ni Healthcare. Tampoco funciona en el modo de voz, en Codex ni en las aplicaciones de escritorio, según la misma página. La empresa agrega que el aviso puede variar según el país.
Cuando se activa la intervención, la conversación se detiene y no puede continuar. Si el usuario había iniciado sesión, el chat se oculta del historial y no puede reabrirse.
OpenAI dijo que diseñó el enfoque con organizaciones y asesores académicos que investigan la prevención del abuso sexual infantil, entre ellos Protect Children y la Lucy Faithfull Foundation. Joel Scanlan, de la Universidad de Tasmania, evaluó de forma independiente una prueba de mensajes disuasorios.
Frances Frost, directora de Promoción y Comunicaciones de la Lucy Faithfull Foundation, afirmó que su línea de ayuda Stop It Now ya recibe con frecuencia llamadas de personas a quienes un chatbot de IA las derivó a ese servicio.
Un detector que marca menos imágenes y acierta más
El segundo anuncio es un clasificador de imágenes, un programa que analiza archivos y asigna una puntuación según la probabilidad de que muestren abuso. Está pensado para detectar imágenes nuevas, que no figuran en bases de datos de material ya conocido. OpenAI afirma que es el primero de amplia disponibilidad con una señal específica para indicar si el material pudo ser generado con IA.
Lo entrenó y evaluó con ayuda del Centro Nacional para Menores Desaparecidos y Explotados de Estados Unidos (NCMEC), organización que opera la línea de denuncias CyberTipline. El acceso es gratuito, por la API de OpenAI, para organizaciones verificadas que lo soliciten.
En una prueba con imágenes subidas por usuarios, OpenAI estimó que el nuevo sistema señalaría 48% menos imágenes que su herramienta actual y encontraría aproximadamente la misma cantidad de abusos. Las imágenes marcadas tenían el doble de probabilidades de contener abuso.
Entre los primeros socios, fal informó que sus revisores confirmaron como material nuevo el 72% de las alertas de alta confianza. SafetyKit indicó que detectó el 90% de los casos de dibujos o animaciones que sexualizan a menores. Son resultados de pruebas de la empresa y de socios que ya usan la herramienta.
Guía para desarrolladores y apoyo a investigadores
OpenAI publicó además una guía para desarrolladores, elaborada con la Tech Coalition, Thorn, el NCMEC y la Internet Watch Foundation. También ofrecerá herramientas y capacitación a unidades policiales especializadas. La primera herramienta ayudará a revisar chats extensos y a armar cronologías, con acceso sujeto a la autorización de cada agencia.
OpenAI informó que la capacitación inicial será una presentación con una guía práctica, y que las siguientes se propondrán en conferencias regionales, nacionales e internacionales.

articles.title: Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login
articles.text:
Six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in, Dutch security consultancy Midnight Blue said earlier this week.
No patch is available, and the researchers say the newest firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the flaws.
Government cybersecurity agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany told operators this week to take the controllers' management interfaces off the internet.
For a controller left on the internet, updating the firmware, changing default passwords or turning on Strict mode is not enough on its own, the Belgian and Irish agencies said. Strict mode is a login protection that requires encrypted connections and session tokens, but one of the six flaws is in the gateway that enforces it.
The AK-SM800A runs a store's fridges and freezers, and maintenance firms can manage it remotely. Such controllers were targeted in attacks in France starting October 11, and in a second wave across Europe that began last week. The attacks caused unwanted defrost cycles and destroyed stock.
Germany's federal IT security agency, the BSI, says in a security notice that the AK-SM800A was involved in earlier incidents in which refrigeration units in several countries were tampered with.
The agency has no information about any exploitation of the six new flaws, and neither other agencies nor researchers link the flaws to those incidents.
The researchers examined firmware version 5.3.2, then the newest, and say every version up to and including it is affected.
No CVE identifiers have been assigned. The researchers are keeping technical details private while they work on disclosure with Danfoss, the Danish company that makes the controllers.
The vendor lists software package 5.4.0, dated November, as its newest release for the AK-SM800A. Its 5.4.0 readme and November update guide cover upgrade steps, and the guide adds a stricter password rule. Neither mentions a fix for any vulnerability.
In a follow-up statement carried by trade publication Cooling Post, the researchers said 5.4.0 does not patch the flaws: "It's not really possible either because according to the file timestamp this firmware was likely built on October 29, before the second wave of cyber attacks and well before our vulnerability reports."
The German agency first said in a press release this week that 5.4.0 was not affected. Later the same day, it changed that in a corrected statement: it cannot rule out for now that 5.4.0 is affected.
The vendor's advisory page lists no advisory for the six flaws as of today, and no date for a fix has been published.
Midnight Blue researcher Carlo Meijer found the six flaws in less than an hour of manual review, using firmware the vendor offers for download, and described them in a technical write-up.
Five of the flaws are in web request handlers that do not require a login, inside a program that runs as root. Through one of them, the researchers ran code as root on older firmware, version 3.3.0, and they found the same bugs in 5.3.2.
Strict mode closes almost all of the controller's web attack surface to users who have not logged in, including the flaw used in that demonstration. The sixth flaw is in the gateway that enforces Strict mode, a separate program that blocks every request except the login until a user has logged in.
When the researchers ran firmware 5.3.2 in an emulator with Strict mode on, that flaw crashed the gateway. The crash could be turned into code execution with more work, the researchers say, and the gateway lacks basic exploit defenses such as stack canaries.
With code running as root, an attacker could change the controller's settings, start defrost cycles and hide that activity from its logs.
The controllers do not use secure boot, the researchers found, so an attacker could plant code that survives a factory reset and a firmware update. An attacker could also make a controller unusable until it is replaced.
The researchers say the code almost certainly holds more flaws like these, and they call patching flaws one by one or turning on Strict mode "a misallocation of scarce security and personnel resources."
What Operators Can Do
Removing internet exposure must not wait for a patch, and it is needed even where firmware is current and Strict mode is on, the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium says.
The Belgian advisory and a similar Irish advisory recommend these steps:
- Find every controller whose management interface can be reached from the internet, including through a 4G or 5G modem, and remove that exposure.
- Give remote access only through a secure VPN or a protected internal network. Allowing only a service company's IP addresses through a firewall is a short-term measure.
- Check temperature setpoints, defrost schedules, alarm settings, user accounts and remote-access settings for changes you did not make.
The German agency adds that anyone who suspects a compromise should change all credentials and check that equipment connected to the controller works properly.
Before cutting off the data a controller sends to its refrigeration service company, operators should check contract and insurance terms, the Belgian advisory says. They should also set up protected remote access so that monitoring can continue.
Danfoss's own update guide says the AK-SM800A should not be directly reachable from the public internet, adding: “This recommendation applies to all software versions, including those with Strict Mode enabled.”
Ireland's National Cyber Security Centre also advises running the latest supported firmware, changing default passwords and turning on Strict mode, but says operators should not rely on those steps alone.
Danfoss told Cooling Post on October 12 that most units hit in France were either older models that no longer receive updates or current AK-SM800A units running outdated firmware.
The vendor fixed earlier flaws in the AK-SM800A in 2023 and 2025, including login bypass and command injection bugs. Version 5.3.2, which the researchers examined, is newer than all of those fixes.

articles.title: Instagram permitirá a los creadores poner enlaces de Amazon en cada video y publicación para ganar comisiones
articles.text:
Instagram anunció que los creadores de contenido podrán agregar enlaces de afiliado de Amazon directamente en sus Reels y publicaciones del feed, hasta 30 productos por video y 20 por publicación. Cada compra hecha a través de esos enlaces le dará una comisión a quien los publicó.
Un enlace de afiliado es una dirección web que identifica al creador que recomendó un producto, de modo que Amazon le pague un porcentaje cuando alguien compra. Hasta ahora, los creadores compartían esos vínculos en historias, mensajes privados o en la biografía de su perfil.
La función llega por ahora solo a Estados Unidos. Según Wired, los creadores deben ser adultos residentes en ese país, con una cuenta profesional y más de 1.000 seguidores. Engadget informó que Meta, la dueña de Instagram, no dijo si la extenderá a otros países.
Para activarla, el creador conecta su cuenta de Instagram con su cuenta de influenciador de Amazon desde la sección de monetización del panel profesional, según TechCrunch. Después, la red social agrega sola el enlace de afiliado cuando se etiqueta un producto de Amazon, aunque el creador pegue un enlace común.
Quién cobra y cómo se ve el enlace
Instagram afirmó que agregar los productos es gratis y que no cobra comisión ni cargos por transacción. Amazon sigue pagando las comisiones, y el creador puede ver la tasa estimada de cada producto antes de sumarlo a su contenido.
Wired describió un ejemplo que compartió Meta: una mujer se maquilla frente a la cámara y, sobre su nombre, aparece una pequeña imagen del producto. Al tocarla se abre una página dentro de Instagram con el precio. Si el usuario toca el artículo, la app lo lleva a Amazon para completar la compra.
Meta dijo a TechCrunch que los enlaces puestos directamente en Reels y publicaciones reciben cerca del doble de clics que los de la biografía. Cabe señalar que esa cifra es de la propia compañía.
Meta promete que el feed no se llenará de ventas
Megan Buckley, portavoz de Instagram, respondió a Wired sobre el efecto en los usuarios. “No esperamos una afluencia repentina de contenido de compras”, dijo. Agregó que los sistemas de recomendación seguirán mostrando contenido según los intereses de cada persona.
Durante años, Instagram permitió un solo enlace en la biografía. Eso impulsó servicios externos como Linktree, donde los creadores reunían varios vínculos en una página. En 2023 la red amplió el límite a cinco enlaces, según Wired.
En marzo, Meta presentó herramientas de afiliados en la conferencia Shoptalk. Nicola Mendelsohn, directiva de Meta, dijo entonces que “la era del enlace en la biografía por fin terminó”, según Retail Dive. Para Facebook, la empresa anunció a Amazon como primer socio en Estados Unidos, con Temu y eBay previstos para más adelante.
Engadget señaló que estos enlaces también dan a Meta información sobre los intereses de sus usuarios. Wired planteó que la medida podría molestar a quienes ya reciben mucha publicidad en internet. Meta lanzó el cambio justo antes del Black Friday y de la temporada de compras de fin de año.
Por ahora, la compañía no precisó cuándo ni dónde ampliará la función. Solo los creadores de Estados Unidos que cumplen los requisitos pueden conectar su cuenta de Amazon.
Qué es realmente Amazon
Amazon es una corporación multinacional de tecnología y comercio electrónico fundada por Jeff Bezos. Lo que comenzó en el garaje de Bezos en el estado de Washington como una modesta librería en línea, se transformó rápidamente bajo su liderazgo en la tienda minorista de internet más grande del mundo, vendiendo prácticamente cualquier tipo de producto.
Más allá de revolucionar las compras digitales y la logística global con servicios como Amazon Prime, la empresa se ha expandido para dominar otros sectores clave, destacando especialmente en la computación en la nube a través de Amazon Web Services (AWS) y el entretenimiento digital. Aunque Bezos dejó su puesto como director ejecutivo (CEO) en 2021, continúa guiando la visión general de la compañía desempeñándose como su presidente ejecutivo.
