articles.title: Cómo evitar que mi vecino esté conectado a mi red WiFi y mejorar la velocidad del internet
articles.text:
Una conexión lenta, cortes frecuentes o dispositivos desconocidos en la lista del router pueden indicar que alguien ajeno al hogar como un vecino usa la red WiFi.
En este sentido, se explican varios ajustes que se pueden realizar en casa para proteger la red de internet de intrusos que no solo roben banda de ancha; pueden en casos más graves intentar acceder a datos guardados en los dispositivos conectados.
Qué ajustes hacer en la configuración inicial del router
El router funciona como la puerta de entrada a internet de teléfonos, ordenadores, televisores, cámaras y otros dispositivos conectados. Si mantiene sus parámetros iniciales, una persona con conocimientos básicos puede identificar el modelo, buscar sus claves predeterminadas e intentar entrar al panel de control.
Las credenciales de fábrica de muchos routers están disponibles en manuales, foros y sitios web. Cambiar el usuario y la contraseña de administración permite recuperar el control sobre la red y evita que una clave conocida por terceros abra la puerta a la configuración interna del dispositivo.
El primer paso consiste en conectar un ordenador al router mediante un cable de red. Esa vía permite realizar los cambios desde una conexión directa, sin depender del WiFi que se busca proteger. Antes de modificar opciones, conviene anotar los datos actuales o tomar capturas de pantalla de la configuración.
Luego, se debe abrir un navegador e ingresar la dirección del router. Las más frecuentes son 192.168.1.1 y 192.168.0.1, aunque pueden variar según el proveedor de internet y el modelo. El manual del aparato suele incluir la dirección correcta, junto con el usuario y la clave de acceso iniciales.
Por qué se deben modificar las contraseñas
La prioridad es modificar la contraseña del panel de administración y la clave de la red inalámbrica. Ambas deben ser diferentes entre sí y distintas de las que figuran en la etiqueta del router. Una clave extensa, con letras, números y símbolos, dificulta los intentos de acceso por prueba automática.
Asimismo, es aconsejable guardar esas contraseñas en un gestor seguro en lugar de anotarlas en papeles visibles o enviarlas por mensajes. Si los datos de acceso ya fueron cambiados y nadie los recuerda, es posible restablecer el router a sus valores de fábrica mediante el botón de reinicio y crear nuevas credenciales.
Cómo saber si hay dispositivos ajenos conectados al WiFi del hogar
La interfaz de gestión del router muestra una lista de aparatos conectados, tanto por WiFi como por cable. Allí pueden aparecer el nombre de cada dispositivo, su dirección de red y, en algunos casos, la marca del dispositivo. Revisar esa relación permite detectar teléfonos, ordenadores o televisores que no son del hogar.
Ante un dispositivo desconocido, se puede expulsarlo desde el panel y bloquear su dirección en la lista de acceso restringido, si el modelo ofrece esa función. Después conviene cambiar la clave inalámbrica para evitar que vuelva a ingresar. La revisión periódica de los equipos conectados ayuda a detectar intrusiones a tiempo.
Por qué se debe cambiar el nombre de la red WiFi
El nombre de la red, conocido como SSID, puede revelar información innecesaria. Algunos routers incluyen de forma automática el nombre del proveedor de internet, la marca del aparato o referencias al lugar de domicilio.
Es preferible elegir una denominación neutra, sin apellidos, números de departamento, direcciones ni datos que permitan identificar a la familia.
Ocultar el SSID puede sumar una capa adicional de discreción, aunque no sustituye una contraseña segura porque usuarios con conocimientos técnicos todavía pueden detectar la red. La medida central sigue siendo una clave robusta y un sistema de cifrado actualizado, como WPA2 o WPA3, si el router lo admite.

articles.title: AMD-Powered Lux Supercomputer Opens to Scientific Users at Oak Ridge
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
AMD-Powered Lux Supercomputer Opens to Scientific Users at Oak Ridge
AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced that the Lux SI + HPC supercomputer is open to scientific users at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). Ranked No. 14 on today's TOP500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers, Lux was developed through a public-private partnership between AMD and the DOE. The supercomputer provides the first dedicated U.S. AI Factory for the Genesis Mission, the DOE-led initiative to advance AI-driven science.
Lux brings together AMD EPYC processors, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD Pensando networking and AMD ROCm software in a system built by HPE. The system combines AI with high-performance modeling and simulation to expand U.S. capabilities in science, energy and national security.
Thomas Zacharia, senior vice president, Global Public Sector and Strategic Partnerships, AMD"Lux shows what is possible when national laboratories, government and industry work together to advance scientific discovery. By bringing high-performance computing and AI closer to researchers, we are helping them explore new approaches to complex problems and make better use of simulation and experimental data. This partnership builds on a strong foundation at Oak Ridge and supports an open, sovereign AI stack with tools that can benefit researchers across the country".
Georgia Tourassi, associate laboratory director for Computing and Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory"Lux represents the first major addition to DOE's computing infrastructure in support of the Genesis Mission, translating an ambitious national vision for SI-driven science into tangible capabilities for researchers. By expanding the computational resources available to the scientific community, Lux will help accelerate the integration of SI, modeling and simulation, and experimental data to advance discovery in areas critical to our nation's energy, economic competitiveness and security."
Trish Damkroger, senior vice president and general manager, HPC & AI Infrastructure Solutions at HPE"Together with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD, we have delivered breakthrough engineering innovation to advance the nation's scientific computing resources, and now with the debut of Lux, we are furthering what we can accomplish as a proven public-private partnership. We're proud of our continued collaboration and investment in the Genesis Mission to stand up one of its first AI systems that will scale scientific research and make transformative breakthroughs to advance national initiatives."
Expanding Computing Access for the Genesis Mission
The Genesis Mission projects allocated to run on Lux include AI-assisted fusion power plant design, an AI-based foundation model factory for materials development and advanced manufacturing, and Earth system prediction to forecast water availability, streamflow and river temperature in the Tennessee Valley Authority region.
Lux marks the next chapter in the longstanding relationship among AMD, HPE, DOE and Oak Ridge to advance American science. Building on the computing foundation established at ORNL by the Frontier supercomputer, the first supercomputer to break the exascale barrier, Lux expands that foundation with dedicated capacity for AI-driven research. The upcoming Discovery supercomputer will extend this commitment with deeper integration of AI and high-performance computing. Together, these systems support the Genesis Mission by helping researchers connect simulation, AI and scientific data to accelerate discovery.
AMD is also working with ORNL to support DOE's American Science Cloud, a national platform designed to extend advanced AI and high-performance computing capabilities across DOE laboratories, universities and mission partners in support of the Genesis Mission.
For researchers, Lux provides an opportunity to train and refine models using scientific data, to combine AI with established simulation methods, and to investigate problems that require computing beyond their home institutions. Its delivery extends the AMD and ORNL collaboration behind Frontier into dedicated capacity for AI-driven science.
Researchers and organizations interested in using Lux to advance Genesis Mission research are encouraged to contact ORNL's Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF) to discuss their computing needs and applicable access pathways. Visit the ORNL Lux resource page to learn more about the system and connect with the OLCF team.

articles.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max with training, attention optimizations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max with training, attention optimizations
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. today introduced Qwen4-Max, its newest and most capable large language model.
The algorithm not only generates higher-quality output than its predecessor but also costs less. Those improvements are the result of a new architecture, Qwen4, that made the LLM’s training run more efficient. Additionally, Alibaba has equipped the model with an upgraded attention mechanism.
Qwen4-Max’s backbone, the part of an LLM that functions as its main processing engine, comprises 2.4 trillion parameters. The model activates only 71 billion at any given time. The backbone is supported by 328 billion so-called N-gram parameters, which function as a kind of cache. They save the results of oft-repeated calculations and thereby remove the need to compute them from scratch every time.
An LLM’s artificial neurons are organized into sets known as layers. When the model learns something new during training, a piece of data called a gradient travels through the layers and refines their output. The gradient moves through them one by one starting from the last layer, which finalizes and displays prompt responses.
Qwen4-Max includes a feature that enables the gradient to skip some layers. That feature, or residual, is effectively a shortcut inside the LLM. Its purpose is to reduce errors during the training workflow, which in turn lowers costs and improves output quality.
Residuals can also be found in many other LLMs. Historically, the mechanism was implemented as a single gradient transportation channel. Qwen4-Max’s implementation of the technology features four channels. Moreover, those channels have a “gate” that can adjust the movement of gradients to further improve the training process.
Qwen4-Max’s attention mechanism, a module that helps it understand user prompts, features two key customizations. The first is a technology called Gated DeltaNet that lowers the amount of hardware needed to process large prompts. The second optimization, QSA, skips pieces of data that the LLM doesn’t need to answer a prompt. That arrangement further lowers infrastructure costs.
Alibaba compared Qwen4-Max with its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, using an internal benchmark that includes knowledge work tasks. The former model achieved a higher score and used up to 35% fewer tokens to complete tasks. Those savings grew to 49% when the models were tested using the Terminal-Bench 4.0 suite of coding challenges.
Qwen4-Max is available through Alibaba’s cloud platform. The company plans to open-source a collection of smaller models based on the same technologies further down the line. It’s also open-sourcing Qwen-Live-Delivery-Plugin, an extension that makes Qwen4-Max better at performing time-consuming tasks.
When an LLM is assigned a long-horizon project, users often have to wait until the model completes its work before they can review the results. Alibaba’s plugin shortens the wait. It enables Qwen4-Max to quickly deliver an initial draft and then iteratively add improvements. Users can give the model feedback along the way to refine its work.

articles.title: Researchers ‘recognize that AI will never replace HPC,’ says AMD executive — high-precision workloads will ‘exist for a very long time’ even as AI usage expands
articles.text:
Researchers ‘recognize that AI will never replace HPC,’ says AMD executive — high-precision workloads will ‘exist for a very long time’ even as AI usage expands
When FP64, AI, and quantum collide
While AI continues to reshape industries across science and mathematics, traditional supercomputing has seemingly taken a back seat. However, AMD's Scott Tease told Tom's Hardware Premium that most HPC sites “recognize that AI will never replace HPC,” and suggests that building a heterogeneous compute stack is the best path forward to tackle bleeding-edge research, despite Nvidia pushing performance on lower-precision data types higher for AI workloads at the cost of native performance for the important double-precision FP64 format that’s critical for HPC workloads.
A heterogeneous compute stack brings together quantum, HPC, and AI under one roof, a fleet that AMD is helping pilot at Oak Ridge National Laboratory alongside IBM. Tease is AMD’s corporate vice president of HPC and sovereign AI, who joined the company earlier this year after more than a decade at Lenovo (and, before that, another 13 years at IBM). We spoke with Tease ahead of SC26 to get a read on the state of HPC, how it intersects with AI, and what’s actually driving the research community in a time when computer chips are driving headlines about international espionage plots.
An awful lot of numbers
FP64 is important for HPC workloads because of its precision. FP64 is a hot-button issue, largely due to how Nvidia’s GPUs have progressed over the past two generations. Or rather, how they haven't progressed. Nvidia’s latest Rubin GPU has 33 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, which is lower than the four-year-old H100’s 34 TFLOPs of FP64. For context, AMD’s year-old Instinct MI355X peaks at 78.6 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, while its upcoming HPC-angled MI430X peaks at 288 TFLOPs.
Nvidia has leaned on emulation to drive FP64 performance higher, a tactic that AMD is now pushing back on, but regardless, it’s easy to see why the HPC world could feel left behind in this new AI era. AI is defined by fuzzy, low-precision data formats, which is diametrically opposed to the accuracy of high-precision FP64. And, over the last generations of hardware from the big green giant that is Nvidia, FP64 performance has seemingly stalled in favor of driving low-precision data formats for AI workloads.
“Maybe a few years ago, people in HPC might have felt a little threatened by AI because it was taking some of the limelight,” Tease told Tom’s Hardware Premium. “But I think now they’ve come to realize that AI is an essential part of scientific discovery today. It’s just, how are you going to deploy it?”
That central question recontextualizes the apparent conflict between AI compute and HPC compute. Tease pointed to researchers spawning dozens of agents to explore viable paths for a given intent, while still leaving the complex simulations for a traditional FP64-driven HPC fleet. “...to try to do that with old approaches where you have islands of CPUs or islands of GPUs or something like that, and they're very different. They're not interconnected. It's just not going to be able to keep up,” Tease said.
Enter quantum
One of the challenges right now is actually connecting those systems, which is an area AMD is exploring with its recent collaboration with IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory to deploy AMD’s “classical” computing stack in the Umbra HPC system alongside IBM’s 129-qubit Quantum Nighthawk quantum computer. The systems will connect to the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, allowing researchers to “explore how integrated quantum, AI, and scientific computing can accelerate scientific discoveries and national security.”
If the HPC crowd felt slighted by AI, you can imagine how quantum researchers probably feel.
Regardless, Tease says the future of scientific computing looks like a unified fleet that brings together AI, HPC, and quantum. “There [are] going to be a lot of problems where quantum will not be the be-all, end-all. There are some problems like human health, chemistry, where quantum’s going to allow us to do things we really can’t do with classical computing today. So having those things coexist, having them in a single workload, is where we want to get to.”
Scheduling workloads for HPC is a solved game, with open-source schedulers like Slurm driving much of the TOP500 to properly schedule workloads on supercomputers. Tease described something that goes deeper to connect these systems. “What we want to be able to do is not only do those kinds of ‘where should it go, here or there’ for HPC, we want to figure out when AI could be applied to it, when [GPU acceleration is] appropriate… and also when is it best to go in a quantum environment?”
The Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility is a test bed for figuring out how to hook these systems together properly. The press release explicitly states that it’s a “shared environment to evaluate the architectures, software, and workflows that future hybrid quantum systems will require.” The system is a co-design initiative with IBM, bringing together quantum and classical computing into one system.
With the system, researchers are exploring how to accelerate quantum error correction with classical systems, a critical step in quantum computing to weed out environmental influences. The goal is ultimately to accelerate quantum systems in the Quantum Genesis Q competition, an initiative launched by the U.S. Department of Energy that will provide up to $215 million in funding for quantum research.
By late 2028, the competition calls for quantum computers “with at least 100 logical qubits that are capable of performing hundreds of millions [of] fault-tolerant operations.” IBM describes the error correction research that will be performed at Oak Ridge as a “key component” in driving toward that goal. Separately, AMD announced last week an investment in quantum outfit PsiQuantum to provide CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs to drive the company’s first fault-tolerant quantum system.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: Oubliez le bruit, cette machine à café prépare 50 recettes dans un silence absolu
articles.text:
| Facilité d'emploi |  | 
| Dimensions (HxLxP) | 25.1 x 25.1 x 45.2 cm | 
| Carafe à lait | Oui | 
| Deux cafés simultanément | Oui | 
| Type de broyeur | acier | 
| Deux bacs à grains | Non | 
| Contenance | 300 g | 
| Trappe pour café moulu | Oui | 
| Réservoir d'eau | 1.8 L | 
| Cartouche filtrante | Oui | 
Avec l'Aromis LatteGo Pro, Philips voit les choses en grand. Machine volumineuse et résolument premium, elle s'appuie sur un superbe écran tactile pour piloter un catalogue pléthorique de 50 recettes et décline toutes les (meilleures) fonctionnalités embarquées par les machines premium.
Dans l'univers des machines à café automatiques avec broyeur, il y a les modèles compacts qui se font discrets, et il y a la Philips Aromis LatteGo Pro (également désignée sous la Série 8000). Ce modèle élitiste, lancé autour de 1000 €, est aussi imposant qu’exhaustif.
Conçue comme la machine de tous les superlatifs, elle embarque un très large écran tactile donnant accès à pas moins de 50 recettes. Capable d'extraire à chaud comme à froid, elle est livrée avec deux carafes LatteGo, histoire de multiplier les plaisirs lactés. Une telle polyvalence a logiquement un impact sur son tour de taille, mais la promesse d'une expérience “barista” à domicile, appuyée par un fonctionnement annoncé comme ultra-silencieux, est particulièrement alléchante.
Autant le dire d'emblée : la Philips Aromis n'est pas faite pour les cuisines exiguës. C'est un beau bébé, lourd et particulièrement volumineux, qui exigera une place de choix sur le plan de travail. Côté design, les matériaux inspirent globalement confiance. On note même une petite touche de bois très élégante (et plutôt inédite) située au-dessus de la buse vapeur. Néanmoins, à ce niveau de prix, on aurait apprécié que le fabricant intègre davantage d'acier ou d'inox. Ici, le plastique règne en maître et certains emboîtements manquent d'un poil de précision.
C'est en façade que la montée en gamme prend tout son sens. Si la récente Philips 5500 LatteGo proposait déjà une prise en main facilitée avec ses sept touches sensitives colorées et son petit afficheur central, l'Aromis pousse le concept à son paroxysme.
Fini les touches physiques autour d'un petit cadran : la machine déploie un large et superbe écran tactile TFT couleur sur toute sa largeur, ringardisant instantanément la gamme inférieure. La lisibilité est parfaite, le tactile très réactif, et toutes les boissons sont écrites en toutes lettres pour naviguer avec fluidité dans le catalogue gargantuesque de 50 recettes.
Le niveau de personnalisation est, lui aussi, exceptionnel. Pour chaque boisson (café, lacté, chaud ou froid), l'utilisateur peut ajuster la quantité en tasse, celles d'eau et de lait, la température (trois niveaux) ou encore l'intensité (cinq à sept niveaux selon la recette via My Coffee Choice).
La personnalisation est pleinement aboutie et rendue simple grâce à l'écran tactile, dans lequel on peut naviguer sans aucun problème, sans avoir besoin d'un diplôme d'ingénieur en barista.
Pour les boissons lactées, on retrouve avec plaisir le système LatteGo, véritable marque de fabrique du fabricant. Il s'agit d'un petit pot en deux parties qui vient se clipser au niveau de la buse vapeur. Fait notable, la machine est livrée avec deux carafes distinctes : une pour le chaud, une pour le froid. S'il n'est pas possible de régler mécaniquement l'épaisseur de la mousse de lait, le résultat en tasse est absolument divin et l’autrice de ces lignes en a encore les papilles toutes retournées…
Côté contenants, l'Aromis voit large au sommet : son bac à grains offre une très généreuse capacité de 300 g, de quoi espacer les recharges. À l'intérieur, Philips reste fidèle à son broyeur 100 % en céramique (matériau reconnu pour sa durabilité et qui évite de surchauffer la mouture), réglable sur 12 niveaux de finesse pour s'adapter à toutes les torréfactions. On y trouve également la traditionnelle trappe pour café moulu. L'eau, quant à elle, est stockée dans un réservoir de 1,2 l logé en façade, ce qui facilite grandement son extraction.
Le principal point noir de cette débauche technologique ? Sa lenteur. Entre la mise sous tension, le temps de chauffe et le rinçage des buses, l'Aromis met 73 s avant d'être prête à couler le premier café, figurant de fait parmi les modèles les plus lents de notre comparatif.
L'entretien est souvent le talon d'Achille des machines hyper-équipées, mais Philips maîtrise son sujet grâce à son système LatteGo. Dépourvu de tuyaux, le petit pot à lait se démonte en un clin d'œil et se rince sous l'eau en quelques secondes (ou passe au lave-vaisselle).
L'autre grande force de cette Aromis réside dans sa gestion intelligente de l'eau. Contrairement à de trop nombreuses concurrentes, la Philips anticipe. Elle calcule si le niveau du réservoir sera suffisant pour la recette demandée et prévient l'utilisateur avant de broyer le grain. Un excellent comportement qui évite le gaspillage.
Les rinçages automatiques sont par ailleurs très économes : la machine utilise seulement 14,1 ml d'eau à l'allumage et 22,8 ml à l’extinction, là où une Ninja Auto Barista Pro gobe près de 60 ml à chaque fois.
Enfin, point crucial pour la pérennité de l'appareil, le groupe d'extraction est entièrement amovible : on y accède très simplement en retirant le réservoir d'eau afin de le rincer sous l'eau claire.
Pour aller plus loin :
Le passage de la Philips Aromis LatteGo Pro dans notre laboratoire révèle des performances de haut vol en matière de broyage et de chauffe.
L'Aromis propose pas moins de sept niveaux d'intensité. Sur le réglage le plus bas, notre balance affiche très exactement 7 g de mouture. C'est un excellent point, puisque cela correspond parfaitement à la dose requise théorique pour préparer un véritable expresso dans les règles de l'art ! Le niveau intermédiaire distribue 8,8 g de café, tandis que le réglage maximal grimpe jusqu'à un très impressionnant 13,4 g pour les amateurs de boissons particulièrement corsées. Nous sommes dans les bonnes proportions.
La gestion de la température est, elle aussi, d'une rare précision. La machine propose trois réglages de température. Au niveau minimal, nous avons mesuré entre 82 et 84 °C. Au niveau intermédiaire, l'eau oscille entre 86,8 et 87,1 °C. Enfin, courtisée au maximum, elle atteint 91 à 96 °C. Ce sont des températures d'extraction absolument parfaites, capables de sublimer n'importe quel type de torréfaction sans jamais brûler le grain ni altérer le goût.
La machine se montre en revanche un brin moins pointilleuse sur le respect des volumes en tasse. Quand on lui demande de couler 40 ml, elle en délivre 51,8 ml. De même, une demande de 30 ml se solde par 37 ml. Elle a donc tendance à être un peu trop généreuse en eau, un détail qu'il faudra impérativement garder à l'esprit lors du paramétrage de vos recettes préférées pour éviter de surdiluer votre boisson.
Enfin, le temps d'extraction, chronométré à 19 s, frôle de très près l'idéal théorique (situé entre 20 et 30 s) pour garantir une belle crema.
C'est la véritable prouesse de cette machine. Oui, l'Aromis LatteGo Pro est un monstre de silence. En phase de broyage — l'étape généralement la plus assourdissante —, notre sonomètre affiche un exceptionnel 53 dB. Elle se hisse instantanément au panthéon des machines les plus silencieuses de notre comparatif, dans la droite lignée de la Philips 5500.
L'extraction est tout aussi feutrée, mesurée à seulement 47 dB. Vous pouvez préparer votre café à 6h du matin sans aucune crainte de réveiller votre ado en pleine hibernation ni risquer la séparation avec votre moitié.
La Philips Aromis LatteGo Pro est une machine qui assume sa démesure. Volumineuse et un brin fainéante au réveil (il lui faut un peu de temps pour chauffer), elle demande de la place et de la patience. Mais une fois ces concessions acceptées, elle déploie une expérience utilisateur remarquable. Son grand écran offre une navigation limpide au cœur d'un catalogue pharaonique (50 recettes), les extractions bénéficient de températures parfaites et son système lacté brille par sa simplicité d'entretien. Le tout est couronné par un silence de fonctionnement quasi absolu lors du broyage. Une véritable bête de compétition pour les caféinomaniaques qui aiment s'entendre penser le matin.
Sur le segment très exigeant des machines ultra-polyvalentes à grand écran, la Philips Aromis LatteGo Pro croise le fer avec des pointures comme la De'Longhi Eletta Explore. Si l'Italienne conserve l'avantage d'une mise en route bien plus véloce et d'une finition un peu plus léchée (davantage de métal, moins de plastique), la Philips réplique avec des arguments de poids. Son silence de fonctionnement est tout bonnement inégalé, son catalogue de 50 recettes donne le tournis, et son système LatteGo s'avère bien moins contraignant à nettoyer au quotidien que les carafes traditionnelles. C'est une alternative de choix pour les buveurs de lattes qui privilégient le confort acoustique.

articles.title: Cómo transferir fotos, datos y contactos al iPhone 18 Pro Max desde otro iPhone o Android
articles.text:
Pasar fotos, contactos y aplicaciones al nuevo iPhone 18 Pro Max no requiere un solo camino: Apple ofrece distintos métodos según el equipo de origen, y elegir el adecuado evita pérdidas de información y demoras innecesarias.
Quien llega desde otro iPhone puede usar Inicio Rápido o restaurar una copia de iCloud; quien viene de un dispositivo Android cuenta con una aplicación específica para trasladar sus datos durante la configuración inicial. En ambos casos, conviene preparar el terreno antes de encender el teléfono nuevo.
Qué preparar antes de iniciar la migración
Antes de arrancar conviene verificar el acceso a la Cuenta de Apple, con su contraseña y el método para recibir códigos de verificación. También es recomendable actualizar el teléfono anterior y generar un respaldo reciente.
Comprobar cuánto espacio ocupan fotos, videos, aplicaciones y archivos resulta igual de importante: ese contenido debe entrar en el almacenamiento disponible del iPhone 18 Pro Max. Si la migración es inalámbrica, se necesita además una conexión Wi-Fi estable.
Ambos equipos deben permanecer conectados a una fuente de alimentación durante el procedimiento. El tiempo necesario varía según la cantidad de información y las condiciones de la red: una biblioteca grande de fotos y videos puede hacer que el proceso tarde varias horas.
Transferencia directa desde otro iPhone
Inicio Rápido es el método recomendado para quien conserva su iPhone anterior. Permite configurar el equipo nuevo y elegir entre transferir los datos de manera directa o descargarlos desde iCloud.
El procedimiento exige activar Wi-Fi y Bluetooth en el iPhone viejo y dejarlo desbloqueado en la pantalla de inicio. Al acercar el iPhone 18 Pro Max, aparece la opción de usar la Cuenta de Apple para configurar el nuevo dispositivo, seguida del escaneo de una animación y la configuración de Face ID.
La decisión central llega después: la transferencia directa no depende del espacio disponible en iCloud y traslada todo el contenido del teléfono anterior, aunque obliga a esperar con ambos equipos juntos hasta el final. La opción desde iCloud, en cambio, descarga apps y datos en segundo plano, lo que permite usar el teléfono nuevo de inmediato, siempre que exista una copia de seguridad reciente.
Entre modelos con USB-C también puede usarse un cable para conectar ambos iPhone físicamente, una alternativa útil cuando el volumen de datos es grande. Apple ofrece, además, almacenamiento temporal en iCloud para facilitar el cambio de equipo cuando el plan habitual no alcanza.
Restaurar desde una copia de iCloud o de computadora
Cuando el iPhone anterior no está disponible (se perdió, se rompió o ya se vendió), la alternativa es restaurar desde una copia de iCloud. Durante la configuración inicial, el asistente ofrece iniciar sesión con la Cuenta de Apple y elegir el respaldo correspondiente según su fecha y tamaño.
También existe la vía de la computadora. En Mac se utiliza el Finder y en Windows la aplicación Dispositivos Apple (o iTunes en versiones anteriores del sistema). Conviene generar primero una copia cifrada del iPhone viejo si se quieren conservar datos sensibles, como contraseñas guardadas o información de Salud, y después restaurar el iPhone 18 Pro Max seleccionando esa copia desde el equipo conectado por cable.
Esta vía resulta más rápida cuando hay mucho contenido y la conexión a internet es lenta.
Migrar desde Android con la app Pasar a iOS
Quien cambia de sistema operativo debe recurrir a la aplicación Pasar a iOS (también llamada Trasladar a iOS), disponible en Google Play o descargable como APK si el Android no tiene acceso a la tienda.
Con ambos teléfonos conectados a la corriente y el Android en una red Wi-Fi, la configuración del iPhone 18 Pro Max ofrece la opción “Transferir datos desde Android”. El vínculo entre ambos equipos se cierra con un código de seis dígitos y la conexión del Android a la red Wi-Fi temporal que crea el iPhone.
La aplicación traslada contactos, historial de mensajes, fotos, videos, archivos, calendarios, marcadores del navegador, cuentas de correo, y mensajes y archivos multimedia de WhatsApp. Las aplicaciones gratuitas con versión equivalente en la App Store también pueden recuperarse, aunque conviene revisar cuáles faltan tras la migración.
Música, libros y archivos PDF no se transfieren con esta herramienta y deben moverse por otra vía, como un servicio en la nube.

articles.title: Cuatro clásicos y un remake: así es el pack de The Legend of Zelda que trae una Game & Watch y el nuevo 'Ocarina of Time'
articles.text:
Nintendo suele hacerlo bastante bien a la hora de crear remakes de sus videojuegos y 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time' es una nueva muestra de ello. Tras las buenas críticas que ha recibido este título, algunas tiendas no se han limitado a lanzar descuentos, sino a incluirlo en algunos packs de lo más interesantes como el que tiene PcComponentes que tiene un precio de 119,99 euros.
Game & Watch + The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2)
Un pack con varios videojuegos retro
Este pack que podemos encontrar en PcComponentes incluye dos cosas: en primer lugar, el mencionado videojuego de 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time' para Nintendo Switch 2; en segundo lugar, la consola retro Game & Watch de la saga The Legend of Zelda.
La Game & Watch es una serie de consolas que lanzó Nintendo con versiones de algunas sagas, y la de The Legend of Zelda es especialmente interesante por los cuatro videojuegos que vienen incluidos:
- 'The Legend of Zelda'
- 'Zelda II: The Adventure of Link'
- 'The Legend of Zelda: Link’s Awakening'
- 'Vermin', videojuego original de Game & Watch con Link como protagonista.
Por supuesto, no podemos olvidarnos de la segunda parte de este pack, el videojuego 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time'. Se trata del remake del título original que ha recibido una gran acogida por parte de público y prensa. La tienda no lo menciona, por lo que entendemos que se trata del título sin carátula especial.

articles.title: UAE's Vision Makers secures $4 million in a dual round
articles.text:
UAE's Vision Makers secures $4 million in a dual round
- Dubai-based Web3 startup Vision Makers has secured $4 million in cumulative funding across pre-seed and seed rounds, with its latest financing completed at a $20 million valuation. Investors include MH Ventures, Castrum Capital, Titans Ventures, Archer Capital, M2M Capital and Mira Capital.
- Founded in 2023 by Paul Farhi, Vision Makers develops a platform combining cryptocurrency research, blockchain data analysis, token discovery, market intelligence and decentralised trading tools.
- The funding will support platform development, product integration, technology infrastructure and improvements to its market intelligence and trading capabilities. Vision Makers has also secured a listing for its AI Hub in the Telegram Apps Center.
Press release:
Dubai-based Web3 startup Vision Makers has raised a cumulative $4 million across its pre-seed and seed funding rounds, with its latest financing completed at a valuation of $20 million.
The company named 11 investors across the rounds, including MH Ventures, Castrum Capital, Titans Ventures, Archer Capital, M2M Capital, Gemhead Capital, MYR Venture, AITECH Cloud Network, Block Rise, Zerone Ventures and Mira Capital.
Founded in 2023 by Paul Farhi, Vision Makers develops a platform that brings together cryptocurrency research, market intelligence, token discovery, blockchain analytics and decentralised trading tools. The company aims to reduce the need for users to navigate multiple services when researching and trading digital assets.
Its platform includes conversational AI-powered research tools that help users analyse market information, identify digital assets and access trading functions. Vision Makers has also launched an AI Hub, listed in the Telegram Apps Center, featuring AI agents, simulations, digital items and marketplace functionality.
The company said it has surpassed 600,000 registered users across its ecosystem, with more than 110,000 marketplace transactions completed and over 14,000 listings created. It also reported more than 30,000 active users during a 30-day period, although it did not specify the dates covered.
The funding will support further platform development, improvements to user experience and deeper integration across its existing products. Vision Makers also plans to strengthen its technology infrastructure, market intelligence capabilities and trading tools.
The company did not disclose how the $4 million was divided between its pre-seed and seed rounds or the amount raised in its most recent financing.

articles.title: [NDA 11/16@11AM PT] AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year — new Lux system developed between AMD and Department of Energy debuts at no. 14 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPUs
articles.text:
AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year — new Lux system developed between AMD and Department of Energy debuts at no. 14 with EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPUs
Lux is the first of two machines AMD is developing as part of a $1 billion deal with the DOE.
With the coming of SC26, also comes a fresh edition of the TOP500 list, which ranks the world's most powerful supercomputers. The newly released list illustrates that AMD powers 40% of the list, up 14% compared to 2025. AMD-powered systems now tally up to 202 on the list, up from 177 last year. New to the list is Lux, a “SI + HPC supercomputer” developed by AMD and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), which debuted at position 14.
AMD’s representation in the top 10 is familiar. After debuting in June, China’s LineShine remains in the top slot. El Capitan, powered by AMD chips, is in the second slot, followed by Frontier in third, HPC7 in sixth, and HPC6 in eighth, the same as the most recent TOP500 list.
Lux was announced a little over a year ago in a $1 billion deal between the DOE and AMD to develop two supercomputers. This is the first of the two, and the first time it’s been on the TOP500. The system was built by HPE and developed by AMD and DOE as part of the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission. The machine is housed in Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF), alongside machines like Frontier.
Lux relies on over 4,000 Instinct MI355X GPUs separated into over 500 nodes. For HPC workloads using FP64, the machine is capable of 317 PetaFLOPS. For AI training, the machine peaks at 20 ExaFLOPS of FP8, and for inference, 40 ExaFLOPS of FP4. With 288 GB of HBM3E per GPU, the entire system has access to 1.1 PB.
The machine uses AMD EPYC host CPUs — we weren’t able to find details on the specific generation— and AMD’s Pensando networking, with nodes built inside HPE’s ProLiant Compute XD685.
| TOP500 Top 10 (Nov. 2026) |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Rank | Prev. Rank | Name | System | 
| 1 | 1 | LineShine | LingKun, LX2 304C 1.55GHz, LingQi, Kylin OS | 
| 2 | 2 | El Capitan | HPE Cray EX255a, AMD 4th Gen EPYC 24C 1.8GHz, AMD Instinct MI300A, Slingshot-11, TOSS | 
| 3 | 3 | Frontier | HPE Cray EX235a, AMD Optimized 3rd Generation EPYC 64C 2GHz, AMD Instinct MI250X, Slingshot-11, HPE Cray OS | 
| 4 | 4 | Aurora | HPE Cray EX - Intel Exascale Compute Blade, Xeon CPU Max 9470 52C 2.4GHz, Intel Data Center GPU Max, Slingshot-11 | 
| 5 | 5 | JUPITER Booster | BullSequana XH3000, GH Superchip 72C 3GHz, NVIDIA GH200 Superchip, Quad-Rail NVIDIA InfiniBand NDR200, RedHat Enterprise Linux | 
| 6 | 6 | HPC7 | HPE Cray EX255a, AMD 4th Gen EPYC 24C 1.8GHz, AMD Instinct MI300A, Slingshot-11, RHEL 9 | 
| 7 | 7 | Eagle | Microsoft NDv5, Xeon Platinum 8480C 48C 2GHz, NVIDIA H100, NVIDIA Infiniband NDR | 
| 8 | 8 | HPC6 | HPE Cray EX235a, AMD Optimized 3rd Generation EPYC 64C 2GHz, AMD Instinct MI250X, Slingshot-11, RHEL 8.9 | 
| 9 | 9 | Supercomputer Fugaku | Supercomputer Fugaku, A64FX 48C 2.2GHz, Tofu interconnect D | 
| 10 | 10 | Alps | HPE Cray EX254n, NVIDIA Grace 72C 3.1GHz, NVIDIA GH200 Superchip, Slingshot-11, HPE Cray OS | 
The machine has 3.5 million node-hours (one node running for one hour) per year, half of which are reserved for Genesis Mission research. Genesis Mission was established through an executive order in November 2025 with the stated goal of creating a “dedicated, coordinated national effort to unleash a new age of AI‑accelerated innovation and discovery that can solve the most challenging problems of this century.”
More specifically, the order lays out training scientific foundation models on Federal datasets, and creating “AI agents to test new hypotheses, automate research workflows, and accelerate scientific breakthroughs.” Lux is the first dedicated supercomputer for the Genesis Mission, but it joins existing machines that have been at least partially dedicated to research, including the Intel-powered Aurora at Argonne National Laboratory, which arrived fourth in the most recent TOP500.
Lux is built primarily for AI research, not as a successor to Frontier. Discovery is on track to debut as a next-gen flagship exascale supercomputer in 2028, also developed jointly by the DOE, AMD, and HPE.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: La Chine fait voler un avion électrique à 10 moteurs : l'Europe est définitivement à la traîne
articles.text:
Airbus et Boeing viennent peut-être de se faire ridiculiser par un concurrent chinois baptisé Comac. Ce 14 novembre 2026, le constructeur aéronautique chinois a fait voler pour la première fois le Comac CE-25A, un petit avion uniquement équipé de moteurs électriques.
Un premier vol habité pour le CE-25A, un petit avion électrique chinois
Ce samedi, le CE-25A a décollé de Binzhou, dans la province de Shandong, avec deux pilotes et un ingénieur d’essais à bord. L’avion est resté en l’air 16 minutes et 38 secondes exactement, parcourant 60 kilomètres environ. Comac indique que l’appareil a fonctionné normalement et que ces indicateurs de performance ont répondu à ses attentes.
En vérité, ce n’est pas la première fois que l’avion quitte le sol : en février dernier déjà, l’avion avait volé en total autonomie, sans personne à son bord. Puis ont ensuite été réalisés 19 vols de validation sans pilote avant d’y placer de vrais humains. Ce vol du CE-25A était donc la première démonstration de Comac d’un avion commercial électrique chinois avec un pilote.
Dévoilé pour la première fois à Shanghai en 2023, il aura fallu trois ans seulement à Comac pour développer cet avion. Il est conçu pour transporter 19 passagers sur des liaisons régionales courtes ; son autonomie ne lui permet pas d’aller plus loin. Selon les données communiquées par le constructeur, il affiche une masse maximale au décollage de 10 tonnes, une vitesse de croisière de 300 km/h, une altitude de croisière de 2 400 m et une autonomie annoncée de 400 km. Cet avion dispose de dix ventilateurs électriques carénés installés au-dessus des ailes. Fini les gros moteurs ou les turboréacteurs : Comac fait le pari de multiplier les petits moteurs électriques.
Une prouesse technique dont l’Europe et les États-Unis ne sont pas capable
Faire voler un avion électrique de 10 tonnes avec équipage est une prouesse car à cause de cette masse, il faut des batteries énormes et denses et trouver le bon équilibre entre poids et puissance. Les petits avions électriques existent depuis longtemps, mais concevoir un avion commercial avec plusieurs places à bord est une autre histoire. Pour le moment, le CE-25A n’est pas certifié, mais ça ne saurait tarder. Avec cet avion, la Chine poursuit sa stratégie de décarbonation entamée dans tous les secteurs.
Pour le moment, en Europe ou aux États-Unis, chez Airbus ou Boeing, aucun avion 100% électrique de cette envergure n’a profité d’une démonstration. Il y a bien le français Aura Aero qui développe l’ERA, un avion régional hybride électrique de 19 places dont le premier vol est prévu en 2027. Outre-Atlantique aussi on s’intéresse à l’électrique avec le X1 de Heart Aerospace, mais il est surtout là pour développer des appareils hybrides également. Pour rester dans la course, les constructeurs européens et étatsuniens vont devoir pousser la manette des gaz. D’autant plus que Comac vient concurrencer Airbus aussi sur les avions longs courriers.

articles.title: Xbox : Microsoft ressuscite les écrans de démarrage mythiques des premières consoles
articles.text:
Pour célébrer les 25 ans de Xbox, Microsoft a décidé de faire un joli cadeau aux joueurs nostalgiques, avec les animations de démarrage des premières consoles de la marque. Et c’est franchement réussi !
En cette fin d’année 2026, Xbox fête ses 25 bougies. Un quart de siècle déjà depuis l’arrivée de la première console de Microsoft, un 15 novembre 2001. Pour marquer le coup, la firme américaine multiplie les clins d’œil à son histoire et aux joueurs qui l’accompagnent depuis ses débuts. Et parmi les petites attentions qui font plaisir, il y en a une toute récente (et gratuite) qui devrait réveiller quelques souvenirs.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Le plein de nostalgie chez Xbox
Comme l’a notamment relayé The Verge, Microsoft déploie actuellement une mise à jour permettant de retrouver plusieurs animations de démarrage historiques sur Xbox One et Xbox Series. Au programme : le boot emblématique de la toute première Xbox, mais aussi deux séquences tout aussi mémorables de la Xbox 360, celles de 2005, puis de 2010.
La mise à jour est en cours de déploiement et, bonne nouvelle, il y a de fortes chances qu’elle soit déjà disponible sur votre console. Nous avons d’ores et déjà pu essayer les différentes animations sur notre Xbox Series X, et quel plaisir de retrouver ces séquences pleines de nostalgie ! Notre préférence va évidemment au logo vert de la première Xbox, avec son ambiance sonore si particulière.
Pour en profiter, il suffit de se rendre dans les paramètres de la console, puis dans les options système et de démarrage, afin de sélectionner l’animation souhaitée. On peut ainsi passer d’une génération à l’autre en quelques secondes. C’est un détail, certes, mais qui permet d’ajuster son degré de nostalgie avant même de lancer son jeu (et c'est gratuit).
Cette initiative s’inscrit dans une célébration plus large des 25 ans de Xbox, avec notamment le lancement récent d’une manette dédiée et d'une console collector. Microsoft a aussi remis en lumière son catalogue historique, avec 21 nouveaux jeux de la première Xbox désormais compatibles avec les PC Windows, certains profitant même de succès à débloquer. Au total, 25 jeux Xbox sont compatibles PC.
De quoi prolonger les retrouvailles avec quelques classiques, sans forcément ressortir sa vieille console du placard.
PlayStation avait eu la même bonne idée… avant de faire marche arrière
Microsoft n’est pas le premier constructeur à jouer sur cette corde sensible. Pour les 30 ans de PlayStation, en décembre 2024, Sony avait lui aussi proposé aux possesseurs de PS5 de retrouver l’interface et les animations de démarrage des différentes générations de consoles, avec notamment le mythique lancement de la première PlayStation.
Une initiative qui avait été particulièrement bien accueillie par les joueurs. Mais cette parenthèse nostalgique n’avait malheureusement pas vocation à durer, puisque Sony avait rapidement retiré ces thèmes anniversaire, au grand regret d’une partie de la communauté.
Et c’est peut-être là que réside toute la bonne idée de Microsoft. Au-delà de la célébration ponctuelle, pourquoi ne pas laisser ces animations à disposition des joueurs ? Après tout, il ne s’agit que d’une option de personnalisation, qui ne gêne personne… Et qui fait manifestement plaisir à beaucoup de monde.
- La rétrocompatibilité au top
- Le Quick Resume, difficile de revenir en arrière
- Taillée pour l'avenir (HDMI 2.1, dolby vision/atmos, VRR)

articles.title: Knowledge graphs: 3 insights from GraphSummit 2026 - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Three insights you might have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of GraphSummit 2026
AI agents need more than enterprise data to be effective; they also need the business context that data lives in. Knowledge graphs could consolidate the enterprise context currently fed to different AI agents into a single knowledge layer.
Developers are already providing AI agents with business context through prompts. But without a central source of truth, they must repeat that work every time they build a new agent, rather than drawing on a shared knowledge layer, according to Jesús Barrasa (pictured), field chief technology officer of gen AI at Neo4j Inc.
“This knowledge layer, this idea of capturing your enterprise knowledge and using it as the context engine for your agents, not only gives you the consistency … it gives you the explainability,” he said during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. “That’s the source of my data. These are the elements that I use to produce the answer.”
During interviews at GraphSummit, theCUBE Research’s John Furrier spoke with industry experts from Collibra BV, Blitzy Inc., Raymond James Financial Inc., and Qiagen N.V., among others. They discussed how knowledge graphs can ground AI agents in shared, traceable enterprise knowledge to improve explainability, enable safer coding at scale, support drug discovery and transform business operations. (* Disclosure below.)
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Jesús Barrasa:
Insight #1: Runtime governance helps keep autonomous AI agents in check.
Governance is a key question for enterprise AI deployments. How do you ensure AI agents behave appropriately as they become more autonomous? Judgment calls that used to be made by people now need to be made by agents in seconds, requiring a shift toward runtime governance, according to Felix Van de Maele, chief executive officer and co-founder of Collibra BV.
Collibra has introduced several capabilities – Live Map, Maestro, Guardian Agents and Agent Contracts – built on Neo4j’s graph database. Together, they form a control system that helps businesses make sure their AI agents use the right information and follow the rules.
“The challenge is: how do you govern at the speed of AI, which is different than the way we had to govern five years ago?” Van de Maele told theCUBE. “Maestro gives our customers the ability to build these governance steward agents that automate up to 80% of the governance work. You’re able to govern quickly and efficiently enough to keep up with the demands of new AI workloads.”
Other solutions, such as Agent Contracts, focus on enforcing boundaries around AI agents’ behavior. They monitor agents’ actions and block those that violate predefined rules, helping prevent unauthorized actions, according to Van de Maele.
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Felix Van de Maele:
Insight #2: Knowledge graphs help AI agents work accurately and safely.
Changing one small piece of software can unexpectedly break something somewhere else. For Blitzy Inc., which runs thousands of AI coding agents at once to help businesses make large-scale system changes, a knowledge graph can map dependencies and the risks of change within a system.
A knowledge graph gives agents the context they need to make changes safely without being overwhelmed by millions of lines of code, according to Neeraj Deshmukh, director of engineering at Blitzy. The company also uses human-approved action plans and automated testing to keep the coding process on track.
“On top of that, we have agents who are watching other agents to make sure that they abide by the spec, the plan that we had created and approved by the human in the loop,” Deshmukh told theCUBE. “That ensures that there is no drift or hallucination.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Neeraj Deshmukh:
Insight #3: Knowledge graphs help financial firms verify AI accuracy and build trust in agent-driven workflows.
A knowledge graph helps Raymond James Financial Inc. put AI agents to work on data from established sources, according to Naveen Mahankali, vice president of technology at Raymond James.
We have golden sources; we have systems that we can rely on today, and we’re able to use agents to build and compare what we are building against the golden sources,” he told theCUBE. “With the knowledge graph, even when we pull the data from different sources, it sits in the Neo4j, and we run evals compared to the golden sources and make sure they’re 100% accurate before launching.”
Raymond James is also exploring how AI agents can help financial advisors serve clients more efficiently. The company has already launched Raimond, its proprietary AI assistant, explained Jeff Griffith, vice president of AI engineering and data science at Raymond James, who joined Mahankali during the interview.
“We have an AI assistant … it’s gotten huge adoption, and it’s just going to get smarter,” Griffith said. “That’s part of the core evolution of what we’re doing in terms of engineering. We’re changing how people — how everyone — works with a desktop that gives people the best AI tools to move from doing all the menial tasks to managing agents that are doing those tasks. In terms of skills and what we are looking for, it is shifting just from people who can do tasks to people who have a drive to solve a meaningful problem.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Jeff Griffith and Naveen Mahankali:

articles.title: 'Massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers': Surfshark joins the GTA VI excitement with an in-app easter egg — but warns of the risks the launch brings
articles.text:
'Massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers': Surfshark joins the GTA VI excitement with an in-app easter egg — but warns of the risks the launch brings
A Miami-themed visual skin arrives on iOS and Android alongside warnings that more than 750 scam sites could target eager gamers by launch day.
Anticipation for the latest Grand Theft Auto game is at fever pitch. But with cybercriminals looking to profit from the excitement, Virtual Private Network (VPN) provider Surfshark is marking the occasion with an in-app easter egg and a stern warning to those looking to grab the new game before release day.
The provider revealed that its researchers tracked more than 200 GTA-themed domains registered immediately after recent beta announcements. At least one in four of those sites was created to defraud eager players.
The company projects that the number of malicious or opportunistic domains will exceed 750 by the time the game finally hits store shelves.
The finding fits into a wider pattern of gaming fraud, echoing Surfshark's prior scam research showing how threat actors exploit major cultural moments to trick unsuspecting consumers.
A neon Easter egg on mobile
Firstly, to celebrate the release, Surfshark has rolled out a hidden visual theme across its iOS and Android apps.
Inspired by Google Doodles, the cosmetic skin is based on the neon-soaked Miami aesthetics closely associated with the franchise's fictional Vice City setting.
The feature is rolling out gradually to mobile users in the lead-up to launch day. It serves as a lighthearted touch for gaming enthusiasts who use the app on phones and tablets.
“As a huge gamer myself, I’m just as hyped as everyone else for this release, and sneaking a little game-inspired Easter egg into the app is a great testament to our teams’ creativity and drive for giving something fun back to the gaming community,” said Dovydas Godelis, CEO of Surfshark, in a press release.
“At the same time, massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers, and as a cybersecurity company, we must remind our users of that.”
Fake PC builds and bogus beta keys
Behind the colorful promotion lies a genuine security problem. Threat actors know that millions of players want early access or alternative ways to play. That demand makes gamers easy targets for credential harvesting and payment fraud.
According to Surfshark, existing fraudulent sites are baiting visitors with fake pre-orders, non-existent mobile installations, bogus beta keys, and cryptocurrency schemes. Others advertise cracked PC versions of the game, taking advantage of desktop gamers who do not want to wait for a delayed computer release.
"Cybercriminals thrive on cultural hype, and this release is the biggest opportunity in gaming history," added Godelis. "Gamers are being baited into downloading cracked builds or entering payment details on fake storefronts. We wanted to remind everyone to stay level-headed, double-check URLs, avoid suspicious third-party links, and keep their guard up. Scammers are counting on the moment when excitement outgrows caution."
Can a security app actually protect you from these scams? Only up to a point. While Surfshark's DNS-filtering and ad-blocking tools can block known malicious domains, software cannot stop you from handing over credit card numbers or account passwords on a convincing fake storefront if you ignore browser warnings.
Staying safe requires skepticism. Stick exclusively to official publisher announcements, verify website addresses carefully, and treat any download promising early PC builds or beta access as an immediate red flag.
Rene Millman is a seasoned technology journalist whose work has appeared in The Guardian, the Financial Times, Computer Weekly, and IT Pro. With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.

articles.title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026 — new chip accelerates agentic HPC workloads, arrives in 2028
articles.text:
Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026 — new chip accelerates agentic HPC workloads, arrives in 2028
Rubin HPC puts "over 50,000" CUDA cores on a chip, implies four-die layout
The Supercomputing 2026 conference is under way, and despite continuing turmoil elsewhere in the company, Nvidia has lots to reveal at the show. Foremost among its announcements today, Nvidia took the wraps off a new member of the Rubin GPU family called Rubin HPC, a chip that the company says is meant to accelerate agentic workflows and simulation for scientists, engineers, and analysts working with large data sets.
To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C.
Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip's physical layout alongside the announcement. (The representative image shared by the company wouldn't appear to take this into account.)
To keep data moving between Rubin HPC GPUs, Nvidia will use its NVLink 7 interconnect. The company didn't share any new details of the bandwidth or physical layer of this interconnect within the rack, but past disclosures about the tech have indicated that it retains the 3.6 TB/s of per-GPU bandwidth that NVLink 6 delivers while enlarging the size of its scale-up domain.
Nvidia didn't share any details of the Rubin HPC GPU's HBM capacity or bandwidth, and it also didn't share whether this part includes a rebalancing of compute resources towards native FP64, as AMD and Intel are touting at the conference with their own GPUs this week.
Nvidia instead touts the suitability of this chip for scientists and engineers using agentic workflows, for which the company expects faster simulation performance and therefore faster opportunities for discovery in those fields thanks to better agent performance in those domains.
In fields like climate research, genomic analysis, and financial simulation, Nvidia says the Rubin HPC GPU's "balanced design," with both higher compute resources and (presumably) faster data movement between nodes, will help feed the chip with the massive data sets typical of those workloads, minimizing idle compute resources and achieving better utilization.
Researchers, engineers, and analysts marshaling agent swarms to explore the problem spaces in their domains will also be able to take advantage of Nvidia's CUDA-X domain-specific libraries to boost performance on Rubin HPC, tightening the reasoning loop from hypothesis to simulation to refinement and hastening the pursuit of the most promising results.
Nvidia says Rubin HPC will arrive sometime in 2028.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.

articles.title: Melhor TV Box e Sticks: 6 modelos 4K para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor TV Box e Sticks: 6 modelos 4K para comprar em 2026
Precisa transformar sua TV em smart? Encontre os melhores modelos de TV Boxes e Sticks compatíveis com conteúdo em resolução Ultra HD
TV Boxes e TV Sticks são ótimas opções para quem quer transformar o televisor em um modelo smart, sem precisar comprar uma nova TV. Esses dispositivos também servem para smart TVs mais antigas, com poder de melhorar a fluidez de navegação.
Dongles avançados como o Fire TV Stick 4K Max são ideais para TVs 4K compatíveis com formatos HDR. Também há TV Boxes mais simples, a exemplo da Smart Tv Box 4K Intelbras, que focam no suporte aos principais apps de streaming.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista seis opções de TV Boxes ou Stick com resoluções de até 4K UHD. Confira modelos da Amazon, Xiaomi, Roku, Vivensis e Intelbras.
O Fire TV Stick 4K Max é o dispositivo de streaming mais potente da Amazon. O dongle oferece saída de imagem de até 4K UHD (3840 x 2160 pixels), chega com 2 GB de RAM e 16 GB de armazenamento para alocar seus aplicativos de streaming e jogos favoritos.
Além disso, o Fire TV Stick também suporta as tecnologias Dolby Vision e HDR10+ para aproveitar os realces de brilho, cor e contraste de conteúdos HDR em TVs elegíveis. E ainda é compatível com Dolby Atmos para uma experiência sonora mais imersiva.
O padrão Wi-Fi 6E é um dos diferenciais, já que é compatível com a banda de 6 GHz para alcançar velocidades de conexões mais rápidas e com menos latência. O dispositivo roda sob o sistema Fire OS da Amazon e tem saída HDMI 2.1 para conexão com televisores.
Dimensões: 108 mm (C) x 30 mm (L) x 14 mm (E)
A Xiaomi TV Box S 4K é um dispositivo de streaming ideal para quem deseja instalar vários aplicativos, já que possui 32 GB de armazenamento. Além disso, a TV Box com resolução máxima 4K UHD possui 2 GB de RAM para entregar desempenho fluido de navegação.
Há suporte para formatos de vídeo avançados como Dolby Vision e HDR10+, além de experiência sonora com Dolby Atmos e DTS:X. Vale lembrar, no entanto, que o televisor também precisa ser compatível com essas tecnologias para aplicar as melhorias de imagem e áudio.
O dispositivo opera sob o sistema Google TV, com Google Assistente e espelhamento de smartphones facilitados com o Google Cast. E também conta com Wi-Fi 6 para conexões mais rápidas, Bluetooth 5.2 e uma porta USB-A 2.0 para dispositivos de armazenamento externos.
Dimensões: 97 mm (C) x 97 mm (L) x 17 mm (A)
O Roku Streaming Stick Plus é um dongle custo-benefício focado em streaming com resoluções de até 4K. Ele tem apenas 1 GB de RAM, mas o sistema RokuOS é leve e otimizado, o que ajuda a reduzir o consumo de memória.
O dispositivo suporta HDR10 e HDR10+ e consegue reproduzir esses conteúdos se sua TV também for compatível com esses formatos. No entanto, o Roku Streaming Stick Plus não pode reproduzir imagens em Dolby Vision, ainda que seu televisor conte com a tecnologia.
Já falando sobre conectividade, o Roku Streaming Stick Plus chega com Wi-Fi 5 e conectividade Bluetooth, apesar de a empresa não especificar a versão.
Dimensões: 97 mm (C) x 20 mm (L) x 13 mm (E)
O Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K é uma versão mais modesta do modelo Max. Ele também oferece resolução máxima de 4K UHD e 2 GB de RAM, mas tem um processador menos potente e 8 GB de memória interna — a metade da capacidade da variante Max.
Outra diferença está no padrão Wi-Fi adotado, que é o Wi-Fi 6. Ele também utiliza o padrão de rede wireless 802.11ax e suporta as mesmas velocidades de acesso do Wi-Fi 6E, embora não funcione na frequência de 6 GHz que está sujeita a menos congestionamento de rede.
Ainda assim, o dongle roda sob o sistema Fire OS e é compatível com as tecnologias Dolby Vision e HDR10+ para reproduzir imagens de alta qualidade no padrão HDR.
Dimensões: 108 mm (L) x 30 mm (A) x 14 mm (E)
A Vivensis Stick VX Smart 4K é uma TV Box para quem quer assistir a séries, filmes, novelas e programas televisivos. Ele é o único dispositivo da lista que recebe sinal de TV aberta via satélite (banda KU), oferecendo mais de 80 canais gratuitos.
Fora isso, o aparelho também roda os principais apps de streaming sob o sistema operacional Android TV com resoluções de até 4K. E também é compatível com conteúdos HDR10 e HDR10+, caso seu televisor também tenha suporte.
O dispositivo ainda traz duas portas USB, conectividade Wi-Fi 5 e porta RJ45 para conexões cabeadas mais rápidas e estáveis. Há Bluetooth integrado, mas a versão 5.0 não dispõe de melhorias de estabilidade e eficiência das versões mais recentes.
Dimensões: 120 mm (C) x 120 mm (L) x 26 mm (A)
A Smart Tv Box 4K Intelbras é um dispositivo básico para transformar qualquer televisor em uma smart TV. Para isso, a TV Box roda o sistema Android TV, compatível com os principais apps de streaming como Netflix, Prime Video e HBO Max.
O aparelho é mais indicado para TVs simples que não suportam conteúdos em HDR, já que não possui suporte a HDR10 ou Dolby Vision.
Em compensação, ele traz uma porta RJ45 para conexões cabeadas à internet, duas entradas USB 2.0 e Bluetooth integrado na versão 5.0.
Dimensões: 162 mm (C) x 162 mm (L) x 75 mm (A)
A escolha pela melhor TV Box deve considerar desde o aspecto físico do dispositivo até as especificações de hardware, levando em conta também as limitações da TV. Fique de olho em:
TV Box e TV Stick são dispositivos que conseguem transformar TVs comuns em smart TVs. Mas os aparelhos têm formatos e conexões diferentes.
TV Boxes têm formato de caixa e precisam de um espaço para fixação no rack ou bancada. Eles também precisam estar conectados à tomada para funcionar e costumam oferecer portas USB e RJ45. Alguns modelos ainda podem receber sinal de antena parabólica, como o Vivensis Stick VX Smart 4K.
Já TV Sticks são extremamente compactos, em formatos similares ao de um pen drive. Eles não precisam ocupar uma entrada de tomada, já que a alimentação simples pode ser feita via USB do próprio televisor. Em compensação, eles não oferecem as portas de conexão que TV Boxes costumam entregar.
Não necessariamente. Uma TV Box precisa de internet para acessar apps de streaming e ferramentas que só funcionam online. Contudo, alguns modelos recebem sinal digital de TV aberta ou podem reproduzir conteúdos gravados em cartões microSDs e dispositivos de armazenamento, sem depender de internet.
TV Boxes falsificadas costumam ter falhas de impressão na embalagem, incluindo acabamentos de baixa qualidade e fontes diferentes. Enquanto isso, embalagens de produtos originais têm detalhes de fabricação completas e informações claras de fabricação.
Encontrar a certificação Play Protect nas informações da Google Play Store também é um bom indicador de produto original. E vale abrir o Mi Home pela Xiaomi TV Box e emparelhar o controle remoto: apenas produtos originais vão se conectar corretamente e aparecer no ecossistema Xiaomi.
Depende muito do modelo de sua TV e do quanto você está disposto a gastar. Comprar uma TV Box é a forma mais acessível de transformar seu televisor em um modelo smart. Mas se a TV for muito antiga, ela talvez não consiga aproveitar de tecnologias como HDR, processadores recentes e construções de tela mais modernas.
Por outro lado, adquirir uma smart TV elimina a necessidade de adquirir TV Boxes ou sticks à parte e ainda garante compatibilidade com tecnologias atuais. E ainda que o custo seja maior do que uma TV Box ou Stick, você pode encontrar smart TVs boas e baratas.

articles.title: Intel Faces Class Action Lawsuit Over PC Sales Slowdown Disclosures
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Intel Faces Class Action Lawsuit Over PC Sales Slowdown Disclosures
A class action lawsuit has been filed against Intel on November 13 in federal court in San Jose, naming CEO Lip-Bu Tan and CFO David Zinsner as defendants. Reuters reports that a Michigan pension fund is leading the shareholder lawsuit, which also covers investors who bought shares between July 23 and October 29. The main claim in the lawsuit is that Intel did not appropriately disclose just how badly its PC business was slowing down, to put it in plain terms. The lawsuit argues that Intel was too slow to disclose its weak consumer CPU demand, the excess inventory it was sitting on, and how that would hurt sales. The claim also points to August 2026, when Intel sold $23 billion worth of stock to raise capital, at $95 per share.
Intel has been struggling with sales in the client segment recently, as evidenced by its Q3 2026 earnings. In Q3, its client segment slipped 5% year over year to $8.1 billion, while its Q4 guidance of $15 to $16 billion came below Wall Street expectations. That sent Intel's stock price down about 29% the next day. Intel and AMD both expect PC sales to slow down in 2027, and CFO David Zinsner has given figures of about 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. The culprit is said to be the global memory crisis, which has resulted in higher overall system prices and lower sales. Due to this weaker demand in the consumer segment, we have seen Intel move some production capacity from Oregon's 18A fab to Xeon chips.
Source:
				Reuters

articles.title: Sabika secures new investment to expand gold and silver trading platform
articles.text:
Sabika secures new investment to expand gold and silver trading platform
- Egypt-based digital precious metals investment platform Sabika has announced the completion of multiple funding rounds for an undisclosed amount. The company did not reveal the investors, funding stages or the number of rounds completed.
- Founded in 2022 by Mohammed Darwish and Ibrahim Anwar, Sabika enables users to buy and sell gold and silver, monitor market prices, set price alerts, manage their holdings and request physical delivery of purchased metals.
- Sabika said its user base has surpassed 120,000, as it seeks to expand its presence in Egypt's digital precious metals investment market.
- The funding will support further development of Sabika's platform, strengthen its technology infrastructure and enable the launch of new gold and silver savings and investment products.
- Last year, Sabika secured a six-figure USD investment, led by M-Empire Angels.
Press release:
Sabika, a digital platform for investing in gold and silver, announced the successful completion of its funding rounds. The funding will support Sabika’s plans to develop its digital platform, strengthen its technological capabilities and expand its range of services. The company’s user base has also surpassed 120,000.
The Sabika platform lets users buy and sell gold and silver, track prices and set price alerts at target levels. Users can also manage their holdings, review their transaction history and request physical delivery of their purchases.
Commenting on the move, Ahmed Khaled, CEO of Sabika, said, "Our successful funding rounds reflect investor confidence in Sabika’s business model and growth potential. They also underscore our ability to continue improving the digital gold and silver investment experience. We see promising opportunities to use technology to make precious metals more accessible to individuals and to offer services that meet their expectations.”
Khaled added: “We believe technology proves its real value when it delivers an integrated experience for users, one that combines digital convenience with the option of physical delivery. We make sure innovation shows in every detail of that experience. That includes easy-to-follow steps, clear information and the ability for customers to track their transactions and manage their holdings.”
Khaled continued: “Surpassing 120,000 users marks an important milestone for Sabika and reflects growing demand for our services. Our user base also gives us deeper insight into our customers’ needs, which we will use to develop our services in the next phase.”
As part of its expansion plans, Sabika continues to develop new products and services that give customers more options for saving and investing in gold and silver. It focuses on offering solutions that address real market needs and deliver clear value to users. The company will announce details of these products and services as they become ready for launch.
The plans come in a market where Egyptians bought around 22 tonnes of gold in the first half of 2026, according to World Gold Council data. Purchases were split between 11.9 tonnes of gold bars and coins and 10.1 tonnes of jewellery. The figures reflect gold’s standing as a savings and investment tool for individuals. They also point to opportunities for digital solutions that give people easier access to investment gold and more flexibility when buying and selling it, as digital financial services expand.

articles.title: L’iPhone Duo aura finalement droit à la reconnaissance faciale
articles.text:
Après des années d’attente, l’arrivée du tout premier iPhone pliant il y a quelques mois a ravi les fans d’Apple. Et bien que l’iPhone Duo soit un excellent smartphone, cette première mouture n’est pas exempte de quelques défauts. À la surprise générale, le premier smartphone pliant d’Apple a fait l’impasse sur l’une des fonctionnalités les plus pratiques qu’Apple ait intégrée à ses iPhone au cours des dernières années : Face ID.
Le système de reconnaissance faciale d’Apple, présent depuis l’iPhone X et redoutable d’efficacité, a été remplacé par Touch ID sur l’iPhone Duo. Une régression pour beaucoup d’utilisateurs qui voyaient dans cette absence le principal défaut de l’appareil. L’absence de Face ID sur l’appareil fait en effet partie des concessions qu’Apple a dû faire, faute de place suffisante dans l’appareil pour y accueillir le capteur TrueDepth indispensable au fonctionnement de Face ID.
En attendant qu’Apple corrige le tir dans une prochaine version de l’iPhone Duo, la firme de Cupertino vient de bricoler une solution de secours pour offrir un semblant de reconnaissance faciale à son iPhone Duo.
Une reconnaissance faciale limitée
Dans la deuxième bêta développeur d’iOS 27.3, Apple vient d’introduire une option de reconnaissance faciale 2D reposant sur la caméra frontale de l’appareil. Mais celle-ci, bien loin de Face ID (qui fournit une reconnaissance faciale en 3D), s’accompagne de quelques contraintes.
Concrètement, cette reconnaissance faciale ne fonctionne que lorsque l’iPhone Duo est fermé, depuis l’écran de verrouillage. Moins sécurisée que Touch ID, l’option reste facultative, mais les données de reconnaissance faciale restent enregistrées dans la Secure Enclave de l’appareil.
Cette nouvelle option de reconnaissance faciale qui intègre l’iPhone Duo est par ailleurs restreinte dans son utilisation. Vous ne pourrez pas vous en servir pour accéder aux mots de passe, ni pour valider des paiements avec Apple Pay, Touch ID restant obligatoire pour ce cas précis. Autre limitation, et pas des moindres, cette reconnaissance faciale ne fonctionne pas dans le noir, contrairement à Face ID.
Surtout, au-delà de 45 minutes d’inactivité sur l’iPhone Duo, le déverrouillage de l’appareil par reconnaissance faciale n’est plus disponible. Il faudra impérativement utiliser Touch ID pour s’authentifier de nouveau.
Enfin, Apple a ajouté une nouvelle fonction « Fermer pour verrouiller » qui permet de verrouiller automatiquement l’iPhone Duo dès lors que vous le fermez, plutôt que de transférer le contenu affiché sur l’écran intérieur vers l’écran extérieur.
