articles.title: Florida extiende la emergencia por dengue mientras una startup universitaria prueba una trampa con IA para combatir el brote
articles.text:
Cuando un equipo de control de mosquitos captura una muestra, identificar qué especies atrapó puede tardar hasta tres días. Para cuando el especialista termina de revisar cada insecto bajo el microscopio, el brote ya avanzó.
Ese margen de tiempo es el problema que Digitomy, una startup de la Universidad del Sur de Florida (USF), busca eliminar con una trampa que usa inteligencia artificial para dar resultados el mismo día, según informó Fox News.
La urgencia no es teórica. El condado de Hillsborough acumula 407 casos de dengue de transmisión local en 2026, la cifra más alta de su historia.
Las personas afectadas contrajeron el virus dentro del estado, sin haber viajado al exterior. En todo Florida, el número total asciende a 524 casos confirmados hasta el 31 de octubre.
El dengue provoca fiebre alta, dolores de cabeza intensos y fuertes molestias musculares. En los casos más graves, puede derivar en complicaciones que amenazan la vida.
El 13 de noviembre, las autoridades de Hillsborough extendieron el estado de emergencia local hasta el 19 de noviembre, con tratamientos aéreos y terrestres activos en distintos barrios.
Por qué el brote no cede aunque el verano terminó
A diferencia del resto del país, donde las temperaturas de noviembre reducen la actividad de los mosquitos, Florida mantiene condiciones climáticas que permiten su reproducción durante todo el año. Eso hace que el riesgo persista cuando en otros estados ya desapareció.
Las autoridades sanitarias continúan con campañas para que la población adopte medidas de protección.
La respuesta tecnológica al problema de vigilancia
La trampa alcanza más del 98% de precisión en pruebas de laboratorio, afirmó el medio. Detrás del desarrollo están el profesor asociado Ryan Carney y el profesor Sriram Chellappan, con investigaciones que se remontan a 2018.
El equipo se puede colgar de una rama baja o colocar en el suelo. Atrae a los mosquitos con luz o cebo, un ventilador los aspira hacia el interior y los insectos quedan adheridos a una superficie pegajosa. Dos cámaras integradas los fotografían y un sistema de inteligencia artificial compara esas imágenes con una base de datos para determinar la especie capturada.
Según los investigadores, el sistema también distingue entre machos y hembras, y detecta si el mosquito se alimentó de sangre recientemente. Ese dato tiene valor sanitario directo: solo las hembras pican a las personas y pueden transmitir enfermedades.
Cómo se usa y qué viene después
Mientras el sistema tradicional tarda días, Digitomy apunta a entregar los resultados en horas. Esa diferencia puede ser determinante para contener un brote antes de que se expanda.
El sistema envía la información a un panel de mapas al que acceden los equipos de control. Si varias trampas detectan un aumento del mosquito Aedes aegypti —la especie responsable de la transmisión del dengue en Florida— en un mismo barrio, las autoridades pueden intervenir en ese punto antes de que crezca el número de contagios.
Los investigadores integraron los datos de las trampas en una capa privada del Global Mosquito Observations Dashboard, disponible en mosquitodashboard.org.
Esa plataforma ya reúne más de medio millón de registros de ciencia ciudadana, y la incorporación de las trampas automatizadas busca combinar ambas fuentes de información.
La USF realizó pruebas del dispositivo en su propio campus y trabajó con el Distrito de Control de Mosquitos Anastasia, en el condado de St. Johns. Además, el equipo prepara una validación en campo en el condado de Hillsborough, donde el brote fue más intenso.
Digitomy trabaja con la Oficina de Transferencia de Tecnología de la USF para licenciar el sistema de identificación a fabricantes de trampas ya establecidos, lo que permitiría incorporar la tecnología a equipos existentes en el mercado.
En el verano de 2026, la startup recibió una beca de USD 25.000 del acelerador Bull Ring de la USF para acelerar esa transición al mercado.
Por el momento, tal como precisó Fox News, la universidad no anunció una fecha de lanzamiento comercial ni un precio de venta al público. El equipo también trabaja en una plataforma educativa en línea para que profesionales del control de mosquitos y ciudadanos puedan practicar la identificación de especies con apoyo de la IA.

articles.title: Google tiene una idea para que programar con IA gaste menos: que el modelo caro solo piense y el barato haga el trabajo
articles.text:
Las herramientas de programación tienen un selector de modelos para elegir uno u otro según la tarea. ¿Un programa sencillo? Suele servir con lo más básico. Que, de rebote, es también lo más rápido y económico. ¿Quieres montar un clon del GTA VI? Toca señalar al modelo de mayores capacidades y preparar el presupuesto para la quema de tokens. El problema llega cuando la tarea se sitúa en el medio o, simplemente, tiene diversos niveles de dificultad.
El orquestador. Igual que los modelos MoE (mixture-of-experts) activan solo una parte de sus parámetros según lo que necesitan generar, los orquestadores seleccionan el modelo más adecuado para cada paso de la tarea. Esto es muy útil cuando se genera código, por ejemplo.
En el caso de Anthropic, Claude Code incluye algo parecido con su opusplan. Una vez activo, la herramienta usará Sonnet para la generación de código e implementación, mientras se reserva un modelo superior, Opus, para el modo de planificación. ChatGPT Codex no tiene nada similar integrado, aunque sí incluye una función de esfuerzo de razonamiento. Además, siempre es posible hacerlo “manualmente”: se le puede decir a Codex o a Claude Code que usen un modelo inferior para los pasos de la tarea que requieran ejecución y no razonamiento.
Planifica el grande, ejecuta el pequeño. La tendencia de la IA no va solo hacia modelos cada vez más grandes, sino también hacia los de mayor eficiencia. Hacer lo máximo posible con las herramientas que ya hay a mano. Y los orquestadores son una buena muestra de cómo se puede rentabilizar el gasto en IA sin perder calidad en los resultados. Al menos sobre el papel.
Google Antigravity incluye ya su nuevo Orchestrator en la app y en la línea de comandos. Llega junto con Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Y, una vez activado el orquestador, este usa el modelo superior para razonar la mejor estrategia (Argon o Carbon) y el inferior para ejecutarla (Hydrogen).
Si el pequeño se atasca, llega en su ayuda el grande. Argon y Carbon son como el arquitecto que diseña el edificio y cómo debe construirse; Hydrogen se convierte en el capataz y los obreros que se encargan de levantar las paredes. Pero estos roles no son rígidos en el Orchestrator de Antigravity, ya que Hydrogen devuelve el control al modelo superior cuando la ejecución se atasca.
La eficiencia también se nota en los resultados: la promesa es acercarse a la calidad de un modelo de vanguardia gastando menos y terminando antes. Según Google, Orchestrator en Antigravity alcanza en Terminal-Bench 4.1 una tasa de éxito cercana a la de Gemini 4 Carbon con un 24 % menos de cuota y una ejecución un 19 % más rápida.
Ya en las suscripciones. Orchestrator está ya disponible en Antigravity con dos variantes: Orchestrator (Carbon) y Orchestrator (Argon). La primera se reserva para los suscriptores de Google AI Ultra (tienen ambas), la segunda llega también a los de Google AI Pro de pago. Para las empresas, Google introduce el acceso a través de Gemini for business.

articles.title: Black Friday : malgré la hausse des prix d’Apple, la Fnac affiche ce MacBook Air M5 à 1 199€
articles.text:
À onze jours du Black Friday, fixé au 27 novembre, la Fnac affiche le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 399 €, alors qu’Apple a relevé ses prix. Notre test, noté 8/10, porte sur une version plus chère que celle de l’offre.
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces associe la puce M5, avec 10 cœurs de processeur et 8 cœurs graphiques, à 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de stockage, ici dans le coloris Minuit. La Fnac l’affiche à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 399 €, soit -14 % sur son prix barré, Apple ayant relevé ses prix. Cdiscount la proposait au même tarif lors de notre relevé du 16 novembre. Cette configuration à 16 Go de mémoire vise surtout la bureautique, les études et la création légère.
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 (16 Go, 512 Go, Minuit) est affiché à 1 199 € chez la Fnac, contre 1 399 € barrés, soit -14 % selon le marchand.
Pourquoi choisir le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 ?
- Un ultraportable sans ventilateur : la puce M5 travaille sans bruit, ce qui compte en bibliothèque, en réunion ou dans le train.
- Un SSD enfin rapide : ses vitesses de lecture et d’écriture doublent par rapport aux anciens modèles, ce qui profite aux gros fichiers et aux exports, avec plus de stockage à tarif inchangé.
- Un écran et un clavier solides : la dalle IPS de 13,6 pouces monte à 500 cd/m² et reste bien calibrée en DCI-P3, tandis que le duo clavier et trackpad reste l’un des points forts de la machine.
Bureautique, cours et montage léger : ce que fait cette machine
Au quotidien, le MacBook Air M5 vise la bureautique, la navigation, la visio et les études. L’autonomie mesurée tourne autour de 10 heures en usage mixte et de 12 heures en lecture vidéo, soit une heure de moins que sur le M4 dans ce test. Son processeur domine la concurrence en mono-cœur, mais il se montre moins à l’aise en multicœur face aux puces à 16 cœurs de certains PC Windows. Ces mesures viennent de la version 1 To et GPU 10 cœurs de notre test du MacBook Air M5, et non de la version 512 Go de l’offre.
Ce Mac convient à l’étudiant, au télétravailleur ou à quiconque veut un portable fin, d’à peine plus de 1,2 kg pour 11,3 mm d’épaisseur. La retouche photo et le montage vidéo occasionnel restent à sa portée. Il convient moins à ceux qui enchaînent les calculs lourds, car nous avons relevé une légère baisse de performance sous charge prolongée, ni à ceux qui tiennent au 120 Hz, absent ici.
Face aux ultraportables Windows et aux autres marchands
Le MacBook Air M5 n’est pas seul sur ce segment. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables, le Dell XPS 14 prend la tête avec une autonomie de 12 à 17 heures et un écran OLED en option, tandis que l’Acer Aspire 14 AI joue la carte de l’accessibilité. Le Mac se distingue par son silence, sa finition et sa puissance mono-cœur, pas par l’autonomie. Chez Cdiscount, le prix relevé le 16 novembre est le même : le marchand se choisit donc sur le service plutôt que sur le tarif.
✅ Les points forts
- Puce M5 sans ventilateur, donc silencieuse
- SSD deux fois plus rapide que sur les anciens modèles
- Écran IPS de 500 cd/m², bien calibré en DCI-P3
- Clavier et trackpad excellents
- Léger : à peine plus de 1,2 kg
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie en baisse : 10 à 12 heures mesurées
- Chauffe plus marquée que sur le M4, jusqu’à 51 °C au point le plus chaud
- Écran limité à 60 Hz
- Très peu de nouveautés de design depuis 2022
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 (16 Go, 512 Go, Minuit) est affiché à 1 199 € chez la Fnac, contre 1 399 € barrés, soit -14 % selon le marchand.
À 1 199 €, le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 16/512 Go reste un excellent ultraportable : notre test lui attribue 8/10 et le range parmi les meilleurs du marché. Apple ayant relevé ses prix, les 200 € de remise affichés par la Fnac ramènent la machine sous son tarif actuel, et Cdiscount affiche le même prix. Seule réserve : notre test porte sur la version 1 To, pas sur celle de l’offre.
L’achat se justifie si vous cherchez un portable fin, silencieux et fiable pour travailler ou étudier, et si le coloris Minuit vous convient. Si vous pouvez attendre, les offres du Black Friday peuvent encore évoluer, sans aucune garantie. Une baisse sous 1 199 € serait le signal à guetter, et les amateurs de calcul lourd ou de jeu soutenu regarderont plutôt du côté des PC Windows.

articles.title: Talkdesk's life sciences play shows why industry depth beats AI cost-cutting - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Talkdesk’s life sciences play shows why industry depth beats AI cost-cutting
The customer experience arena, specifically the contact center, has been the low-hanging fruit for artificial intelligence deployments, with much of the focus on cost-cutting. The goals include fewer agents, shorter calls, higher containment and lower cost per interaction.
Those are legitimate goals, but they lead every vendor to the same pitch. When everyone sells the same savings, the market becomes a price war that favors the companies with the deepest pockets.
Talkdesk Inc. is taking a different path, and today’s announcement reinforces that. This week, the company introduced Talkdesk Life Sciences Experience Cloud, a platform designed for biopharmaceutical companies’ patient services operations. The goal is not to make calls cheaper. It is to move patients from a written prescription to therapy faster and keep them there.
That outcome is one a pharma executive will pay for, and one a generic contact-center-as-a-service platform is poorly equipped to deliver. This adds to Talkdesk’s portfolio of industry clouds, including financial services, government, retail, travel and others.
The news
The new offering connects AI agents, human specialists, systems, and workflows across the specialty care journey, which typically includes enrollment, prior authorizations and specialty pharmacy handoffs. Talkdesk cites IQVIA research showing that nearly one in three commercially insured patients cannot access a prescribed therapy within 30 days, and Boston Consulting Group data indicating that 90% of biopharma leaders view fragmented platforms as their primary bottleneck.
The platform analyzes patient service conversations to pinpoint where patients get stuck, assists specialists in real time, and coordinates tasks among hubs, providers, payers, specialty pharmacies and safety teams. It supports the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures and integrates with existing customer relationship management, hub, pharmacy and safety systems.
One of the world’s five largest pharmaceutical companies has already deployed it. That customer uses AI to classify and route inbound calls and to monitor live conversations for potential reportable events, or PREs, which are adverse event signals that must be captured and sent to pharmacovigilance systems. When the system detects a PRE, it guides the frontline agent to collect the required details, preserves the source conversation and triggers approved workflows to document and route the information.
“A prescription should mark the start of healing, not the beginning of an administrative maze,” said Patty Hayward, general manager of healthcare and life sciences at Talkdesk. “We are focusing first on Therapy Access because quickly getting patients onto prescribed treatments is one of the most urgent, measurable challenges in healthcare today.”
Hayward’s choice of the word “measurable” is the key point. Time to therapy is a metric that appears on a drug maker’s revenue line and in patient outcomes, not just on a contact center dashboard.
Industry focus is how a smaller vendor wins
Talkdesk competes in a crowded market against much larger companies. NiCE Ltd. and Genesys Cloud Services Inc. have scale in the contact center, while Microsoft Corp., Salesforce Inc., and Amazon Web Services Inc. can bundle customer service capabilities into platforms that customers already own. A smaller company cannot outspend those rivals on horizontal features, and it should not try.
What it can do is go deeper into specific industries than the giants are willing to go. Talkdesk has been building industry-specific clouds for several years, and life sciences is a logical next step from its healthcare work. Pharmacovigilance workflows, Part 11 compliance, hub services and specialty pharmacy coordination are not features a horizontal vendor casually adds to its roadmap. They require domain expertise, regulatory knowledge and integrations that take time to build, and that time becomes a competitive moat.
The industry approach also changes the sales conversation. A generic platform is evaluated on price per seat and feature checklists, usually by the information technology department and the contact center leader. An industry platform is evaluated on whether it solves a business problem the executive team already worries about.
In pharma, patient abandonment between prescription and first fill represents lost revenue and a failed treatment. That conversation happens with the head of patient services, which is a much better place for a smaller vendor to be.
The industry approach has helped channel partners sell Talkdesk. I asked Joe Rittenhouse, co-CEO of Converged Technology Professionals Inc., one of the premier communications resellers, about it.
“We’re no longer leading with features or price per seat,” he said. “We’re leading with the customer’s workflows, their compliance requirements and the outcomes they’re measured on. That industry approach is a key differentiator for us. It lets us skip the generic AI conversation and get straight to the problems that keep the business up at night, shortening the sales cycle and making the deployment stick.”
CXA needs industry context to work
The bigger story is how this fits into Talkdesk’s customer experience automation or CXA strategy, which is not a typical contact center-as-a-service sell. The idea is to coordinate AI agents, people, knowledge and enterprise systems to resolve a customer need from start to finish, rather than simply answering or routing an interaction faster. Resolving issues across systems is a far bigger value proposition than call deflection, but it is also much harder to deliver in the abstract.
That is where industry depth becomes critical. End-to-end automation is only possible when the platform understands what “end” means. In a retail return, the end might be a refund. In specialty pharma, the end is a patient who has completed benefits verification, obtained prior authorization, had the drug shipped and is still taking it six months later.
Each step involves different systems, organizations and regulatory obligations. A horizontal AI agent cannot orchestrate that journey without someone first mapping it. Talkdesk is effectively packaging that work into the product.
This is also why the industry approach shifts AI from a cost story to a transformation story. Using AI to reduce handle time on patient service calls might save a few dollars per interaction, and identifying that patients in each program repeatedly stall at prior authorization, then fixing that bottleneck, can change how many patients start therapy. The first is an efficiency gain. The second changes the economics of the business.
The pharmacovigilance use case makes the same point. Missing a reportable adverse event carries regulatory consequences. AI that detects those signals and routes them correctly reduces risk and improves quality, rather than reducing headcount, a value proposition that is far easier to justify to a board.
What this means for buyers
For life sciences leaders, the lesson is to stop evaluating customer engagement technology based solely on contact center metrics. Start with the patient journey, identify where patients drop off and measure vendors on their ability to shorten time to therapy and improve adherence. Insist on proof of regulatory readiness, particularly for Part 11 and adverse event handling, and validate integration with the hub, CRM and safety systems already in place.
For buyers in other industries, the broader point still holds. AI that only cuts costs will eventually commoditize. AI that understands your business’s specific workflows, regulations and outcomes can transform it. Ask CX vendors how well they understand your industry, not just how good their models are.
For Talkdesk, life sciences is a smart focus area. It will not win every horizontal deal against larger rivals, but it does not need to. By targeting industries with complex, regulated journeys tied to clear outcomes, it can make CXA tangible and give customers a reason to buy that has nothing to do with price.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Monitor gamer barato: 5 modelos por menos de R$ 800 em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Monitor gamer barato: 5 modelos por menos de R$ 800 em 2026
Selecionamos as melhores opções de monitor gamer com preço baixo para quem precisa economizar; lista inclui modelos com resolução Full HD e taxa de atualização de até 200 Hz
Encontrar um monitor gamer barato em 2026 não significa abrir mão de recursos importantes para jogar. Modelos com taxas de atualização de 100 Hz a 200 Hz e tecnologias de sincronização adaptativa oferecem alternativas para diferentes perfis, desde jogadores casuais até quem prioriza jogos competitivos.
Para ajudar na escolha, o Tecnoblog selecionou 5 monitores por menos de R$ 800, de marcas como AOC, Samsung e LG. Confira as características, vantagens e limitações de cada modelo.
O AOC Agon G50 é uma opção para quem procura um monitor de entrada voltado a jogos competitivos. Ele traz tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas, resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels) e taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz, permitindo exibir movimentos com maior fluidez que monitores de 60 Hz.
O tempo de resposta é de 0,5 ms (MPRT), que pode ser útil em jogos competitivos. O monitor também oferece compatibilidade com Nvidia G-Sync, recurso de sincronização adaptativa que ajuda a reduzir cortes na imagem, além de suporte a HDR10 para contraste mais definido.
Nas conexões, o AOC Agon G50 oferece HDMI e DisplayPort e também conta com saída de áudio, recursos de assistência para jogos e compatibilidade com suportes VESA de 100 × 100 mm.
O que significa o tempo de resposta do monitor? 🎯
O MPRT (Tempo de Resposta da Imagem em Movimento) indica por quanto tempo a imagem permanece visível enquanto está em movimento, o que influencia o desfoque percebido.
O GtG (Cinza para Cinza) mede quanto tempo um pixel leva para mudar de um tom de cinza para outro.
Como medem coisas diferentes, 0,5 ms MPRT e 5 ms GtG não dizem, por si só, qual monitor deixa menos rastros nos jogos.
A taxa de atualização de 200 Hz é o principal diferencial do AOC Agon G42, tornando-o uma alternativa para jogadores que priorizam fluidez em jogos competitivos, como FPS e de corrida. O modelo traz painel IPS de 23,8 polegadas, resolução Full HD e tempo de resposta de 0,3 ms (MPRT).
O monitor também oferece compatibilidade com Nvidia G-Sync e outros recursos como Shadow Control, para ajustar a visibilidade em áreas escuras, modo de baixa latência e suporte a HDR10. O conjunto de conexões inclui uma entrada HDMI 2.0, uma DisplayPort 1.4 e saída de áudio.
O produto também possui suporte VESA de 100 × 100 mm e acompanha cabo DisplayPort. A base, porém, permite apenas ajuste de inclinação, sem regulagem de altura ou rotação.
O Samsung Essential S3 pode atender quem procura um monitor para jogar e realizar atividades cotidianas no mesmo computador. A tela plana de 24 polegadas utiliza painel IPS, resolução Full HD e 120 Hz de taxa de atualização, combinação adequada para jogos, navegação e produtividade.
O painel possui brilho típico de 250 nits e tempo de resposta de 5 ms (GtG). Entre os recursos estão o Game Picture Mode, que disponibiliza configurações de imagem voltadas a jogos, o Eye Saver Mode e a tecnologia Flicker Free.
Em contrapartida, a Samsung informa que o modelo não possui suporte a AMD FreeSync ou Nvidia G-Sync, uma ausência relevante para jogadores que procuram pelo recurso.
A conectividade é composta por duas entradas HDMI 1.4, permitindo conectar dois dispositivos sem trocar fisicamente os cabos. O monitor também possui ajuste de inclinação e compatibilidade com suportes VESA de 100 × 100 mm, mas não oferece regulagem de altura, saída para fones ou alto-falantes integrados.
O LG MS500 também tem uma proposta de uso misto, combinando recursos para jogos casuais com características voltadas a trabalho e estudos. Seu painel IPS de 24 polegadas possui resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels) e taxa de atualização de 100 Hz.
Essa frequência oferece maior fluidez do que monitores tradicionais de 60 Hz, embora fique abaixo dos 144 e 200 Hz disponíveis nos modelos da linha Agon deste guia. A tecnologia IPS também favorece a visualização em diferentes ângulos.
Entre as especificações estão o tempo de resposta de 5 ms (GtG) e recursos para jogos, como Dynamic Action Sync, voltado à redução do atraso de processamento, Black Stabilizer, que ajusta a visibilidade em cenas escuras, e Crosshair, que adiciona uma mira virtual à tela.
O monitor da LG possui duas entradas HDMI e saída para fones de ouvido, permitindo conectar diferentes equipamentos ao monitor. Também conta com ajuste de inclinação de -5° a 15° e compatibilidade VESA de 75 × 75 mm.
O AOC B35 pode ser interessante para quem busca um monitor gamer compacto. Ele traz painel VA de 21,5 polegadas com resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels).
A combinação resulta em uma densidade de pixels superior à dos modelos Full HD de 23,8 polegadas deste guia, favorecendo a definição de textos e elementos pequenos em distâncias semelhantes.
Apesar de ser anunciado com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, o B35 possui frequência nativa de 100 Hz, sendo necessário utilizar overclock para alcançar o máximo pela entrada HDMI. O tempo de resposta é de 1 ms (MPRT), útil em jogos competitivos.
O modelo também oferece Adaptive-Sync, recurso que ajusta a frequência de atualização de acordo com a saída de dispositivos compatíveis. Nas conexões, o produto oferece uma entrada HDMI 1.4 e uma VGA. O monitor também possui tratamento antirreflexo, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA de 100 × 100 mm.
A escolha do melhor monitor gamer barato depende dos jogos que você costuma jogar, do espaço na mesa e do equipamento que pretende conectar. Verifique o seguinte:
Um monitor Full HD pode funcionar melhor no Xbox Series S, pois os jogos rodam em resolução menor nesse console. É ideal ter uma TV 4K para jogar no PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X para aproveitar mais detalhes nos jogos que oferecem essa resolução.
Depende do modelo. Alguns monitores atingem a frequência máxima tanto por HDMI quanto por DisplayPort. Em outros, a taxa máxima de Hz só é possível pela HDMI com overclock, enquanto a VGA fica limitada a uma frequência mais baixa em Full HD.
Sim, alguns monitores gamer de entrada têm alto-falantes embutidos, mas o recurso varia de um modelo para outro. O som integrado costuma ser suficiente para ouvir diálogos e sons do jogo.
Mas, se você valoriza graves mais presentes ou quer perceber melhor a direção dos sons, vale considerar um headset avançado ou caixas de som externas.
Monitores gamer QHD são mais caros, por isso ficaram de fora desta seleção. A resolução 2560 × 1440 pixels ajuda a preservar a nitidez da imagem em telas maiores, como as de 27 polegadas. Assim, o preço tende a subir quando o monitor combina essa resolução com uma taxa de atualização alta.
No PC, jogar em QHD também exige mais da placa de vídeo para manter a mesma taxa de quadros. Se a prioridade é economizar e jogar com fluidez em uma tela de 24 polegadas, o Full HD costuma oferecer um bom equilíbrio.

articles.title: Trump calls for Jensen Huang reinstatement as Nvidia CEO — Nvidia board reportedly refuses to reinstate disgraced CEO due to ongoing national security investigation into Jensen
articles.text:
Trump calls for Jensen Huang reinstatement as Nvidia CEO — Nvidia board reportedly refuses to reinstate disgraced CEO due to ongoing national security investigation into Jensen
"A lot of people are asking Jensen, they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea"
Following reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is plotting a return to the company, President Donald Trump has voiced his own support for such a move, Bloomberg reports. However, according to new insight from CNBC, Nvidia's board of directors is not considering the move and is instead focused on its ongoing investigation into Huang's extramarital affairs and a national security investigation, likely into possible allegations of chip smuggling into China.
Trump reportedly made his comments in support of Huang's return to reporters at the White House on Monday, ahead of his trip to Asia. "I would not mind that," he said. "A lot of people are asking Jensen; they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea.” While Trump noted Huang's financial situation, he said the CEO did not put national security at risk and did not know Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
Last week, the President said that Apple's former CEO Tim Cook was the only man to replace Huang in Nvidia's top job. Trump's comments also contrast sharply with those of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who this week has called for Nvidia to replace Huang with an outsider, while giving the company 100 days to explain its dealings with China.
As mentioned, Jensen Huang's purported return does not seem to be an option the board is seriously considering. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the board of directors is focused on investigating Huang's conduct and a national security investigation and is not discussing his return.
A large petition has started circulating pertaining to Huang's reinstatement, with Elon Musk the most notable to sign. Musk had ventured so far as to say it would be an 'honor' to hire Huang, presumably to his Terafab project, following revelations of his exit.
While rumblings of possible illicit chip smuggling into China have dogged Nvidia for well over a year, Huang's tenure as founder and CEO ended somewhat abruptly last week after a series of revelations spiraled to bring about his resignation. In the wake of reports that US officials were said to be concerned about his close relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, it later transpired that Huang had indeed had an affair with Ms. Huang, and that there were suspicions she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Since that news broke, it has further been revealed that Huang also had an inappropriate relationship with one of his direct reports, Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell, and that the company covered up the fling. Perhaps more concerningly for Jensen Huang, it has been alleged that Ms. Huang and Megaspeed may have been involved in chip smuggling into China to the tune of more than $7 billion, with hundreds of thousands of H100 and H200 chips said to have found their way into the country at her behest, a factor analysts believe may be the true reason behind Huang's exit.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
For now, Nvidia's former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, with one of her first orders of business the company's earnings call on November 17. The company's shares have tumbled sharply in the last week, perhaps understandably. Shares were down more than 4% on Monday, and more than 10% over the last five days, with the stock on course to lose nearly one-third of its value in the last six months.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Also follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Stephen is Tom's Hardware's News Editor with almost a decade of industry experience covering technology, having worked at TechRadar, iMore, and even Apple over the years. He has covered the world of consumer tech from nearly every angle, including supply chain rumors, patents, and litigation, and more. When he's not at work, he loves reading about history and playing video games.

articles.title: Jennie aparece en la lista filtrada del álbum de GTA 6 junto a Dua Lipa, Travis Scott y otras 31 estrellas
articles.text:
La voz de Jennie sonará en las calles virtuales de Vice City: la integrante de Blackpink figura en la lista de artistas filtrada del álbum oficial de Grand Theft Auto 6, según confirmaron medios especializados internacionales a partir de una filtración ocurrida el sábado 14 de noviembre.
La filtración se produjo cuando imágenes de la contraportada de un vinilo del álbum comenzaron a circular en X (antes Twitter) y otras redes sociales. Según NME (New Musical Express) , un empleado de una tienda de discos habría vendido copias del LP antes de la fecha oficial de lanzamiento. Las publicaciones de Rolling Stone y Billboard confirmaron de forma independiente, a través de fuentes cercanas al proyecto, que la lista es auténtica. Rockstar Games, la desarrolladora del juego, no ha emitido ninguna confirmación oficial.
En la lista de 34 canciones filtrada, Jennie ocupa el puesto 21, en la cara C del vinilo, con el tema titulado “Power Trip”. Es la única artista coreana entre los 34 participantes del álbum, y su nombre no había sido incluido en el anuncio oficial que Rockstar realizó en septiembre, cuando la compañía adelantó seis temas con figuras como Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen y Keith Richards, guitarrista de The Rolling Stones.
Rapera principal y vocalista de Blackpink, Jennie Kim debutó junto al grupo bajo el sello YG Entertainment el 8 de agosto de 2016. Nacida en Seúl y criada en parte en Nueva Zelanda, fue la primera integrante de la agrupación en lanzar material en solitario: su sencillo “SOLO” (2018) encabezó el Circle Digital Chart surcoreano y el Billboard World Digital Songs, y su video se convirtió en el primero de una solista coreana en superar los mil millones de reproducciones en YouTube.
A fines de 2023 fundó su propio sello, ODD ATELIER, y en 2024 firmó con Columbia Records para su expansión en el mercado estadounidense. Su álbum debut, Ruby (marzo de 2025), vendió más de un millón de copias en todo el mundo, debutó en el puesto 7 del Billboard 200 e incluyó colaboraciones con Dua Lipa, Doechii, Dominic Fike, Childish Gambino y Kali Uchis.
En enero de 2026 se alzó con cuatro premios en los Golden Disc Awards, incluido el primer galardón a Artista del Año que esa ceremonia otorga. Su trabajo más reciente previo a esta participación es el EP digital Fallen Angel, publicado en agosto de 2026.
El resto del tracklist filtrado abarca géneros y generaciones: Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Cardi B, Camila Cabello, SZA, Zara Larsson, Tove Lo, Playboi Carti, Burna Boy, Future, Don Toliver, Gunna, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Omar Apollo, Kali Uchis, Rina Sawayama y Arca, entre otros.
El medio tecnológico Notebookcheck describió la alineación como digna de los cabezas de cartel de Coachella. Entre las colaboraciones más llamativas figura la de Justice con Tame Impala, SZA y King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard en “Flower In A Hurricane”, tema que ya había logrado el primer ingreso de King Gizzard al Hot 100. Lana Del Rey tiene además presencia adicional en el juego: hace un mes se reveló que co-conduce una de las estaciones de radio virtuales junto a su esposo y a Morgan Wallen.
El proyecto musical fue anunciado en septiembre por Rockstar Games en asociación con el sello estadounidense Atlantic Records. Se trata de un álbum de canciones inéditas creadas específicamente para el juego, y no una compilación de los temas que suenan en las radios ficticias de GTA 6.
El lanzamiento está previsto para el jueves 19 de noviembre, el mismo día que el videojuego, en formatos físicos —vinilo y CD— y plataformas digitales. Los vinilos de edición limitada se agotaron al instante desde su anuncio y en el mercado de reventa llegaron a cotizarse hasta USD 440. Según Rolling Stone y Billboard, la filtración no fue producto de un hackeo, sino de la venta anticipada de copias físicas.
GTA 6 llega 13 años después del título anterior y sale el 19 de noviembre en consolas
Grand Theft Auto 6 es la primera entrega numerada de la franquicia desde GTA 5, publicado en septiembre de 2013. El nuevo título está ambientado en Vice City, una ciudad ficticia inspirada en Florida, y llega a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S el próximo jueves, tras varios retrasos. La música es un componente central de la experiencia de la saga: los jugadores pueden sintonizar distintas estaciones de radio mientras conducen por la ciudad. La primera entrega de la franquicia data de 1997.
Paralelamente al lanzamiento, el sábado 21 de noviembre está programado un festival en Miami con artistas del soundtrack, entre ellos Cardi B, Kodak Black y Don Toliver. Para el 11 de diciembre está prevista además la publicación de una partitura original de 50 canciones compuesta íntegramente por Justice, un lanzamiento independiente del álbum de canciones.
El tracklist completo filtrado, distribuido en cuatro caras de vinilo
La lista de las 34 canciones de Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, según el vinilo filtrado y confirmado por Rolling Stone y Billboard, es la siguiente:
Cara A: “Starting from Zero” (Justice feat. Michael McDonald), “That’s It” (Yung Lean feat. Future & Metro Boomin), “Ahh Yea” (Playboi Carti), “Rhyno” (Travis Scott), “Sexy Magic” (CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. & Étienne de Crécy), “Flower in a Hurricane” (Justice feat. articles.title: Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
Microsoft has now explained the recent Microsoft 365 outage in a preliminary post-incident report. According to Microsoft, customers were impacted for just under 24 hours, from 4:20 PM UTC on November 12 to 4:10 PM UTC on November 13. The outage prevented many users from accessing their mailboxes in Outlook and delayed email delivery. Moreover, Microsoft Teams, Copilot, SharePoint, and OneDrive were all affected in some way, which is expected since these services all have features that rely on Exchange Online.
The company has traced the outage to three problems that hit Microsoft at the same time. The main culprit is said to be a fix that had been prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 gateway servers. This particular fix, which introduced lock contention in an internal Windows process that exhausted CPU and memory under certain loads, went unnoticed for over three months. That was probably because Microsoft's load testing used weaker machines that couldn't stress the fix properly. Teams also failed over onto the primary gateway it shares with Exchange Online, which worsened the problem. Traffic then shifted to remaining servers, which buckled under the extra load. Apparently, more than 80% of the servers were unresponsive at the worst point of the outage.After that, the recovery process was full of hurdles too. The restored servers were swamped by queued traffic, and the old fix couldn't be hastily undone using the usual rollback tools. This is Microsoft's preliminary explanation of the outage. Currently, Microsoft claims that the problem has been resolved, and a final report on the incident is expected by November 20. The company maintains that the outage was not linked to any cyberattack or AI malfunction.

articles.title: Crypto : un homme interpellé pour un home jacking à 900 000 euros
articles.text:
C'est une autre affaire d'attaque à domicile en lien avec les cryptomonnaies sur laquelle la police avance. Un homme vient d'être interpellée pour un rapt dont la rançon a été particulièrement élevée.
Les fortunes rapides faites en cryptomonnaies attirent malheureusement la convoitise des malfaiteurs - et ce, particulièrement chez nous en France. On a ainsi vu un certain nombre d'affaires de kidnapping, allant jusqu'au cofondateur de Ledger, se multiplier en France, avec l'objectif d'obtenir une rançon. Et certaines fois, les kidnappeurs vont directement au domicile de leurs victimes, pour les y menacer et obtenir une somme conséquente. Comme dans cette affaire.
Un couple séquestré à son domicile, pour une rançon en crypto d'une valeur de 900 000 euros
Au mois de mars dernier, un homme et une femme dans la cinquantaine et vivant au Chesnay étaient la cible d'une attaque à leur domicile de la part d'un groupe de trois hommes. L'un d'eux a alors utilisé un couteau pour menacer la femme du couple, afin d'obliger l'homme à payer une rançon en cryptomonnaies.
Il a alors cédé à la menace, et a payé la somme exigée en bitcoins, d'un valeur estimée à environ 900 000 euros. D'après les informations de la police, les deux personnes du couple ont ensuite été installées sur leur canapé, puis ligotées, après quoi les malfaiteurs ont fui le domicile. Et depuis, une enquête pour séquestration et vol en bande organisée a été ouverte.
Un homme interpellé à la suite du rapt
Aujourd'hui, cette enquête connaît une avancée notable avec l’interpellation d'un homme dans son domicile à Blois (Loir-et-Cher), dans le cadre de ce dossier. Il a été ensuite mis en examen puis en détention préventive, sans que le parquet de Versailles n'ait pour le moment produit les détails de ses chefs de mis en examen.
Reste maintenant à savoir à quel point ces actions seront efficaces sur le long terme. Car malgré l'alarme sonné depuis déjà un certain temps, le nombre d'enlèvements liés aux cryptomonnaies a continué à augmenter entre 2025 et 2026. Ils étaient ainsi entre 45 et 67 l'an dernier, selon les bilans, alors qu'ils étaient déjà plus de 70 sur les huit premiers mois de l'année 2026, d'après le Parquet national anticriminalité organisée.
Source : Le Figaro

articles.title: Plus de 1 000 km d’autonomie à 37 000 € ? Ce SUV BYD n’arrivera pas chez nous de sitôt
articles.text:
La voiture électrique aux 1 000 km d’autonomie ? C’est un fantasme aussi inutile qu’ancien qui deviendra très bientôt réalité. Chez Mercedes, l’EQS peut aujourd’hui parcourir 925 km. Chez Lucid, la Air pousse même le délire à 960 km. De bien jolies valeurs provenant néanmoins de modèles hors de prix. Avec ses 912 km d’autonomie, la BMW i3 joue déjà dans une gamme tarifaire inférieure, sans se montrer encore accessible, entendons-nous.
Et puis, tout le monde ne veut pas faire de compromis sur la praticité. Mauvaise nouvelle, les véhicules précités sont tous des berlines qui ne sont naturellement pas les reines du déménagement. BYD dégaine donc une solution au problème avec le Denza N8, un SUV électrique aussi habitable qu’endurant. Avec 5,15 mètres de long, 1,99 mètre de large et 1,82 mètre de haut, l’engin est capable de tout engloutir, ou presque.
Jusqu’à 1 003 km d’autonomie et une recharge éclair en 9 minutes
Contrairement au N8L rallongé, le N8 se limite à cinq occupants pour privilégier un volume de coffre grimpant à 1 046 litres. Le tout est complété par un rangement avant de 205 litres, ce qui devrait largement suffire pour ranger les câbles de recharge. Côté technique, le N8 s’octroie des batteries de 105,8 et 130,2 kWh offrant entre 800 et 1 003 km d’autonomie sur le cycle CLTC. Les valeurs dépendront largement de la version choisie.
Car le Chinois propose deux variantes en propulsion de 435 et 503 ch, accompagnées d’une déclinaison trimoteur développant en cumulé 1 210 ch, ce qui n’a pas grand sens, nous sommes d’accord. Côté recharge, les batteries équipées de la technologie Blade 2.0 admettent un 10 à 70 % en 5 minutes et un 10 à 97 % en 9 minutes sur une borne appropriée. Vraiment remarquable vu la taille des batteries, et pas illusoire.
Un tarif équivalent à 37 000 €… mais interdit d’Europe
Les premières stations Flash Charging de BYD sont en cours de déploiement en Europe pour fournir une puissance de charge en courant continu DC de 1 500 kW. Vous pourrez alors y brancher votre Denza Z9GT ou votre BYD Atto 8, mais pas ce Denza N8. Et pour cause, il n’est pas vendu chez nous. On se doute bien que le tarif qui équivaut à 37 000 € est surtout destiné aux Chinois…
Frustrant, mais de plus en plus proche de nous, tout de même… L’équipement peut aussi faire jaser, avec un écran tactile de 30 pouces surmonté d’un bandeau numérique de 1,1 mètre de large, des suspensions pneumatiques intelligentes, quatre roues directrices et la conduite autonome God’s Eye 5.0. Une version hybride rechargeable offrant 435 km d’autonomie en mode électrique suivra.

articles.title: TRIUMF: Taking a Tour of Canada’s Particle Accelerator - EE Times
articles.text:
Canada’s particle accelerator is smaller than CERN’s flagship Large Hadron Collider, but it occupies a distinct place in the international research ecosystem: TRIUMF combines high-intensity beams, rare-isotope production, and specialized materials probes, including capabilities that advance semiconductor research.
Located on the University of British Columbia’s (UBC’s) main, forested campus in Vancouver, the research center was conceived in 1965 as the Tri-University Meson Facility, a joint initiative of UBC, Simon Fraser University, and the University of Victoria. The addition of the University of Alberta as a founding partner soon made the original name less apt. Cyclotron construction began in 1971 and was officially commissioned in 1974. Now the facility is simply known as TRIUMF and is run by a consortium of 21 member universities across Canada.
TRIUMF’s strengths lie in rare‑isotope beams, beta-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β‑NMR), muon spin rotation (μSR), and dedicated nuclear‑astrophysics spectrometers. TRIUMF often contributes specialized detector components, accelerator technology, and computing expertise to large, international experiments, including those at CERN, while its facilities serve as Canada’s main hub for accelerator‑based science and isotope supply.
At the heart of the 13.5-acre site is the 520-MeV cyclotron, the world’s largest normal-conducting cyclotron. The machine is 18 meters across, its pinwheel-shaped magnet weighs 4,000 metric tons, and it has driven the lab’s science program since its first proton beam on Dec. 15, 1974. It accelerates negative hydrogen ions to 75% of the speed of light; a carbon foil strips away both electrons, leaving protons that are steered into beamlines running across the site to experiments and isotope-production stations.
Every year, the machine shuts down for about three months while engineers break the vacuum seal, lift the lid, and climb inside for repairs and upgrades.
Intensity, not energy
While CERN serves as the global focal point for collider-based high-energy physics, TRIUMF is a complementary, intensity-frontier laboratory. Its high-current proton and electron beams drive isotope production, materials studies, and precision nuclear and astrophysics experiments rather than multi-TeV collisions.
The cyclotron feeds the ISAC rare-isotope beamlines, while the superconducting ARIEL electron linac, the world’s highest-power e-linac for rare-isotope production, is designed to add photon-induced fission as a second rare-isotope production route. TRIUMF said ARIEL will roughly triple annual rare-isotope beam availability, from an aggregate of about 3,000 hours to 9,000 hours.
Probes, payloads, and radiation hardening
What might interest electronics engineers the most are TRIUMF’s Centre for Molecular and Materials Science (CMMS) and its Proton Irradiation Facility (PIF) and Neutron Irradiation Facility (NIF).
CMMS is home to μSR and β-NMR, condensed-matter probes that are rare, and TRIUMF claimed its specialized βw-NMR capabilities are unique. In β-NMR, beams of spin-polarized lithium-8 ions are implanted 5 to 200 nm deep in thin films and heterostructures, a capability used to study semiconductor quantum wells, superconductors, and battery materials. μSR similarly uses implanted muons as ultra-sensitive local probes of magnetism inside bulk materials.
PIF was designed primarily for single-event-effect studies and characterization of electronic components for the space environment, while NIF also serves terrestrial electronics and avionics testing. Their beams reproduce the radiation found at ground level, aircraft altitude, and low Earth orbit—but at far higher intensity, so companies can find out quickly whether, and how, their components will fail before they are committed to a launch.
Beam as currency
Getting beam time is itself an exercise in precision.
Our guide described it as “almost like a currency at the lab.” Committees allocate it, schedules are set years in advance in some cases, and they are adhered to minute by minute.
TRIUMF’s main control room is staffed 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, blending modern readouts with older tactile tuning controls that operators still prefer. Thousands of devices are hardwired into the room. TRIUMF is developing model-assisted and machine-learning tools to reduce tuning overhead. In one reported demonstration, a beam-tuning task that took operators hours was completed in about six minutes.
A portal to big science
Canadian universities work through TRIUMF on more than 50 international collaborations and experiments, including CERN’s ATLAS experiment. ATLAS-Canada—TRIUMF and seven universities—is providing 1,500 of the approximately 7,000 silicon strip modules for the endcaps of ATLAS’s new, all-silicon Inner Tracker, being installed for the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade. The same pipeline feeds industry: Compact cyclotrons derived from TRIUMF designs produce medical isotopes in hospital basements across Canada.
For a lab whose name dates back to three founding universities, TRIUMF’s pitch today is that particle beams are national infrastructure to support science, medicine, and business, as well as a materials-and-radiation toolbox that Canada’s electronics sector would be hard-pressed to replicate.

articles.title: At KubeCon 2026, the illusion of AI control meets the reality of implementation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
At KubeCon 2026, the illusion of AI control meets the reality of implementation
I revisited Salt Lake City for KubeCon/CloudNativeCon NA 2026 hoping to find practical approaches to delivering customer value amidst a rapidly shifting kaleidoscope of artificial intelligence-driven solutions that are making it increasingly difficult to trust our own eyes and ears.
This year, the host Cloud Native Computing Foundation set its theme as “Cloud Native Without Limits,” and judging by the record-shattering pace of new community developments with more than 230 active projects, and the increasing adoption rate of AI for building and consuming applications, the momentum will only grow.
“If you look back at last year’s KubeCon in Atlanta, OpenClaw was not released yet, MCP was less than a year old, and inference in cloud native was just getting started,” Chris Anzyzcyk, chief technical officer of CNCF, said in the opening remarks.
“We knew we were moving out of a phase where most of the AI compute was used for training and we were going to massively ramp up inference,” said Jonathan Bryce, executive director of CNCF. “Just in the last eight months, we’ve seen a 4X increase in inference traffic across the industry. That’s really an incredible increase in the AI footprint. Inference is no longer just an opportunity, it’s now a cloud-native production workload.”
With more than 350K CNCF contributors and 21.2 million cloud-native developers worldwide, fully three-quarters of them are already using AI coding agents, according to the latest State of Cloud Native Development Q3 2026 report, and a show of hands in the room hinted at a much higher presence of AI tooling on the engineer’s desktop.
Likewise, two-thirds of self-described AI-driven organizations are standardizing on Kubernetes and related open-source technologies.
There’s a clear connection here, but AI is not the whole story. Enterprises still need to modernize their application fleets, and deploy, scale, secure and observe their most critical systems, in order to get beyond the AI hype and realize business value.
With an open mind and a skeptical eye, here were some of the interesting new perspectives and vendor solutions I encountered at the show.
Building open paths to Kubernetes and AI productivity
With the rapid enterprise rollout of agentic AI, every developer is being challenged to apply human decision insight while working at agent speed, one of the major themes of the show.
Getting there will take more than new technologies, it will also require a lot of collaboration and understanding. The Kubernetes AI Conformance Program launched at KubeCon NA 2025 now has 42 major participating vendors agreeing to consistent standards, and this year there are new Kubernetes AI Certifications for upskilling engineers, whether they are just starting out, or if they are “Golden Kubestronauts” who already passed every course CNCF offers.
“Kubernetes has become the standard API for deploying a workload to a computer, including AI,” said Dan Ciruli, vice president and general manager for cloud native at Nutanix Inc. “The reason, in my opinion, is because the CNCF gave a safe haven for anyone from the smallest startup of two people to the largest companies on Earth to feel safe in donating labor, and code, and IP, and agreeing on things. And that, in turn, gave everybody, from governments to financial services to hot startups, the confidence that they could consume it.”
The firm recently introduced their Nutanix Agent Gateway and an NKP Metal solution that allows Kubernetes clusters and workloads to run on bare metal as well as virtual machines in EKS, AKS or GKE for what they call a “dual-native” experience.
“How are you going to safely and sustainably connect thousands of agents to the systems of record that actually run the business such as customer loyalty or inventory?” asked Matt DeBergalis, CEO, Apollo Graph Inc., doing business as Apollo GraphQL, which supports the popular open source GraphQL query language, presenting a new semantic domain model for deterministically interpreting AI prompts and controls for each record.
Eliminating resource constraints, both digital and human
Last year CNCF announced a Dynamic Resource Allocation or DRA capability, which unlocked new possibilities for the community to optimize AI workloads running in Kubernetes. This year, sandboxing, or running agents in secure instances to prevent escapes, hijacking and overprovisioning, was the watchword.
Development has moved fast in this area, with two new projects: a Agent Substrate layer contributed by Google that optimizes resource consumption of thousands of agent sandboxes, and OpenShell, an Nvidia Corp.-contributed project for secure sandboxed runtimes.
Startup Apelogic Inc. doing business as HyperShell built an operational agent envelope based on OpenShell that defines guardrails what systems an autonomous agent can access, and what actions it can take, based on the business or system intent the agent was intended to serve.
Cast AI started out as a cloud cost optimization layer for rightsizing clusters on major hyperscalers, but as cloud native infrastructure started taking over enterprise environments, it now finds itself automating and optimizing more AI workloads across CPUs and GPUs, memory and storage. New at KubeCon, their Kimchi code agent governs and deploys application infrastructures from a prompt, which allows developers shift left agentic reviews before production tuning.
Floxdev Inc., which I covered as a startup with their Nix-based lean containerized environment deployments in 2025, put its Flox platform directly in the AI delivery path, giving agents skills to stamp out identical complete environments that include all dependencies, without reproducing any element of the software supply chain inventory that wasn’t intended to change. This moves agentic loops faster with lower compute costs, but the real value is when human engineers can reduce future maintenance and security remediation costs.
Observability isn’t just for SREs anymore
This year’s CNCF graduation of the OpenTelemetry project couldn’t come at a better moment, making OTel the lingua franca of application performance, scalability and reliability.
While observability was traditionally considered the domain of engineers and operators, now everyone from data analysts to business executives may be using an LLM or an agent to interact with enterprise applications, potentially changing software, or delivering more agents, in the process.
Splunk, a division of Cisco Systems Inc. has added to its agent observability suite with a specialized language model called Eval-G1 that can run prompt-and-response evals in sub-second times at sub-cent costs, giving engineers the ability to interrupt a faulty response in real time, before it reaches customers. A new Evaluation Studio helps teams generate guardrails in a low-code graphical environment. Also cool, a tokenomics feature (from the recent acquisition of Galileo, which we just covered) that analyzes token spend versus system and business performance metrics.
“It’s been exciting to see how OpenTelemetry, which started out as tens of thousands of adaptors for every application and client, has transitioned with the AI revolution so that now, we have frameworks that just emit OTel natively,” said Morgan McLean, senior director of product management at Splunk and OpenTelemetry co-creator. “So Splunk, and our competitors, can just launch new observability features without putting 30 people on writing new integrations.”
Since a lot of AI projects start out as experiments, observability stalwart Dynatrace LLC has made several moves to meet smaller teams where they are in validating each feature for performance and reliability before enterprise-scale rollouts. It recently acquired Bindplane for OTel-native telemetry pipelines, BlueBox, which gives developers a custom agent for debugging and checks within a coding IDE, and Arize, which maintains the popular Phoenix open-source tool for AI evaluations.
New Relic Inc. released a new Autopilot Kubernetes Agent, a virtual SRE that users can interact with via natural language to look across telemetry and APM data to assess the health of the cluster and application, triage issues with a complete stack trace, and recommend resolutions.
“Especially when you bring agents into your environment, you can’t just take your telemetry and throw it over to a general-purpose LLM, because there are known deterministic patterns and historical insights about Kubernetes we’ve been working to resolve for years,” said Jemiah Sius, vice president of market strategy and developer relations at New Relic.
Making agent deployments safer, by making them easier to sustain
A lot of the governance difficulty with agents and sandboxes and policies isn’t a technical problem; it is about user experience. Human engineers don’t like being “in the loop” for AI, aka “Meat Proxies,” that continuously pass along approvals. Humans need to be in control, with less toil and more focus on what customers want out of AI applications.
“You can try to create a secure agent sandbox with a policy where everything is disabled by default until a human approves it, but eventually, someone gets tired of being in that approval loop,” said Simone Morellato, senior director of product marketing, Rafay Systems Inc., an AI infrastructure delivery platform used by leading neoclouds. “So you give an agent access to one thing, and eventually you end up giving them access to everything. And at that point, you are back at square one.”
Since I covered Edera Inc. last year, this hardened runtime container vendor is finding new traction in this agentic age by continuing to strengthen the stack from the bottom up, with an agent runtime and OCAP bounded authority that acts as a switchboard for discretely defined agent capabilities, rather than assigning agents credentials or access to MCP servers or APIs or other agents that can be expanded or exploited for another HuggingFace-type incident.
“You can consume capabilities in our system and publish capabilities,” said Edera founder and Chief Technology Officer Alex Zenla. So, for example, for an MCP server, we publish each tool call as a capability. And then when you spin up your agent, you ask for the tool calls that you want. And then it consumes just those capabilities. And we’re able to enforce policies because we have one central pathway for everything to go through, so we can know exactly which agents are using which capabilities.”
“I love the focus on reliability that I’ve seen in the talks and on the floor here at KubeCon,” said Kolton Andrus, CEO of Gremlin Inc., which was there demonstrating their new Foresight AI solution that proactively injects failure conditions in order to identify and remediate failure risks. “You can no longer wait for things to fall apart before taking action. “Everyone’s moving 100 miles an hour trying to keep up with AI, and waking up to the fact that reliability can’t be an afterthought anymore. You can no longer wait for things to fall apart before taking action.”
The Intellyx take
This being my eighth KubeCon, I keep coming back because the community atmosphere here is unparalleled. There’s a real sense of camaraderie among developers and engineers from wildly different backgrounds, as they build new fundamentals and enjoy the journey toward a cloud native future.
We’ve come a long way over the last eleven years since Kubernetes was introduced. Interoperability, portability, control planes, observability, networking, identity, security and many more mature capabilities are there for the taking. Now AI is being layered on top. But that’s not the story here.
What really impresses me is how much this open source community gives back for the benefit of everyone. All of these people have real jobs to do, and yet they invest their own time, as much as the software industry invests in them.
Indeed, as CNCF’s own Jonathan Bryce said: “Some problems can only be solved in the open.”
Jason English is a principal analyst and chief marketing officer at Intellyx. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE. At the time of writing, Gremlin and Rafay are current Intellyx customers, Dynatrace, New Relic, Nutanix and Splunk are former customers, and none of the other companies mentioned here is an Intellyx customer. articles.title: Las denuncias por material de abuso sexual infantil generado con IA se multiplicaron más de 8.400% en dos años
articles.text:
Un informe del Childlight Global Child Safety Institute (Instituto Global para la Seguridad Infantil Childlight) revela que las denuncias por abuso sexual infantil en internet pasaron de unas 4.700 en 2023 a más de 400.000 en 2025.
Los reportes de material generado con inteligencia artificial se multiplicaron más de 8.400% en apenas dos años, al pasar de unas 4.700 denuncias en 2023 a más de 400.000 en 2025, según un informe del instituto con sede en Edimburgo. El material incluye imágenes falsas producidas con deepfakes y aplicaciones conocidas como “nudify apps”, que pueden utilizarse para extorsionar a menores y exigirles dinero o más imágenes.
La investigación analizó los reportes que empresas tecnológicas presentaron ante el National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), organismo con sede en Estados Unidos, y se concentró en el este de Asia y el Pacífico, América Latina y el Caribe, y América del Norte. Estudios anteriores del mismo instituto habían examinado la situación en Europa occidental.
Más allá del entorno digital, el informe también relevó datos sobre abuso sexual fuera de línea. En Norteamérica, casi un tercio de las niñas y más de uno de cada diez niños sufrieron abuso sexual presencial durante la infancia, en delitos que incluyen agresión sexual, violación y el llamado “upskirting”. A nivel global, Childlight estima que más de 300 millones de menores son víctimas cada año de al menos una forma de explotación o abuso sexual facilitado por tecnología, y que aproximadamente uno de cada cuatro niños sufrirá algún tipo de abuso antes de cumplir 18 años.
En Estados Unidos, la tasa de reportes vinculados a material de abuso sexual infantil creció un 63% entre 2024 y 2025, frente al 18% registrado en Canadá en el mismo período, según datos recogidos por The Guardian.
La Internet Watch Foundation ya superó en 2026 el total de casos investigados en todo 2025
Un informe reciente de la Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), organización no gubernamental del Reino Unido que monitorea material de abuso a nivel global, determinó que la cantidad de material ilegal investigado en lo que va de 2026 ya supera el total del año anterior. Sus analistas identificaron más material de abuso sexual infantil con apariencia fotorrealista en el primer semestre de 2026 que en todo 2025: 6.310 imágenes generadas por inteligencia artificial que cumplen la definición legal de abuso sexual infantil, un 40% más que las 4.500 del año previo.
Debi Fry, directora global de datos de Childlight, advirtió que “la velocidad a la que la inteligencia artificial está cambiando la amenaza para los niños es profundamente preocupante”. En declaraciones recogidas por The Guardian, Fry señaló que, si bien una parte del aumento podría explicarse por mejoras en la detección y los sistemas de denuncia, las cifras “subrayan por qué los gobiernos y las empresas tecnológicas deben actuar con urgencia para comprender y prevenir estas formas emergentes de abuso y eliminar el material con rapidez”.
Childlight pide reconocer la explotación sexual infantil como emergencia de salud pública prevenible
Paul Stanfield, director ejecutivo de Childlight, llamó a los gobiernos a reconocer la explotación sexual infantil como una emergencia de salud pública que puede prevenirse. “Millones de niños están siendo sometidos a explotación y abuso sexual, pero los gobiernos trabajan con demasiada frecuencia con un panorama incompleto de dónde ocurre el daño y quiénes están en mayor riesgo”, sostuvo el ejecutivo en declaraciones a The Guardian. El director también reclamó mayor inversión en evidencia y coordinación internacional para “intervenir antes y dar a millones más de niños la infancia segura que merecen”.
Fry, por su parte, subrayó que el análisis conjunto de encuestas, registros policiales y otras fuentes permite “construir una imagen más clara de los riesgos que enfrentan los niños, identificar debilidades en los sistemas de protección y orientar recursos e intervenciones donde más se necesitan”.

articles.title: Hoy es uno de los desiertos más inhóspitos del planeta. Hace 125.000 años, Arabia Saudí tenía lagos, hipopótamos y humanos con armas
articles.text:
Hoy el Rub' al-Khali, el célebre Cuarto Vacío del sur de Arabia Saudí, es uno de los mares de arena más áridos e inhóspitos del planeta. Sin embargo, hace 125.000 años, en su margen suroccidental se extendía un lago de agua dulce de 340 kilómetros cuadrados rodeado de pastizales y palmeras. Ahora un nuevo estudio publicado por Science reconstruye la vida cotidiana que se vivía en estas orillas, donde grupos de humanos pudieron convivir con hipopótamos y búfalos gigantes mientras tallaban miles de herramientas de sílex.
Un lago. El hallazgo se concentra en el yacimiento de Uruq al-Julaybah, situado en la cuenca del antiguo lago Mundafan, al sur de Arabia Saudí. La investigación, publicada a principios de noviembre, se centra en el modelado satelital del terreno, el análisis de los sedimentos y sobre todo los datos geomorfológicos. Con todo esto, el equipo pudo lograr cartografiar las dimensiones de aquella masa de agua durante el último periodo interglaciar hace aproximadamente 125.000 años.
En ese momento, el lago Mundafan cubría una superficie cercana a los 340 kilómetros cuadrados y alcanzaba una profundidad máxima de 29 metros, manteniendo un ecosistema de agua dulce relativamente estable, flanqueado por vegetación ribereña y sabanas abiertas.
Y muy rico. El registro paleontológico recuperado en el lecho seco confirma la riqueza biológica de aquel entorno. Durante las prospecciones sistemáticas por cuadrícula, los investigadores documentaron más de 500 especímenes fósiles de plantas, invertebrados y vertebrados repartidos en más de 130 puntos distintos del yacimiento. Entre la fauna identificada destacan animales que se suelen encontrar alrededor de grandes masas de agua permanentes, como los hipopótamos, búfalos de cuernos largos, camellos o avestruces.
En definitiva, hablamos de un paisaje que encaja dentro del fenómeno climático conocido como la "Arabia verde". Este se pudo ver en un estudio publicado en Nature en 2025, donde se demostró que la península arábica atravesó al menos seis grandes fases húmedas a lo largo de los últimos ocho millones de años, impulsadas por desplazamientos en los sistemas monzónicos que transformaban las dunas en corredores habituales para la fauna.
Herramientas. Además de los restos de animales que han quedado en esta zona, también se ha visto que Uruq al-Julaybah es un enclave excepcional por el instrumental que se ha encontrado y datado con diferentes técnicas. Aquí se ha podido ver que el inventario arqueológico reúne 5.511 herramientas de piedra de más de dos centímetros, de las cuales más del 96% fueron fabricadas en sílex con la técnica Levallois.
Pero lo interesante es que, al combinar el reensamblaje tridimensional de las piezas con análisis microscópicos de la superficie, el equipo logró identificar residuos orgánicos extraordinariamente raros en yacimientos al aire libre de esta antigüedad. Por ejemplo, los rastros de resina y tejido leñoso demuestran que aquellas puntas de sílex iban enmangadas en astiles de madera para formar armas compuestas.
Y con veneno. Con el objetivo de ser más agresivos con sus armas, los investigadores detectaron la presencia de residuos procedentes de plantas tóxicas sobre las herramientas. De confirmarse esto, estaríamos ante una de las primeras evidencias de este tipo registradas en Arabia Saudí, puesto que lo que sabíamos es que las primeras armas con veneno se dieron hace unos 60.000 años. Esto lo atrasaría hasta los 125.000 años si se acaba confirmando.

articles.title: Facebook a espionné les photos prises par 20 millions de smartphones, comment désactiver cet accès par défaut ?
articles.text:
L’autorité italienne de protection des données a infligé le 14 novembre une amende de 805 millions d’euros à Meta Platforms Ireland, la plus lourde de son histoire. En cause, la fonction de Facebook sur Android qui propose, pendant la navigation, des photos et des vidéos puisées dans la galerie locale du téléphone. L’autorité retient qu’environ 20 millions d’utilisateurs italiens y ont été exposés sans avoir donné d’accord spécifique.
Lire aussi : Facebook veut un accès à vos photos personnelles, mais pas pour entraîner l’IA de Meta (pour l’instant)
Comment désactiver la permission qui ouvre vos photos à Facebook ?
Apparue en 2023 et activée par défaut, la fonction affiche au fil de la navigation des suggestions de publication tirées de la pellicule, y compris des fichiers que leur propriétaire n’a jamais mis en ligne. L’application accédait pour cela aux photos, aux vidéos et à leurs métadonnées sur la base d’une autorisation générale couvrant plusieurs usages à la fois, sans que l’information fournie ne mentionne distinctement ces suggestions.
La décision ne coupe rien à elle seule : l‘inversion du réglage par défaut fait partie des mesures imposées à Meta, qui conteste. La fonction reste donc active à ce jour sur les comptes qui ne l’ont jamais désactivée. Pour la couper dans l’application, direction Paramètres et confidentialité, puis Paramètres, rubrique Préférences, page « Suggestions de partage depuis la pellicule ». Désactivez-y les deux options, les suggestions personnalisées tirées de la galerie et celles proposées pendant la navigation sur Facebook. Le verrou le plus étanche se trouve côté système : retirez à Facebook l’autorisation Photos et vidéos dans les réglages d’Android.
L’instruction a été ouverte en juillet 2025 après l’alerte d’une association de consommateurs de Bolzano. Elle s’appuie sur l’article 122 du code italien de la vie privée, transposition de la directive européenne ePrivacy : lire le contenu d’un terminal exige un consentement préalable et éclairé, même sans transfert de données ni préjudice démontré.
Meta plaidait l’incompétence du régulateur italien, l’affaire relevant à ses yeux de l’autorité irlandaise, son interlocutrice habituelle en Europe. L’argument a été rejeté : la directive ePrivacy ne prévoit aucun guichet unique, et chaque autorité nationale peut sanctionner seule sur son territoire.
805 millions d’euros, et 60 jours pour tout débrancher
Le montant représente environ 0,47 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial du groupe. Pour le fixer, l’autorité a retenu le nombre de personnes touchées, un manquement toujours en cours, un précédent de 2019 visant déjà l’entreprise et une coopération jugée faible pendant l’enquête. Les correctifs apportés après la plainte n’ont d’ailleurs touché que les applications mises à jour.
Lire aussi : Nouveau scandale Facebook : des milliers de photos privées ont été compromises
La sanction s’accompagne d’un calendrier serré : un point d’étape sous 30 jours, puis une demande de consentement distincte et spécifique sous 60 jours. Celle-ci devra expliquer l’objectif de la fonction, son accès à la galerie et la manière de la couper. Les suggestions devront aussi repasser en position désactivée par défaut, y compris chez les utilisateurs qui avaient déjà dit oui, avec un compte rendu final sous 90 jours. Passé ce délai sans mise en conformité, la fonction ne pourra plus s’activer pour personne sans consentement valide.
Meta annonce un appel, juge l’amende « disproportionnée » et assure que les suggestions ne fonctionnent qu’après une autorisation de l’utilisateur, modifiable à tout moment dans les réglages. L’enquête n’a pas porté sur l’usage de ces contenus pour entraîner des modèles d’IA, que l’entreprise dément ; le traitement des galeries dans le cloud, introduit cette année, fera l’objet d’un examen séparé.

Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
Alecto Conveyancing Ltd., a London-based artificial intelligence-native law firm, today announced it raised $20 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners to make the law more accessible to the general public.
Firstminute Capital, Blue Lion Global, Andrena Ventures, FJ Labs, Antiportfolio Ventures, the Rigby Group and Mischon de Reya LLP also joined in the round. Angel investors participating in the round included Octopus Group Chief Executive and founder Simon Rogerson and SwiftKey founder John Reynolds.
Founded in September 2025 by CEO Will Rice (pictured), a serial entrepreneur who previously built fintech mortgage lender Gen H, Alecto’s first service targets the United Kingdom conveyancing market, the legal work required to buy and sell property. Rice drew on his experience building a mortgage company and decided to focus initially on bringing more people into ownership. With that expertise, Alecto aims to use AI to help give everyday people greater access to the law.
Alecto argues that traditional legal services are starved, with too few qualified attorneys and too few hours a day. Billing is based on hours, not outcomes and the service model doesn’t lean toward customers; this leads to unpredictable costs and a process that leaves customers in the dark.
The law firm said it’s using AI and legal experts to explain opaque legal processes in plain language and help clients make informed decisions. The company intends to target the property conveyancing market, which represents almost $3.3 billion in the U.K. alone, and aims to become the number one leader in property legal services by 2027.
“For too long, the legal industry has expected customers to work on its terms; now, AI presents the opportunity to put the consumer in control,” Rice said. “People don’t want to buy a lawyer’s time; they want results. Alecto exists to make the law accessible to everyone, giving control back to the consumer.”
Consumer legal services in the U.K. value growth pushed revenue over £55 billion, around $72.5 billion, in 2026, according to a report from Research and Markets. Business and commercial practices lead with 51% market value, followed by growth in the injury and conveyancing law markets.
“Property is where we prove the model. We’re building the technology and operations to rapidly break into new countries and new areas of law,” Rice added. “Ultimately, access to exceptional legal support should not depend on how much money you have or how confidently you can navigate the system.”
