articles.title: Jouer à GTA 6 avant tout le monde en France, c’est possible sur Xbox grâce à une "simple" astuce
articles.text:
Une astuce permet de jouer à GTA 6 dès le mercredi 18 novembre à midi sur Xbox Series, en réglant la console sur la Nouvelle-Zélande. Les joueurs PS5, eux, devront attendre la sortie française.
GTA 6 sort officiellement dans la nuit du mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre en France, mais les joueurs Xbox peuvent prendre douze heures d'avance. Comme le détaille Numerama, il suffit de faire croire à sa Xbox Series X|S qu'elle se trouve en Nouvelle-Zélande, le premier pays où le jeu se débloque. La manipulation prend deux minutes, Microsoft joue la carte du laissé faire, et les joueurs PS5, plus malheureux sur ce coup, devront patienter quelques heures supplémentaires.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Deux minutes de réglages pour jouer à GTA 6 plus tôt grâce au… décalage horaire !
Rockstar n'a pas choisi de lancer GTA 6 à la même seconde partout dans le monde. Le jeu se débloque à minuit, heure locale, pays par pays, comme Sony l'a confirmé sur le PlayStation Blog. Chaque joueur doit donc attendre que minuit sonne chez lui. Or, la Nouvelle-Zélande est l’un des tout premiers pays à changer de jour, comme il est chaque année le premier à passer à la nouvelle année et à nos offrir les premières images du feu d'artifice tiré pour l'occasion.
En novembre, c’est même l’été là-bas, puisque les saisons y sont inversées, et l’heure d’été lui donne carrément douze heures d’avance sur la France. Du coup, quand il sera minuit à Auckland, le jeudi 19 novembre, il ne sera que midi, le mercredi, à Paris. Autant vous dire que les spoilers et images risquent de circuler bien avant minuit chez nous, sur les réseaux sociaux notamment.
Pour en profiter, il faut une Xbox Series X ou S et une version numérique de GTA 6, déjà préchargée. Les acheteurs de la boîte, vendue depuis le 12 novembre sans disque mais avec un code, doivent donc l'avoir activé et téléchargé. Suivez ensuite le chemin Paramètres > Système > Langue et région : on choisit la Nouvelle-Zélande comme région, on redémarre la console, puis on lance le jeu mercredi à partir de midi. Il n'y a pas besoin de VPN ni de basculer la console en anglais, c'est le réglage de la région qui fait tout.
Microsoft ferme les yeux, Sony ferme la porte
Officiellement, Microsoft recommande de ne changer de région qu'en cas de déménagement durable, car certains contenus peuvent ne pas fonctionner d'une région à l'autre. Dans les faits et historiquement, le constructeur laisse faire tant que l'astuce ne sert pas à acheter des jeux moins chers, et aucun bannissement n'a d'ailleurs été signalé dans un tel cas, selon nos confrères. Xbox s'en est même amusé puisqu'en 2021, lors de l'accès anticipé à Forza Horizon 5, son compte australien et néo-zélandais souhaitait la bienvenue à « tous ceux qui ont déménagé en Nouvelle-Zélande la nuit dernière », un message un brin ironique qui en dit long.
Sur PS5, hélas, l'astuce tombe à l'eau, car c'est le pays du compte PlayStation Network qui compte, et il ne peut plus être modifié après sa création. Il faudrait donc un compte néo-zélandais, alimenté par un moyen de paiement local. Côté Xbox, évitez tout achat pendant l'essai, puisque la boutique peut afficher ses prix en dollars néo-zélandais. Si le jeu reste verrouillé, ne le rachetez pas, et fuyez les offres de « déblocage garanti » payant. Numerama assure qu'on peut repasser la console en France une fois le jeu lancé, mais d'autres sites appellent à la prudence, alors notre conseil qu'il vaut mieux attendre le déblocage français pour revenir. Pensez enfin à prévoir jusqu'à 212 Go libres selon la console, pour un jeu qui visera 30 FPS sur toutes les consoles.

articles.title: Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026
Guia reúne telas IPS de 120 Hz a 300 Hz com baixo tempo de resposta e fidelidade de cor para jogos competitivos, campanhas imersivas e uso diário em 2026
Escolher um monitor gamer IPS em 2026 exige equilibrar taxa de atualização, tempo de resposta e precisão cromática de acordo com o perfil de jogo.
Os painéis IPS (In-Plane Switching) consolidaram-se como o padrão preferido para setups versáteis porque oferecem amplos ângulos de visão de 178° e cobertura de cores superior aos painéis TN e VA tradicionais, sem sacrificar a agilidade exigida em títulos competitivos.
Nesta lista, selecionamos 8 modelos disponíveis no mercado brasileiro que cobrem diferentes faixas de desempenho e orçamento, partindo de opções de entrada de 120 Hz até telas avançadas de 300 Hz com retroiluminação MiniLED e resolução Quad HD.
O TCL 25G64 eleva o patamar dos monitores competitivos ao combinar um painel IPS Full HD (1920 x 1080) de 25 polegadas com retroiluminação QD-MiniLED, taxa de atualização de 300 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
Essa combinação elimina rastros em movimentos bruscos de câmera em jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa (FPS), enquanto o controle local de iluminação proporciona pretos mais profundos e brilho máximo de 600 nits com certificação HDR600.
Para quem busca fidelidade visual além da velocidade, o modelo entrega profundidade de cor de 10 bits, cobertura de 96% do espectro DCI-P3 e calibração de fábrica com precisão Delta E menor que 2.
A conectividade inclui duas portas HDMI 2.1 e uma DisplayPort, acompanhadas de base ergonômica com ajuste de altura e compatibilidade com AMD FreeSync Premium.
Voltado para jogadores que priorizam definição de imagem sem abrir mão da fluidez, o AOC Agon Q27G4F traz tela Fast IPS de 27 polegadas com resolução Quad HD (2560 x 1440 pixels), taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,5 ms MPRT).
A maior densidade de pixels garante nitidez superior para identificar alvos a longa distância e amplia a área útil de trabalho no dia a dia. O painel cobre 120% do espaço de cores sRGB, conta com brilho típico de 300 cd/m² e suporte a HDR10, entregando tonalidades vibrantes em jogos de mundo aberto.
Compatível com NVIDIA G-SYNC e Adaptive Sync para evitar cortes na imagem (screen tearing), o modelo ainda se destaca pela base completa com ajustes de altura, inclinação, giro e rotação (pivô), além de entradas DisplayPort 1.4 e HDMI 2.0.
O Samsung Odyssey G40 de 25 polegadas é projetado especificamente para o cenário de eSports, operando com painel IPS Full HD, taxa de atualização nativa de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
O formato compacto de 25 polegadas mantém toda a ação dentro do campo de visão periférico do jogador, permitindo reações imediatas em partidas ranqueadas de alto nível.
Com brilho típico de 400 cd/m² e suporte a FreeSync Premium e G-SYNC Compatible, o monitor mantém boa visibilidade mesmo em ambientes bastante iluminados e sincroniza os quadros da GPU sem engasgos.
O conjunto oferece duas entradas HDMI, uma DisplayPort e suporte ergonomicamente ajustável em altura, inclinação e modo retrato.
O Dell SE2426HG entrega especificações de nível competitivo em um chassi sóbrio de 24 polegadas, equipado com painel IPS Full HD de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 0,5 ms. Essa configuração garante transições de pixels limpas e baixa latência de entrada, atendendo jogadores de títulos competitivos que buscam alto desempenho com investimento controlado.
O modelo integra suporte a AMD FreeSync, compatibilidade com HDR10 e tecnologias de conforto visual, como tela antirreflexo, redução de luz azul e operação livre de cintilação (Flicker-Free). Conta ainda com conectividade DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI e furação padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm para instalação em braços articulados.
Posicionando-se acima do padrão tradicional de 144 Hz e 180 Hz, o AOC Agon 24G42HE apresenta tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 200 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,3 ms MPRT). O ganho extra de frequência proporciona rastreamento de alvos mais suave e resposta rápida aos comandos do mouse.
Com brilho de 300 cd/m², contraste estático de 1000:1 e cobertura de 116% do padrão sRGB, o painel reproduz cores vivas em jogos e conteúdos multimídia.
O monitor possui certificação NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible, design sem bordas em três lados, entradas HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA.
O LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B equilibra velocidade e precisão cromática em um painel IPS de 24 polegadas (23,8 polegadas visíveis) com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta real de 1 ms (GtG). A combinação reduz o efeito fantasma (ghosting) em cenas rápidas sem comprometer a estabilidade das cores.
O display cobre 99% da gama sRGB, suporta HDR10 e oferece ampla compatibilidade com NVIDIA G-SYNC e AMD FreeSync. Entre os recursos voltados para jogos estão o Dynamic Action Sync (redução de atraso de entrada), o Black Stabilizer (clareamento de áreas escuras) e mira integrada na tela, conectados via HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4.
Para quem prefere uma área de visualização maior mantendo a resolução Full HD, o LG UltraGear 27G411B traz tela IPS de 27 polegadas com taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms com Motion Blur Reduction (5 ms GtG nativo).
O tamanho ampliado favorece a imersão em jogos de corrida, RPGs e consumo de vídeos, sem exigir uma placa de vídeo topo de linha para empurrar os quadros.
O painel apresenta contraste estático de 1500:1 — superior à média da categoria IPS —, cobertura de 99% sRGB, suporte a HDR10 e sincronização adaptativa via NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible e AMD FreeSync.
A construção inclui bordas finas em três lados, entradas HDMI e DisplayPort, saída para fones de ouvido e padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm.
O Samsung Essential S3 LS24F320GALMZD é o modelo mais básico da lista, mas ainda usa painel IPS e resolução Full HD, se saindo melhor para jogos casuais, trabalho remoto e uso multimídia.
A taxa de atualização menor que a de modelos gamer avançados limita o apelo competitivo. Mesmo assim, recursos como FreeSync, baixo input lag e boa reprodução de cores ajudam em consoles, notebooks e PCs simples.
A indicação é para quem quer gastar pouco e evitar painéis de qualidade inferior. O Essential S3 funciona como monitor IPS de entrada para jogar ocasionalmente, estudar e montar um setup econômico em 2026.
A escolha do monitor gamer IPS ideal depende da potência da sua placa de vídeo (GPU), dos gêneros de jogos praticados e do espaço disponível na mesa. Antes de fechar a compra, avalie quatro critérios técnicos fundamentais:
Na faixa de entrada intermediária, modelos de 24 polegadas Full HD entre 180 Hz e 200 Hz, como o LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B e o AOC Agon 24G42HE, oferecem o equilíbrio mais eficiente entre preço e desempenho.
Ambos entregam painéis IPS rápidos de 1 ms GtG, boa cobertura de cores sRGB e sincronização adaptativa sem exigir placas de vídeo avançadas.
Para quem busca salto de resolução e ergonomia completa pagando menos que em modelos OLED, o AOC Agon Q27G4F (27″ QHD 180 Hz) destaca-se como a opção mais equilibrada da categoria intermediária.
A taxa de atualização ideal começa em 144 Hz para jogos competitivos. Esse patamar já oferece movimentos mais suaves que 60 Hz ou 75 Hz e melhora a resposta visual em partidas rápidas.
Monitores de 180 Hz são o ponto de equilíbrio em 2026, pois entregam fluidez alta sem exigir tanto quanto 240 Hz. Eles combinam bem com placas de vídeo intermediárias em Full HD.
Modelos de 240 Hz, como o Samsung Odyssey G40, fazem mais sentido para jogadores de e-sports. Para aproveitar a tela, o PC precisa manter taxas próximas em jogos como CS2, Valorant e Overwatch 2.
Os painéis IPS dominam o mercado de monitores gamer por equilibrarem velocidade e qualidade de imagem, mas apresentam limitações físicas inerentes à tecnologia LCD:
O monitor OLED entrega contraste praticamente infinito, pretos reais e tempo de resposta extremamente rápido. Em jogos HDR, terror e single-player cinematográfico, a imagem costuma ser superior à de um IPS tradicional.
O monitor IPS vence em preço, disponibilidade e menor risco de burn-in. Para uso prolongado com HUD fixo, planilhas, navegador e barra de tarefas, ele tende a ser uma escolha mais tranquila.
Em 2026, OLED é a opção premium para quem busca qualidade máxima. IPS continua sendo a melhor compra racional para a maioria, especialmente em monitores Full HD e QHD com 144 Hz a 240 Hz.
O monitor IPS é melhor para quem prioriza cores, ângulo de visão e resposta mais previsível em jogos rápidos. Nossa equipe prefere IPS para FPS competitivo, uso misto e setups com duas telas.
Já o monitor VA oferece contraste maior, com pretos mais profundos e imagem forte em filmes ou jogos escuros. Porém, alguns modelos podem apresentar ghosting em transições rápidas, especialmente em cenas com tons escuros.
A escolha depende do perfil do jogador. Para e-sports e versatilidade, IPS é mais seguro; para imersão, contraste e consumo de mídia, VA pode agradar mais se o modelo tiver boa resposta.

articles.title: Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business — deal positions company as leading vendor of qubit chips, acquisition to close by the first half of 2027
articles.text:
Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business — deal positions company as leading vendor of qubit chips, acquisition to close by the first half of 2027
Intel becomes a top-to-bottom quantum computing company.
After having spent more than a decade pursuing quantum computing research, Intel is making its first real push at commercializing its efforts. First, with the pending acquisition of quantum computing company Classiq, which has an existing list of enterprise customers. Intel says it'll be the only company that can produce qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics at scale; the deal would give it a complete top-to-bottom hardware-to-software stack, and Intel will also gain the chance to become a leading vendor of quantum computing products. Intel's acquisition of Classiq is expected to complete in the first half of 2027.
The key ingredient of that strategy is the pending acquisition of Classiq, which offers a hardware-agnostic quantum software development platform that enables engineers to design, synthesize, optimize, simulate, and execute quantum algorithms using high-level programming tools and AI-assisted automation, essentially untying software design from the complexity of quantum hardware. Meanwhile, Intel also plans to manufacture quantum processors using specialized versions of its 18A process technology, offer foundry services, and eventually sell complete quantum computers. Although the company expects its quantum business to become profitable, it acknowledges that commercial success will take time.
Intel has spent more than a decade developing quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin-qubit processors, cryogenic control electronics, and software for hybrid quantum-classical computing. However, the company has largely treated these activities as research and development projects rather than an actual business. The acquisition of Classiq, which Intel expects to complete in the first half of 2027, marks a shift toward commercialization as Classiq already has many clients and established revenue streams.
"Up until now […] our quantum computing group for the last ten years was […] purely a research and development project," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel, during a media briefing. "It was not really viewed as a commercial activity."
Intel's quantum hardware: The journey so far
Intel's quantum computing journey kicked off in 2015 with a research collaboration with QuTech — the quantum research institute of TU Delft and TNO — to develop quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin qubits. The idea was to leverage Intel's extensive expertise in silicon transistor development and its high-volume semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure to produce quantum processors in the same fabs that make conventional CPUs, overcoming the manufacturing scalability challenges alternative quantum computing architectures faced at the time. Intel subsequently developed Horse Ridge, a cryogenic control SoC manufactured using a 22nm process technology in 2020. Three years later, the company introduced Tunnel Falls, a 12-qubit silicon spin processor manufactured on a 300mm wafer.
Intel's quantum computing effort focuses on silicon spin qubits, which use spin states of individual electrons to store and manipulate quantum information. The company chose this approach partly because silicon spin qubits can be manufactured using equipment and processes similar to those employed for conventional semiconductor devices. This compatibility enables Intel to re-use most of its existing manufacturing infrastructure and expertise rather than build dedicated semiconductor fabrication facilities for quantum processors that yet have to become commercial products.
Despite the recent cuts at Intel, the company sustained its quantum computing project. Intel has developed two specialized versions of its 18A manufacturing technology for quantum computing: 18A-Q for silicon spin-qubit processors and 18A-CC for cryogenic control and readout electronics. To define/build 18A-Q, Intel has collaborated with Hitachi, AIST, and NEDO (three major supporters of quantum computing from Japan), and there appears to be a design kit intended to support large quantum computing systems. Without a doubt, 18A-Q and 18A-CC put Intel on the map of quantum computing chips in a big way. A couple of things should be kept in mind, though.
"The underlying device that we use, underlying process that we use to make the actual qubit device is a unique process, but it fits into those design rules," Ranade explained. "We can make these chips […] in the same fab that we use to make our CPUs."
Although Intel 18AQ uses BEOL interconnect geometry and design rules derived from Intel 18A, its underlying qubit devices require a different manufacturing process. According to Ranade, the technology requires a specialized thin-film stack and several additional manufacturing tools. Nevertheless, more than 90% of the manufacturing equipment is identical to that used for conventional semiconductor production, according to Intel.
"Intel 18A-CC, meanwhile, uses 18A-based geometry but requires additional characterization for operation at cryogenic temperatures," Ranade said. "Crucially, Intel can manufacture quantum processors alongside conventional CPUs in existing semiconductor fabs, which could reduce the capital expenditure required to scale production. […] More than 90% of the process equipment is exactly the same."
A major piece in the quantum computing puzzle: Classiq
For conventional x86 architectures and IA-64 (while it was active), Intel has historically offered compilers that made software run better on its hardware (and sometimes on AMD hardware too). By contrast, with its quantum computing efforts, Intel has generally focused on hardware and while it has its own Quantum SDK that includes a compiler, this is not enough in the quantum computing realm as Classiq's offering operates at a higher abstraction level. With the acquisition of Classiq, the company intends to fill that gap.
Classiq develops a hardware-agnostic quantum software platform that applies electronic design automation (EDA) principles to quantum programming, which lets developers design, synthesize, and optimize quantum algorithms without manually constructing circuits from individual quantum gates. The company's software provides high-level modeling, automated algorithm synthesis, optimization, debugging, and execution capabilities across different quantum computing architectures, which somewhat resembles Intel's approach to its x86 compilers, albeit working at a different level.
Intel already has its Quantum SDK, which includes a C++-based compiler, runtime environment, and simulator for hybrid quantum-classical applications. Classiq's platform will sit above these tools and provide an application-development environment for programmers who lack extensive expertise in quantum computing.
Intel compares the potential significance of Classiq's software layer to Microsoft's MS-DOS, which helped establish the personal computer software ecosystem; Nvidia's CUDA, which enabled developers to exploit GPUs for general-purpose accelerated computing; and EDA tools, which abstracted high-level design descriptions from the complexities of transistor-level integrated circuit implementation and essentially set the stage for the multi-billion foundry industry today.
Furthermore, unlike Intel's quantum hardware business, Classiq already has commercial customers and generates revenue. The company employs approximately 130 people and serves more than 50 enterprise customers, including BMW, Comcast, Lufthansa, Rolls-Royce, and Toshiba. It also participates in more than 10 national quantum computing programs and supports over 50 quantum processors and simulators.
As existing quantum processors remain insufficient for many practical applications, companies can develop and optimize software ahead of hardware availability. As a result, these customers primarily use Classiq products to develop quantum algorithms, train engineers, and create intellectual property in preparation for commercially useful quantum computers.
Intel's CTO described Classiq's revenue and anticipated growth as healthy, but did not disclose actual financial figures.
"They have a very healthy revenue this year and a very healthy revenue CAGR over the coming years," Ranade said. "We hope that… we want that to continue."
It is necessary to note that Intel intends to preserve Classiq's hardware-agnostic approach, which means allowing the company to continue supporting quantum processors and simulators from competing vendors. This is essential to maintain Classiq's existing customer relationships and expand its revenue opportunities, as its clients can/will be able to develop quantum applications without committing to a particular hardware architecture. Obviously, Intel can generate software revenue regardless of which quantum computing technologies ultimately become commercially successful.
"We very much want to maintain that hardware-agnostic platform that they have developed to attract more and more customers," Ranade said.
From quantum chips to complete systems
When it comes to quantum computing, Intel's ambitions extend beyond manufacturing silicon spin-qubit processors. The company intends to become a supplier of complete quantum computing systems, which would combine quantum processors, cryogenic control electronics, classical computing resources, and software. For now, Intel has most of the building blocks required to develop complete quantum computing systems, but it still has to demonstrate that it can integrate them into commercially viable quantum computing at scale.
"We want to be in the business of building quantum foundry components, but also complete quantum systems," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel.
Intel is also considering opportunities to provide quantum foundry services to other hardware developers. While its internal processor development will remain focused on silicon spin qubits, the company is open to manufacturing components for alternative quantum computing technologies, which somewhat resembles its approach to its x86 CPU and foundry businesses.
"We are committed to spin qubits," Ranade said. "But we are also open to providing foundry services to other modalities."
Intel believes that its capabilities in photonics, advanced packaging, and semiconductor manufacturing could become commercially relevant even to companies developing quantum processors based on different physical principles than silicon qubits.
Can quantum computing become profitable?
Intel's decision to expand its quantum computing activities with the takeover of Classiq comes as chief executive Lip-Bu Tan emphasized profitability, financial discipline, and high-margin products across the company’s established businesses. Given that Intel's quantum computing initiative barely generates any revenue, let alone profits, the CEO stance raises questions about the viability of quantum computing for Intel, especially in a situation where the industry has yet to demonstrate widespread practical applications that justify the cost of large-scale quantum hardware.
When asked how Intel’s quantum computing strategy fits Tan's profitability requirements, Ranade explained that the company's immediate financial priorities primarily concern its established client and server processor businesses. Nevertheless, Intel must continue investing in emerging technologies that could shape future computing markets.
"This is really a bet on the future," Ranade said. "This is something we also have to do in addition to our mainstream businesses today."
The Intel CTO acknowledged that quantum computing is not set to become a high-margin business in the near future. Meanwhile, the acquisition of Classiq gives Intel an established commercial software operation and revenue stream here and now, as well as an opportunity to expand customer relationships well before its own quantum processors reach commercial maturity. Intel also hopes that combining its hardware and software capabilities (probably including Classiq) will attract customers interested in complete quantum computing solutions.
When asked whether vertical integration would make Intel's quantum computing operations profitable, Ranade acknowledged that he could not predict gross margins of the quantum computing business because the industry is still in its infancy. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence in the commercial prospects of Intel's quantum hardware and software.
"I expect it to become a profitable business very quickly on the hardware side, but too early to tell," Ranade said.
Quantum computing will remain hybrid
Even though quantum processors evolve at a rapid pace, the technology is unlikely to replace existing CPUs and GPUs for conventional computing any time soon. Instead, Intel expects quantum computing systems to operate alongside the usual processors in data centers and supercomputing environments.
Classiq's software platform will provide high-level quantum algorithm development capabilities, while Intel Quantum SDK will handle compilation, simulation, and hybrid quantum-classical execution. This approach differs from Nvidia's CUDA-Q, which is designed to integrate quantum computing workflows with existing accelerated computing infrastructure. According to Classiq chief executive Nir Minerbi, Classiq operates at a higher level of abstraction and can complement CUDA-Q rather than compete with it.
"CUDA Q is very much low-level; it is gate-level. It is a good platform, by the way, but it is very low-level," said Minerbi. "The reason companies like Rolls-Royce and BMW and others use the Classiq platform on top of CUDA Q is due to the level of abstraction. It is much, much easier to develop quantum programs with Classiq and then to simulate it with CUDA Q rather than only with CUDA Q."
Meanwhile, commercial success of quantum computing still depends on substantial advances in quantum hardware, including qubit scalability, error correction, control electronics, and system integration. For now, many Classiq customers are developing applications for quantum computers that have yet to reach the scale required for commercially valuable workloads.
Summary
Intel expects to complete its acquisition of Classiq in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The company has not disclosed the purchase price or other financial terms.
The transaction will bring Classiq's software development capabilities and established customer relationships into Intel's quantum computing organization, but will preserve the platform's compatibility with competing hardware technologies. For Intel, the acquisition represents an opportunity to turn more than a decade of quantum computing research into a commercial business unit as it will have all the building blocks required to create quantum systems. Furthermore, Intel's quantum computing business will be open to third parties in the sense that Intel will be able to build quantum processors for partners using its 18AQ and 18ACC process technologies.
Whether Intel's quantum computing business eventually delivers the high margins Intel seeks will depend not only on Intel's ability to build systems, produce quantum chips for others, or Classiq's software revenue, but also on the industry's ability to develop quantum processors and systems capable of solving real-world problems that people are willing to pay for.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: How friends from Coimbatore built GOAT Robotics into an Rs 8 crore business with global reach
articles.text:
How friends from Coimbatore built GOAT Robotics into an Rs 8 crore business with global reach
Starting from a rented 2BHK in Coimbatore, GOAT Robotics grew from Rs 10 lakh in turnover to over Rs 8 crore. Discover how nine engineering graduates pivoted from hotel robots to industrial automation and expanded internationally.
GOAT Robotics, a startup founded by friends who studied B.E. Robotics and Automation Engineering at a private engineering college in Coimbatore, a Tier 2 city, has achieved success by providing robotic services to several countries.
What began with a turnover of just Rs 10 lakh has now grown into a large company that spends Rs 40 lakh every month on salaries alone.
Muthu Vangaliappan, one of the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of GOAT Robotics, shared the company's success story with us.
The nine founders of GOAT Robotics come from different districts, including Coimbatore, Erode, and Salem. All of them graduated in 2015 with a B.E. in Robotics and Automation Engineering from PSG Engineering College in Coimbatore. After securing jobs through campus placements, they moved to different companies across various states.
“During our college days, the nine of us were a close-knit group. We shared the same dream of studying well and achieving great heights in life. As time passed and we continued working, we began thinking about starting our own business. In 2015, Naveen, Dharmaraj, Mugesh, and I came together to establish a company called Katomaran Technologies Pvt. Ltd.,” said Muthu.
In the initial days, the four friends conducted seminars at colleges and provided robotics-related training to students and aspiring entrepreneurs.
To expand their business, they rented a 2BHK house in Coimbatore in 2018 and formally started operating Katomaran Technologies Pvt. Ltd. This beginning has now grown into a large company generating a turnover of more than Rs 8 crore.
Friends Who Started Their Journey Amid Severe Setbacks
Muthu says they faced several serious challenges and setbacks during the initial stages of their business before recovering.
“While we were providing automation and robotics services to small companies in India, we got an opportunity to work for a few companies in Singapore. We realised that there was always a shortage of around 40% of security personnel there. This led us to start using robotics and automation technology in the security sector.
“We made their work easier and addressed the manpower shortage by introducing various automation technologies, including automated toll gates and cameras, for people traffic, vehicle traffic, utility management, and surveillance. This project gave us good profits and valuable experience.
“We also began introducing robots in hotels. As the years passed, we started thinking about why we couldn't use the same technology in India. With that idea, in 2019, we continuously visited major hotels across India and submitted proposals for using robots,” Muthu shared, recalling the company's early days.
“However, we did not achieve the same level of success that we had experienced in Singapore. This was because the use of robots in India was very limited, and many people were unwilling to adopt them.
“While our business was doing well in Singapore, we faced setbacks when we shifted our focus to India.
Nevertheless, we continued working in hotels, not just with robots but also in areas such as 3D gaming and gaming simulators,” he said.
The Story Behind the Formation of GOAT Robotics
From 2019 to 2022, the team focused extensively on manufacturing specialised robots for hotels. They developed various robots, including room-service robots, hotel room-cleaning robots, bellboy robots, and dispensers, supplying them to five-star and seven-star hotels.
However, during the COVID-19 pandemic, they faced severe difficulties as they stopped receiving orders.
“While our business was progressing this way, five other friends who had studied with us were already running a company called Dotworld Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
“In 2023, their company and ours merged, and we established GOAT Robotics in Coimbatore. GOAT stands for Greatest of All Technologies,” he explained.
“When we started this company, we already had extensive experience in manufacturing, while the new group of friends had significant experience in marketing. Combining the expertise of both teams, we planned to provide automation and robotics-related services to major hotels in India.
“We frequently approached hotels and hospitals, conducted demonstrations, and submitted proposals. That was when we realised an important truth: this business model would work in foreign countries such as Singapore and Malaysia, but it would be difficult in India.
“We realised that we were running fast in the wrong direction. As we reached a point where we risked losing our business, we decided to develop a different category of robotics.”
They first began manufacturing and supplying lifting robots capable of carrying heavy loads. They developed robots for several companies to lift and move heavy objects. Later, they began manufacturing packing robots and providing automation solutions.
“We continued working with small companies through contracts. Within a few months, we received a good response. We then decided to pitch our idea to a major company for the first time.
“We sent our idea to Toyota, and they liked it and signed an agreement with us. Our journey with Toyota began in December 2023,” said Muthu.
From Coimbatore to Serving Countries Across the World
Muthu shared that getting an opportunity to work with a major company like Toyota, despite having started as an ordinary business in Coimbatore, became a major turning point for them.
He continued:
“Although we began our journey with GOAT Robotics in December 2023, we recorded a turnover of just Rs 10 lakh during 2023–2024.
“After that, we recognised our strengths, addressed our weaknesses, and began providing services to companies using various technologies in the robotics and automation sector.”
“During 2024–2025, the GOAT Robotics team began working not only with Toyota but also with several major and multinational companies, including Volvo, Maruti, Suzuki, Pricol, and Timken.
“Our turnover, which was just Rs 10 lakh, increased to Rs 6 crore in 2024–2025.
“Today, we are providing services across several countries, including India, the United States, Australia, Middle Eastern countries, Singapore, and Malaysia,” he said.
“All the members of our team come from middle-class family backgrounds and have faced considerable financial difficulties.
“Therefore, we have started an initiative to make robots accessible not only to large companies but also to small businesses.
“We are manufacturing and supplying robots at affordable prices to entrepreneurs like us,” he added.
From a 2BHK House to a Company Paying Rs 40 Lakh in Monthly Salaries
The company has robots capable of lifting or moving loads weighing 100 kg. It also manufactures robots capable of handling weights ranging from 100 kg to 5,000 kg.
To make robots accessible to ordinary entrepreneurs and micro, small, and medium enterprises, the company manufactures and sells robots priced between Rs 12–13 lakh and Rs 45 lakh, as well as robots valued between Rs 45 lakh and Rs 2 crore.
“Our journey, which began in a simple 2BHK house, has grown to the point where we established our own dedicated 6,000 sq. ft. office in 2024.
“Our company, which started with just nine people in Coimbatore, now employs 77 people.
“We provide opportunities to engineering graduates who are eager to learn and develop their knowledge after completing their education.
“We offer a minimum salary of Rs 30,000. Every month, we spend a total of Rs 40 lakh on salaries alone for the staff and interns working at GOAT Robotics,” Muthu proudly shared, describing the company's growth.
“There are nine of us. This success has been possible because each of us works in teams of two.
“We have divided ourselves into teams based on our experience in manufacturing, communication, service, marketing, and research and development. This division of responsibilities has made it easier for us to achieve success.”
“Every year, the Central Government encourages micro, small, and medium entrepreneurs by presenting awards.
“In 2025, we won the Central Government's Make in India Excellence Award 2025 and received a cash prize of Rs 10 lakh from the government.
“So far in the current financial year alone, we have achieved a turnover of Rs 8 crore.
“Our target is to reach a turnover of Rs 25 crore during this financial year,” he said.
In March 2025, the company raised Rs 2.66 crore (approximately $311K–$320K) in a funding round led by Campus Angels Network, with participation from TiE Coimbatore, NativeLead Angels, Pontaq Ventures, and others.
“Deep Affection Is What Will Make Us Successful”
Muthu also offered some advice to people planning to start a new business and those considering starting a business with partners.
“Those who run businesses with friends or other partners can achieve great success only if they always have deep affection and care for one another.
“When failures occur, they must be willing to make compromises, support one another, face problems positively, and overcome difficult times together. By doing so, they can achieve success more easily.
“Similarly, when starting something worthwhile, we should not wait for the right time. We must understand the risks involved and start the business immediately.
“If we simply watch from the sidelines or hesitate, time will leave us behind, and we may not even be able to begin what we had planned.
“If we lose time, we will neither be able to take risks nor grow,” Muthu Vangaliyappan said, sharing the lessons he had learned from his entrepreneurial journey.

articles.title: Estos son los 4 cambios que tendría el iPhone Duo de Apple en el año 2027
articles.text:
Apple ya estaría trabajando en cuatro cambios para la segunda generación del iPhone Duo, el teléfono plegable que llegó al mercado hace apenas unas semanas. Pese a lo reciente de su lanzamiento, la compañía necesita definir pronto las características del sucesor si quiere cumplir con su calendario habitual de presentación en septiembre.
Así lo detalló Mark Gurman en Bloomberg, donde señaló que la empresa ya cuenta con prototipos del dispositivo, identificado internamente con el nombre en clave V78, y que trabaja en paralelo en cuatro frentes de mejora.
Cuáles son los cambios que tendría el iPhone Duo
- Face ID
El primer cambio, y el más urgente para Apple, es la incorporación de Face ID al iPhone Duo 2. El modelo actual utiliza Touch ID, un sistema que funciona de forma correcta pero que resulta menos cómodo que el reconocimiento facial para buena parte de los usuarios.
Según Gurman, la compañía ya desarrolló prototipos del dispositivo con Face ID integrado en la pantalla exterior. Los ingenieros continúan trabajando en esa integración, aunque todavía no está confirmado si la tecnología también llegará a la pantalla interior del plegable.
El reconocimiento facial seguro requiere Face ID, un sistema que proyecta e interpreta un mapa de puntos infrarrojos para identificar el rostro del usuario. Su llegada al iPhone Duo 2 depende de si Apple logra ubicar los componentes necesarios dentro de un chasis plegable con espacio limitado.
El tiempo juega en contra de este objetivo. Si el lanzamiento se mantiene en septiembre del año próximo, la compañía debe cerrar las definiciones de hardware en las próximas semanas, lo que convierte a Face ID en un desarrollo todavía incierto para la versión final que llegue al público.
- Un botón de acción compartido con la cámara
El segundo cambio contemplado es la incorporación de un botón de acción, ausente en el primer iPhone Duo. Se trata del único modelo de iPhone sin ese conmutador o botón dedicado a silenciar el equipo o ejecutar funciones rápidas, una omisión que, según Gurman, respondería a limitaciones de espacio dentro de un chasis compacto.
Para resolverlo sin sacrificar superficie interna, Apple evalúa combinar esa función con el botón de control de cámara, de manera que un mismo componente cumpla ambas tareas. La medida resulta coherente con reportes de usuarios que señalan un uso poco frecuente del botón de cámara en su formato actual.
- Cámara teleobjetivo
El tercer punto de la hoja de ruta apunta al sistema de cámaras. Pese a que los resultados fotográficos del iPhone Duo actual resultan convincentes, el dispositivo carece de una cámara teleobjetivo pese a tratarse de un modelo más caro que los iPhone Pro.
Apple estudiaría sumar una tercera cámara principal con esa función, aunque el desafío vuelve a ser el espacio disponible: en un cuerpo plegable donde la mayor parte del volumen interno se destina a la batería y al sistema de bisagras, cualquier cámara adicional implica rediseñar buena parte de la placa.
- Diseño más delgado
El cuarto objetivo es el más exigente en términos de ingeniería: un diseño más delgado y liviano que el actual, sin reducir el tamaño de pantalla ni las prestaciones. Apple buscaría lograrlo mientras suma, al mismo tiempo, Face ID, un botón adicional y una cámara extra, aunque Gurman no precisó en qué magnitud se reduciría el grosor del equipo.
Plazos ajustados y margen de cambios
Gurman advirtió que el desarrollo del iPhone Duo 2 se encuentra en una etapa temprana. Apple suele finalizar sus prototipos definitivos hacia febrero, para luego someterlos a pruebas de fábrica antes de iniciar la producción en julio, con vistas a un lanzamiento entre septiembre y octubre.
Esa ventana implica que alguno de los cuatro objetivos podría quedar descartado si los plazos se ajustan antes de lo previsto. El periodista remarcó que la información disponible retrata el estado actual del desarrollo, sin garantizar que todas las funciones lleguen al modelo final.
Según Gurman, los compradores del primer iPhone Duo no deben esperar que sus comentarios o encuestas de satisfacción influyan en el diseño del Duo 2. El cronograma de la segunda generación ya estaba definido antes del lanzamiento del modelo original, por lo que cualquier ajuste basado en la opinión de los usuarios recién podría incorporarse en una eventual tercera versión.

articles.title: En Oviedo han montado un cowork en mitad de la naturaleza y no faltan ni ayudas ni wifi de alta velocidad
articles.text:
Hay coworkings con unas vistas fantásticas en plantas de torres de oficinas, o en naves industriales reconvertidas. También los hay que son bajos y locales con humedades que da miedo verlos. Y luego está el que han montado en un bosque de Ribera de Arriba, a poco más de cinco minutos de Oviedo, con contenedores marítimos por despachos y 25 plazas de aparcamiento gratuito.
El invento se llama Cowtainers, que es un juego de palabras entre coworking y containers. No, lo de "cow" no viene por las vacas, aunque en Oviedo no es tan difícil verlas. Expansión ya lo contó en octubre de 2025, y un año después la web presume de 38 puestos, 8.000 metros cuadrados de terreno y un 5,0 en Google con 54 reseñas. Nunca he trabajado en un coworking más allá de un par de horas, pero si tuviera que elegir alguno sería este. Y no por el WiFi, aunque parece que va perfecto.
Quién está detrás. El proyecto es de Víctor Pérez Arce, arquitecto, y Pablo Díaz Campbell-Smith, ingeniero, dos amigos de la infancia que habían hecho carrera fuera de Asturias y querían volver con algo distinto. La idea llevaba casi cinco años gestándose cuando abrieron, y el coworking está plenamente operativo desde el 30 de junio de 2025. Según cuentan, buena parte de la obra la hicieron ellos mismos, con sus manos. El arranque económico fue un premio de 20.000 euros del programa Entama de EDP, más el apoyo del ayuntamiento de Ribera de Arriba.
De escombrera a oficina. El terreno donde se levanta era una antigua escombrera. Ahora hay contenedores marítimos reutilizados, con energía solar, aerotermia y aislamientos de alta eficiencia para recortar la huella de carbono. Los fundadores admiten que la parte difícil fue la logística: llevar a un entorno rural unos módulos pensados para barcos y dotarlos de todos los servicios. Si el aliciente de vivir en un pueblo sin pagar la vivienda no es suficiente, La España vaciada que en realidad está concentrada puede encontrar aquí un aval extra.
Qué ofrece y cuánto cuesta. Hay puestos flexibles en una sala compartida para hasta 20 personas, despachos privados para equipos de 2 a 4, salas de reuniones para 8 y una oficina virtual por 65 euros al mes. Según la web, un día sale por 22 euros más IVA, un pack de cinco días por 65, medio mes por 110 y un mes completo por 200. Ahora mismo aplican además un 30% de descuento en las suscripciones de mes y medio mes (un 15% por ser socio nuevo y otro 15% por permanencia). El acceso es 24/7 y la tarifa incluye wifi, suministros, limpieza y cocina.
Por qué Ribera de Arriba. Los propios fundadores explican que tener la sede en un concejo rural y de tradición minera da acceso a ayudas como los fondos Leader, el ticket rural y las subvenciones MINER y MINIMINER. Por eso ofrecen domiciliar la empresa allí con la oficina virtual. Su clientela va desde autónomos hasta empresas con sede en Madrid o Berlín que quieren sacar a parte de su equipo a un entorno natural. Con los precios disparados del alquiler, la jugada tiene sentido. Y la cocina está bastante bien equipada, según describen en otra entrevista.
Un poco de salario emocional. Cowtainers también se alquila para eventos, talleres y team building de entre 22 y más de 46 asistentes. En su primer año organizaron un Afterwork Rural y prepararon un "Vermú de Productores" con miel, quesos, cerveza artesanal y música al aire libre. Se puede visitar gratis y llegar en coche son unos 13 minutos desde Mieres o unos 25 desde Gijón.
Otros coworkings locos. Un bosque con contenedores es una propuesta tirando a sensata si se mira lo que hay por el mundo. Solo hace falta mirar al país vecino para toparse con el Village Underground (en Lisboa). Es el pariente más cercano de Cowtainers, se levantó con contenedores y autobuses de dos pisos reciclados que hacen la función de oficinas, estudio de grabación, restaurante y sala de conferencias. Entre medias caben conciertos, fiestas de música electrónica y skate.
O los Replica House Studios (en Londres), como ya contábamos en Trendencias: el local ocupa una iglesia metodista victoriana de Islington, con sus vidrieras a la vista. Igual de alucinante es el coworking del Regnum Christi instalado en una casa de dos piso, en La Barca (Bogotá: tiene una capilla con misa diaria a unos pasos de los escritorios y una cesta a la entrada donde dejar intenciones de oración.
Y si esto te parece poco, en Naplab (Bangkok) hay un cowork donde se prima que se pueda dormir bien (el descanso es tan importante como el trabajo, dicen) o el CoBoat, un coworking flotante en un velero, con sitio para hasta 20 personas, clases de navegación y una ruta que va cambiando. Visto así, trabajar en un contenedor reciclado entre árboles, a un paseo de la ciudad y con parking gratis, parece algo bastante normalito.

articles.title: Filtre antireflet efficace, ce TV OLED Samsung perd 199,33 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – Le téléviseur Samsung 55S92H à 1 290,00 € (-13%)
Le téléviseur Samsung 55S92H passe sous les 1300 € chez Son-Video.com soit une baisse d'environ 13% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Avec son S92H, Samsung reprend la recette du S90F en l’améliorant sur deux points importants : un filtre antireflet beaucoup plus efficace et une dalle Oled désormais rafraîchie à 165 Hz. Un très bon millésime 2026.
Samsung 55S92H
-

- 
                            Jeux vidéo
                            
            
-

Points forts
- Contraste parfait grâce à l’Oled.
- Excellente colorimétrie en SDR et HDR.
- Filtre antireflet Samsung très efficace.
- Ni blooming ni clouding.
- Réactivité de la dalle pour le jeu vidéo.
Points faibles
- Pas de prise en charge du Dolby Vision.
- Perception du noir légèrement affectée en pièce lumineuse.

articles.title: New WinPOPBit tool bypasses Windows 11 CPU restrictions to support truly ancient PCs
articles.text:
In brief: Unlike previous releases, Windows 11 significantly limits the number of systems on which users can attempt to install the new operating system. Needless to say, some developers have recognized Microsoft's challenge and raised the stakes considerably.
A new open-source utility is bringing the latest Windows editions to places where Microsoft developers dared not go. Initially released a few weeks ago, WinPOPBit is designed to "pop" some of the most restrictive hardware requirements in newer Windows 11 versions. The project is progressing rapidly, which means even more ancient CPUs could soon become "compatible" with the latest PC operating systems.
WinPOPBit primarily targets Windows 11's requirement for CPUs with POPCNT and SSE4.2 instruction support, as well as Windows 10's NX bit requirement. Microsoft introduced the new CPU requirements with the Windows 11 24H2 update, preventing OS enthusiasts from installing the latest release on PCs still running decades-old processors.
Despite acknowledging these new "hard" CPU requirements, WinPOPBit's developers have found a way to restore compatibility. The Python tool is essentially an "experimental patcher" capable of modifying a few relevant bytes in Windows system files, allowing newer OS releases to boot and run on CPUs that date back to before Windows 7 was even a thing.
 – Bob Pony (@TheBobPony) November 7, 2026
WinPOPBit is designed to directly patch binary files that host the Windows NT kernel (ntoskrnl.exe), the system boot loaders (winload.efi and winload.exe), and several additional DLL files. The developers explain that Windows 11 24H2 and newer versions check for POPCNT and SSE4.2 CPU support but do not actually require these newer instructions for 99% of their files. Meanwhile, Windows 10 primarily requires the NX bit for its innermost, ring 0-level kernel code.
WinPOPBit has already restored Windows 11 and Windows 10 compatibility on some truly ancient x86 processors, including AMD's Athlon II and Intel's Pentium 4 "Northwood" CPU from 2002. Now, the developers are working to expand the tool's capabilities even further, bringing support to increasingly old hardware.
The latest code commits could allow Windows 10 and Windows 11 23H2 to run on AMD systems based on Socket 754, 940, and 939, as well as AM2-based CPUs from the AMD K8 family. The upcoming WinPOPBit release should also force Windows 11 to boot on the Athlon 64. You heard that right: thanks to a third-party Python script, hardware enthusiasts may soon be able to install a modern 64-bit Windows release on AMD's first 64-bit processor, released in 2003.
Additionally, WinPOPBit is expected to support patched versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11 23H2 on Intel LGA 775 systems, including those powered by Pentium 4 "Prescott" and Pentium D "Smithfield" processors. Using the tool isn't for the faint of heart, and the WinPOPBit developers clearly state that Microsoft will not provide official support for this kind of tinkering.

articles.title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
articles.text:
A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza.
Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC. The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak, supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago.
This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons.
The company has demonstrated a humanoid robot named the Phantom MK-1 and is touting an upcoming robot called the Phantom MK-2. Foundation has touted its humanoid robots for roles in warehouses and other workplaces—but has courted media coverage by claiming it is developing humanoid robots for battlefield use.
Now CNBC’s reporting based on “people with direct knowledge of the matter” indicates that insiders worry the startup could soon collapse without additional funding.
Foundation’s business claims
Eric Trump holds an equity stake in Foundation and was announced as its chief strategy advisor in March 2026, according to the Financial Times. Investment funds linked to both Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. are involved with multiple military technology companies that have received Pentagon loans and contracts worth more than $3.2 billion as of July 2026, according to The Washington Post.

articles.title: Critics raise competition, affordability concerns over Quebcor-Telus merger
articles.text:
Comments are coming out from key figures across the country following reports of a proposed merger between Quebecor and Telus.
For context, Montreal-based Quebecor, which owns the telecom brands Videotron, Fizz, and Freedom Mobile, sent Telus a proposal to purchase the company in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $19.45 per share, or $31 billion.
Quebecor initially proposed the merger in June 2026, and sent a revised proposal to the company on Nov. 9.
In a statement issued by the Canadian Government on Monday, Industry Minister Melanie Joly said that the government has “taken note” of Quebecor’s proposal to Telus, and that “the transaction will be independently and rigorously reviewed by the Competition Bureau and the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission and will follow regulatory processes under the Telecommunications Act.”
“We will not predetermine the outcomes of the reviews related to this or any other specific transaction,” Joly added in the statement.
There is also considerable doubt about the proposal. Scotiabank analyst Maher Yagi spoke to BNN Bloomberg and noted that a potential deal would face significant obstacles, including the previously mentioned CRTC, Competition Bureau, and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), as well as additional reviews or approvals that might be required “given the strategic nature of Canadian telecommunications infrastructure.”
Alongside this, Michael Phillips, the President of United Steelworkers Local 1944 (USW1944), the largest representative for Telus employees, said that it “seems doubtful whether it would get approved by [the federal government] at this point,” pointing to the federal government’s priority of “keeping the industry competitive and affordable.”
Yagi also made a similar point to BNN Bloomberg, adding that this merger would “undo the competitive structure regulators set up when they required Freedom to be divested as part of the Rogers-Shaw approval.”
Phillips also noted that his biggest worry with the deal was instability, adding that “our members at this point are tending to want stability and security at Telus after many years of industry downsizing, and this is another thing for them to wonder about.”
USW 1944 represented workers affected by Rogers’ lockout of Shaw employees and added that “we had never had a dispute in the many years that Shaw was running the operation, but we have to attribute some of the instability to the new management post-merger.” For context, USW 1494 also represented Rogers workers who went on strike in Abbotsford, BC.
Canada already has some of the most expensive phone plans in the world. We should be breaking up the telecom monopolies, not adding another.
The Competition Bureau must block this sale.
www.cbc.ca/news/busines…
— Avi Lewis (@avilewis.ca) November 16, 2026 at 1:49 PM
Federal NDP leader Avi Lewis said in a post to Bluesky that Canada already has “some of the most expensive phone plans in the world,” while adding that “we should be breaking up the telecom monopolies, not adding another.”
Phillips also noted something similar, adding that “consumers have made it clear that they are looking for choice, and they’re looking for affordability.”
Update Nov. 16, 2026, at 6:12 p.m. ET: Corrected the abbreviation for the United Steelworkers 1944.
Header image credit: Shutterstock

articles.title: AMD Completes Acquisition of World Labs
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
AMD Completes Acquisition of World Labs
AMD today announced the completion of its acquisition of World Labs, expanding its capabilities across the AI stack with a world-class model team. The acquisition brings together leading AI model researchers and AMD engineers to shape the next generation of AMD hardware, software and systems for the open AI ecosystem.
"Delivering the infrastructure that will power the next era of superintelligence requires us to optimize compute platforms and models together," said Dr. Lisa Su, chair and CEO of AMD. "We are thrilled to welcome Fei-Fei Li and the exceptional World Labs team to AMD. Their pioneering model research will help shape our future hardware, software and systems. Together, we will enable researchers and developers across the ecosystem to push the boundaries of what AI can do."World Labs develops AI models that create and simulate interactive 3D environments, as well as technology for robotic learning and simulation. Dr. Fei-Fei Li joins AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting directly to Su.
The World Labs team will continue advancing foundational model research while collaborating with AMD engineers to apply insights from emerging model capabilities to the development of future AI infrastructure for customers and developers across the open AI ecosystem.

articles.title: Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 review: A quiet and compact Wildcat
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Minisforum’s smallest and cheapest mini PC packing Intel's Wildcat Lake silicon is here. It is small, quiet, and easy to stow away, but this machine's performance is really only for light workloads.
Reasons to buy
- + Compact and light
- + Quiet
- + Low power use
- + Capable enough for home office and media consumption
- + Expandable RAM and SSD
Reasons to avoid
- - Weak performance in creator tasks
- - Only old or lightweight games and emulators are playable
- - Plastic top shell
- - Not a cheap option unless you have spare parts and go barebones
- - Single SODIMM and single M.2 slot
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Minisforum’s Intel-based M2 line includes mini PCs with powerful processors such as the Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H (with 16C/16T CPU and B390 graphics), and the Core Ultra 7 356H (16C/16T). But there are more modest systems, too. The M2 Air-304 here is the most affordable option, based around the Intel Core 3 processor 304 with its 5C/5T CPU (1x Cougar Cove P-core and 4x Darkmont LP E-cores) and an iGPU with just a single Xe3 core.
No surprise, the little brother in the pack, both in terms of physical size and computing resources, is the most affordable. It currently starts at $263 for a barebones version. However, our test sample with 16GB DDR5-5600, a 500GB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro is listed at $559 - direct. That’s an introductory price, and Minisforum’s small text threatens that our configuration will bump up to $699 at some point in the future. Such a rise would put this product offering on very shaky ground, and we see B&H Photo has already raised the price at $729.
Overall, this Mini PC was pleasant to use, though. It ran quietly and only strained in gaming and productivity benchmarks which put it under loads that casual users aren’t going to be running on such a machine.
Design of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 Mini PC
The Mini M2 Air looks stylish enough, and feels solid. Looks can be deceiving, though, and the top shell is a silver colored plastic, not a metallic alloy. Sometimes a metal shell can be used to help conduct away heat, but that seems less important with this actively cooled machine with a 15W processor. We note that there are thermal pads connecting the installed RAM and SSD to the bottom of this mini PC, which is metal.
A VESA mounting bracket is provided in the box if you prefer to hide the tiny device out of sight. It doesn’t have a remote power switch like the MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG we reviewed earlier in the year, though, so you’ll have to consider reachability. A simple LED-lit power button is on the front of the device, alongside a couple of handy ports (more on the ports later). It also has a reset / clear CMOS hole on the front, and a Kensington lock slot on the rear.
Minisforum’s component choices mean this is a particularly small and light mini PC. The official M2 Mini specs state it is 112 x 112 x 37.15mm, which is roughly 4.4 x 4.4 x 1.5-inches. That’s a volume of 0.47 liters. It weighs in at just 440 grams, which is 0.97 pounds.
The power supply isn’t built-in. There’s a surprisingly bulky 65W power brick in the box, which connects to using a detachable figure-eight cable. However, this mini PC can be powered by USB-C, too, so you could pack a far more compact multipurpose power brick if portability is important.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Specifications of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 Mini PC
| Processor | Intel Core 3 304 (5C/5T) ‘Wildcat Lake,’ up to 4.3 GHz, 15W | 
| Graphics | Intel integrated graphics, 1x Xe3 core runs at up to 2.3 GHz, supports up to 3x displays | 
| RAM | 16GB in single SODIMM slot which can fit up to a 64GB DDR5-6400 module | 
| Storage | 1x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD slot (up to 2TB), microSD card expansion | 
| Physical Ports | Front: 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2, 3.5mm audio. Rear: 1x USB4 (40Gbps, DP Alt Mode, PD), 1x USB-C 10Gbps, 1x USB 2.0, 2x HDMI 2.0, 2x RJ-45 2.5GbE LAN, DC-IN. Side: microSD card slot. | 
| Wireless | Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Dimensions | 112 × 112 × 37.15 mm (0.47 L chassis) | 
| Operating System | Windows 11; barebone model available without OS | 
| Price (as configured) | $559.00 limited-time price(16GB RAM, 500GB SSD, Windows 11 Pro) | 
Ports and Upgradeability
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
On the front of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 there are 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2 ports and a 3.5mm audio jack. Turn it to the side and you’ll see the microSD card slot. Then, around the back you have access to 1x USB4 (40Gbps, DP Alt Mode, PD), 1x USB-C 10Gbps, 1x USB 2.0, 2x HDMI 2.0, 2x RJ-45 2.5GbE LAN, and a DC-IN barrel jack.
Some might like to have at least one of the Type-C ports on the front, instead of two Type-As. But for its size the Mini M2 Air packs quite a few ports, including the very capable USB4, two HDMI ports, and two Ethernet ports. Realistically, a machine like this won’t be connected to oodles of wired peripherals, but if you found the port count lacking, USB4 allows for a capable and fast dock.
Wireless connectivity seems adequate, with an M.2 2230 card inside providing Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.4. I had no problems with either during the test period. The wireless card is socketed. It's located under the SSD, making it easy to repair or upgrade down the line.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Accessing the components inside the Minisforum Mini M2 Air is straightforward, but you need to peel off all the four rubber feet to get to four long fastening screws. When they’re removed, just flip off the metal bottom to access the M.2 slots and SODIMM. Be aware there’s some adhesive force holding this metal plate in place, due to the sticky thermal pads on the RAM and storage.
There’s just a single M.2 2280 storage slot and one SODIMM slot, both populated. That means, there’s no way to upgrade the RAM than swapping the module you already have in place. Our sample came with a 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM, but the system supports up to DDR5-6400. This only non-barebones configuration also came with a 500GB SSD in the M.2 slot.
| System | CPU | (i)GPU | Memory | Chassis | 
| GMKtec Evo-T2 | Intel Core Ultra X7 358H (16C/16T: 4P + 8E + 4 LPE), up to 4.8 GHz | Intel Arc B390 (Xe3, 12 cores, up to 2.5 GHz) | 2x 32GB LPDDR5X-8533 soldered | Dual-fan,1.72 liters | 
| MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG | Intel Core Ultra 9 386H (16C/16T: 6P + 8E + 2LPE), up to 4.9 GHz | Intel Graphics (Xe3, 4 Cores, up to 2.5 GHz) | 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm | Single fan, 0.52 liters | 
| Geekom A9 Max 2026 | AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.2 GHz | Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 3.1 GHz) | 1x 32GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm | Single fan, 0.82 liters | 
| Arctic Senza AI 370 | AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.1 GHz | Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 2.9 GHz) | 2x 16GB LPDDR5X‑8000 soldered | Passive, 4.82 liters | 
| Beelink SER10 MAX | AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.2 GHz | Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 3.1 GHz) | 2x 32GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm | Single fan, 0.81 liters | 
| Geekom IT13 Max 2026 | Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (16C/22T: 6P + 8E + 2LPE), up to 5.1 GHz | Intel Arc graphics (Xe-LPG, 8 cores, up to 2.35 GHz) | 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 Soldered | Single fan, 0.97 liters | 
| GMKtec Evo-X3 | AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T: 16x Zen 5), up to 5.1 GHz | Radeon 8060S (RDNA 3.5, 40 CUs, up to 2.9 GHz) | 2x 64GB LPDDR5X-8000 Soldered | Triple-fan, 2.69 liters | 
| Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air | Intel Core 3 processor 304 (5C/5TL 1P + 4LPE), up to 4.3 GHz | Intel Graphics (Xe3, 1 Cores, up to 2.3 GHz) | 1x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM | Single fan, 0.47 liters | 
Productivity Performance on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
We have Intel’s latest 18A silicon inside this tiny PC, but not that much of it. Our review unit came with an Intel Core 3 304 "Wildcat Lake" chip that runs up to 4.3 GHz. Previous mini PCs based on Intel 300 series mobile silicon like the previously MSI and the GMKtec Evo-T2 came with a 16C/16T CPU. However, here we have just 5C/5T, and that’s just one performance core supported by four low power efficiency (LPE) cores.
Still, single core performance continues to be important for system and app responsiveness. The proof of the pudding is in the testing, though. And while this system felt perfectly usable in Windows 11, internet browsers, and word processing — preparing and writing this review, for example — the benchmarks are somewhat tougher.
Single-Threaded
View Original
View Original

Multi-Threaded

View Original
As we expected, the single core tests show Wildcat Lake has some bite. It easily beats its AMD-based rivals in the POV Ray single core rendering tests, for example. Moreover, in tests like Cinebench 2024 single core, the Mini M2 Air might trail the pack, but not by very much. It's roughly 107 points is actually within touching distance of the 120 points scored by ‘high performance’ mini PCs like the Beelink SER10 MAX (Gorgon Point) and MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG (Panther Lake).
Multicore tests exposed obvious weaknesses of the 5C/5T CPU configuration with single-channel RAM. All the other mini PCs we’ve tested this year come with 12C/24T (AMD) or 16C/16T (Intel), so the productivity benchmarks we run which can take advantage of multithreading for demanding rendering or encoding tasks make the Minisforum here seem weak. However, it might still be acceptable for transcoding a short video or two, occasionally, as long as you aren’t in a rush. If you are coming from an older, less efficient desktop sporting something like an i7-7700K or i5-10400, this 15W Wildcat Lake chip is an improvement in both single and multicore performance.
During our demanding tests, the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 stayed cool and quiet thanks to its 15W processor and capable cooling.
Gaming and Graphics on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
For anything other than the most casual gaming or emulation of older consoles you should look at other devices. We’ve looked at Intel 300 silicon powered devices with iGPUs packing 12 Xe3 cores, and four Xe3 cores, but this just has one, and it is further hampered by sharing the single-channel system RAM.
Prepare to see some low frame rates / scores in our standard tests. I felt that some of these tests probably shouldn’t be run on this mini PC, but did it anyway, for completeness. However, some 3DMark benchmarks simply wouldn’t run, as Intel has pruned the features that work on this iGPU due to limited resources. For example, 3DMark Solar Bay doesn’t run on this system, and neither does Speed Way. Error messages about unsupported hardware pop up when you try these tests.
Steel Nomad ran, though, and the Minisforum and its solo Xe3 core achieved a score of 135. The aforementioned Evo-T2 with Intel Core Ultra X7 358H and (B390) iGPU with 12x Xe3 cores scored 1,624. That’s incredibly close to 12x faster than the Core 3 304’s ‘Intel Graphics.’ A score of 135 means Steel Nomad ran at just a little more than 1 FPS, which actually doesn’t hurt your eyes to watch as much as 10 FPS.
Using the multi-scene benchmarks built into Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Cyberpunk 2077 using our standard settings selections resulted in some unpleasant experiences. Performance of no better than 10 or 12 FPS was observed in these tests. To achieve 25 or even 30 FPS in these titles I found that reducing the game resolution to 720p and low/lowest settings would just about get there.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
So, for some actual fun on the Mini M2 Air I decided to try the latest version of the Sony PSP emulator PPSSPP and play some Wipeout Pure. I managed to run this game on my 1440p monitor with a 6x render resolution, and it achieved a nice steady 60 FPS, delivering an enjoyable futuristic racing experience. It would also therefore likely be good for retro emulation of similar era and older consoles as well as home computers.
Power, Heat, and Noise when using the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
During my day-to-day use, the Minisforum system consumed around 9W when idling on the desktop. When under the heaviest loads I threw at it, the highest system power consumption I saw was around 31W.
I didn't find it surprising that this low-power system ran cool and quiet. System tools showed that during light activities like browsing the web the CPU temperature remained in the low 30s Celsius. Playing games or benchmarking for length periods, I never saw the reported CPU temperature rise beyond the low 70s Celsius.
Minisforum’s tiny mini PC was a quiet operator at idle and under load. My measurements from about half a foot in front of the device show noise levels under 30 dBA at idle, which is very quiet and actually said to be beneath the measurement threshold of my meter. Stressing the system with simultaneous CPU and GPU loads I managed to observe just a reading of a little over 37 dBA from the system.
Software and Warranty on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
The Mini M2 Air ships with Windows 11 Pro installed in the configuration we received. I found no pre-installed bloatware. The official specs don’t mention compatibility with other OSes like Linux.
Minisforum sells this mini PC with a two-year warranty and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 configurations
Minisforum sells only two Elite Mini M2 Air-304 configurations in the U.S. There’s a barebones model, or the configuration we tested with pre-installed RAM, SSD, and OS.
At the time of writing our 16GB / 500GB / Windows 11 Pro configuration is listed by the mini PC maker at $559 but the product page says the price is normally $699. The barebone model is currently $263, discounted from $329. We don’t know when the prices might get adjusted. However, we’ve noted U.S. retailers like B&H Photo are now selling the 16GB / 500GB model at $729.
Bottom Line
Though the Mini M2 Air’s performance may lack in performance, it also probably the smallest cheapest, and least power-hungry mini PC we’ve tested all year. If these kinds of qualities are important to you, the Minisforum might be appealing.
It is admirable that this mini PC is so small but leaves RAM and storage upgrades on the table for later. Other positives are the sturdy build, despite the use of plastic for the top shell, and a good port selection considering its size. In addition to being easy to hide due to its small stature, and supplied VESA mount, you probably won’t hear it very much, either.
Of course, the performance is a weakness that can’t be ignored, especially in the context of our ever-growing tested mini PCs chart from 2026. It is great to see this latest-gen processor barebones at just over $260 direct from Minisforum. If you have a spare DDR5 SODIMM and SSD, perhaps from a laptop upgrade or wherever, this might help you get a new mini PC system up and running cheaply. However, the 16GB RAM and 500GB SSD (and Windows 11 Pro license) currently more than doubles the list price (it adds $296). That’s a bit painful.
Furthermore, if the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air ever rises to its apparent MSRP of $699, we’d definitely look elsewhere. Around this price, especially during sale periods, you can shop for mini PCs employing far more powerful previous-gen processors. One good alternative candidate might be the Geekom IT13 Max 2026 we reviewed in August at $799. Price trackers show this Core Ultra 185H machine with 24GB RAM has been available for under $600 with discount / coupon over the last few months. There are also a lot of capable older gen AMD mini PCs to ponder over at attractive prices.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Coup dur pour Audi : la très attendue berline électrique est repoussée à 2029
articles.text:
Audi en retard ? Oh, jamais de la vie ! Pour preuve, la marque avait prévu le coup en annonçant une A4 électrique il y a maintenant quatre ans, histoire de tailler des croupières à la Tesla Model 3. BMW et Mercedes avaient aussi des plans similaires dans les cartons, sans encore avancer quoi que ce soit à l’époque. Les anneaux avaient donc une belle avance. Hélas, les années sont passées sans grandes nouvelles.
Et les deux grands rivaux ont dégainé entre temps les i4, i3 et Classe C sans aucune réaction de la part d’Audi. Pire encore, il s’avère que les modèles précités sont d’indéniables réussites. Où est donc passée l’A4 électrique ? Aux oubliettes ? Non, bien heureusement, mais il faudra en revanche se montrer patient pour espérer la découvrir. D’après Autocar, la berline devrait débarquer d’ici… 2029. On voit déjà BMW et Mercedes sabrer le champagne.
Problèmes financiers et plateforme inédite : les raisons de la douche froide
Quelle est donc la raison d’un tel retard ? Audi a voulu faire les choses bien avec une plateforme inédite, la Scalable Systems, pour armer au mieux son modèle. Sauf que les problèmes financiers traversés par le groupe Volkswagen ont sérieusement contrecarré les plans de la marque. L’A4 devait être présentée en 2026, elle le sera finalement trois ans plus tard. La douche froide, en quelque sorte…
Qui dit nouvelle plateforme dit bien souvent nouveau logiciel. Et ce dernier connaît aussi d’importantes difficultés de développement. Rien d’inédit dans le groupe, car on se rappelle encore du lancement assez chaotique de l’ID.3 et de la Golf, qui avaient rencontré de gros soucis à ce sujet. Et la situation est encore plus compliquée pour Audi aujourd’hui car le nouveau logiciel est conçu étroitement avec Rivian.
Logiciel complexe avec Rivian et casse-tête technique
Des va-et-vient incessants sont donc nécessaires avec ce partenaire pour ajuster minutieusement chaque détail. Cela prend évidemment du temps. Pour optimiser le confort, Audi voulait aussi des caves à pieds plus profondes, ce qui empêche alors la création d’un plancher plat traditionnel. Les ingénieurs ont donc dû repenser la structure des batteries et des machines électriques pour satisfaire le cahier des charges.
L’auto, elle, devrait adopter une silhouette proche de l’A6 avec une ligne fuyante optimisant l’aérodynamisme, et donc l’autonomie. Nous n’avons encore aucune donnée technique, mais il est possible que le véhicule propose un rayon d’action dépassant les 700 km. Ce serait nécessaire vu que l’i3 atteint sans peine les 912 km et la Classe C touche les 760 km. Rendez-vous d’ici quelques années pour en savoir plus sur le sujet, donc !
