articles.title: Google Messages prépare une grosse mise à jour des messages vocaux
articles.text:
Continuer à lire des messages vocaux tout en quittant la conversation en cours, voici ce que proposera Google Messages à l'avenir. Cette fonctionnalité devrait faciliter la vie de nombreux utilisateurs.
Google travaille sur plusieurs changements liés aux messages vocaux dans Google Messages. Ces fonctions ne sont pas encore disponibles pour le grand public, car elles sont encore en développement. Toutefois, envoyer des messages vocaux et en écouter serait plus pratique, pour les utilisateurs qui savent faire plusieurs choses en même temps.
Une nouvelle icône et un libellé modifié
Après les potentiels jeux dans les conversations, Google améliore son application de messagerie avec des fonctionnalités pratiques. Le premier changement concerne l'interface d'enregistrement. Dans la fenêtre de conversation, le bouton des messages vocaux affiche aujourd'hui une icône en forme de forme d'onde. Elle pourrait être remplacée par une icône de microphone lors d'une prochaine mise à jour.
Dans la fenêtre d'enregistrement, le libellé « Joindre » pourrait par ailleurs devenir « Envoyer ».
Une lecture audio qui continue quoi que vous fassiez
Actuellement, lorsqu'un utilisateur passe à une autre application ou revient à l'écran d'accueil, le fichier audio se lit tout de même. Cependant, si vous revenez à la liste des conversations dans la page d'accueil de Google Messages, la lecture se stoppe net. Aucune commande de lecture n'apparaît dans le volet de notifications.
Mais une fonctionnalité change ce paramètre. En effet, avec la nouvelle mise à jour, la lecture d'un message vocal se poursuit même après un retour à la liste des conversations. Le volet de notifications affiche alors des commandes de lecture : pause, lecture, avance et retour rapides. Les boutons d'avance et de retour rapide semblent faire des sauts de cinq secondes. Des icônes pour des sauts de 10 et 30 secondes auraient également été repérées.
Les « Voice Moods » pendant l'enregistrement
Google préparerait également une évolution de la fonction « Voice Moods » existante. Pour l'instant, l'utilisateur choisit une ambiance vocale une fois l'enregistrement terminé.
Une prochaine mise à jour pourrait lui permettre de la sélectionner pendant qu'il enregistre son message.
Source : AndroidAuthority
- L'application est gratuite à télécharger.
- On peut écrire des messages dans des groupes.
- Elle s'intègre parfaitement dans l'écosystème logiciel de Google.

articles.title: Onde roda GTA 6? Confira os requisitos para console • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Onde roda GTA 6? Confira os requisitos para console
O GTA 6 está chegando aos consoles de nova geração, como PS5 e Xbox Series X/S, mas sua versão para PC deve estrear apenas em algum momento de 2027
O aguardado GTA 6 chega oficialmente aos consoles PS5 e Xbox Series X/S após 13 anos desde o último título da franquia. O novo título da Rockstar Games promete revolucionar o mundo dos games com um mapa imersivo e gráficos ultrarrealistas.
Entre os hardwares compatíveis, o PS5 Pro se destaca como a melhor opção para quem busca máxima fidelidade gráfica, fluidez e outros recursos. Já a chegada do GTA 6 no PC ainda exigirá paciência, pois a versão deve demorar mais alguns meses para sair.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra a lista de requisitos e detalhes de desempenho do GTA 6 nas plataformas disponíveis.
O GTA 6 está disponível nativamente para consoles da atual geração, como PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X/S, e em certos dispositivos via streaming. Conforme a Rockstar, o jogo terá desempenho travado em 30 quadros por segundo (fps), garantindo fluidez visual estável em todas essas plataformas.
| Plataforma | Qualidade | 
|---|---|
| PlayStation 5 | Versão nativa | 
| PlayStation 5 Pro | Versão nativa aprimorada | 
| PS Portal | Via PS Remote Play | 
| Xbox Series X | Versão nativa | 
| Xbox Series S | Versão nativa com recursos limitados | 
| Xbox One | Via Cloud Gaming | 
| PC | Versão nativa (ainda não anunciada) | 
Até o momento, a versão para PC segue sem data oficial de lançamento divulgada pela Rockstar Games. Além disso, a desenvolvedora não confirmou planos de levar o título ao console híbrido Nintendo Switch 2.
O PS5 Pro entrega a melhor qualidade visual para GTA 6 com reflexos realistas (ray tracing) e imagens mais nítidas via inteligência artificial (PSSR), embora ainda rode com 30 fps. Segundo a Rockstar Games, a família PlayStation oferece imersão superior pelos carregamentos rápidos, áudio espacial e às respostas táteis do controle DualSense.
O PS5 padrão e o Xbox Series X mantêm um nível gráfico equivalente entre as plataformas. Já o Xbox Series S vai rodar GTA 6 com cortes na resolução e nos detalhes visuais para preservar a estabilidade por conta do hardware mais limitado.
O Xbox One roda GTA 6 exclusivamente via Xbox Cloud Gaming com qualidade visual equivalente ao Xbox Series S, enquanto o antigo Xbox 360 fica de fora. Sem a necessidade da instalação local devido ao processamento nos servidores da Microsoft, é indispensável ter uma internet rápida e estável para evitar atrasos ou falhas na imagem.
Para jogar GTA 6 dessa forma, é obrigatório comprá-lo separadamente, já que ele não faz parte do catálogo padrão do Xbox Game Pass. Além da cópia do jogo, o usuário precisa de uma assinatura com tempo de nuvem incluso ou adquirir horas avulsas do serviço.
Não, o GTA 6 não roda no PlayStation 4 ou PlayStation 3, pois ele foi desenvolvido exclusivamente para a nova geração de consoles. Ou seja, não há possibilidade de comprar e instalar o jogo localmente nestes aparelhos mais antigos.
Não há especificações oficiais para GTA 6 no PC, pois o título está previsto para chegar ao computador em algum momento de 2027. O game deve estrear em lojas digitais como Steam, Epic Games e no próprio aplicativo da Rockstar.
Com base no poder dos consoles atuais, estima-se que os requisitos mínimos de GTA 6 exijam um processador (CPU) de 6 núcleos, 16 GB de memória RAM, armazenamento SSD e uma placa de vídeo (GPU) com 8 GB de memória dedicada (VRAM).
Para quem deseja aproveitar o GTA 6 com resoluções mais altas e gráficos no máximo, a máquina “perfeita” deve ter uma CPU de 8 núcleos, 32 GB de RAM, SSD NVMe ultrarrápido e GPU com 12 GB de VRAM.
O GTA 6 exige até 212 GB de armazenamento livre, embora o tamanho exato dos arquivos de instalação possa variar ligeiramente conforme o console escolhido. Confira no quadro abaixo a estimativa de espaço que você precisa reservar no SSD de cada plataforma antes do download.
| Plataforma | Quantidade de armazenamento | 
|---|---|
| PlayStation 5/PS5 Pro | Mínimo de 212 GB. | 
| Xbox Series X / Series S | Acima de 212 GB, dependendo do console. | 
Além desse volume inicial para baixar o jogo base, vale manter uma folga extra na memória interna do videogame ou computador para futuras atualizações e patches de correções.

articles.title: Sumo Logic expands AWS Observability Solution with one-click deployment and new regions - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Sumo Logic expands AWS Observability Solution with one-click deployment and new regions
Data analytics software firm Sumo Logic Inc. today released an expanded AWS Observability Solution, a monitoring package for Amazon Web Services Inc. users that can now be deployed in one click from AWS Marketplace.
Sumo Logic is pitching the update at cloud teams that would otherwise have to build their own dashboards before they can properly watch an AWS environment. Much of the company’s recent product work has gone into artificial intelligence agents that take on incident investigations.
Support for AWS regions in Zurich, Melbourne and New Zealand takes the number covered by the solution to 20. Workloads running in those three regions can now be watched with the same prebuilt alerts Sumo Logic offers elsewhere on 12 core AWS services. Lambda, DynamoDB and Application Load Balancer are among them.
Zurich has been on the company’s list since February, when Sumo Logic said its security products would come to the AWS Europe (Zurich) Region for customers bound by Switzerland’s Federal Act on Data Protection.
Anyone signing up through Quick Launch, the AWS Marketplace option behind the one-click deployment, can now do the whole thing — buying the package, setting it up and getting it deployed — without stepping outside their own AWS account. Sumo Logic says the deployments themselves are versioned, in Terraform and CloudFormation alike, which the company expects will mean less configuration drift over time.
Root Cause Agent, which Sumo Logic put into preview for operations teams on Oct. 13, is where much of the telemetry the package collects ends up. When an alert fires, the agent goes digging through the data on its own. A company blog post from the launch says every finding it turns up can be rerun as a search in one click.
The agent belongs to Dojo AI, the agentic AI platform Sumo Logic introduced for security operations teams in September 2025. Root Cause Agent carries that investigative work over into observability. Alongside it in October came new Dojo AI packages that bill all of a customer’s agent use, with Mobot, the SOC Analyst Agent and Root Cause Agent included, against one monthly credit pool.
“AI agents are only as good as the telemetry and context provided to them,” said Keith Kuchler, chief product and technology officer at Sumo Logic. Kuchler added that teams on AWS shouldn’t have to keep “working around regions their tools can’t reach.”
Back in September, Sumo Logic gave customers a way to trim telemetry before ingestion when it expanded its Data Pipelines service. The company, taken private by Francisco Partners in 2023 for $1.7 billion, will show the AWS package at AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas Nov. 30-Dec. 4.
Through Sumo Logic’s listings in AWS Marketplace, version 3.0.0 of the solution is available now to customers that monitor AWS infrastructure.

articles.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
articles.text:
A hidden defect in Microsoft’s cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company’s history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft’s report lists the incident’s final status as “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.”
Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.
The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report, and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates.
A perfect storm
Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout.
The second factor was server load. Microsoft said that “Traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug.” The company keeps two independent gateway systems in place to access Microsoft 365 for resilience. If one system encounters trouble and users can’t get through the front door, the other is opened to keep traffic flowing. According to the report, about 15 hours prior to the outage, traffic from Teams was shifted from the alternate gateway to the primary, where Exchange Online access is maintained. The switchover was a standard fail-safe, but it left the gateway handling more traffic, with a different mix of requests than before. As requests continued to pile up, affected servers exhausted their capacity and refused new connection requests.

articles.title: Auch ohne Face-ID-Technik: iPhone Duo bekommt Gesichtserkennung per Software-Update
articles.text:
Auch ohne Face-ID-Technik: iPhone Duo bekommt Gesichtserkennung
Mit einem Startpreis von 2.300 Euro ist das iPhone Duo Apples mit Abstand teuerstes Smartphone. Trotzdem bekommt man nicht in jedem Bereich die besten Komponenten. Im Vergleich zu den Pro-Modellen muss man Abstriche bei der Kamera machen, mit Blick auf alle anderen iPhones zudem bei der Entsperrmethode. Während selbst das günstige iPhone 17e mit der Gesichtserkennung Face-ID ausgestattet ist, muss man sich am teuren Duo per Fingerabdruck authentifizieren.
Laut Apple hat das den Vorteil, dass man das iPhone unabhängig davon, ob es geöffnet oder geschlossen ist, auf dieselbe Weise entsperren kann. Eine Erklärung, warum das Unternehmen auf die Face-ID-Technik verzichtet hat, gibt es nicht. Möglicherweise sind Platzprobleme im kompakten Gehäuse die Ursache. Trotzdem will Apple das iPhone Duo mit iOS 27.3 nun um eine Gesichtserkennung erweitern, wie unter anderem Wired berichtet.
iPhone Duo bekommt Gesichtserkennung ohne Face ID
Zu finden ist die neue Funktion zunächst in der zweiten Entwickler-Beta von iOS 27.3 in den Einstellungen für „Touch ID & Code“. Laut 9t05Mac ist der Einrichtungsprozess ähnlich gestaltet wie jener von Face-ID. Nutzer:innen müssen dafür lediglich einmal kurz nach rechts, links, oben und unten schauen. Wired zufolge bedient sich Apple hier der Technologie, die auch im Smarthome-Display Homeview zum Einsatz kommt, um bis zu sechs Nutzer:innen zu identifizieren. Dabei werden allerdings auch weitere Faktoren wie die Stimmen berücksichtigt. Das System sei allerdings nicht so umfassend wie Face-ID und könnte anfälliger für Angriffe sein.
Wohl auch deswegen beschränkt Apple, was man mit der neuen Entsperrmethode machen kann. Während ihr Face-ID unter anderem nutzen könnt, um Zahlungen via Apple Pay zu autorisieren („Pay with your Face“) oder die Passwort-App freizuschalten, könnt ihr mit der Gesichtserkennung auf dem Duo lediglich das iPhone entsperren. Für alles Weitere ist nach wie vor der Fingerabdruck oder aber die Eingabe des Display-Codes nötig. Außerdem müsst ihr die Funktion alle 45 Minuten erneut per Fingerabdruck oder Code-Eingabe aktivieren. Und: Mit der „Facetime“-Kamera des inneren Displays funktioniert die Lösung nicht. Das Entsperren per Gesichtserkennung ist im aufgefalteten Modus also nicht möglich.
iPhone Duo sperrt sich beim Schließen
Neben der neuen Entsperrmethode kommt das praktische Gegenteil hinzu: Das Duo lässt sich so einstellen, dass es sich sperrt, wenn man es zuklappt. Bislang wird durch den Vorgang der äußere Bildschirm aktiviert. Nutzer:innen müssen proaktiv auf die Seitentaste drücken, um das iPhone zu sperren.
Wann genau das Update auf iOS 27.3 erscheint, ist bislang nicht bekannt. Apple hatte aber den Start der neuen Health-App für Ende 2026 versprochen. Sie ist (bislang) Teil von iOS 27.3.

articles.title: Instagram fine-tunes recommendation systems in India to curb sexually suggestive, violent content
articles.text:
Instagram fine-tunes recommendation systems in India to curb sexually suggestive, violent content
The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself
Meta Platforms said on Tuesday that it has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced artificial intelligence models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.
The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself, the company said.
The announcement comes against the backdrop of increased regulatory scrutiny of social media algorithms in India. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, in an October 10 advisory, asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems to ensure potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not disproportionately amplified.
Meta, however, did not say if the changes were linked to the government advisory.
The changes have helped halve the frequency with which users report recommended content compared with a year ago, Meta said in a post on its website.
The platform said it had strengthened default protections over the past year, tailoring its systems to content that users in India have said they do not want to see. The measures apply to recommendations across Reels, Explore and Feed, where Instagram surfaces content from accounts users do not already follow.
As part of the upgrades, Instagram is using more capable AI models to assess content directly against its Recommendations Guidelines, enabling its systems to detect and limit potentially objectionable material proactively rather than waiting for users to report or hide it.
"Today, our systems keep more of this content out of recommendations, including sexually suggestive content and content that depicts violence," Meta said.
The company said the improvements had enabled it to proactively reduce the amount of content in India that does not meet its recommendation standards. It did not disclose the absolute volume of content affected, the proportion of recommendations filtered or the methodology used to calculate the decline in user reports.
Instagram's recommendation standards are distinct from its Community Standards, which govern content prohibited on the platform. Material that violates Community Standards is removed, while content that may be objectionable, sensitive or low-quality but does not breach those rules can remain accessible without being recommended to a wider audience. Content unlawful in a particular country is restricted there, the company said.
Recommendations determine how users discover content beyond accounts they actively follow, giving the platform's algorithms considerable influence over what appears in their feeds and is amplified across the service.
Alongside platform-wide recommendation filters, Instagram offers users controls to customise the content they see and manage interactions on the platform.
Its Sensitive Content Control allows users to opt for less sensitive material across Search, Reels, Explore, suggested accounts and in-Feed recommendations. Instagram said its systems in India already exclude the most mature content from recommendations, with the setting allowing users to further limit exposure to other sensitive material.
Users can also choose to see less political content recommended from accounts they do not follow, flag posts through the "Not Interested" option and filter selected words, phrases and emojis from comments and message requests using the Hidden Words feature. Its blocking function prevents specific accounts from finding profiles, viewing posts or sending messages, including through new accounts they may create.
Teenagers receive additional age-appropriate protections through Instagram's Teen Accounts, introduced in India last year. These accounts automatically place younger users in a 13-plus content setting governed by the platform's age-appropriate content guidelines.
The changes come amid growing scrutiny of social media platforms over online safety, algorithm-driven content distribution and the exposure of younger users to potentially harmful material.
Meta said user feedback, including when people hide posts or select "Not Interested", also informs its recommendation systems and helps identify content audiences do not want surfaced to them.
The company said it would continue to refine its detection systems as user behaviour and technology evolve, with feedback from users in India guiding further changes.

articles.title: Cómo crear imágenes de los Saja Boys de Las Guerreras K-pop como personajes de Phineas y Ferb
articles.text:
Los Saja Boys, la banda rival de Las Guerreras K-pop, pueden adaptarse a una estética de animación televisiva similar a la de Phineas y Ferb con herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA).
La clave consiste en describir qué elementos deben conservar los personajes y cuáles deben cambiar para llevarlos a otro universo gráfico.
Elegir bien las imágenes de referencia, usar una plataforma de generación, redactar un prompt detallado, revisar los errores y preparar una versión para colorear permite obtener un resultado que combine los dos universos.
Qué imágenes se deben descargar antes de empezar
El primer paso es reunir imágenes oficiales o capturas nítidas de los Saja Boys. Conviene buscar retratos individuales y una imagen grupal para identificar el peinado, el color de cabello, las prendas, los accesorios y la expresión habitual de cada integrante. Esto ayuda a que la herramienta diferencie a los personajes y evite mezclar sus rasgos.
Asimismo, se necesita una referencia visual del tipo de caricatura que se busca. En este caso, se pueden tomar como guía las formas simples, los contornos negros, los colores planos, las expresiones marcadas y los paisajes suburbanos que suelen asociarse con Phineas y Ferb.
Cuál herramienta sirve para generar la ilustración
Con las referencias seleccionadas, el siguiente paso es abrir una aplicación de generación de imágenes, como Gemini, y adjuntar los archivos en la conversación.
La plataforma de Google puede tomar esos materiales como orientación para conservar la cantidad de integrantes, los tonos principales del vestuario y algunos rasgos reconocibles del grupo.
Antes de pedir la ilustración, es clave decidir la orientación. Un formato horizontal ofrece espacio para mostrar a los cinco personajes en una misma escena, mientras que uno vertical puede servir para un retrato o una imagen centrada en uno de ellos. Se debe definir si la imagen será a color, en blanco y negro o si tendrá un fondo detallado.
Cómo redactar un prompt que dé instrucciones claras a la IA
Un prompt funciona mejor cuando organiza la información en bloques. Primero debe indicar quiénes aparecerán y cuántos serán. Luego puede describir la pose, el vestuario, el escenario y el tipo de dibujo. La precisión es importante para evitar que la aplicación agregue personajes, cambie posiciones o modifique atributos centrales.
Una opción de prompt es: “Crear una ilustración original de cinco integrantes inspirados en los Saja Boys de Las Guerreras K-pop, con una estética de animación 2D similar a Phineas y Ferb. Deben estar de pie en una calle residencial, con casas, árboles y cielo azul. Usar líneas negras definidas, colores planos, proporciones estilizadas y expresiones juveniles. Cada personaje debe tener un peinado y una ropa diferente”.
El pedido puede sumar detalles concretos, como la ubicación de cada integrante dentro de la escena, una paleta de colores o determinados gestos. Por ejemplo, se puede pedir que uno salude, otro cruce los brazos y otro adopte una pose pensativa.
Cómo generar una lámina para colorear
Una vez obtenida una versión a color, la misma composición puede convertirse en una lámina para colorear. Para lograrlo, hay que pedir una segunda versión con una instrucción específica: “Transformar esta imagen en una página para colorear, con fondo blanco, contornos negros uniformes, sin colores, sombras, degradados ni texturas”.
El resultado debe conservar los rasgos principales de los personajes, aunque conviene simplificar algunos elementos del fondo. Las áreas amplias en la ropa, el cielo, la calle o las fachadas facilitan el uso de lápices, fibras y marcadores.
Qué hacer luego de que el resultado sea el esperado
Después de seleccionar la versión definitiva, hay que descargarla en la mayor resolución disponible. El formato PNG es el adecuado para conservar contornos definidos y colores planos. Si se quiere imprimir la lámina, puede guardarse una copia en PDF para evitar cambios de tamaño al enviarla o abrirla desde otro dispositivo.
Antes de cerrar el proceso, es clave comprobar que los personajes no queden cortados por los bordes, que no haya textos agregados y que el fondo mantenga la coherencia con el estilo elegido.

Una de ellas es Lidl que, con su Black Week, tiene con descuento parte de su popular catálogo. Y entre sus chollos más interesantes destaca el protagonizado por este cubo de enchufes con conector de pared plano, rebajado a 7,99 euros.
SUDEERY Enchufe 6 en 1 Cubo con USB C
No es fácil encontrar este buen precio en esta clase de dispositivos. Pero si buscamos una alternativa de Amazon a este de Lidl, por aprovechar la suscripción Prime (con 30 días gratis para nuevas altas) y los envíos gratuitos, por 9,52 euros encontramos esta regleta alargada con conector plano. O también con conector plano, este otro cubo por 24,99 euros. Todas ellas (la de Lidl y las de Amazon), unas excelentes opciones de compra que solucionan un problema bastante habitual en casa.
Con cuatro tomas de enchufe y tres puertos USB
Dependiendo de la distribución del mobiliario que tengamos en casa, es muy común que muchos enchufes de pared queden bloqueados e inaccesibles tras muebles y sofás. Lo que, en hogares donde no tenemos demasiados de estos a mano, complica aún más conectar electrodomésticos o cargar dispositivos.

En el caso del cubo de Lidl, son cuatro los enchufes que conseguimos, además de tres puertos USB (dos USB A y uno tipo C). En total, siete tomas a cambio de una (la de pared). A tener en cuenta que no indica su potencia, pero lo habitual en este tipo de dispositivos es que se alcance un máximo de 3.680 W. articles.title: This Kickstarter speaker plays Game Boy soundtracks straight from the cartridge
articles.text:
The big picture: A top-tier soundtrack is arguably just as important as gameplay mechanics and storyline when it comes to creating a great game. Unfortunately, there isn't a wealth of quick and easy options if you want to revisit your favorite tunes without having to actually play a game. A promising new piece of hardware, however, aims to make things a bit more accessible.
YouTube and other streaming platforms can scratch the itch for popular works, but even then you're going to run into copyright issues and similar hurdles when trying to build a playlist. Obscure tracks might not exist on any streaming service. That's where the Retro Song Bird swoops in.
This plug-and-play speaker allows you to play soundtracks from classic games without the fuss. The device supports Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges, and is straightforward enough – simply insert a cart into the speaker, and the game's soundtrack starts playing.
A Kickstarter campaign for the Retro Song Bird notes support for more than 1,900 games. Physical buttons on the speaker enable full playback control, while a stereo out plug lets you play audio on another device like a home theater system or a soundbar. There's even the option to back up ROMs, restore save files, and export audio as a WAV file.
Interested parties can back the project over on Kickstarter. A pledge of $79 is all that is needed to ensure you'll be among the first to bring a Retro Song Bird home although as with any such campaign, there are no guarantees. Should everything go according to plan, the first wave of speakers is expected to ship in April 2027.
The Retro Song Bird is an interesting concept and one that could expand to other platforms should it prove popular enough. As of writing, more than 420 backers have collectively contributed north of $45,000 to the project – well above its modest $15,000 goal.

articles.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview cut AMD MI355X onboarding from up to 12 months to around three days
articles.text:
Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat
If AI can write the low-level code that ties models to Nvidia, CUDA matters less.
Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding.
Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.
Anthropic's claim that the job used to take six to 12 months comes from past work, from its “historical experience bringing up new accelerators using traditional engineering approaches,” where tailoring the code to each hardware platform was a challenge. Removing that onboarding barrier could reduce things to a purchase decision, and Anthropic started working with AMD GPUs for the first time this year, with an agreement for up to 2 gigawatts now in place.
CUDA, Nvidia’s programming platform, is very mature at nearly two decades old. AMD has an equivalent, ROCm, with HIP as its programming layer. Code written for CUDA has to be transformed to work there, and AMD even built a tool called HIPify for the process. There is still a conversion cost to switching, and AMD’s vice president of AI software, Anush Elangovan, told EE Times in April that “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in.”
AMD has been making the argument that AI can write this type of code since August of last year, presenting a research agent that fell short of human experts at the time. In September of that year, AMD CEO Lisa Su said on the Possible podcast that much of AI software is written in CUDA, which needs to be “translated to AMD,” and “a ton of that can now be done in software.”
Moving forward to July earlier this year, AMD’s senior vice president of AI, Vamsi Boppana, said its engineers were using AI models to generate GPU kernels, and Su said that when she asked whether her team was helping the Anthropic engineer working on the MI355X, she was told they didn’t need any help. Boppana said that in some cases, the resulting kernels were even “better than the most manually tuned versions.” Under its July agreement with Anthropic, AMD is also using Claude to optimize workloads for its Instinct GPUs and to speed up ROCm development.
At AMD’s Advancing AI event in July, OpenAI’s Philippe Tillet said that once OpenAI got its Helios racks, a single engineer confirmed everything worked within a few days, and that “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers.” Before the event, AMD’s Andrew Dieckman, corporate vice president and general manager of the company’s data center GPU business, told reporters that he has had practically zero conversations with AMD’s customers about CUDA.
| Date | Who | What they said or showed | Where | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug. 1, 2025 | AMD researchers | Published GEAK, an AI agent that writes GPU kernels; against 30 expert-written kernels it got 19 right, at 0.92 times the experts’ speed on average | AMD’s ROCm blog | 
| Sept. 24, 2025 | Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO | Asked about AI coding tools, said much of the code written for CUDA can now be translated to AMD in software: “We’re using software to significantly optimize our customers’ code so that they can run on AMD” | Possible podcast | 
| April 1, 2026 | Anush Elangovan, AMD vice president of AI software | Compared Claude with HIPify, AMD’s tool for converting CUDA code: “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in” | EE Times interview | 
| April 15, 2026 | Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO | “We use a ton of AI to create the kernels that we have”; “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” | Dwarkesh Patel interview | 
| July 23, 2026 | Andrew Dieckman, AMD corporate vice president and general manager, data center GPU business | “I have almost zero conversations with our customers about CUDA at this point in time” | PC Gamer, from a pre-event AMD briefing | 
| July 23, 2026 | Vamsi Boppana, AMD senior vice president of AI | AI-assisted GPU programming will “remove any remaining barriers to broad adoption” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| July 23, 2026 | Philippe Tillet, OpenAI | “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| July 23, 2026 | Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | One engineer asked Claude to bring up an MI355X rack and left it running “over the weekend” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| Nov. 10, 2026 | Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | Mythos “got Claude running on AMD in just three days with basically no human intervention”; the slide footnote limits the three days to prompt processing for one model | Anthropic’s IPO roadshow video | 
Until this week, though, all of this came from AMD or its stage, not from Anthropic to its own investors. Anthropic buys the chips rather than selling them, and it’s heading into its IPO next week, so its multi-chip approach — now with at least some numbers to back it up — carries more weight than a chipmaker’s claims. Its prospectus says it in writing, too, though without a number: “We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took.”
| Where Anthropic said it | Who did the work | How long | What it covered | What it replaced | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AMD’s Advancing AI keynote, July 23 | One engineer and Claude | Not stated; left running “over the weekend” | Its “leading model” on an MI355X rack, with performance climbing | What it called “a big effort” | 
| IPO roadshow video, narration, Nov. 10 | Mythos, with “basically no human intervention” | Three days (“in just three days”) | Getting “Claude running on AMD”; Claude “ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels” | Work that “took dozens of engineers months” | 
| IPO roadshow video, slide footnote, Nov. 10 | Claude Mythos Preview | About three days (“~3 day timeline”) | Bringing up “prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs at a useful level of performance” | Six to 12 months (“~6-12-month estimate”), from “historical experience bringing up new accelerators” | 
| Prospectus (S-1/A No. 2), Nov. 10 | Its engineering teams, “leveraging Claude” | No figure; “more quickly” | Bringing “new chip platforms into production”; no chip named | What it calls “intense engineering effort over many months” | 
The prompt processing (prefill) part of the workload is the step where a model reads and processes what it’s been given before it starts replying, and Anthropic hasn’t said whether the replying step (decode) was included as well. Anthropic’s chart, with its axis labeled “Time to onboard new silicon,” shows both lines reaching the same “~100%” mark without saying 100% of what. The company also hasn’t said how fast the model ran on AMD’s GPUs versus Nvidia’s, and that’s the comparison we want to see to show whether AMD’s chips, running AI-written code, can match Nvidia silicon.
On the other hand, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in an April interview with Dwarkesh Patel that Nvidia already uses AI on its own kernels and knows its chips best — “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” — and can get the most out of them. Asked why labs like Anthropic use other accelerators, he called Anthropic “a unique instance, not a trend.” Nvidia and AMD, among seven companies, are buying $26.0 billion of Anthropic’s stock at the IPO price, so Nvidia is investing in the very company Huang called the exception.
In late July, SemiAnalysis published an article, “Can AMD break the CUDA Moat?,” which essentially said that software creation is not the same moat it was even a year ago. That said, the catch for AMD is that with agentic coding, “each agent requires GPUs to test their code against,” which means that the AI writing the code still needs the hardware. It has found a constant lack of GPUs inside AMD for this type of development, which has held AMD back and may be a new bottleneck.
That leaves CUDA’s moat somewhere in between. Getting a model running on a new chip, once the expensive part, appears to be getting cheaper, and better AI may wear down Nvidia’s claim that it knows its hardware best. As for Anthropic’s fungible pool, the chips in it aren’t fully interchangeable — Google’s TPUs are increasingly specialized, for example — and getting the most out of any of them still takes the hardware to test on. The moat is narrowing, but is not gone.
Anthropic’s first AMD MI450 chips, in Helios racks, are expected in the first half of 2027. That’s a new generation and an opportunity to see if the three-day bring-up can be repeated. Anthropic’s IPO comes sooner, after which it will report as a public company.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: TSMC confirms cyberattack and data breach — chip giant says personal employee data has been leaked online
articles.text:
TSMC confirms cyberattack and data breach — chip giant says personal employee data has been leaked online
Threat actor offered a sample of stolen TSMC data online
- TSMC confirmed employee data was exposed through a third-party cloud provider rather than its own systems
- Stolen records reportedly include employee personal and banking information, with around 46,000 records offered for sale
- Company is notifying affected personnel and investigating the breach alongside authorities and security experts
TSMC, the world’s largest semiconductor manufacturer, has confirmed suffering a cyberattack and losing sensitive files after a threat actor offered a large database for sale on the dark web.
This comes after a threat actor with the alias “SmithBianl” recently posted a new thread on an underground forum offering a text file with 499 rows of data they claim was nabbed from TSMC. The text file, they claim, provides a sample of a much larger dataset they owned, which contains 46,000 employee records and weighs almost 7GB.
They also said the stolen archive contains TSMC employees’ national ID numbers, addresses, contact details, and banking information, and are asking 3 BTC in exchange (just below $200,000 at current prices). They also said that they would leak the entire archive if a buyer doesn’t step forward by November 15 2026 - a deadline which has now expired.
Third-party cloud service provider struck
Following the leak, the company’s Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Wendell Huang, issued a short statement confirming that the company was not breached and that the stolen files were hosted on a third party:
“TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization,” the announcement read.
“Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised. This information has been verified to match data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider, but is unrelated to the company’s operations or customer-related data.”
Huang would not say which third-party cloud provider that was, and the company is currently not responding to media inquiries. Therefore, we also don’t know how that company was breached, and if it hosted - and lost - data belonging to other companies, as well.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
We also don’t know exactly how many people had their data exposed in this incident. 46,000 employee records doesn’t necessarily mean 46,000 people, since victims lost different records such as names and banking information.
Some of them might be TSMC staff, given the curious choice of words in Huang’s letter.
“We have been informing impacted personnel and are providing them with necessary support,” he said. “TSMC has engaged with both the cloud service vendor, the relevant investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to jointly ascertain the facts and take necessary actions. We remain firmly committed to protecting employee privacy and safeguarding data security.”
Not TSMC's first rodeo
TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to give it its full name, is the world’s largest contract chipmaker, building some of the most advanced semiconductors on the planet to power smartphones and computers, data centers and AI systems, cars and smart home devices, with the likes of Apple, Nvidia and AMD among its clients.
Its importance to the global economy is enormous, as much of the world's advanced semiconductor supply depends on its manufacturing capabilities. At the end of 2025, it reportedly employed more than 90,000 people and generated around $122.4 billion in revenue (up by more than a third compared to the year before). It also reported approximately $55.2 billion in net profit, making it one of the most financially successful companies in the semiconductor industry.
This is not TSMC’s first data breach - it has had multiple incidents over the years. In 2018, a malware infection spread across several manufacturing facilities, disrupting production and causing an estimated $85 million losses.
Three years ago, the LockBit ransomware gang claimed to have stolen data from the company and demanded $70 million, but as it turned out, the data originated from a supplier called Kinmax Technology.

articles.title: Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.
Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.
Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”
In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the new report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes attackers may find it more efficient to point LLMs at n-day vulnerabilities than to hunt for zero-days.
How quickly the gap between disclosure and a working exploit can close shows in the case of two flaws in print management servers from PaperCut Software Pty Ltd., chained together and exploited as zero-days in late August. Security researchers and Huntress Labs Inc. used large language models to generate working exploits within a day of disclosure.
A campaign tracked by GreyNoise Intelligence Inc. four days after disclosure is believed to have relied on LLMs to build its exploits before it hit hundreds of organizations. One foothold in that campaign reached domain administrator within minutes, GreyNoise found.
Elsewhere, open-source agentic penetration testing frameworks are being used to automate discrete steps of live intrusions. During one intrusion against the U.S. aerospace sector, a threat actor was observed using the multi-agent framework CAIRN.
Another actor ran a customized platform built on PentAGI between late August and early October to scan a wide range of organizations in Asia for vulnerabilities. For now, the noisy forensic trail left by unrestricted autonomous execution is said to make the frameworks easier to detect.
According to GTIG, influence operations now use models for far more than writing posts. Using cloud phone farms, a turnkey platform that one commercial contractor was building with help from the Gemini API is designed to run more than 100,000 social media accounts. To make generated photos pass as smartphone shots, prompts behind a separate platform, which targeted political sentiment across Europe and the Middle East, are said to have called for deliberate camera flaws.
Among government-backed actors, photos on the fake recruiter profiles that a suspected North Korean group tracked as UNC6836 used to approach cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe were found to carry Google’s SynthID watermarks. By way of altered .claude/settings.json files in internal code repositories, the group later rigged each launch of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code to download its SOMBERMEME backdoor.
Google said it disabled the accounts and assets tied to the Gemini misuse it found. Google DeepMind has also used the findings to strengthen its classifiers.

articles.title: Google Maps change radicalement : Gemini peut organiser vos vacances et prendre vos rendez-vous
articles.text:
Google Maps vient d’être enrichi d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité baptisée « Demander à Maps ». Il serait question de « la plus grande mise à jour de Google Maps depuis plus de dix ans », selon Google. Le principe est simple : Gemini est intégré à Google Maps pour vous aider à planifier vos vacances, réserver vos plats ou encore prendre des rendez-vous à votre place. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
Gemini se transforme en guide de voyage
La fonctionnalité « Demander à Maps » se présente sous la forme d’une fenêtre conversationnelle disponible aussi bien sur le web que sur l’application Google Maps. Google précise que cette fonctionnalité est basée sur les données de plus de 300 millions de lieux et sur les avis de plus de 500 millions de contributeurs.
À travers la fonctionnalité « Demander à Maps », l’utilisateur peut par exemple demander à Gemini d’établir un itinéraire de vacances sur plusieurs jours. Il pourra par ailleurs bénéficier de la section « À savoir avant de partir » qui donne des conseils pratiques, des informations en temps réel sur la météo, des informations sur le stationnement à chaque étape ou encore des indications sur les péages. Il peut par ailleurs poser toutes sortes de questions, comme « Où est-ce que je peux recharger mon téléphone au plus vite ? », « Trouve-moi un court de tennis public éclairé pour jouer ce soir » ou encore « Conseille-moi des événements à proximité ». Gemini peut par ailleurs comparer des hôtels.
Bien entendu, il n’est pas nécessaire d’être en voyage pour utiliser « Demander à Maps ». L’utilisateur peut poser n’importe quelle question concernant son environnement direct.
Gemini peut prendre des rendez-vous et réserver des plats à votre place
Gemini intégré à Google Maps ne se limite pas à répondre à des questions et à donner des indications : l’assistant IA est aussi capable d’effectuer des actions. Google explique qu’un utilisateur peut par exemple demander à l’application de rechercher des restaurants correspondant à ses envies et de préparer une commande à emporter en ajoutant automatiquement les plats au panier. L’utilisateur n’aurait qu’à fournir certaines indications et à valider le panier final. De son côté, l’IA tiendrait compte lors de ses recherches des adresses enregistrées par l’utilisateur et de ses besoins alimentaires spécifiques. Cette fonctionnalité sera prochainement disponible via Uber Eats.
Gemini serait même capable de prendre des rendez-vous à votre place. Ainsi, si vous demandez à Gemini « Trouvez-moi un rendez-vous pour une manucure à 16 h près de chez moi », l’IA se chargera de trouver une place pour 16 h dans un centre situé près de chez vous.
Gemini intégré dans Google Maps sera aussi capable de répondre à des questions par rapport à vos listes. Ainsi, si vous lui demandez « Parmi mes adresses enregistrées, lesquelles ont une table pour 5 dans 30 minutes ? », l’assistant IA devrait vous fournir les adresses correspondant à votre requête. À noter toutefois que Google ne précise pas comment Gemini entre en contact avec les professionnels, les restaurants et les magasins. Enfin, précisons qu’il sera possible de connecter la fonctionnalité « Demander à Maps » à Gmail, afin que Gemini tienne compte de vos rendez-vous et réservations en ligne.
La fonctionnalité « Demander à Maps » est disponible dès maintenant en France. Par contre, la section « À savoir avant de partir » et les réservations de plats et de rendez-vous seront déployées prochainement.

L'aspirateur robot Mova P70 Pro Ultra passe sous les 500 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com soit une baisse d'environ 11% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
L'aspirateur-robot Mova P70 Pro Ultra multiplie les technologies pour laisser nos sols immaculés. Et grâce à un système de serpillières relevables, il promet de s'adapter automatiquement à chaque type de sol qu'il est susceptible de rencontrer sur son passage.

articles.title: One UI 9.5 se précise, Samsung intègrerait un agent IA pour résumer votre journée
articles.text:
Un bout de code laisse entendre que Samsung va enrichir son OS avec la fonctionnalité Now Brief dans One UI 9.5. Laquelle proposerait un résumé quotidien des messages et des mails, classés par catégorie.
Samsung semble travailler sur une fonction baptisée « Daily Brief », qui prendrait place dans Now Brief, son outil de résumé des événements de la journée. C'est ce que révèle l'analyse du code par nos confrères d'Android Authority. Ces éléments proviennent d'un code en cours de développement et n'indiquent pas de manière sûre que la fonction sera déployée sur les smartphones du fabricant.
Une fonction liée à Galaxy Claw
Le Daily Brief serait l'une des fonctions d'IA attendues de One UI 9.5. Nos confrères avaient déjà repéré une fonction nommée « Galaxy Claw », qui pourrait servir de base à des fonctions d'IA dites « agentiques » sur les appareils Galaxy. Cet outil prendrait en charge de nombreuses tâches, dans les applications système comme dans des applications répandues telles que Gmail et Google Messages.
Ces fonctions reposeraient sur un module nommé Personal Agent Core, qui permet aux applications du système d'échanger des informations et d'exécuter diverses tâches. C'est en examinant le code de ce module que le Daily Brief a été repéré.
Des notifications transformées en cartes
D'après le code, le Daily Brief récupérerait les informations dans les notifications d'applications tierces pour les présenter sous forme de cartes, plus faciles à explorer. Les sources identifiées pour l'instant sont : WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, KakaoTalk et les SMS/RCS. La fonction irait aussi chercher des informations utiles dans les mails.
Les données seraient classées en trois catégories, d'après les chaînes de texte trouvées dans le code :
- Finance et paiements
- Réservations et rendez-vous
- E-mails professionnels
Le nom de la fonction laisse supposer qu'elle délivrera son résumé chaque jour à une heure déterminée, vraisemblablement en début de journée. Les instructions destinées aux développeurs mentionnent d'ailleurs une option « MORNING » dans l'outil de test.
Un équivalent existe sur les Google Pixel
Le Daily Brief de Samsung porte le même nom qu'une fonction déjà présente sur les téléphones Google Pixel, fonctionnant à l'aide de Gemini.
Cette fonctionnalité organise les informations importantes issues des applications de messagerie et des événements de Google Calendar, en donnant la priorité à ceux qui demandent une attention immédiate. La fonctionnalité de Samsung devrait fonctionner de manière similaire.
Un accès probablement payant
Mais voilà, tout n'est pas gratuit dans la vie, et Samsung pourrait bien facturer ce système d'intelligence artificielle. En effet, toujours selon nos confrères, les fonctions reposant sur Galaxy Claw seraient probablement réservées à une offre payante de Galaxy AI.
Samsung n'a pour l'instant rien annoncé à ce sujet, et le contenu comme la disponibilité du Daily Brief pourraient évoluer d'ici une éventuelle sortie. L'autre question concerne la disponibilité en Europe, pour l'instant inconnue également.
Source : AndroidAuthority

articles.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
articles.text:
One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built.
A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward.
Finding the centers
The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts.
In a way, that makes this a very conservative estimate, since 272 facilities believed to be large data centers were left out. But if you’re interested in AI data centers, specifically, it’s also true that some of the facilities included may not fall in that category.
That fact also introduces some uncertainty in the actual power usage of these data centers. Relying on other research, they use a range—some conventional data centers run at an average of about 48 percent of capacity, while AI training loads have been running higher, at around 70 percent.
Putting that together, the total power usage for the year by these 403 data centers was estimated at 68 to 99 terawatt-hours. That amounts to 1.5 to 2.2 percent of total US electricity use, on par with the total used by Wisconsin or Indiana.

articles.title: Lakshmi Venu seeks formal partition of TVS Venu Srinivasan family assets
articles.text:
Lakshmi Venu seeks formal partition of TVS Venu Srinivasan family assets
In a partition notice to her father, she has called upon him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and give effect to a fair and lawful partition.
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of a branch of the TVS family.
In a partition notice to her father, she has called upon him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and give effect to a fair and lawful partition.
Lakshmi, in her statement on Monday, asserted that, under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, she is entitled to her rightful share in the joint family property and has an independent right to seek its partition.
Her claim is also founded on the equal rights of daughters recognised under Section 6 of the Act.
Stating that the assets for which she seeks partition include the family interests held through the VS Trust and other holding vehicles and structures, she said, "These encompass the businesses and assets allotted to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement, including interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton".
Lakshmi maintained that the larger TVS family arrangement did not constitute a partition within the Venu Srinivasan family. No settlement or partition of the assets within her immediate family was ever initiated, let alone concluded.
In her view, management does not confer exclusive ownership or extinguish lawful rights of other family members.
Lakshmi contended that she is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property and alleged that the concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her brother was to the exclusion of her own lawful rights.
She regarded these actions not only as a breach of law but also as a breach of trust."Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India. The rights of daughters to joint family property cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements", she added.
Reiterating her preference for an amicable and equitable resolution, Lakshmi has called for the matter to be settled with fairness, dignity and respect for the rights of all family members.
Meanwhile, another statement from Mallika Srinivasan, MD, Tractors and Farm Equipment Limited, supporting her daughter Lakshmi Venu's legitimate right in the family assets, said, "It is unfortunate that requests for an amicable settlement have not so far progressed in a meaningful and timely way".
She further said, "As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of (Lakshmi's brother) Sudarshan’s. I reiterate that this is a matter to be settled, in the interests of all stakeholders, through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. I sincerely hope that we can move forward constructively, with grace and dignity".

articles.title: Maileva, filial del correo francés, confirmó un ciberataque que expuso nombres y direcciones de 22 millones de personas
articles.text:
Maileva, filial del grupo de correos francés La Poste, confirmó que un ciberataque de mediados de septiembre expuso los nombres, apellidos y direcciones postales de 22 millones de personas. La Poste lo informó el 14 de noviembre en una declaración a la agencia AFP, dos meses después de la intrusión.
Maileva ya notificó el incidente a la Comisión Nacional de Informática y Libertades (CNIL), el organismo francés que vigila el uso de datos personales, y presentó una denuncia. Según La Poste, una investigación judicial está en curso.
La sección de cibercriminalidad de la fiscalía de París abrió una investigación por “atentado contra un sistema de tratamiento automatizado de datos”, según confirmó a la AFP. La Brigada de Lucha contra la Cibercriminalidad quedó a cargo del caso.
La empresa no precisó cómo entraron los atacantes. El sitio especializado Cyberattaque.org reveló el caso antes del anuncio oficial y lo describió como una de las mayores fugas de datos del año en Francia.
Víctimas que nunca fueron clientes
Maileva es una plataforma que imprime y envía correo para empresas: recibos de sueldo, facturas, cartas certificadas y convocatorias a asambleas. Pertenece a Docaposte, a su vez filial de La Poste. Dice tener más de 70.000 usuarios y haber enviado 180 millones de documentos en 2024.
Los afectados no contrataron a Maileva. Son los destinatarios de las cartas de sus clientes: inquilinos, pacientes, empleados o usuarios de servicios públicos. La Poste indicó que todas las empresas afectadas fueron informadas, y que son ellas quienes deben avisar a cada persona, como establece el reglamento europeo de protección de datos.
Según el servicio de prensa de Docaposte, citado por 01net, varios miles de empresas clientes están involucradas. Entre ellas figuran viviendas sociales, laboratorios y hospitales.
Cyberattaque.org, que cita documentos internos atribuidos a Docaposte, calcula que el incidente abarca unos 39 millones de referencias de correo. Al eliminar duplicados, la cifra queda en 22 millones de personas. La empresa no confirmó ese detalle.
Qué datos aparecen en las cartas
El 3 de noviembre, la empresa de vivienda social Flandre Opale Habitat comunicó que pudieron consultarse datos de cartas enviadas en los últimos diez años. Incluyen referencias de vivienda, números de cliente y datos administrativos o financieros, como el monto de una factura.
El Hospital Foch, en Suresnes, avisó a sus pacientes de que cartas de cobro enviadas entre el 9 y el 23 de septiembre pudieron ser leídas. Contienen fechas de atención, números de factura e importes, pero no la naturaleza de los cuidados ni datos bancarios, según el hospital.
Antoine Hautin, secretario general de la empresa de ciberseguridad Almond, dijo a franceinfo que Maileva representa un “riesgo sistémico” porque decenas de miles de organizaciones la usan. Advirtió que la inteligencia artificial facilita automatizar estafas con cartas que parecen legítimas, y recomendó verificar por otro canal cualquier pedido inusual.
El primer aviso público fue el 23 de septiembre, cuando Maileva suspendió sus servicios por actividad sospechosa, según Cyberattaque.org. La plataforma estuvo seis días fuera de servicio. Entonces la empresa habló solo de intentos de acceso no autorizados a cuentas de clientes, sin mencionar un robo de datos.

articles.title: Tras casi cinco años, al fin sabemos quién es la gran ganadora de la guerra de Ucrania: la minería ilegal de ámbar
articles.text:
Si nada cambia (y parece difícil) en febrero la guerra de Ucrania cumplirá cinco años, un lustro de enfrentamientos que se ha saldado con decenas de miles de fallecidos en ambos bandos, un gasto millonario en armamento y ayuda humanitaria y, en general, un tensionamiento en la geopolítica mundial que parece lejos de aflojarse. Hay sin embargo un negocio al que el conflicto parece estar sentándole bastante bien: el comercio ilegal de ámbar ‘made in Ucrania’.
La guerra ha hecho que el esfuerzo regulador activado por Kiev en 2019 pasase a un segundo plano. Hoy la prioridad no es el ámbar, sino el frente.
El negocio del ámbar. China es un mercado de 1.400 millones de potenciales clientes, lo que explica que no haya sector que no sueñe con abrirse camino allí. Si hablamos de ámbar los negocios cuentan además con un aliciente extra: el gigante asiático muestra un interés especial por esta resina fosilizada y preciada en joyería. Tanto, que los exportadores polacos (referencia en el sector) estiman que alrededor del 40% de la producción acaba en China y el Sudeste Asiático.
Los compradores de Pekín, Shanghái, Shenzhen o el resto de metrópolis chinas también despertaron el interés de otros exportadores de ámbar, como Rusia o Ucrania. Y es lógico. AFP recuerda que el aumento de demanda generado en Asia hizo que el sector viviese su particular ‘fiebre del oro’, con valores que se dispararon un 1000% entre 2010 y 2015.
La ‘cara B’ del negocio. Al calor de ese porcentaje, hubo quien decidió lanzarse a la extracción de ámbar sin reparar en los daños que pudiera causar al medioambiente o las líneas rojas que establece la ley. El resultado fue una “mafia del ámbar” que, lamenta Olena Belichenko, de la Asociación Internacional del Ámbar (IAA), causó un “verdadero caos” y una “catástrofe” ecológica.
“La minería se realizaba ilegalmente, el medio ambiente sufría graves daños y nuestros recursos fueron saqueados durante 30 años”, concuerda Oleg Bogelsky, de Amber Galbin, una empresa minera que opera en Rivne, al oeste del país.
La hemeroteca demuestra que tienen motivos para quejarse. En 2017 National Geographic publicó una amplia crónica en la que alertaba de la “minería ilegal” de ámbar en “el salvaje oeste de Ucrania”. Más allá de su impacto en el terreno, con “miles de hectáreas de bosques de pinos y abedules devastados”, su reportero John Wendle hablaba también de bandas que recurrían a las armas para disputarse los mejores yacimientos y “rumores sobre funcionarios corruptos”.
Y llegó 2019. El panorama cambió en 2019, cuando el Gobierno de Ucrania impulsó nuevas normas para “regular” la extracción de ámbar. La idea era promover la extracción legal y, de paso, frenar el mercado negro.
Resulta difícil saber hasta qué punto se alcanzó ese último objetivo, pero los datos de Aduanas sugieren que como mínimo el cambio de 2019 ayudó a desviar mercancía al cauce legal: las exportaciones oficiales de resina sin procesar se dispararon en cinco años, pasando de 0,6 toneladas en 2020 a 88,8 en 2025.
Nuevas prioridades. Por más preocupante que fuese el mercado ilegal de ámbar y su impacto económico, medioambiental y social, el 24 de febrero de 2022 el asunto pasó a un segundo (o tercer) lugar en la lista de prioridades de Kiev. Ese día las tropas rusas avanzaron hacia Ucrania, iniciando una guerra que sigue enquistada casi un lustro después y acumula decenas y decenas de miles de muertos en ambos bandos. Esa situación ha llevado al Parlamento ucraniano a ir prorrogando desde entonces la ley marcial para centrarse en la guerra.
¿Qué tiene que ver con el ámbar? Que según la agencia AFP ese cambio de prioridades ha afectado al celo regulador que se activó con las nuevas normas de 2019. No se trata de que se hayan derogado, sino de si en plena guerra se siguen realizando inspecciones y auditorías que permitan a las autoridades controlar el negocio. Y dada la situación actual en Rivne hay motivos para ser escépticos.
El problema lo reconoce Mykola Kotniuk, de la Asociación de Empresas de Ámbar de Ucrania, quien asume la posibilidad de que a día de hoy haya gente extrayendo resina cuando solo tiene permiso para trabajos piloto o sondeos.
La lógica es muy sencilla: tras más de cuatro años de guerra, toca priorizar recursos. Y la industria minera no parece estar en primer lugar. “Algunos explotadores del subsuelo abusan de su posición y, tal vez, algunos extraen recursos de forma ilegal”, añade el responsable de la patronal del sector.
Más que sospechas. Durante su investigación AFP charló con un directivo de la industria ucraniana que asegura que entre el 60 y 70% del ámbar del país es de origen ilícito. Sea o no cierto, la misma agencia cita un dato oficial: desde 2024 Ucrania ha abierto 360 investigaciones por la extracción y posesión ilegal de ámbar, según datos de la Fiscalía Ambiental.
Entre ellas se cuenta una red minera descubierta en junio. El negocio estaba liderado por un funcionario y se le achaca un daño ambiental valorado en ocho millones de dólares. Con todo, desde el sector hay quien matiza también que las infracciones flagrantes representan casos “aislados”.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics
Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. 
As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design.The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores—more than 50,000 on a single GPU—as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology.
Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps.
Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA"For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery. Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer."
Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery
Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing workloads take a similar shape: an application reaches into an immense dataset, gathers a handful of scattered values, calculates a result and repeats this on an enormous scale. 
To help address the challenge, Rubin HPC will offer a balanced design, scaling data movement and compute together rather than increasing compute alone. 
That balance is what optimizes Rubin HPC for scientific computing. It keeps the GPU's record number of CUDA cores supplied with data, so they spend their time computing rather than waiting. This accelerates recurring patterns of every simulation workload—from sparse matrix operations to stencil computations to sorting and reductions. 
These patterns are prevalent across data analytics, science and engineering workloads, which is why a purpose-built GPU delivering the broadest acceleration can help unlock cross-industry breakthroughs.
NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries offer a growing set of optimized implementations of complex algorithms for agents to use, including those most relevant to simulation and analytics. Used together with Rubin HPC, the libraries can give agents the fastest glide path to reasoning outcomes. 
And faster agent-invoked simulations mean faster feedback—shortening the loop of hypothesis, simulation and refinement, so researchers and engineers can choose next steps sooner and point lab work at the most promising candidates.
Rubin HPC is expected to be available in 2028.
