articles.title: Microsoft adds a way to remotely lock lost Windows 11 laptops without wiping them
articles.text:
In context: Windows 11 allows IT administrators to remotely wipe corporate laptops that have been lost or stolen using Microsoft's Intune device management software. Microsoft is now experimenting with a new Remote Locking option designed to protect sensitive data from unauthorized access without deleting any files.
As explained on Microsoft's Learn website, Remote Lock offers a less destructive way to protect data on lost or stolen devices than Remote Wipe. While Remote Wipe deletes all user data from a device, the new feature leaves the data untouched. If the device is recovered, its authorized user can simply sign in and pick up where they left off without losing any files.
When Remote Lock is activated, Windows signs out all active sessions, hides local sign-in options, and displays a custom "Device Locked" screen, preventing users from accessing the device locally or remotely. However, locked devices remain enrolled in and managed through Intune, while BitLocker stays enabled as an additional layer of security.
Remote Lock remains enabled across restarts and while the device is offline. Only an administrator can deactivate it. According to Microsoft, the lock can be lifted only remotely through Intune, as there is no way to unlock the device locally. The company says this restriction is intentional and is designed to prevent malicious actors from using brute-force attacks to gain access to device data.
Microsoft adds that Remote Lock does not block local boot and recovery options, such as the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), Safe Mode, or booting from USB drives and other media. The company also advises administrators to keep BitLocker enabled to protect data if a drive is removed or a device is reimaged.
Administrators can use Intune to configure Remote Lock on Windows Enterprise, Education, and Pro devices that are MDM-enrolled, Microsoft Entra-joined, or hybrid-joined. The read-only Status node in Intune reports the effective LockState: 0 if the device is unlocked, 1 if it is locked, 2 if the lock is pending, and 3 if an error occurred while attempting to lock the device.
Remote Lock is part of Windows 11 Insider Preview Build 29708.1001 for the Experimental (Future Platforms) channel, released on November 13. Curiously, the release notes also mention Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016, 2019, and 2022, suggesting that Microsoft might eventually extend the feature to additional platforms.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: Lazy Constants, Spring for Apache Pulsar, GlassFish, Hibernate, TomEE, Seed4J
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for November 9th, 2026, features news highlighting: Lazy Constants proposed to target for JDK 28; TornadoVM jitLLM 3.0; point releases of Seed4J; second release candidates of Spring AI and Spring Boot; first release candidates of Hibernate ORM and Hibernate Reactive; fourth milestone release of GlassFish; and the second milestone release of Apache TomEE.
OpenJDK
JEP 547, Lazy Constants (Fourth Preview), has been elevated from Candidate to Proposed to Target for JDK 28. This JEP proposes a fourth preview, with no changes, after three rounds of preview delivered in the upcoming release of JDK 27 and JDK 26 through JDK 25. Formerly known as Stable Values and Computed Constants, this feature introduces the concept of computed constants, defined as immutable value holders that are initialized at most once. This offers the performance and safety benefits of final fields, while offering greater flexibility as to the timing of initialization. The name change from Stable Values to Lazy Constants with the release of JDK 26, better captures the intent of a high-level use case. The review is expected to conclude on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.
JDK 28
Build 24 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 23 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
Spring Framework
The second release candidate of Spring AI 2.1.0 delivers new features such as: a new DecisionModel API, anchored by the DecisionModel interface, that returns the probability of different outcomes instead of generated text based on yes/no answers, questions about text or a set of fields; and a new similaritySearch(float [], SearchRequest) method, added to the VectorStoreRetriever interface to complement the corresponding overloaded methods, to search with a user's embeddings in more vector stores. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
The second release candidate of Spring Boot 4.2.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: support for reading the value defined in a X-Forwarded-Prefix HTTP header in a WebFlux application on Reactor Netty when the server.forward-headers-strategy property is set to native; and a database assigned to the spring.data.redis.database property is now properly applied to master/replica connections if a value is assigned to the spring.data.redis.masterreplica.nodes property. More details on this release may be found in the release notes and this wiki page.
The Spring for Apache Pulsar team has announced that the project is moving as a subproject within Apache Pulsar at the Apache Software Foundation to "foster even deeper integration and collaboration with the broader Pulsar community." As stated in the blog post:
Bringing this integration directly into the Apache Pulsar project allows the community to streamline development, accelerate feature support, and ensure long-term alignment with the evolution of Apache Pulsar.
Spring for Apache Pulsar 2.0.8, released in October 2026, was the final release under the auspices of the Spring ecosystem.
GlassFish
The fourth milestone release of GlassFish 9.0.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: implementation of the Jakarta Persistence 4.0.0-M7 specification with EclipseLink 6.0.0-M1; a move of the Sun Theme module out of the out of the external GlassFish Woodstock Components repository into its own module in GlassFish so that Sun Theme and the Admin Console can be modified together; and an update to versions 1.2.0-M2 and 2.0.0-M1 of Eclipse JNoSQL. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
TornadoVM
Beehive Lab, makers of TornadoVM, has released version 3.0 of jitLLM, a JVM-native LLM inference and serving engine, delivers notable changes such as: 1.43 times faster startup with GraalVM Native Image; an up to 9.3 times faster prefill phase; and a more efficient reading of model weights by eliminating the copy from the mapped GGUF file into a Apple Metal buffer. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Hibernate
The first release candidate of Hibernate ORM 8.0.0 ships with notable changes such as: an implementation of the Jakarta Persistence 4.0.0-M7 and Jakarta Data 1.1.0-M4 specifications (the latter via Hibernate Data Repositories); and support for coordination of graph-based flushing that builds a dependency graph for pending entity and collection mutations. Further details on this release may be found in the what's new page.
The first release candidates of Hibernate Reactive 5.1.0 and 5.0.0 provide notable changes such as: the EXTENDED constant, defined in the Jakarta Persistence PessimisticLockScope enum class, now locks the collection tables as intended to align with the same functionality in Hibernate ORM; and an update to the VertxFactory interface to allow for adding observability without changing the functionality in using the DefaultVertxInstance class. These versions are compatible with Hibernate ORM 8.0.0.CR1. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 5.1.0.CR1 and version 5.0.0.CR1.
Apache TomEE
The second milestone release of Apache TomEE 11.0.0 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: resolutions to 38 CVEs; completion of their implementation of the Jakarta Authorization 3.0 specification; and TomEE Plume, the enterprise version, now ships the modular EclipseLink JPA artifact instead of the eclipselink Uber-Jar. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JobRunr
The release of JobRunr 9.0.4 ships with bug fixes and one new feature that improves build caching and security by moving to hardened Docker images. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JReleaser
The first rolling release of JReleaser 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT provides a new feature in which the -a and -d short option flags, for their respective corresponding --assembly and --download long versions, were removed from the CLI due to the lack of short option flags for the --changelog and --announce flags. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Seed4J
Versions 2.4.0 and 2.3.0 of Seed4J, formerly known as JHipster Lite, deliver bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: install Playwrite only on applications that execute the relevant Playwright component tests; and improved efficiency by creating one global Maven cache that is shared by the Seed4J build and every generated Maven application that replaces a Maven cache for each generated application. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 2.4.0 and version 2.3.0.
Quarkus
The Quarkus team has introduced the Quarkus Resiliency Testing utility that allows developers to reproduce various failure scenarios and their respective responses while testing an application with the @QuarkusTest annotation. An example application using this new utility may be found here.

articles.title: Exaforce's ExaU lets security staff spin up a personal team of AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exaforce’s ExaU lets security staff spin up a personal team of AI agents
Agentic security operations startup Exaforce Inc. today announced the launch of ExaU, a service that lets any security staff member spin up a personal team of artificial intelligence agents.
The new service seeks to move past the first wave of AI agents in security, which Exaforce says were built to offload a single task such as alert triage, risk assessment or penetration testing.
Exaforce argues that as AI absorbs more of the routine work, security staff are now responsible for outcomes that cannot be handed off one task at a time. Added to the mix is that staff are also facing a backlog of tasks, such as checks they mean to run, questions they plan to chase down and briefings owed to senior management.
Leading the list of ExaU features is the ability to create an agent by describing the job in plain language, down to the way a practitioner wants it done. Templates are also available. Each agent is designed to retain decisions, exceptions and past instructions.
To use, a security staff member begins by telling an agent what they are responsible for. The agent then works out what needs doing next and when. The response includes discoveries, questions and recommendations.
The new service also supports sharing agents across a security organization. A chief information security officer’s briefing agent can gather status from the agents used by every team. Exaforce’s own example has a finding setting off a threat hunt, an activity audit and outreach to an employee at the same time. A single assessment then pulls the results of all three together.
Everything runs inside Exaforce on the customer’s own data. With connections to identity providers, cloud services and security telemetry already part of the platform, there are no tokens to mint for ExaU agents. The company’s real-time security knowledge graph is claimed to give each agent an understanding of how systems relate from its first task.
Investigations are carried out by the agents on their own. Under the controls built into ExaU, any action affecting employees, systems or communications requires approval first. Recorded in the Exaforce audit log, every step an agent takes can be reviewed later.
Exabots, the agents Exaforce manages itself, already handle threat detection, alert triage and investigation for every customer on the platform. ExaU is pitched as a complement to that standing workforce. Available now as part of the Exaforce platform, the release follows the September launch of Exaforce AI Security, a kill switch for AI agents that go rogue.
HarbourVest Partners, Peak XV Partners, Mayfield Fund, Khosla Ventures and Seligman Ventures were among the investors in Exaforce’s $125 million Series B round in May. Including that round, total funding since the company’s 2023 founding comes to $200 million.

Nubank libera período de teste grátis do NuCel
Clientes podem testar a operadora do Nubank com número provisório e sem custo. Oferta inclui até 5 GB de internet e WhatsApp ilimitado.
O Nubank começou a oferecer um período de testes gratuito do NuCel, sua operadora móvel virtual. Clientes interessados podem experimentar o serviço por até 10 dias, sem precisar transferir imediatamente o número de outra operadora.
Em resposta ao Tecnoblog, o banco informou que os clientes terão direito a até 5 GB de dados móveis e WhatsApp ilimitado durante o teste. A ativação é feita pelo app do Nubank por meio de um eSIM, sem necessidade de comprar ou receber um chip físico.

Quem decidir continuar com a NuCel pode contratar um dos planos da operadora, com preços a partir de R$ 45 por mês e franquia de 35 GB. Nos três primeiros meses, há um bônus de 10 GB mensais, elevando o pacote para 45 GB nesse período.
O teste termina quando o usuário completar 10 dias ou consumir os 5 GB disponíveis, o que acontecer primeiro. A proposta é permitir que potenciais clientes avaliem a conexão e os recursos do serviço antes de transferir seu número principal.

articles.title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
articles.text:
AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast’s cable broadband service and Wi-Fi is “fiber-powered.”
“This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide,” AT&T’s lawsuit said. “At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are ‘Fiber-Powered.’”
While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds.
In contrast, fiber-to-the-home service can provide symmetrical upload and download speeds. Comcast has deployed fiber-to-the-home in only small portions of its cable territory while advertising its service as fiber-powered in the majority of areas where cable makes the final connection.
AT&T’s lawsuit said that in describing its cable broadband as fiber-powered, Comcast “conveys to reasonable consumers the misleading impression that Xfinity Internet is a fiber-to-the-home service comparable to AT&T Fiber. In fact, the vast majority of Xfinity Internet runs over a hybrid fiber-coaxial (‘HFC’) network, where the critical ‘last mile’ connection to the customer’s home uses copper coaxial cable, not fiber.”
AT&T has its own history of ads that mislead customers about the nature of its network. It used to advertise 4G LTE service as “5GE” or “5G Evolution,” and displayed a 5GE network icon on 4G phones. AT&T claimed that its 5G Evolution ads “served to educate customers about the billions of dollars AT&T has invested to give customers an outstanding experience,” but the BBB National Programs’ National Advertising Division found the term was likely to mislead consumers into thinking they had 5G connections.
AT&T: Fiber-powered is “literally false”
AT&T’s lawsuit said that Comcast’s fiber-powered claim “is literally false” because the cable firm’s HFC “architecture is fundamentally different from true fiber-to-the-home services like AT&T Fiber, which deliver fiber optic cables directly to the customer’s premises.”

articles.title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results.
For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia’s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang.
Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees.
Now, the company is facing questions about its restricted chips allegedly being smuggled into China, especially by Huang’s mistress’ company. Nvidia promised to conduct an internal investigation. Meanwhile, Huang was commanded to answer questions to Congress in a closed-door joint session with three Republican-led committees. Plus, top Democrats have also vowed to investigate the company.
Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Kress should answer.
Huang’s role now and going forward. Huang ran Nvidia with an iron fist, having some 60 direct reports and his fingers in everything. No one knows the company better than him.
An internet petition signed by 180,000 and growing is calling for the board to reinstate him. Huang may also have been mounting an attempt to return, Financial Times reported. However, CNBC is reporting, citing unnamed sources, that the company is not in talks to reinstate Huang.
So, we’ll be looking for language from the interim CEO about Huang’s ongoing involvement with the company, its search for a new CEO, and any talks to bring him back.
China and Singapore. As Huang vehemently argued in favor of easing export restrictions for Nvidia chips to China, Huang said that he’s seen no evidence that its powerful semiconductors were being diverted from legit buyers to China.
But in October 2025, The New York Times reported that the U.S. was investigating Huang’s mistress’ company, Megaspeed, over allegations it was doing just that. Nvidia at the time vouched to CNBC that Megaspeed was legally using the chips for its cloud. However, Nvidia recently told The Wall Street Journal that it had voluntarily blocked Megaspeed from receiving more chips way back in June 2025.
Last year, Nvidia said that Singapore, the region where Megaspeed is located, was one of its fastest-growing, accounting for 22% of its total revenue for its second quarter of that year. After the investigation into Megaspeed came to light, Nvidia changed how it reported revenue. It now reports based on a company’s headquarters, instead of its shipping address. That completely hid sales to Singapore and Megaspeed’s impact.
So we’re listening to what Kress says about the future of sales to the China region and the cloud business in Singapore that was once 20% of sales. We’re especially listening for what she says about Nvidia keeping track of where its restricted chips wind up.
China sales policy. Huang’s argument was, essentially, that the U.S. can’t stop China from developing advanced AI models, so the West is better off selling them less powerful Nvidia chips and keeping them dependent, he said on the Dwarkesh Podcast last summer. Notably, that’s a position that would make Nvidia a lot of money.
The China hawks counter that selling an adversary any powerful chips at all will help them, and U.S. companies shouldn’t do that. So we’re listening for any indications that Kress is reversing Nvidia’s goals with China.
Bankrolling the AI build-out. The expectation is that Kress, the CFO who reportedly had unsuccessfully tried to push back against Huang’s extreme AI dealmaking, will be conservative on such deals going forward. We’ll be listening for what she says about the impacts of existing deals on the books. (Will she subtly try to throw Huang under the bus for those controversial deals?) We’ll also be listening for her future plans.
Governance. With the ousting of Huang and more fallout sure still to come, has the board learned its lesson about too much power in the hands of one person? We’ll be listening for information about how Nvidia might restructure itself.

articles.title: iPhone Duo gets face unlock, but don't call it Face ID
articles.text:
Apple is testing new iPhone Duo features that will make it easier to unlock and lock the foldable, addressing some of the concerns raised by early adopters.
iOS 27.3 Beta 2 will allow iPhone Duo users to opt in to a face unlock feature that’ll let the Duo cover display camera scan your face and unlock your device, with a few caveats.
First, this isn’t Face ID and is therefore less secure than a regular iPhone’s face-scanning capabilities. Once you start using face unlock, you’ll need to use Touch ID around every 45 minutes for added security. Also, you won’t be able to use face unlock for payments or to get into your passwords, and will need Touch ID again.
The Duo’s face unlock uses the Secure Enclave in the Apple silicon, which privately processes the data of the user’s face and confirms a match. Apple says that iOS, apps, users and even Apple itself cannot access this face data. You can find this feature in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode.
This is similar to how the Apple HomeView works, since it also doesn’t use the same technology as Face ID. The HomeView requires you to unlock your smartphone every once in a while for its face unlock to work for security purposes as well.
Also coming to the next developer beta for iOS 27.3 is ‘Close to lock,’ which will let you opt in to lock your device every time you close it. You can find this in Settings, under Display & Brightness.
The first iOS 27.3 developer beta brought Apple Pencil support for the Duo.
You can signup to join the beta program on Apple’s website and after joining check your Settings > General > Software Update and below Automatic Updates, you’ll see ‘Beta Updates’.

Wenn Ausnahmen zur Regel werden

Warum künftig mehr E‑Rechnungen eintreffen
Mit der schrittweisen Einführung der E‑Rechnung entstehen Jahr für Jahr neue Standards im Rechnungsverkehr zwischen Unternehmen. Dadurch werden immer mehr Geschäftspartner Rechnungen in elektronischer, strukturierter Form versenden. Auch für kleinere Unternehmen stellt sich daher nicht die Frage, ob E‑Rechnungen eintreffen werden. Die entscheidende Frage lautet: Wie gut sind die eigenen Prozesse darauf vorbereitet? Gängige Software-Lösungen wie DATEV Unternehmen online können E-Rechnungen schon verarbeiten.

Gemeinsam mit der Steuerberatung vorbereiten
Die Umstellung auf digitale Rechnungsprozesse ist keine Aufgabe, die Unternehmen allein bewältigen müssen. articles.title: Amazon’s Starlink rival sees major setback after 40 satellites destroyed in rocket failure — ‘anomaly’ occurred 10 minutes after the Vulcan launch on Sunday
articles.text:
Amazon’s Starlink rival sees major setback after 40 satellites destroyed in rocket failure — ‘anomaly’ occurred 10 minutes after the Vulcan launch on Sunday
Currently Amazon has 392 broadband satellites in orbit and hoped to move the service out of beta by the end of this year.
Amazon has suffered a major setback in its plans to offer a viable Starlink rival, after 40 satellites destined for low Earth orbit (LEO) were destroyed. Just ten minutes after the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 in Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, there was an “anomaly,” meaning that the rocket “failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.” The language seems quite vague, but the United Launch Alliance (ULA) says that data needs to be analyzed “to understand what occurred today.”
Shortly after the triumphant takeoff clip was shared by the ULA, above, the space tech firm updated its X feed with a confirmation that its mission on behalf of Amazon failed.
Sadly for Amazon, the ULA, and folks who want a viable substitute for Starlink in the satellite internet business, this failure will surely delay the full commercialization of this service. ISPReview notes that Amazon has successfully launched 392 Kuiper communications satellites, but needs at least 500 for basic global coverage. Moreover, Amazon Leo service’s transition from the current commercial beta phase to launching properly at the end of 2026 now looks uncertain.
Reports indicate Amazon has already manufactured 1,000 satellites, but ULA, which is a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, will need to analyze and assure customers that Sunday’s failure won’t be repeated. ULA's Vulcan vehicle had already been out of action for nine months after technical investigations into issues with its solid rocket side boosters and core BE-4 engines (made by Amazon Blue Origin).
For some context, the ULA has (or had) a great track record. Sunday's incident was its first total mission failure in its 20-year history. Early telemetry from the organization is already pointing towards some suspected causes of the destruction of the 40 satellites. Likely fault candidates include the first-stage BE-4 engines burning longer than planned, and there may have been some altitude issues near staging.
The headline failure and essential careful analysis of the anomaly won’t hold up Amazon’s other launch partners, though. A week from today, the Amazon Leo constellation is set to grow by 36 more satellites. They will be sent into orbit aboard a European Ariane 64 Block 2 (LE-04) rocket.
Amazon has approval for an initial constellation of 3,236 LEO broadband satellites, with 392 now in orbit, plus 5,105 for 5G service. Satellite tracking sites suggest Starlink already has 11,200+ satellites in orbit.

articles.title: Renault embauche 2 000 ouvriers en France grâce au succès de ses modèles électriques
articles.text:
Alors qu’une partie de l’industrie automobile européenne broie du noir à coups de fermetures d’usines et de plans sociaux, Renault fait figure d’exception et la marque française en est fière.
Lors d’un point presse organisé ce lundi 16 novembre, Thierry Charvet, directeur industrie, qualité et chaîne d’approvisionnement du groupe, a annoncé une nouvelle plutôt rare dans le secteur : le constructeur va embaucher 2 000 personnes en CDI dans ses usines françaises d’ici fin 2028.
Des embauches pour les usines françaises
Contrairement aux habitudes des grands groupes, ce ne sont pas les bureaux et le management qui vont grossir, mais bien les ateliers. Sur ces 2 000 recrutements, 1 650 concernent directement des postes d’opérateurs sur les lignes de montage, les fameux « cols bleus », complétés par 250 postes en soutien à la production et 100 jeunes diplômés.
Pour les trois quarts, il s’agit de pérenniser en CDI les intérimaires déjà présents sur les chaînes, le reste étant réservé à une nouvelle génération d’employés.
Douai tourne à fond grâce à l’électrique
Si Renault recrute sur le terrain, c’est tout simplement parce que ses voitures électriques se vendent et que les usines françaises tournent à plein régime. Thierry Charvet a d’ailleurs glissé un chiffre parlant : le taux d’utilisation des sites français dépasse désormais les 100 % par rapport à une organisation classique en deux équipes (2×8).
À Douai, dans le Nord, l’usine est passée en 3×8 pour absorber la demande autour des R5, Scénic, Mégane ou encore de la Nissan Micra électrique. Dieppe tourne en revanche au ralenti à cause de l’échec de l’Alpine A390 : le site historique d’Alpine n’est pas menacé, mais il sera visé par des départs volontaires.
Cette dynamique permet au patron de l’industrie, Thierry Charvet, de revendiquer un statut à part en Europe : « On est dans une situation plus saine » que la concurrence, assure-t-il, soulignant que Renault n’a pas subi de plein fouet le retournement des marchés chinois et américain, contrairement aux géants allemands.
1 000 départs malgré tout
Pas question pour autant de crier victoire trop vite. « On n’a jamais été autant challengé » sur le plan industriel, reconnaît Thierry Charvet face à l’offensive des constructeurs chinois en Europe. Même quand un modèle cartonne, le groupe s’impose désormais une « remise en cause tous les 18 mois de nos modèles » pour rester dans le coup technologiquement et financièrement.
En parallèle des embauches en atelier, Renault prévoit jusqu’à 1 000 départs volontaires chez les « cols blancs » liés à la production (contrôle qualité, approvisionnements…). Ils s’étaleront sur six à neuf mois et doivent encore être négociés avec les syndicats. Sur le papier, le solde reste positif, même si les trois quarts des CDI iront à des intérimaires déjà en poste. C’est au moins un contre-exemple à l’idée que la voiture électrique menace forcément l’emploi en France. Pourvu que les ventes de R5 et de Scénic tiennent jusqu’en 2028 !

articles.title: La chute fait très mal : les entreprises liées aux data centers perdent 4 200 milliards de dollars en Bourse
articles.text:
Les fournisseurs de data centers surfaient sur la ruée vers l’intelligence artificielle, mais la fête est finie. Les investisseurs s’en détournent depuis juin… Et le doute gagne tout le secteur.
Depuis des mois, les géants de la tech multiplient les projets de data centers, investissant des centaines de milliards de dollars. Problème, ces dépenses sont de plus en plus financées par la dette, alors même que la colère monte face à ces ogres énergétiques. Aux États-Unis, des dizaines de projets ont déjà été bloqués ou retardés.
Des pertes qui touchent tous les maillons de la chaîne
Et cela a des conséquences claires. D’après une analyse du Financial Times, les groupes industriels, énergéticiens et miniers du monde entier ont perdu 4 200 milliards de dollars de valeur en Bourse depuis juin. Or, ce sont spécifiquement eux qui fournissent le matériel nécessaire à la ruée vers l’IA : les générateurs, la climatisation ou la fibre optique dont les centres de données ne peuvent pas se passer.
Ces pertes effacent près de la moitié des 9 400 milliards gagnés par ces mêmes entreprises au cours des 12 mois précédents. Les plus gros noms n’y échappent pas. Caterpillar, grand fournisseur de générateurs à gaz pour data centers, a vu sa capitalisation fondre de 214 milliards de dollars, soit 44 %, depuis son record du 30 juin. Oklo, spécialiste du nucléaire, a plongé de 49 %, malgré un contrat sensationnel décroché auprès de Meta en janvier. Quant au spécialiste de la climatisation Comfort Systems et au fabricant de fibre optique Corning, ils ont chacun perdu environ la moitié de leur valeur.
Le mouvement dépasse ces seuls cas. Car depuis l’été, les industriels forment le deuxième secteur le plus en difficulté du S&P 500, l’indice vedette de Wall Street, derrière la technologie.
Simple correction ou début d’un retournement ?
Le signal est on ne peut plus clair : les investisseurs craignent que le rythme des dépenses des géants de l’IA ne soit intenable, et que la pression politique contre les data centers ne finisse par casser la dynamique.
À noter, tout de même, que la demande ne faiblit pas. Caterpillar affiche par exemple un carnet de commandes record de 78 milliards de dollars, une donnée malgré tout trompeuse, car par peur de manquer d’équipements, certains clients multiplient les requêtes, parfois par deux ou trois, afin de garder leur place dans la file d’attente. Aux États-Unis, la construction de data centers, hors puces et serveurs, a tout de même atteint 96 milliards de dollars sur 12 mois.
Mais l’actualité politique ne laisse présager rien de bon pour la filière. Car l’effet des moratoires et restrictions largement soutenus par les Américains lors des élections de mi-mandat reste flou. Certains analystes se veulent malgré tout rassurants : les projets visés seront simplement déplacés vers des territoires plus accueillants. Toutefois, force est de constater que la grogne gagne de plus en plus de personnes.
L’essentiel de la consommation vient du calcul (GPU/TPU) et du maintien de conditions stables pour éviter pannes et surchauffes. Une partie importante de l’énergie sert au refroidissement : climatisation, circulation de liquides, pompes et ventilation, ce qui se traduit par un indicateur souvent cité, le PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness). La demande explose aussi parce que l’entraînement des modèles IA mobilise des grappes de serveurs sur de longues durées, puis l’inférence à grande échelle s’ajoute au quotidien. À l’échelle d’un site, cela implique des raccordements électriques lourds, des transformateurs, parfois des générateurs de secours, et des contrats d’approvisionnement qui peuvent peser sur le réseau local.
Financer par la dette consiste à emprunter (obligations, prêts bancaires, crédits syndiqués) pour payer la construction et l’équipement, en misant sur des revenus futurs pour rembourser. Quand les taux d’intérêt augmentent, le coût du service de la dette grimpe et peut rogner la rentabilité, surtout si les revenus attendus tardent ou si l’utilisation des capacités est inférieure aux prévisions. Les data centers sont des actifs très capitalistiques : terrains, bâtiments, alimentation électrique, refroidissement et interconnexions réseau se payent cash, souvent bien avant l’arrivée des clients. En cas de retournement de marché, les investisseurs deviennent plus exigeants sur les flux de trésorerie et pénalisent les entreprises jugées trop endettées.
La chaîne de valeur d’un data center mobilise des fournisseurs d’électricité, des fabricants d’équipements (groupes électrogènes, onduleurs, refroidissement), des câbliers/fibre optique et des acteurs des métaux nécessaires à l’infrastructure. Si des projets sont ralentis, annulés ou simplement replanifiés, les carnets de commandes de ces fournisseurs peuvent être revus à la baisse, ce qui pèse sur leurs perspectives de chiffre d’affaires. Les marchés financiers anticipent ces variations : même sans baisse immédiate des ventes, un changement de rythme d’investissement peut suffire à dégrader les valorisations. À l’inverse, quand la demande est perçue comme durable, ces secteurs bénéficient souvent d’un effet d’entraînement via les commandes et les contrats d’approvisionnement.

articles.title: Ola Electric’s dealer-led model reset; Menopause in India’s public health agenda
articles.text:
Ola Electric’s dealer-led model reset; Menopause in India’s public health agenda
The company is betting on a cheaper S1Z scooter and in-house battery manufacturing to win back customers, though the long-term success of its reset depends on retail registrations, supply chain stability, and margin recovery.
Dear Reader,
India’s deeptech ecosystem just got a major capital boost. Multi-strategy asset manager Oister Global has launched the Oister Deep Tech Fund, targeting up to Rs 600 crore to back revenue-generating Indian startups. The fund will build a concentrated portfolio of eight to ten mature companies in the frontier tech ecosystem.
Meanwhile, upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a workforce advisory business that will help organisations redesign how they structure, hire, reward and develop employees amid workplace changes due to AI. The move expands upGrad’s corporate offering as it moves beyond skilling into higher education, professional courses, study-abroad services and enterprise learning.
In other news, India’s deeptech companies raised $914 million in 257 rounds in 2025, 34 times the 2016 level. The harder test is turning research and prototypes into commercial products, according to Speciale Invest’s report, India’s Deep Tech Revolution - From the Lab to Growth and Exits.
Edtech companies aren’t the only ones betting big on AI learning. Government programmes are also rapidly expanding India's talent pipeline. According to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, the Skill India Digital Hub’s SOAR programme now offers 50 AI and AI-application qualifications, drawing over 517,000 enrolments and certifying more than 100,000 learners as of August 2026.
Elsewhere, a new kind of revolution is brewing. About 3.76 crore rural women belonging to self-help groups have achieved Lakhpati Didi status. The Centre’s rural livelihood initiative aims to create 6 crore Lakhpati Didis by March 2029. Additionally, 5.70 crore women have been identified as Potential Lakhpati Didis.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Ola Electric’s dealer-led model reset
- Menopause in India’s public health agenda
Here’s your trivia for today: Which global payments giant began in 1966 when a group of California banks formed the ‘Interbank Card Association’? (Scroll down for the answer)
Analysis
Ola Electric’s dealer-led model reset
EV company Ola Electric is abandoning its direct-to-consumer model and shutting most company-owned showrooms by December 2026 to transition into a dealer-led business. While the broader electric two-wheeler market grew significantly, Ola’s revenue dropped sharply amid severe service backlogs, consumer complaints, and regulatory store closures over missing trade certificates. To recover, Ola rapidly established over 319 dealer outlets, shifting inventory costs to partners and boosting wholesale orders.
Key takeaways:
- The company is betting on a cheaper S1Z scooter and in-house battery manufacturing to win back customers, though the long-term success of its reset depends on retail registrations, supply chain stability, and margin recovery.
- The company's Q2 FY27 revenue dropped by 39% to Rs 421 crore even as the wider electric two-wheeler market grew.
- Between September 2023 and August 2024, the maker of electric two-wheelers received 10,644 complaints through the National Consumer Helpline. Of these, 3,389 concerned service delays and 1,899 were about delayed deliveries, according to media reports.

Health and wellbeing
Menopause in India’s public health agenda
Millions of women in India navigate menopause with little to no support from family or even their healthcare providers. That’s why the Karnataka government’s recent order for a three-month pilot of Ruthu Taare, its Mid-Life Women’s Health and Menopause Programme, in Dakshina district is a welcome step in the right direction.
Key takeaways:
- The programme will feature dedicated clinics, comprehensive health screenings, mental health assessments, nutrition counselling, and referrals for women aged 35 and above.
- The pilot will organise dedicated clinic sessions every Wednesday at primary health centres, taluka and district hospitals. Designated medical colleges may organise special clinics on Saturdays.
- The Ruthu Taare initiative is important because it attempts to bring menopausal care into mainstream conversation and integrate it into public healthcare.
News & updates
- Lawsuit: Intel is facing a shareholder lawsuit alleging the US chipmaker concealed the severity of a slump in its PC business. The class-action complaint follows a grim financial forecast that sent Intel's stock plunging nearly 29% in a single day, wiping out roughly $140 billion in market value.
- Charity: Warren Buffett has announced that he is donating roughly $5.47 billion in Berkshire Hathaway shares to four charities led by his adult children. Accompanying his annual Thanksgiving gift, the legendary investor stated that his confidence in the conglomerate he built over six decades remains “as strong as ever.”

articles.title: Cómo evitar los spoilers de GTA 6 en redes sociales si aún no lo puedes jugar
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI se estrena el 19 de noviembre y trae consigo un problema para millones de jugadores: el riesgo de spoilers antes de poder disfrutarlo en algún momento. El juego llega primero a Nueva Zelanda, lo que generará horas, incluso casi un día completo, en las que circularán videos y comentarios sobre la trama antes de que la mayoría del público hispanohablante pueda jugar.
A esto se suma una gran cantidad de usuarios que no podrán tenerlo desde el día de su lanzamiento, ya sea porque no lo pueden comprar aún o porque no tienen PS5 o Xbox Series X|S, las consolas en las que estará disponible. Por lo que es importante saber cómo evitar este tipo de spoilers.
Las palabras que conviene silenciar antes del estreno
Silenciar siempre que entras a jugar a GTA 6 implica anticiparse y filtrar ciertos términos en redes sociales. Entre las expresiones recomendadas figuran:
- GTA 6
- GTA VI
- Grand Theft Auto 6
- Grand Theft Auto VI
- Jason
- Lucia
- Vice City
- Leonida
- Spoiler
- Leak
- Gameplay
- Filtraciones
- Final
- Misión Secreta
- Historia Completa
- Mapa Completo
- Ending
Bloquear estos términos no garantiza eliminar todos los contenidos, pero reduce las probabilidades de toparse con ellos en el feed o en las notificaciones durante los días más críticos tras el lanzamiento.
Cómo configurar los filtros en cada red social
En X, la opción se encuentra en los ajustes de privacidad, dentro del apartado de palabras silenciadas. Allí se pueden añadir las frases del listado y elegir si el filtro aplica a cuentas que no se siguen o a cualquier cuenta, además de definir cuánto tiempo estará activo: una semana suele ser un margen razonable.
En TikTok, el camino pasa por Perfil, el menú de Ajustes y privacidad, luego Preferencias de contenido y finalmente Filtrar palabras clave, donde se pueden cargar los términos en los distintos feeds disponibles.
En Instagram, el control aparece entre las opciones de contenido sugerido, que permite ocultar recomendaciones que incluyan determinadas palabras o hashtags en el texto, aunque los nombres de los ajustes pueden variar según la versión de la aplicación.
En Facebook, no existe un filtro de palabras como tal, pero se puede pausar durante 30 días a los perfiles, páginas o grupos que suelen compartir spoilers, usando los tres puntos disponibles junto a sus publicaciones.
En YouTube, el riesgo aparece incluso sin reproducir ningún video, ya que una miniatura puede mostrar un personaje o una escena, y un título puede explicar directamente qué ocurre en una parte del juego. Ante canales que repiten esta práctica, conviene usar el menú de tres puntos junto a sus videos y seleccionar la opción de no recomendar ese canal, o marcar “no me interesa” en cualquier contenido relacionado con el título.
Los comentarios y los grupos de amigos, otro foco de riesgo
Incluso cuando una publicación, un video o una noticia logran evitar los destripes, los comentarios siguen siendo un punto débil. Alguien puede filtrar un detalle de la trama por desconocimiento, por error o directamente con la intención de arruinar la sorpresa a otros usuarios, algo que también puede ocurrir en los chats de las transmisiones en vivo.
Por esa razón, conviene mantener cierta prudencia al leer la sección de comentarios en publicaciones relacionadas con el juego, sobre todo durante los primeros días tras el estreno.
En el caso de los grupos de WhatsApp o Discord con amigos, la recomendación pasa por acordar reglas antes del lanzamiento. Crear un grupo o canal específico para hablar de la historia, separado de las conversaciones habituales, permite a quienes ya avanzaron en el juego comentar la trama sin exponer a quienes todavía no llegaron a esas partes.

articles.title: Guerra interna por el control de Nvidia: la vuelta de Jensen Huang como CEO está encima de la mesa
articles.text:
En poco menos de una semana, Jensen Huang pasó de ser uno de los CEO más alabados de Silicon Valley, a verse obligado a presentar su dimisión y dejar de dirigir Nvidia. Tras 33 años, Huang tiraba la toalla como CEO y anunciaba su dimisión como presidente, CEO y consejero, con efecto inmediato. Habían salido a la luz varias relaciones extramatrimoniales, una con una mujer sospechosa de lazos con la inteligencia china.
Cuatro días después, la pregunta es otra: ¿puede volver? Nvidia llegó a la crisis sin sucesor claro. Ahora hay una directora interina, un consejo que busca a un candidato para que tome el relevo y una investigación por espionaje abierta. En cambio, una campaña pública de apoyo a Jensen Huang no para de sumar firmas. Lo de Jensen Huang marcándose un Sam Altman no nos lo vimos venir.
Huang podría estar valorando volver. El Financial Times publicó el domingo que Huang estaba considerando con su círculo de confianza volver a ponerse a los mandos de Nvidia. Lo hace mientras el consejo investiga la conducta que provocó su salida, y que se prohíbe expresamente en el código de conducta de la empresa como "actividades que pueden crear un conflicto de intereses". Una fuente cercana a Huang señaló al FT la existencia de una "sala de guerra" en la que estarían apoyando a Huang destacados ejecutivos de Silicon Valley.
Sin embargo, hay varios obstáculos que el cofundador de Nvidia debe afrontar. Huang no tiene mayoría accionarial, por lo que no puede imponerse al consejo. Tal y como destacan en Forbes, en empresas como Meta, Alphabet o SpaceX, sus CEO tienen en su poder un "supervoto" en el que su criterio se impone al del consejo de administración. Pero Jensen no tiene ese poder, por lo que no puede impugnar la decisión del consejo de aceptar la dimisión de Huang y permitirle volver.
El ejército Huang. Durante años, Huang se ha granjeado la lealtad de sus empleados. Dentro de la empresa, muchos de estos empleados han mostrado abiertamente su apoyo a Huang. Entre los inversores también cuenta con importantes apoyos. Gerstner y Baker, importantes accionistas de Nvidia, piden dejar "todas las opciones sobre la mesa, incluido el posible regreso de Jensen Huang".
De forma paralela, se ha puesto en marcha la campaña "Stand with Jensen"que ya suma más de 181.400 firmas. Sin embargo, su valor como termómetro es dudoso ya que la propia web admite que las firmas son autodeclaradas y no verificadas. Nadie puede comprobar que quien dice ser empleado o accionista lo sea.
El propio Donald Trump, admirador declarado de Huang, ha confirmado a los periodistas que "Desde luego, no me importaría" que Huang volviera a coger las riendas de Nvidia. "Aprendió una gran lección", apostilló el presidente de EEUU.
La industria, partida en dos. El consejo, de momento, no se mueve a su favor y asegura que sigue barajando nombres para posibles candidatos, aunque no ha contactado formalmente con ninguno. El FT asegura que sondeó a René Haas, actual CEO de Arm. Sin embargo, la presión más dura llega de fuera: Scott Bessent, secretario del Tesoro de EEUU contradice a su jefe y pide a Nvidia buscar un sustituto para Huang fuera de la compañía.
Aquí los inversores de más peso tienen algo que decir. Con Huang hay nombres de mucho peso inversor dentro de Nvidia. Elon Musk y Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, están entre quienes respaldaron la carta pública para pedir su vuelta. Sweeney lamentó "un día triste para Nvidia, los desarrolladores, Estados Unidos y toda la humanidad". El inversor Leo KoGuan, que dice tener unos 1.300 millones en Nvidia, avisó de que no habrá más compras sin Jensen.
Estos apoyos pueden ser la clave para el retorno de Huang al timón de Nvidia. La compañía recoge en el Artículo II, Sección 6 de sus estatutos que el secretario debe convocar la junta cuando reciba solicitudes escritas de accionistas que posean al menos el 15% del poder de voto. Ese 15% equivale a unos 3.620 millones de acciones. Huang tiene cerca del 3,58% y los fondos de Gerstner y Baker, unos 10,6 millones de acciones, que se sumarían a las de Leo KoGuan, Elon Musk y otros grandes inversores. Las estimaciones sobre las probabilidades de que Huang vuelva pasaron del 11% del viernes, a más del 51% en la actualidad.

articles.title: Panne mondiale d'Outlook et Teams : comment réclamer un dédommagement à Microsoft ?
articles.text:
Le jeudi 12 et le vendredi 13 novembre derniers, Microsoft 365 a subi une panne mondiale, impactant plusieurs de ses services : Outlook, Teams, SharePoint ou encore Copilot. Selon le rapport préliminaire de Microsoft, la panne a duré près de 38 heures. Bon nombre d’entreprises, qui paient pour pouvoir accéder à ces services, se sont retrouvées totalement immobilisées dans leur travail. Mais savent-elles qu’il est possible de demander un dédommagement à Microsoft ?
Les entreprises touchées peuvent réclamer un avoir de 50 % sur leur prochaine facture
Comme le rappelle le média américain Wired, Microsoft promet dans ses contrats aux entreprises 99,9 % de disponibilité à ses services par mois. En d’autres termes, sur un mois de 30 jours, seulement 43 minutes d’indisponibilité sont acceptées. Seulement voilà, la panne mondiale qui a touché Outlook, Teams, Copilot et SharePoint les 12 et 13 novembre derniers a duré près de 38 heures (sans parler des répercussions au-delà de Microsoft). Par conséquent, selon les conditions contractuelles de Microsoft, les entreprises concernées peuvent demander un avoir correspondant à 50 % du prix de leur abonnement éligible, la panne ayant entraîné une disponibilité inférieure à 99 % sur le mois concerné.
Pour être plus précis, le montant du crédit dépend du taux de disponibilité mensuel des services : il atteint 25 % du prix de l’abonnement lorsque celui-ci passe sous les 99,9 %, 50 % sous les 99 % et 100 % lorsque la disponibilité tombe sous les 95 %. Dans le cadre de la panne mondiale des 12 et 13 novembre derniers, nous sommes donc face à une disponibilité des services de Microsoft se situant aux alentours de 95,8 % (Microsoft calcule ce taux en minutes-utilisateurs). À quelques heures près, les entreprises privées de l’ensemble de ces services auraient donc pu bénéficier d’un remboursement total sur leur prochaine facture.
Attention toutefois, cette possibilité de dédommagement concerne seulement les entreprises (les particuliers ne peuvent pas effectuer de demande). Les abonnements Microsoft 365 Personnel et Famille, sans contrat de service, n’y ont par ailleurs pas droit. Autre point important à souligner : Microsoft ne prendra pas l’initiative de proposer cette compensation. C’est à l’administrateur Microsoft 365 de l’entreprise de faire la demande avant le 1er janvier 2027. Et si l’abonnement a été acheté chez un revendeur, c’est ce dernier qu’il faut contacter.
Comment faire une demande de dédommagement ?
Pour obtenir un avoir correspondant à 50 % du prix de l’abonnement, il faut dans un premier temps se rendre dans le centre d’administration Microsoft 365, puis cliquer sur « Support » et « Nouvelle demande de service » (New service request). Créez une nouvelle demande et intitulez-la, par exemple, « SLA service credit request », suivie de EX1550543 pour Exchange Online et de MO1550821 pour Teams, SharePoint, Copilot et les autres services touchés. N’indiquez la référence TM1550488 que si vos équipes ont été affectées par la panne de Teams survenue jeudi matin, laquelle concernait uniquement l’Amérique du Nord.
Enfin, indiquez l’heure de début et de fin de la coupure au sein de votre entreprise, ainsi que le nombre d’utilisateurs touchés.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Wired

articles.title: Uber’s Legal AI Agent Cuts Contract Review Time by 20% with Rules and RAG
articles.text:
Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent has reduced average contract review time by more than 20%, with 91% accuracy in AI-generated decisions, according to the company. Integrated into Microsoft Word, the agent analyzes proposed contract changes, assesses legal risks, and recommends policy-aligned responses using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic rules. Lawyers retain responsibility for reviewing and approving its recommendations.
The agent identifies edits proposed by external parties, interprets their intent, compares changes with legal policies, and suggests whether to accept, reject, or modify clauses. It also generates comments explaining recommendations and flags changes requiring closer scrutiny. Uber began developing the first generation in early 2024 and piloted it with its Legal team in 2025.
High-level workflow of the Legal Redlining Add-in / Agent (Source: Uber Blog Post)
An initial RAG implementation retrieved relevant sections from legal playbooks to guide language model responses. However, the system struggled with semantic retrieval accuracy, negotiation tone, and scenarios not covered by existing examples. Uber subsequently added a feedback loop that captures lawyers’ decisions, reasoning, and final edited text.
This change allowed the agent to retrieve examples of how similar clauses had been handled rather than relying only on whether a previous recommendation was accepted or rejected. At runtime, similarity search and metadata filtering narrow thousands of historical interactions to approximately 20 candidates. A second language model-based filtering stage evaluates their relevance. Exponential decay weighting, with a configurable half-life currently set to 365 days, prioritizes recent decisions while retaining older examples. The implementation also gives domain experts control over language and negotiation style.
Uber Engineering framed the challenge in its LinkedIn post:
How can AI help streamline repetitive contract review while keeping lawyers in control?
The legal team defines the desired tone and style, while engineers maintain the prompt structure and application workflow. The architecture combines a React and TypeScript Word add-in with a Python backend orchestrated through LangGraph. Parallel workflow nodes handle intent detection, risk assessment, and policy lookup. OpenSearch stores vectorized legal rules and historical feedback, while Redis maintains session state for follow-up questions.
Legal Redlining Agent system architecture (Source: Uber Blog Post)
A deterministic rules engine enforces non-negotiable legal requirements and overrides model recommendations when a matching rule applies. Language models handle tasks requiring contextual interpretation, including clause recommendations and negotiation tone. A final verification step checks generated responses against retrieved rules.
Uber is also exploring agentic harnesses, including Claude Code and OpenCode, alongside skills to structure and automate workflows across its agentic AI efforts. The team plans to investigate legal ontologies and knowledge graphs to represent legal concepts and relationships, providing a semantic foundation for more consistent interpretation and reasoning.

articles.title: FileZilla
articles.text:
FileZilla is a small but powerful FTP client with many features. it includes a site manager to store all your connection details and logins as well as an Explorer style interface that shows the local and remote folders and can be customized independently.
The program offers support for firewalls and proxy connections as well as SSL and Kerberos GSS security.
Additional features include keep alive, auto ascii/binary transfer and more. A nice program for beginners and advanced user alike.
Features
- Easy to use
- Supports FTP, FTP over SSL/TLS (FTPS) and SSH File Transfer Protocol (SFTP)
- Cross-platform. Runs on Windows, Linux, *BSD, macOS and more
- IPv6 support
- Available in many languages
- Supports resume and transfer of large files >4GB
- Tabbed user interface
- Powerful Site Manager and transfer queue
- Bookmarks
- Drag & drop support
- Configurable transfer speed limits
- Filename filters
- Directory comparison
- Network configuration wizard
- Remote file editing
- Keep-alive
- HTTP/1.1, SOCKS5 and FTP-Proxy support
- Logging to file
- Synchronized directory browsing
- Remote file search
You can download the Filezilla source code here.
What's New
- macOS: Fixed a regression in toolbar sizing with certain screen resolutions
- Updated to libfilezilla 0.59.0 and fzssh 1.5.2
- Fixed various crashes
- FTP over TLS: Add strict PROT P requirement, disconnect if input buffer is non-empty after AUTH
- MSW: File editing now disallows setting direct associations to cmd.exe and powershell.exe
- FTP: If the experimental "Strip VMS revisions" is set in filezilla.xml, filenames were not correctly sanitized when connecting to FTP servers configured with server type VMS in the Site Manager
- FTP: Passive mode data connections are now always established to the same IP address as the control connection, this can be reverted to previous behavior in the Site Manager on a per-site basis

articles.title: Moto G77 (256 GB) registra desconto agressivo de 40% na Black November • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Moto G77 (256 GB) registra desconto agressivo de 40% na Black November
Moto G77 conta com tela AMOLED de 5.000 nits, câmera principal de 108 MP e bateria prometida para até 37 horas de uso. Oferta com pagamento no Pix pelo Mercado Livre
O Moto G77 (256 GB) está em promoção com 40% de desconto no Mercado Livre. O smartphone sai por apenas R$ 1.499 no Pix em oferta na Black November 2026. Anunciado em março pela Motorola por R$ 2.499, se destaca pela ficha técnica equilibrada, com destaques para a tela brilhante e câmera principal de alta resolução.
O celular utiliza um painel Extreme AMOLED de 6,8″ que reproduz cores intensas, além de entregar resolução Super HD (superior ao Full HD) às imagens. O brilho máximo de 5.000 nits que o Moto G77 promete atingir em circunstâncias de baixa ou nenhuma luminosidade, sendo um dos mais fortes do segmento intermediário. Enquanto a taxa de 120 Hz assegura experiência fluida de modo geral.
O dispositivo traz uma câmera avançada de 108 MP. O sensor principal conta com estabilização óptica (OIS), zoom de 3x para manter a nitidez mesmo a distância, e recursos de IA via Moto AI. Na parte traseira, ainda há uma ultrawide de 8 MP. Enquanto a lente frontal de 32 MP, possui a função Detector de Sorrisos para aprimorar os resultados das selfies.
Equipado com o processador Dimensity 6400 e 8 GB de RAM física, o celular da Motorola com 256 GB de armazenamento entrega desempenho somente para tarefas básicas. Portanto, é mais voltado para usuários com pouco interesse para rodar jogos e executar multitarefas.
Em relação a construção, o celular utiliza uma carcaça de plástico combinado a certificação IP64, com resistência completa a poeira só que limitada a respingos d’água. Por outro lado, a certificação militar MIL-STD-810H garante a aprovação em condições extremas de pressão, temperatura e outras circunstâncias.
A bateria de 5.200 mAh sugere autonomia para mais de um dia de uso intenso, com promessa pela Motorola de até 37 horas de uso, incluindo reprodução de músicas e vídeos. O componente suporta apenas carregamento com fio de até 30 W.
O Moto G77 (256 GB) com promessa de atualizações até o sistema Android 19 está com 40% de desconto no Mercado Livre, por apenas R$ 1.499 no Pix.

articles.title: Detectify's Agentic Tooling lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running applications - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Detectify’s Agentic Tooling lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running applications
Swedish application security company Detectify AB today launched Agentic Tooling, a set of tools aimed at letting an organization’s own artificial intelligence agents test whether suspected vulnerabilities can be exploited in running applications.
A new Security Ledger, also part of the launch, is designed to record the evidence behind each test. Detectify is pitching the release at DevSecOps teams that are unsure whether they can trust what their AI agents report.
Detectify customers report that roughly 80% of the findings from their AI-driven static application security testing tools are noise. Under pressure to deliver an answer, an agent can also produce a convincing report about a test it never ran, the company warned.
Even before AI agents enter the picture, many security teams are falling behind. Nine in 10 open critical and high-severity vulnerabilities had stayed exposed for more than 90 days, according to Detectify’s H2 2026 Cyber Hygiene Index. In a study by researchers at Fudan University and Tencent Holdings Ltd., 76% of the static-analysis alerts examined were found to be false positives. Each one took developers 10 to 20 minutes to review.
Through Agentic Tooling, agents can tap the testing engines Detectify has built over more than a decade. Included are payload assessments sourced from its ethical hacker community, attack surface data from its Surface Monitoring product and Alfred, an AI system the company launched in March 2025 to automate tests for known vulnerabilities.
Running in a customer’s own environment, the tools connect to agents through either the Model Context Protocol or a command-line interface. They operate only on the data a customer provides and are said to work with whichever agent the customer already uses.
At the center of the design is loop engineering, an emerging practice of running AI agents in automated, repeating workflows rather than prompting them by hand. Kicking off each loop is a trigger such as a continuous integration run. Whether it comes from a code scan, a bug bounty report, a red team or Detectify’s own attack surface data, each finding is turned into a ticket.
Once an agent picks up a ticket, it reads the relevant code before testing the live application from the outside, as an attacker would. Run continuously, the loop becomes what Detectify calls a verification factory.
The requests sent, the payloads used and the results returned are all logged in the Security Ledger each time an agent uses Detectify’s tools. Written by Detectify rather than the agent, the append-only ledger lets teams separate findings backed by actual tests from unsupported AI conclusions. Any ticket that could cause harm, such as a denial-of-service test, is marked unsafe for a person to decide on.
“Ask an agent to write your code, then ask the same agent whether it’s secure. If it says yes, you don’t actually know,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Rickard Carlsson. There are plenty of examples of agents fabricating proof to please the person asking, according to Carlsson, who described Detectify’s aim as “building proof that an agent can’t fabricate.”
Available on request starting today, Agentic Tooling builds on the Detectify MCP Server that the company announced in May to give AI agents access to its security findings. Investors include Insight Partners, which took a majority stake in October 2024, along with Balderton Capital (UK) LLP, Inventure, First Fellow Partners Oy and SquareOne App Ltd.

articles.title: TCL CSOT Showcases Latest IJP OLED Developments and Display Innovations at DTC2026
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
TCL CSOT Showcases Latest IJP OLED Developments and Display Innovations at DTC2026
TCL CSOT's Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026) kicked off on November 13, 2026 in Wuhan. With this year's theme "True Vision, AI in Motion," the event brought together company executives, academics, and industry partners to explore how AI is reshaping display technology and preview the latest advances in TCL CSOT's APEX, IJP OLED, and AI-driven innovation.
Among those attending were Kevin Wang, Chief Executive Officer of TCL Technology; Jun Zhao, Senior Vice President of TCL Technology and Chief Executive Officer of TCL CSOT; Xiaolin Yan, Chief Technology Officer of TCL Technology and TCL CSOT; and Weigang Wan, science writer and winner of the Wenjin Book Award.In a video message to the conference, Li Dongsheng, Founder and Chairman of TCL, said: "AI has become a major force driving industrial transformation, fundamentally changing the way we work and live. TCL CSOT looks forward to working with more partners to deepen the integration of AI and display technologies and help shape a new future for the industry powered by AI."
In his opening remarks, Kevin Wang said: "At TCL, 'AI For Real' means taking AI beyond the lab and into real-world applications. By combining our industry expertise with our AI capabilities, we are able to translate technological advances into greater efficiency across R&D, manufacturing, and operations, delivering real value for our partners and end users."
User-Centric Display Innovation for the AI Era
At the heart of TCL CSOT's vision for the future of displays is APEX, the company's advanced display technology brand. In his keynote, Jun Zhao outlined the philosophy behind APEX and the four pillars on which the brand is built: Amazing Display Experience, Protective of Eye Health, Eco-friendly to Build and Use, and Unlimited Imaginative Potential. Based on these four pillars, APEX is committed to creating a better future through display innovations that faithfully reproduce the visual world while caring for the health of people and the planet.
At DTC2026, TCL CSOT showcased the latest advances across these pillars. Highlights included improvements in color reproduction, contrast, refresh rates and response times; natural-light, full-spectrum and low-glare technologies designed to support visual comfort; and energy-saving approaches using new backlight technologies, dynamic refresh rates, and zone-based control. Alongside these, new high-pixel-density near-eye displays and miniaturized full-color displays present more possibilities for AR and VR applications.
Beyond the new technologies driving improvements in pure display performance, a roundtable session explored the evolving role of screens in human-AI interaction. Jun Zhao, Xiaolin Yan, and Weigang Wan discussed the interplay between AI and display technologies and the screen's vital role as an interface between humans and AI.
The discussion also addressed how AI can move beyond current applications in chatbots and answer generation to contribute to real-world engineering problems. As Yan emphasized, the next stage in AI R&D would lie in "moving beyond optimizing what is already known to exploring the unknown."
AI is reshaping TCL CSOT's R&D, manufacturing and business operations, making R&D more intelligent, production more autonomous and precise, and decisions faster and more informed. These developments reflect two complementary directions the company is taking in its approach to AI. Through "AI for Display," TCL CSOT is applying AI to enhance R&D, manufacturing and operational efficiency. Through "Display for AI," the company is advancing display technologies to deliver better experiences on AI-powered devices.
Driving Innovation Through Display Ecosystem Integration
Advancing display technology requires collaboration across the value chain, from materials innovation and panel development to end-device applications. During this year's DTC, TCL CSOT was joined by a number of upstream and downstream partners who shared how their own innovations are ushering in the next generation of display technologies.
Representatives from TCL CSOT suppliers included Merck, who presented PB-Lens, a proof-of-concept planar optical lens made by coating reactive mesogen (RM) materials onto PET film, with potential applications in near-eye display imaging. 3M showcased a full-color diffractive waveguide solution for AR glasses and its Light Control Film for automotive OLED displays, designed to manage light direction and minimize reflections on vehicle windows. Summer Sprout presented its small-molecule red ink for IJP OLED.
Leading device manufacturers also showed how TCL CSOT's latest technology is already being integrated into gaming and portable computing products. Lenovo presented its Legion R9000P gaming laptop featuring a 16-inch IJP OLED display with a 240 Hz refresh rate, and MSI showed its Claw 8 EX AI+ handheld gaming device equipped with an 8-inch display supporting a 120 Hz refresh rate and Variable Refresh Rate (VRR).
Taking IJP OLED from the Lab to Life
During a dedicated session on IJP OLED, Xiaolin Yan unveiled TCL CSOT's latest progress in display performance, visual comfort, and sustainability. Major technology breakthroughs include combining a Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement and wide color gamut with hardware-level blue-light reduction and anti-glare features to enhance viewing quality. On the manufacturing side, high material utilization and low emissions further support resource efficiency and sustainability. TCL CSOT is also optimizing materials, device structures, and manufacturing processes to improve luminous efficiency and device lifetime.
On October 31, 2026, TCL CSOT began moving equipment into its next-generation IJP OLED production line. The line is expected to enter mass production and begin shipments in the fourth quarter of 2027, marking an important step toward broader commercialization.
Among the IJP OLED innovations showcased at DTC2026 was the 27-inch IJP OLED Oxide Internal Compensation QHD 500 Hz Gaming Display. Combining IJP OLED technology with an oxide backplane and the world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation technology, the display supports refresh rates up to 500 Hz. The in-panel compensation system operates seamlessly in the background, making real-time adjustments without the need for periodic compensation while the screen is powered off. Further optimization of the compensation circuitry and printing processes enhances refresh-rate performance and image uniformity. With a response time of less than 1 ms, the display delivers exceptional clarity and smooth motion for next-generation gaming.
Other IJP OLED products on display included three flagship display products spanning large-screen, mobile and tablet applications. The 115-inch World's Highest Image Quality 16K 2D/3D-Compatible Light Field TV Display uses a proprietary light-field optical architecture to deliver glasses-free 3D viewing with a viewing angle of at least 90 degrees, creating an extended depth of field for multiple viewers simultaneously. The display's native 16K resolution and a 3D light-field resolution of up to 8K, together with its proprietary image enhancement algorithm, allow the display to switch between glasses-free 3D and standard 2D content without compromising 2D picture quality. The 6.36-inch World's First Blue Phosphorescent OLED Mobile Display uses a blue phosphorescent material system with PSF sensitization to boost luminous efficiency by approximately 40% and reduce EL power consumption by approximately 20% at the same luminance. The 10.95-inch World's First Full-Angle Lossless Privacy OLED Tablet Display features a dual-pixel architecture and pixel-level optical path control to provide active 360-degree privacy protection without compromising image quality.
Also on display was a prototype of the 14-inch IJP OLED Ultra-Thin Low-Reflection Notebook Display. Measuring less than 0.66 mm thick and weighing under 66 grams—50% lighter than conventional displays—it incorporates TCL CSOT's Low-Reflection Anti-Glare Eye-Care Technology to achieve an ultra-low reflection rate of less than 1%.
From new technologies and improvements in manufacturing to the latest consumer and professional displays, DTC2026 showed how TCL CSOT is using its APEX vision, ecosystem collaboration, and ongoing progress in AI and IJP OLED to bridge cutting-edge display innovation with industry demand. Looking ahead, the company will continue to drive innovation and work with partners worldwide to advance the display industry in the AI era.

articles.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
articles.text:
On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration’s purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government’s actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications.
The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision.
The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn’t bothered to define DEI, and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search.
In the wake of a Supreme Court decision that held that most grant termination cases had to be heard by a different court, the case was narrowed considerably to just seven UC researchers and a handful of agencies: The Environmental Protection Agency, the National Science Foundation, and the National Endowment for the Humanities.

articles.title: Canadian law firm considering class-action against Microsoft over outage
articles.text:
Frustrated Canadians who experienced problems during a recent Microsoft outage could be part of a potential class-action lawsuit against the tech giant.
Consumer Law Group (CLG), a law firm with offices in Ottawa and Montreal, announced Monday that it is investigating a class-action lawsuit against Microsoft after a global outage affected Microsoft services, including Teams.
The Issue
The outage began on Nov. 12, with hundreds of thousands of North American users reporting issues with Outlook, as well as other services like Teams and Copilot. Microsoft confirmed on X that issues may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region and said it was “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact.
According to CLG, Microsoft managed to restore service for some users, but issues persisted into Nov. 13, “and crippled communications for individuals, governments, and businesses worldwide.” It’s considered one of the longest disruptions in Microsoft’s history.
Canadians were among the hundreds of millions of users impacted, with the outage preventing them from managing calendars, sending and receiving emails, and hosting virtual meetings.
“Consumer Law Group believes action must be taken for all individuals who were unable to use Microsoft Outlook and/or Teams and experienced damages as a result,” states CLG.
What should you do next?
Canadians who experienced problems during the outages can sign up to receive updates on the potential class action, including information about its progress and any possible compensation.
You’ll be asked for your contact details and information about any damages or symptoms you experienced. Visit CLG’s website for details.
With files from Bradley Shankar
