articles.title: India’s deeptech funding record faces a test of scale: Speciale Invest report
articles.text:
India’s deeptech funding record faces a test of scale: Speciale Invest
India’s deeptech funding hit $914 million in 2025, but limited growth capital, manufacturing dependencies and weak commercialisation pathways continue to hinder startups from scaling.
India’s deeptech companies raised $914 million in 257 rounds in 2025, 34 times the 2016 level. The harder test is turning research and prototypes into commercial products, notes Speciale Invest’s report, India’s Deep Tech Revolution - From the Lab to Growth and Exits.
Using Tracxn data through August 31 2026, the study covers 8,293 private companies worldwide, including 482 in India. India accounted for 12.8% of deeptech funding rounds in 2025 but received 1.6% of the capital.
For every 100 seed rounds, India had 23 Series A or B rounds, against 105 globally. Separately, there was one late-stage or private-equity round per 100 Indian seed rounds, against 26 worldwide. Both measures point to funding thinning as companies mature.
Sectoral advantages are uneven. Space firms can tap ISRO testing facilities and suppliers, while life-sciences ventures can draw on India’s pharmaceutical manufacturing base. Private participation in space has widened since 2020 reforms. Registered space startups rose from one in 2014 to about 440 by August 2026.
In July, Skyroot’s Vikram-I became the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit from Indian soil. It was a milestone, though one launch does not establish a repeatable commercial business.
The report says battery makers still rely on imported cells and materials. Separately, Exide commissioned phase one of a 6 GWh Bengaluru cell plant in September. Semiconductor developers remain reliant on overseas fabrication and packaging. Semicon 2.0, approved in July with Rs 1,27,500 crore, aims to expand domestic capacity; the first fab is due in 2028.
The six-year Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Scheme aims to finance high-risk technology. By July 2026, the Technology Development Board had approved 22 projects with Rs 2,192 crore in support. Assistance is mainly through low-interest long-term loans, equity and equity-linked instruments, rather than standard grants.
Turning a successful pilot, or customer trial, into an order remains difficult. Vishesh Rajaram, managing partner at Speciale Invest, said, “Large companies and public-sector buyers can help turn those trials into commercial orders by agreeing upfront on what a pilot must prove and when they’ll make a purchase decision. A first order lets a startup plan production and commit to suppliers.”
Growth capital is smaller too. Indian Series A and B rounds averaged $11.5 million from January to August 2026, against $55.5 million globally, said Vishnu Rajeev, investment partner at Speciale Invest.
“That gap matters when a founder needs to qualify a product with a major customer or commission a production line before commercial revenue is predictable, Rajeev adds. He argues funding should match milestone costs, with project finance once customers make firm commitments.
The report urges faster funding decisions, shared testing facilities, more domestic Series B and C investors, and plant finance before pilots end. It also considers listings, acquisitions, licensing and secondary share sales as exit routes.
Deeptech needs not just research funding, but reliable customers and patient growth capital.

articles.title: Votre ancienne Apple TV reçoit Siri AI, mais les utilisateurs français restent sur la touche
articles.text:
Avec tvOS 27.2.1, Apple apporte Siri AI aux Apple TV 4K de 2021 et 2022. Une bonne nouvelle pour ceux souhaitant prolonger leur box TV, même si cette nouveauté reste inaccessible en France.
Pas besoin de remplacer son boîtier pour profiter du nouveau Siri AI. Alors que la dernière Apple TV 4K arrive dans les salons, Apple ouvre aussi son assistant aux deux générations précédentes. La mise à jour est disponible depuis le vendredi 13 novembre, mais son installation ne suffira pas à débloquer l’IA chez nous. L’explication se trouve du côté de l’iPhone.
Les anciennes Apple TV profitent aussi du nouveau Siri
Comme le rapporte MacRumors, tvOS 27.2.1 active la compatibilité avec Siri AI sur les Apple TV 4K de deuxième et troisième générations. Les modèles commercialisés en 2021 et 2022 rejoignent ainsi le nouveau boîtier, qui bénéficie déjà de l’assistant avec une version spécifique de tvOS 27.2.
Apple promet une meilleure compréhension des demandes, des suggestions tenant compte du contexte personnel, notamment avec la récente introduction des profils utilisateurs sur tvOS, et des réponses à des questions dépassant la simple recherche d’un film ou d’une série.
Mais cette compatibilité ne signifie pas que les anciens boîtiers exécutent seuls toutes ces fonctions. De la même manière que pour la configuration, Siri AI nécessite un iPhone ou un iPad associé, compatible avec Apple Intelligence et sur lequel le nouvel assistant est activé. Si votre iPhone est trop vieux, il faudra donc en changer pour bénéficier de la meilleure expérience sur l’écran du salon.
Il faut également distinguer logiciel et matériel. La mise à jour n’ajoute évidemment pas aux anciens modèles les microphones intégrés à la nouvelle génération, qui permettent de s’adresser directement au boîtier à distance. La télécommande restera le seul point d’accès à Siri, sauf à utiliser votre iPhone comme « zapette » de luxe.
En France, la mise à jour garde tout de même un intérêt
Cette dépendance à l’iPhone et à l’iPad explique la limite géographique. Comme pour l’ouverture de Siri AI aux applications tierces, l’indisponibilité de l’assistant sur ces appareils dans l’Union européenne empêche d’en profiter sur l’Apple TV. Changer de génération de boîtier ne résout donc pas le problème.
Les utilisateurs français ont néanmoins une raison d’installer tvOS 27.2.1. La fiche de sécurité publiée par Apple recense sept vulnérabilités corrigées, concernant notamment Bluetooth, AirPlay et l’accès aux données personnelles.
Certaines pouvaient permettre à un appareil Bluetooth malveillant de s’appairer sans intervention de l’utilisateur. D’autres autorisaient le contournement des limites de tentatives de codes d’appairage, à portée Bluetooth ou depuis le même réseau pour AirPlay. Apple ne signale pas d’exploitation active de ces failles dans cette fiche.
Pour installer la mise à jour, rendez-vous dans Réglages > Système > Mises à jour logicielles > Mettre à jour les logiciels. Siri AI attendra encore pour les utilisateurs français ; les correctifs, eux, sont déjà disponibles.

articles.title: 15e vol du Starship : SpaceX révèle des vidéos inédites de la fusée géante lors de sa capture historique en plein vol
articles.text:
Le samedi 14 novembre a été historique pour SpaceX. Pour la première fois, l’entreprise est parvenue à rattraper l’étage supérieur de sa fusée géante avec les bras de sa tour de lancement, au Texas, après environ 22 heures et demie de vol et 14 tours de la Terre. Aucun étage supérieur de fusée orbitale n’avait encore été récupéré de cette façon.
Naturellement, SpaceX communique beaucoup dessus. Après avoir partagé plusieurs photographies, y compris des clichés du Ship au sol, la société a mis en ligne une série de vidéos inédites sur X ce lundi 16 novembre. Elles montrent l’arrivée du vaisseau au niveau de la tour, l’une des phases les plus délicates du vol, avec notamment des plans depuis l’engin et sur la tour.
Moins d’une minute entre les nuages et la tour
Parmi les clips les plus remarquables, on en retrouve deux figurant dans un tweet invitant à « ne pas paniquer » (« Don’t Panic »). Cette formule peinte sur la coque du Ship 42 est un clin d’œil au Guide du voyageur galactique de Douglas Adams, roman où le nombre 42 tient aussi une place centrale.
Les caméras embarquées montrent l’approche finale depuis l’engin alors qu’il redescend sur Terre, à l’horizontale, avant de traverser une couche nuageuse, puis de se redresser en position verticale. Le tout va très vite : en moins d’une minute, le Ship termine sa course entre les bras mécaniques de la tour, et coupe ses moteurs.
Le second montre le rattrapage vu depuis Mechazilla, le surnom que SpaceX donne à sa tour et à ses bras mécaniques. Le vaisseau paraît d’abord fort loin à l’image, avant de grossir rapidement, tandis que trois de ses six moteurs Raptor manœuvrent pour réorienter le Ship 42. Un autre plan, un peu plus bas, montre mieux les bras en action.
Historiquement, SpaceX avait déjà attrapé trois fois son propulseur Super Heavy, le premier étage de la fusée. Le vaisseau est toutefois plus difficile à saisir, car il redescend de beaucoup plus haut et beaucoup plus vite. Il doit en outre survivre à la rentrée atmosphérique, une séquence qui met son bouclier thermique à rude épreuve.
Il n’y a pas eu de capture du propulseur pendant ce même vol. Celui-ci a fini dans le golfe du Mexique au lieu d’être rattrapé.
Elon Musk, patron de SpaceX, a estimé que le bouclier thermique du Ship 42 « a l’air super » et que le vaisseau pourrait revoler après quelques semaines de remise en état. Il reconnaît toutefois que « de nombreuses petites corrections » restent nécessaires pour arriver à une réutilisation immédiate.

articles.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
articles.text:
Ride-hailing company Uber is notifying nearly 150,000 drivers that attackers stole their data after breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks in early October.
In breach notification letters sent to affected individuals on November 10, Uber said threat actors accessed their personal information after breaching an Uber account with a third-party service provider.
While Uber didn't share the total number of affected drivers in these letters, it revealed in a filing with Maine's Office of the Attorney General that the data breach has exposed the information of 149,346 drivers, including their names, driver’s license numbers, dates of birth, and addresses.
After being informed of the breach, Uber launched an investigation and severed data connections with the service provider to block further malicious access to its data.
"On October 9, 2026, a service provider notified Uber that an unauthorized third party had compromised the service provider's internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account with the service provider," Uber said. "After being notified of this incident, Uber immediately severed data connections with the service provider and launched an investigation. On October 13, 2026, our investigation determined that the unauthorized party had used the compromised credentials to access Uber data connected to the service provider."
Although the company didn't directly name the hacked service provider, TechCrunch first reported that the Uber data breach stems from an October 24 security incident at AI training provider Fireworks, which was hacked after a third-party cloud provider hack.
Fireworks has attributed the attack to a financially motivated cybercriminal threat actor group linked to a series of large language model hijacking (LLMjacking) attacks.
The Fireworks breach also led to security incidents at AI coding platform Cursor and digital workspace platform Notion, which also reported that the attackers stole data from a limited number of customers and (in Cursor's case) infected users' devices with backdoor malware.
An Uber spokesperson was not immediately available for comment when BleepingComputer reached out for more information about the data breach.
The company disclosed another data breach in December 2022 after a threat actor leaked IT asset information, employees' email addresses, and corporate reports stolen from third-party service provider Teqtivity.
Uber previously confirmed that hackers who breached some of its systems in October 2016 stole data from 50 million users and 7 million drivers, and that the Lapsus$ extortion group also hacked it in September 2022 in an MFA fatigue attack using the stolen credentials of an Uber EXT contractor.

articles.title: Los fontaneros expertos avisan: si abres el grifo y cae un chorro de agua débil, el problema ya ha comenzado y puede ser peor de lo que parece
articles.text:
Que el agua salga del grifo con menos fuerza de la habitual puede parecer una molestia menor, pero también puede ser el primer aviso de que algo no funciona en la instalación de tu casa. Y detrás de este problema puede haber muchas cosas, desde un aireador sucio hasta una fuga. Aquí, los fontaneros advierten que no siempre se trata de una avería grave, aunque tampoco conviene dejar pasar semanas antes de mirarlo.
Un grifo o toda la casa. Lo primero es averiguar hasta dónde llega el problema, si es cosa de la fontanería de tu casa o de la red. Por ejemplo, si es solo un grifo ya sabes que el problema está en casa, pero si afecta a toda la vivienda pueden ser más cosasa, desde una llave de paso mal abierta a unas tuberías envejecidas, pasando incluso por un problema en la red pública. Y también importa si el bajón se nota sólo con el agua caliente o en todo.
La cal del aireador. Cuando el culpable es un único grifo, lo más probable es que la pieza que tiene en la boca, el aireador, se haya ido llenando de cal y otras partículas. Lo mismo pasa si el problema sucede solo en las alcachofas de la ducha. La solución es bastante sencilla, y basta con desenroscarlo, dejarlo un rato en vinagre, frotarlo con un cepillo de dientes viejo, aclararlo bien y volver a colocarlo. Eso sí, si el chorro sigue flojo toca revisar la llave de paso de ese grifo, que puede haberse quedado medio cerrada tras una reparación o un golpe accidental.
Cuando falla toda la casa. Las tuberías antiguas, sobre todo las de acero galvanizado, van acumulando depósitos por dentro que acaban estrechando el paso del agua, que también recuerda que la llave general tiene que quedar abierta del todo después de cualquier trabajo de fontanería. Vamos, que el tubo se va estrechando por dentro. Otra posibilidad es que falle la válvula reductora de presión, y en ese caso lo recomendable es que lo revise un fontanero.
La fuga que no se ve. Pero lo complicado llega cuando tenemos una fuga, porque puede manifestarse como una pérdida de presión antes de que aparezca ningún charco. Hay otras pistas, como una factura que sube sin que hayas cambiado tus hábitos, manchas de humedad o pintura que se levanta. Y las paredes que siguen húmedas también son un aviso, algo que la Agencia de Protección Ambiental de Estados Unidos pide vigilar en su lista para detectar fugas.
Agua caliente y pozos. ¿Y si sólo pierde fuerza el agua caliente? Pues entonces conviene mirar el termo o el acumulador, donde se van depositando sedimentos. En las viviendas con pozo, el fallo puede estar en la bomba o en el presostato, que puede quedarse atascado y dejar la casa sin presión, o en un filtro sucio, que también puede restar presión.
Y antes de llamar a nadie, merece la pena preguntar a los vecinos. Si ellos tienen una presión normal, el problema está en tu casa, pero si les pasa lo mismo puede deberse a una rotura en una conducción principal o a un pico de consumo en la zona, o incluso trabajos de mantenimiento en la red. En estos casos, lo que toca es consultar a la compañía de abastecimiento, porque por mucho que revises las tuberías de casa no vas a encontrar nada.

articles.title: El FSD de Tesla es ilegal en casi todo el mundo, así que 80 conductores han hecho un jailbrake para desbloquearlo. Se enfrentan a dos años de cárcel
articles.text:
80 personas han sido detenidas en Corea del Sur. El motivo: llegar donde Tesla no ha llegado. Ilegalmente, claro. Porque 80 dueños de coches de la marca estadounidense habrían activado ilegalmente el sistema Full Self Driving (FSD, por sus siglas en inglés) en sus coches. Un sistema que, al menos de momento, no está permitido utilizar en el país.
¿Qué ha pasado? Cuentan nuestros compañeros de Motorpasión que 80 conductores de Tesla han sido detenidos por utilizar el FSD, el sistema más avanzado de ayuda a la conducción de la marca, en sus coches. El problema es que este sistema es ilegal en el país y no ha obtenido el visto bueno de los reguladores para ser utilizado. O no, al menos, para todos los coches.
El FSD. El FSD es el sistema de ayuda a la conducción más avanzado de Tesla. Éste permite seleccionar un destino y que el coche nos lleve de forma autónoma, sin tener que poner las manos en el volante o pisar los pedales. El sistema también está activo en zonas urbanas pero obliga siempre a prestar atención a lo que ocurre alrededor y estar en alerta para poder tomar el mando en cualquier momento.
Desde hace meses, la Unión Europea está estudiando su aceptación en los países miembros pero algunos de ellos están reflejando dudas sobre su seguridad o quieren obligar a Tesla a que quite la opción para que el coche se salte los límites de seguridad automáticamente. De momento y por muchos rumores que se han publicado, el FSD sigue sin estar activo en la Unión Europea.
Made in... La clave de todo este lío está en dónde se produjeron estos coches. Realmente, Corea del Sur sí permite utilizar el sistema FSD de Tesla pero de sólo en aquellos coches que han sido fabricados en Estados Unidos y, por tanto, se han importado desde el país. Según cálculos de la empresa de investigación de mercado automotriz Carisyou Data Lab recogidos por los medios locales, estaríamos hablando de alrededor del 20% de los Tesla vendidos en el país.
Y es que en Corea del Sur hay contabilizados alrededor de 229.000 Tesla, sin embargo, sólo algo más de 47.000 unidades pueden utilizar este sistema. Estos son los Tesla Model S y X importados desde Estados Unidos, los Tesla Model 3 y Model Y salidos de las fábricas chinas y europeas quedan fuera de esta aprobación.
¿Qué han hecho? Para poder utilizar este sistema, a los detenidos se les acusa de haber hackeado el coche con dispositivos que permitían desbloquear estas funciones avanzadas de ayuda a la conducción. Con ellas podían circular con todas las ventajas del sistema y, por tanto, ceder el control al vehículo por completo incluso en áreas residenciales.
Señalan en InsideEVs que la mayoría de los conductores habrían comprado los dispositivos para romper el sistema de seguridad de Tesla pero que algunos de ellos, siguiendo tutoriales en GitHub, habrían conseguido crear sus propios dispositivos y desbloquear estas funciones.
¿Es un riesgo? Por su puesto. Y es que romper el sistema de seguridad de Tesla y utilizarlo como si se hubiera pagado por él legalmente puede provocar errores en el reconocimiento que el vehículo hace del entorno. Esto es clave porque dependiendo del tráfico y de elementos como los peatones o la luz de los semáforos, el coche actúa de una u otra manera.
¿A qué se enfrentan? Ahora, según el medio local Korea JoongAng Daily, los conductores ahora se enfrentan a una pena de cárcel de dos años y una multa de unos 14.000 euros (20 millones de wones). Además, las autoridades ya han señalado que se mantienen activas para encontrar más infractores por lo que las detenciones no podrían haber quedado aquí.

articles.title: Uber says hackers stole information on close to 150,000 driver's licenses during data breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Uber is notifying close to 150,000 drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.
In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California and Iowa, the ride-hailing giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.
The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.
The stolen data includes affected drivers’ names, addresses, dates of birth, and driver’s license numbers.
TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open-weight AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.
Online productivity startup Notion and AI coding startup Cursor have both confirmed that they had data stolen during the Fireworks hack.
In Uber’s case, the company said it had alerts enabled to detect unauthorized access to its Fireworks environment, but because the hackers used Fireworks’ own internal credentials, “no alerts were triggered.”
When reached for comment, an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch: “The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” and deferred our questions to Fireworks.
A spokesperson for Fireworks confirmed that the company identified a security issue involving unauthorized access to some of its systems, which affected customer data, but the spokesperson did not address our questions about the incident.
Fireworks attributed its breach to a financially motivated cybercriminal group whose goals are to sell stolen tokens for accessing large language models, or LLMs. No known cybercriminal group has taken credit for the data theft.
In a notice filed with Oregon’s attorney general, Uber said it notified 149,346 people in total that their information had been taken in the breach at Fireworks.
TechCrunch previously reported that Uber has notified drivers in California, Illinois, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and South Carolina. We’ve also seen data breach notices filed in Texas and Vermont.
When asked by TechCrunch, Uber’s spokesperson did not say how many drivers are affected by the breach, nor how many drivers it was notifying about the incident.
It’s unclear if the number of affected drivers is expected to rise, and Uber did not respond to a follow-up email sent Monday.
This is Uber’s second known data breach this year. The company reported a security incident at its Uber Freight truck shipping unit, for which an extortion gang took credit for stealing data.
First published on November 13, and updated with a response from Fireworks, and again with a new updated figure of affected individuals from Oregon’s attorney general.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage led to chlorine gas leak at German hotel, poisoning of 15 guests and sending four to hospital
articles.text:
WTF?! The recent global outage of Microsoft 365 services affected millions across the world, but the impact on people varied enormously. Take, for example, the 15 guests at a hotel in Germany who were exposed to a chlorine gas leak as a result of the debacle. That sounds a lot worse than not being able to use Teams.
According to regional publication WDR (via Notebookcheck), the incident happened at the Hotel Ling Bao, part of Phantasialand theme park in Germany. It experienced a malfunction with its dosing system, which pumped too much chlorine into the pool.
The facility uses a maintenance safety system in its sauna area that sends emails warning when chlorine levels are too high. But because of the Microsoft 365 service disruption, the emails never arrived.
Forty first responders were dispatched to the incident. Fifteen people required triage due to respiratory irritation, four were taken to the hospital, and one had to remain under observation due to an injury.
The disruption began on November 12, when users around the world started reporting problems with Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Copilot. Downdetector received nearly 150,000 complaints, while Microsoft said its servers were experiencing unusually heavy loads. Outlook users couldn't send emails or access their inboxes, and some servers went offline again after being restored.
In Japan, businesses and government agencies were forced to dig out fax machines and landline phones when cloud services stopped working. The country's shared government IT infrastructure was also disrupted. Xbox users struggled to sign in, launch digital games, and synchronize cloud saves.
 – Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 14, 2026
Microsoft has now revealed that the outage was caused by a software defect introduced in July, which went undetected for more than three months. A surge in server traffic, combined with reduced network capacity, triggered the bug and caused more than 80% of the affected gateway servers to become unresponsive within two hours. The company admitted that its testing had failed to catch the problem.
While software failures can cause inconvenience and financial losses, there are often more serious consequences like this one. In July 2024, a faulty CrowdStrike update caused Windows systems worldwide to crash. Hospitals couldn't book patients, some 911 emergency call centers were affected, and airlines grounded flights.
In one of the strongest examples of software failures destroying lives, bugs in the UK's Horizon accounting system contributed to wrongful convictions of hundreds of Post Office workers. Some were imprisoned, many suffered financial ruin, and the scandal was linked to at least four suicides.
In 2018, Wells Fargo revealed that a software error had incorrectly denied mortgage modifications to around 625 customers who should have qualified for them. The mistake had devastating consequences, with approximately 400 borrowers losing their homes through foreclosure.

articles.title: ChatGPT can now buy things using your credit card — I thought it was a terrible idea, but after seeing how it works, I'm starting to change my mind
articles.text:
ChatGPT can now buy things for you with your credit card — and watching it complete a purchase in seconds makes the future of online shopping feel very real
ChatGPT using your credit card works exactly as you’d want it to
My first reaction to the idea of letting ChatGPT use my debit or credit card was an immediate no. The thought of giving an AI agent access to my money, and wondering what it might start buying without my permission, wasn't particularly appealing. But after watching OpenAI's demo of how ChatGPT handles purchases, and what it does with your bank details, I'm actually feeling a lot less worried.
OpenAI has just launched ChatGPT Wallet. It’s a digital wallet that its agents (called dots) can use to pay for things. They can’t just start buying things willy-nilly though — each payment requires a security check. ChatGPT Wallet has been built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa and currently requires a ChatGPT Pro account in the US to use. Additionally users must be aged 18 or over with eligible US-issued cards.
Over on the OpenAI announcement about the new feature, there’s a video showing how it works — and it looks exactly as low-friction as you’d have hoped. You ask ChatGPT to find you something, it searches using its dots agent, finds something suitable, then reports back at which point you decide to buy and a payment screen pops up for you to approve.
What makes it reassuring
What's particularly reassuring is that ChatGPT's agent never actually gets to see your card details. Instead, the payment network creates a substitute set of payment credentials for each approved purchase, meaning your real card information isn't shared with the AI agent or the retailer. You also retain your usual card rewards and protections for eligible disputes. That's a pretty important distinction, and one that makes me feel considerably more comfortable about the whole idea.
As smooth as the demo is, I would still expect some hiccups in the real world. To be useful in the real world, the payment system needs to avoid being blocked by websites and recognized as a legitimate purchase made by the agent.
To help achieve this OpenAI says, “We’re starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro users, so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability.”
Christmas shopping
While a FaceID or fingerprint security check is needed right now, OpenAI says that over time it expects people will be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters, like spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
OpenAI is going to need to do a lot of work going forward with banks, businesses and payment networks to ensure that its agent payments work smoothly all the time. We’re still at the very beginnings of agent payments, and we still need to understand if the demand from people to use a service like this is there as well.
Would I trust an AI agent to do my Christmas shopping? I'm not sure I would right now, but having seen how ChatGPT Wallet works, I'm certainly more open to the idea than I was before. For now, I'm happy to let AI find things for me and leave the actual buying to me. But give it a few years, prove the safeguards work, and I might just be persuaded to let ChatGPT loose on my Christmas list.

articles.title: Tesla fait machine arrière et vend finalement son Cybercab, mais à une condition très coûteuse
articles.text:
Tesla avait longuement vanté le Cybercab comme la solution de transport ultime permettant de se déplacer souplement d’un endroit à l’autre sans contrainte. Il suffisait de passer commande pour se faire conduire, ni plus ni moins. La promesse est alléchante, mais néanmoins hors de portée : la marque a toujours affirmé que le véhicule ne sera jamais vendu aux particuliers.
Pourtant, il semblerait que le constructeur rétropédale sur le sujet. Un petit peu, du moins… Des personnes sélectionnées sur le volet ont en effet reçu un e-mail d’invitation menant droit à une page de commande du Cybercab. Sur une interface assez similaire à celle des autres modèles Tesla, on y trouve donc le véhicule affiché au prix de 29 990 $. Il s’agit de fait de la voiture la moins chère du catalogue, la Model 3 étant vendue à 36 990 $ au minimum.
Le gros piège caché derrière ce prix plancher
Si un acompte non remboursable de 1 000 $ est requis pour passer commande, il ne faudra guère se montrer patient pour recevoir son jouet : les livraisons sont pour le moment prévues pour décembre ! Un délai éclair qui contraste grandement avec les heures fastes de la Model 3. Le Cybercab a donc juste sur toute la ligne. Tenons-nous enfin la petite Tesla pas chère tant attendue ? Pas vraiment…
Car il y a une immense condition pour pouvoir utiliser le véhicule. Vu que l’engin est livré sans volant ni pédales, il sera une nouvelle fois entièrement autonome. Et forcément, cela demande une certaine quantité d’énergie que la marque ne manquera pas de vous facturer ! Acheter une bonne fois pour toutes la voiture puis l’utiliser en illimité était bien trop beau pour être vrai. Comment en effet justifier l’utilisation sur demande d’un Cybercab, alors ?
299 $ par mois et des zones géographiques limitées : la douche froide
Après avoir dépensé 29 990 $, vous voilà donc avec un abonnement imposé à 299 $ par mois. N’espérez pas contourner la chose, les petites lignes indiquent explicitement qu’il s’agit d’un passage obligé : « abonnement et entretien régulier du véhicule requis pour l’utilisation ». Le loyer éternel est une chose, les restrictions d’usage en sont une autre. Car vous ne pourrez pas vous balader n’importe où avec le Cybercab.
L’email indique aussi que le véhicule est « disponible uniquement dans les zones couvertes par le service ». Cela comprend huit villes : Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth et San Antonio. Pire encore, la couverture n’est pas intégrale dans les zones précitées. Mieux vaut donc bien se renseigner avant de passer commande, au risque de se retrouver avec une voiture entièrement payée, mais complètement inutilisable.

articles.title: No pagó el alquiler casi cuatro años y la casera no reparó las humedades: la Audiencia rebaja la deuda en un tercio
articles.text:
La inquilina había denunciado los problemas de humedad de su vivienda. Sin embargo, sin que la propietaria hubiese subsanado estos problemas, dejó de abonar el alquiler. Finalmente, la dueña le reclamó 31.340,07 euros por las rentas pendientes (de mayo de 2020 a marzo de 2024). En la Audiencia Provincial de Barcelona se ha confirmado el deber de pago de la inquilina. Sin embargo, han rebajado la cuota a pagar en un tercio. La arrendadora también tuvo algunos problemas de incumplimiento.
El contrato se firmó en noviembre de 2017 y duraba tres años. La renta era de 650 euros inicialmente. En el momento de este proceso era de 666,81 euros.
La propietaria (Patrimonis Bersach, S.L.) ha reclamado los impagados y, por su parte, la inquilina pidió 6.000 euros por daños. En primera instancia, el juzgado ha fallado a favor de la empresa. Las costas las pone a cargo de la arrendataria.
Los problemas de humedad eran insuficientes para dejar de pagar toda la renta
Los técnicos han manifestado las deficiencias, aunque hay algunas discrepancias. El perito de la propiedad ha constatado la presencia de hongos en la pared de la fachada. Ha hablado de “ambiente muy cargado”. Además, ha señalado que falta ventilación. La empresa para la que trabaja ha presupuestado la obra por 1.800 euros.
Por otro lado, la arquitecta técnica (que actuó a petición de la inquilina) hizo un análisis visual. Indicó que había filtraciones del baño de arriba. También destacó que existían humedades por condensación (en sala y dormitorio) y concluyó que no estaba en condiciones mínimas de habitabilidad.
La Audiencia ha considerado que no estaba en condiciones de inhabitabilidad. La inquilina siguió viviendo en el piso y, por eso, no puede quedar liberada de su obligación de pagar.
Asimismo, está comprobado que la propietaria tenía la obligación de subsanar los problemas. En la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (artículo 21) se establece que corresponderá al arrendador efectuar todas las obras y reparaciones que sean precisas para mantener la vivienda en estado de habitabilidad, excepto aquellas que sean atribuibles al inquilino.
El magistrado que no está de acuerdo propone una indemnización
Roberto García Ceniceros coincide en que debe pagar la inquilina. Sin embargo, no acepta la rebaja. En su voto particular considera que el deber de reparar “no es mesurable”. Es decir, o se cumple o no. Considera que la ley permite resolver el contrato y pedir una indemnización; sin embargo, no debe cambiar el precio.
Propondría mantener los 31.340,07 euros. Asimismo, aceptaría los 6.000 euros de daño moral. Ambos se compensarían. Quedarían en 25.340,07 euros. Señala que la rebaja (de 10.446,69 euros) es superior a la indemnización solicitada.

articles.title: Apagão da Microsoft leva à contaminação por gás cloro; entenda • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apagão da Microsoft leva à contaminação por gás cloro; entenda
Falha no dosador elevou o nível de cloro na piscina de um hotel na Alemanha. Alerta enviado por e-mail não chegou aos funcionários durante a pane do Outlook.
Quinze pessoas foram afetadas por uma exposição a níveis elevados de cloro na piscina de um hotel na Alemanha. O incidente ocorreu durante a pane global que deixou Outlook e outros serviços da Microsoft instáveis. A interrupção impediu que um alerta automático sobre o problema chegasse aos funcionários do estabelecimento.
O caso aconteceu no Hotel Ling Bao, que faz parte do parque temático Phantasialand, na cidade de Brühl. Segundo a emissora alemã WDR, uma falha no sistema automático de dosagem fez com que uma quantidade excessiva de cloro fosse despejada na piscina.
O sistema de segurança responsável por monitorar a manutenção da área detectou o problema e enviou um aviso por e-mail aos funcionários. Como o Outlook e o Exchange Online estavam fora do ar, a mensagem não foi entregue. A equipe só percebeu que havia algo errado depois que pessoas na piscina começaram a apresentar problemas respiratórios.
Equipes de emergência e bombeiros foram acionados para atender as vítimas. Ao todo, 15 pessoas passaram por avaliação médica, a maioria com irritação nas vias respiratórias. Quatro foram levadas ao hospital, e uma delas permaneceu internada em observação por causa de ferimentos considerados moderados.
A piscina foi fechada temporariamente. Depois de identificar a falha no equipamento de dosagem, as equipes substituíram a água. O local foi liberado para uso novamente após as verificações, segundo a WDR.
O parque confirmou à emissora alemã que a pane no Outlook impediu o recebimento dos avisos enviados pelo sistema de segurança. Cerca de 40 profissionais de emergência participaram do atendimento, segundo a imprensa internacional.
A interrupção do Microsoft 365 começou na quinta-feira (12/11) e afetou Outlook, Teams, SharePoint e Copilot em diferentes países por mais de 24 horas. A falha também prejudicou ferramentas que dependem da infraestrutura de e-mail da companhia.
Após a pane, a Microsoft publicou um relatório sobre o incidente e atribuiu a falha a um problema em uma atualização de software. O Outlook foi o serviço mais afetado.
A empresa descartou qualquer relação com ataques cibernéticos ou sistemas de inteligência artificial e pediu desculpas pelos transtornos causados.

articles.title: Biowaffen durch KI-Einsatz? „Ein Virus, das uns alle von der Platte putzt, ist einfach Unsinn“
articles.text:
Biowaffen durch KI-Einsatz? „Ein Virus, das uns alle von der Platte putzt, ist einfach Unsinn“
Vom Kot, mit dem die alten Römer ihre Feinde beworfen haben sollen, über Tests mit Pest-, Anthrax- und Malariaerregern in den beiden Weltkriegen bis zu Gerüchten um ethnische Bomben. In Kriegen und auch bei Terroranschlägen haben sich Biowaffen bisher nicht durchsetzen können. Doch moderne, kostengünstige Gentechnologien und KI erleichtern die Entwicklung ganz neuer Erreger und könnten daher die Bedrohungslage verschärfen, zumindest in der Theorie.
Droht uns also bald eine von der KI designte Pandemie, ein Supervirus, das massenweise Menschen tötet? Falls ja: Wie können wir uns davor schützen? Antworten von Klaus-Peter Saalbach, der sich an der Universität Osnabrück mit dem Thema Cyberwar, Waffen – auch biologischen – und KI beschäftigt.
MIT Technology Review: Bereitet Ihnen das Thema neue Biowaffen auch privat Kopfzerbrechen?
Klaus-Peter Saalbach: Nein. Die Hürden von der theoretischen Planung eines Erregers, bis er dann wirklich freigesetzt wird, sind nach wie vor sehr hoch. Aber bei der Planung ist mittlerweile sehr viel möglich.
Was genau?
Bei der allgemeinen KI, wie wir sie auch im Alltag verwenden, zeigte unter anderem eine Studie des Massachusetts Institute of Technology und der Harvard University, wie weit die KI schon ist. MIT-Studenten hatten ChatGPT‑4 nach geeigneten Erregern für Biowaffen gefragt. Und ChatGPT war so frei, nicht nur vier Erreger zu benennen – zwei Influenza-Viren, das Nipah-Virus und Pocken-Viren –, sondern nannte auch noch Anbieter von DNA-Synthesen, die bei einer Bestellung nicht viele Fragen stellen. Außerdem lieferte der Chatbot Herstellungsprotokolle und insgesamt eine Reihe wertvoller Basteltipps.
Auch Gemini 2.5 Pro zum Beispiel war bei Fachprüfungen besser als bis zu 94 Prozent der promovierten Virologen. Und die spezialisierten, KI‑gestützten Tools sind noch wesentlich leistungsfähiger: AlphaFold zum Beispiel, zur Vorhersage von Proteinen, oder Evo2.

articles.title: Meta dijo que no obedecerá una orden de Canadá que debilite el cifrado de WhatsApp
articles.text:
Meta afirmó que se negará a cumplir cualquier orden del gobierno de Canadá que la obligue a debilitar el cifrado de sus servicios, entre ellos WhatsApp. La empresa lo dijo antes de declarar ante el Senado canadiense, que examina el proyecto de ley C-22 sobre el acceso de la policía a datos de usuarios.
Rachel Curran, jefa de política pública de Meta Canadá, dijo al diario The Globe and Mail que, si recibe una orden así, la compañía evaluará todas sus opciones. “No vamos a debilitar ni a romper nuestros sistemas. Es una línea roja para nosotros”, afirmó. El cifrado de extremo a extremo impide que alguien, salvo quien envía y quien recibe, lea un mensaje.
Curran recordó que Apple retiró de Reino Unido su servicio de cifrado avanzado para copias en la nube cuando recibió una orden parecida del gobierno británico. Meta, añadió, ya bloqueó las noticias en Facebook e Instagram en Canadá en 2023 para quedar fuera de otra ley del país.
La ley permite órdenes secretas y guardar datos medio año
El proyecto C-22 obligaría a los proveedores de servicios electrónicos, incluidas las aplicaciones de mensajes, a modificar sus sistemas cuando el gobierno lo pida, para dar capacidad de vigilancia a la policía y al Servicio Canadiense de Inteligencia de Seguridad. El ministro de Seguridad Pública podría emitir órdenes que las empresas deberían mantener en secreto.
La ley también exigiría conservar metadatos de los clientes durante un máximo de seis meses. Una enmienda redujo ese plazo desde 12 meses. Los metadatos no incluyen correos, historial de navegación, redes sociales ni mensajes de texto, pero sí pueden mostrar qué números telefónicos se comunicaron entre sí y la ubicación de una persona.
Curran dijo que Meta no recopila hoy esa información y que obligarla a hacerlo crearía “una base de datos de vigilancia prospectiva que trata a todos los canadienses como posibles delincuentes”. También sostuvo que es “el peor momento” para pedir que se debiliten sistemas seguros, por el aumento de intentos de hackeo, muchos con ayuda de IA.
El gobierno niega que exija puertas traseras
Simon Lafortune, vocero del ministro de Seguridad Pública, Gary Anandasangree, respondió que el proyecto no autoriza una vigilancia indiscriminada ni obliga a crear vulnerabilidades en los sistemas, las llamadas puertas traseras. Según Lafortune, una enmienda establece que ninguna obligación de la ley exige descifrar información protegida de extremo a extremo. Su oficina dijo estar abierta a más cambios.
Google considera insuficiente esa enmienda. En una nota enviada a los senadores en octubre, advirtió que el texto permitiría crear una “nueva infraestructura de vigilancia” y exigir la retención masiva de datos. En junio ya había dicho que los cambios aprobados en comisión no resolvían muchos de los problemas centrales.
Apple tampoco los acepta. En mayo, Erik Neuenchwander, su director sénior de privacidad de usuarios, dijo ante un comité de la Cámara de los Comunes que no conoce una forma de aplicar cifrado que dé acceso solo a los buenos sin abrir un camino a los malos. “Cuando se construye una puerta trasera, cualquiera puede cruzarla”, afirmó.
Signal, la aplicación de mensajes cifrados, dijo en mayo que se retiraría de Canadá si le pidieran comprometer la privacidad de sus usuarios. En octubre de 2026, su vicepresidente de estrategia, Udbhav Tiwari, señaló que las enmiendas de junio no bastaban para que cambiara esa decisión.
Meta, Signal y Tailscale declaran ante el Senado
Según Bloomberg Law, ejecutivos de Meta, Apple y Alphabet, matriz de Google, hacen una ofensiva de último momento en Ottawa para reescribir el proyecto antes de que se apruebe. La audiencia del Senado, de la que participan Meta, Signal y Tailscale, es clave para definir la forma final de la ley.
Curran y Tiwari declaran ante el comité de Seguridad Nacional del Senado el 16 de noviembre. Curran dijo que el gobierno de Estados Unidos también está preocupado, porque una orden de Canadá podría debilitar la seguridad de usuarios estadounidenses.

articles.title: Ransomware affiliate suspect extradited to US, faces 27 years in prison
articles.text:
A Kazakh national has been extradited from Italy to face charges alleging he targeted US schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities in ransomware attacks.
43-year-old Roman Khlynovskiy was an alleged member of the "8-Digits Team" ransomware group, known for its affiliation with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations.
Together with his accomplices, Khlynovskiy is believed to have extorted victims in at least six US states (including hospitals and schools) after breaching their networks and stealing sensitive data.
After exfiltrating data from victims' compromised systems, they pressured them to pay the ransoms by threatening to release the stolen files online.
"The conspirators boasted that they possessed over 50 terabytes of data consisting of more than 70 million confidential health records," the Department of Justice said.
"The conspirators also threatened to publicize this highly sensitive medical information to increase pressure on victims to pay ransom demands. The coconspirators' actions resulted in over $500 million in ransom demands."
Khlynovskiy faces up to 27 years in prison if convicted of conspiracy to commit computer fraud, identity theft, wire fraud, extortion, money laundering, and threats to disclose non-consensual intimate images.
INC Ransom and Lynx ransomware operations
The INC Ransom cybercrime gang, whose leak site lists over 1,000 victims, emerged as a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation in July 2023.
Its victims include many education, healthcare, government, and industrial entities, such as Scotland's National Health Service (NHS), Yamaha Motor Philippines, Pennsylvania's Office of the Attorney General, food retail giant Ahold Delhaize, and the US division of Xerox Business Solutions (XBS).
Lynx ransomware, which surfaced in July 2024, is believed to be a rebrand of INC ransomware rather than a new extortion group and has added over 400 victims to its dark web leak site since then.
The group's operators have used an encryptor likely based on the source code of INC Ransom malware, which was allegedly put up for sale on the Exploit and XSS hacking forums for $300,000 in May 2024. 
However, this could also be a rebranding effort to help the INC Ransom gang operate under less law enforcement scrutiny.
BleepingComputer also found in August 2024 that Lynx ransomware and recent INC encryptors were mostly the same based on a string analysis.

articles.title: macOS 27.3 : pourquoi Apple ne veut plus qu'on donne les clés du Mac aux agents IA — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les agents IA, ces assistants qui ouvrent des apps et agissent à la place de l’utilisateur, ont besoin de droits très larges pour fonctionner sur Mac. Jusqu’ici, macOS les accordait d’un bloc.
Dans macOS 27.2, une app qui a reçu le réglage « Contrôle de l’appareil et accès aux disque » peut lire et envoyer des mails, enregistrer l’écran, surveiller le clavier et contrôler n’importe quelle app.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Ce lundi 16 novembre, Apple a détaillé dans une note aux développeurs comment la deuxième bêta de macOS 27.3 découpe ces droits.
Apple avait prévenu le 2 octobre, dans un premier message aux développeurs. La marque y reprochait à certains d’utiliser l’accès complet au disque d’une façon qui expose fichiers, mails, messages et historique de navigation sans que l’utilisateur le comprenne vraiment. Elle ajoutait que ces risques allaient grandir avec des agents IA de plus en plus autonomes.
Mail oui, Messages non
Dans macOS 27.3, l’ancien réglage devient deux options. D’une part, une option d’accessibilité, réservée aux technologies d’assistance pour les personnes handicapées. D’autre part, un nouveau paramètre « System & App Protection Override » pour les apps qui doivent contourner les protections de macOS pour piloter d’autres apps ou automatiser des tâches, soit exactement ce que font les agents IA.
On accorde désormais ces droits d’une seule façon, en choisissant l’app dans une liste. Surtout, le réglage est désormais bien plus granulaire : un agent peut recevoir le droit de piloter Mail sans toucher à Messages, et une app avec accès complet au disque peut rester cantonnée à certains dossiers.
macOS 27.3 permet aussi d’obliger une app à redemander la permission à chaque fois qu’elle en a besoin. Enfin, une icône s’affiche dans la barre de menus quand une app en contrôle une autre par ce nouveau système.
Les autorisations accordées avant macOS 27.3 restent actives, et les apps déjà repérées par Apple gardent leur fonctionnement sans aucune démarche. Les développeurs d’apps de sauvegarde ou d’assistance pourront demander une autorisation spéciale délivrée par Apple, pour garder la même expérience sur les nouvelles installations.

articles.title: Meta is now testing Zuckerberg's prediction-market app, but it doesn't use real money
articles.text:
Rumor mill: Meta Platforms employees have started testing a prediction-market app that lets them bet on the outcome of questions and events using points instead of dollars, according to people familiar with the matter. The app, called Takes, rewards correct calls with "cred," short for credibility, and takes it away for wrong ones, the people said. The test brings Meta closer to a market led by Kalshi and Polymarket, but unlike those platforms, the app doesn't let users bet real money.
The project has been underway for months. This summer, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg directed a small team to build a prediction-market app, which was internally called Arena at the time.
The mechanics are simple. Employees stake cred on the answers to questions or the outcomes of events, gaining points when they're right and losing points when they're wrong, according to the sources. Because the system runs on points instead of cash, a user's balance goes up or down based only on whether their predictions are correct.
The questions cover a wide mix of subjects. On Thursday, one question on the app asked whether Tim Cook, the former Apple CEO, would become Nvidia's next chief executive, the people said. Most voters bet he would not. Another question asked who would win Friday night's episode of the popular trivia show "Jeopardy!" the people said.
For now, only people inside Meta can use it. The company routinely runs new apps, products and features past its own staff before a public launch, a practice known as "dogfooding." Not every product makes it out of that testing phase, and names and features can change before release. It is unclear when the app might become public, if ever. Meta declined to comment.
The app comes as Meta's leadership talks about building more products. Zuckerberg hasn't discussed the prediction-market app in public. In an internal meeting with employees this spring, however, the CEO said he talked to product chief Chris Cox about building as many as 50 new apps, according to a recording The Wall Street Journal reviewed.
Prediction markets have grown quickly in recent years. Kalshi and Polymarket have become especially popular with Gen Z users, an age group Meta is working to keep engaged with its products.
That growth has also brought legal trouble. Kalshi and Polymarket face a number of lawsuits from US states accusing them of running illegal gambling platforms. Both companies say they are federally regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
New York has sued both platforms. In response, a Kalshi spokeswoman called New York Attorney General Letitia James's legal action "political theater." Polymarket's legal chief said the company would "fight for our users."
So far, Takes runs only on points. Whether Meta will keep it that way or release the app at all is still undecided.

articles.title: Getting CRA Compliant Hardens the Code and Gets Your Company Closer to Digital Sovereignty
articles.text:
In this episode, Christopher "CRob" Robinson, CTO of OpenSSF, Akrites and Chief Security Architect of the Linux Foundation, explores the state of software supply chain security amid multiple security incidents and explains how tools like Scorecard, the Security Baseline framework, and SLSA help harden software.
The conversation also delves into the impact of global cybersecurity regulations like the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), digital sovereignty, and the role of AI in software engineering. Chris shares insights on OpenSSF's Cyber Reasoning System, practical guardrails for AI-assisted development, and how open-source projects are adapting AI contribution policies.
Key Takeaways
- Frameworks like OpenSSF’s Security Baseline translate compliance mandates (EU CRA, NIST SSDF) into 41 practical, verifiable controls for maintainers and enterprise consumers alike.
- SLSA (Supply Chain Levels for Software Artefacts) complements Security Baseline by hardening development infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and source repositories across maturity levels.
- The EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is setting a global benchmark for consumer-focused software security regulation, encouraging international harmonisation across regions like the UK, India, Japan, and Australia.
- AI tools accelerate software creation but require structured harnesses, such as OpenSSF's Cyber Reasoning System and upcoming security skills, to enforce established software engineering discipline.
- Open-source software and local-first data paradigms are essential for digital sovereignty, enabling organisations to retain data control and avoid vendor lock-in.
Subscribe on:
Transcript
Olimpiu Pop: Hello, everybody. I'm Olimpiu Pop, an InfoQ editor, and I have with me Christopher Robinson, who goes by CRob these days. I'll let him introduce himself and share a bit more background.
Christopher Robinson: Hello, everybody. Thank you for having me today. My name is Chris Robinson, also known as CRob. I am the CTO and Chief Security Architect for a couple of Linux Foundation projects. First, the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF), which focuses on application security, supply chain security, and AI security—predominantly helping support upstream maintainers. My other role is leading a new project called Akrites, which is an upstream open-source coordinated incident response team.
Olimpiu Pop: That sounds like a lot! You wear multiple hats, as people often see in your presentations.
Christopher Robinson: Yes. Yes.
OpenSSF’s Tooling and Intended Audience [01:32]
Olimpiu Pop: OpenSSF is definitely a stronghold for security. Before the recent surge in AI, there was a strong push to move security to the left—getting tools and practices closer to development teams. Historically, security was often left for the end alongside documentation and other crucial tasks.
In my experience, whenever something bad happened, the security architect had to scramble down, fix it, and then try to convince developers to adopt the fix. As we record this in early November, we've seen widespread scrambling over PyPI incidents and others, as security incidents continue to rise. We saw an example with PHP where maintainers noted they never expected all four conditions to occur simultaneously—yet they did, with AI contributing to that complexity.
Christopher Robinson: Yes, helping.
Olimpiu Pop: Exactly. When and who should turn to OpenSSF? Who is your target audience?
Christopher Robinson: We focus on two primary personas. First is the upstream open-source developer and maintainer. We provide comprehensive guidance, best practices, tooling, and training to teach software engineers the expected security controls and practices needed to harden their projects and infrastructure. That is our primary audience.
Secondarily, we care deeply about everyone consuming those projects. Sometimes that is another open-source maintainer integrating a project as a dependency, but predominantly it includes downstream manufacturers and enterprises—such as banks, hospitals, and retailers—running their core operations. We offer tools and guidance to help these consumers evaluate and understand the security posture of projects they plan to integrate, such as Scorecard, which we discussed earlier.
Scorecard serves a dual purpose. It helps upstream maintainers choose the right dependencies, and for maintainers looking to demonstrate their security rigor, it acts as a strong public signal showing adherence to security best practices. Consumers can then look for these signals to inform their decisions.
When evaluating two packages for integration into a solution, consumers can select the option with the stronger security posture.
Olimpiu Pop: That aligns with what we discussed regarding Scorecard examining more than just technical aspects. Many recent issues stems from social engineering or oversight—such as typosquatting or version manipulation in the Python ecosystem, where picking the highest available version bypassed protections.
This focus is especially critical now. While recent incidents draw attention, this shift has been building since the pandemic. During that period, many developers focused heavily on building projects, but subsequent industry reports highlight a different trend.
Security Baseline and SLSA Supply Chain Specification [05:26]
For instance, Sonatype reports showed a decline in open-source project maintenance, opening doors for attack vectors. Aside from Scorecard, what other tool would you highlight? OpenSSF excels at making best practices actionable. Knowing what is good is one thing; operationalizing it is the real challenge. What other tool would you single out?
Christopher Robinson: I'm going to cheat and I'm going to say two.
Olimpiu Pop: Excellent. Great.
Christopher Robinson: First, I would highlight our Security Baseline, which represents the next evolution of Scorecard. The Baseline includes 41 recommended security controls and practices. We analyzed global regulations like the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) and frameworks like the NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) to curate a practical list of actions for project maintainers and consumers.
It combines technical configurations—such as enabling branch protection settings on source code repositories—with organizational controls, like publishing a clear security policy or documenting contributor onboarding and maintainer progression paths.
The Security Baseline is structured across three maturity levels. Level 1 is the most straightforward, roughly equivalent to a mid-range Scorecard score, and takes an experienced developer about two hours to implement. It focuses heavily on documentation. While non-profit open-source maintainers are generally not legally bound by cybersecurity regulations like the EU CRA, downstream manufacturers and governments care immensely about compliance.
The EU CRA explicitly exempts open-source maintainers who do not profit from their work. However, commercial consumers must comply. The Security Baseline translates complex regulatory requirements—from the EU CRA, US Executive Orders, and Japanese legislation—into accessible, practical steps for maintainers without requiring them to digest raw legal texts.
By offering a tiered implementation aligned with modern security practices, the Security Baseline makes projects more attractive to downstream consumers. This increased visibility helps attract more contributors, users, feature requests, and code reviews to strengthen the project.
The second framework I recommend is SLSA (Supply Chain Levels for Software Artifacts), which addresses supply chain provenance, pedigree, and integrity. While Scorecard and Security Baseline focus on code and process quality, SLSA secures the underlying infrastructure—including IDEs, developer workstations, source repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and distribution systems.
SLSA defines progressive levels of maturity to harden development infrastructure. By pairing process-oriented frameworks like Scorecard or Security Baseline with SLSA, organizations can verify how software moves securely through the supply chain and assess infrastructure resilience.
OpenSSF’s Cyber Reasoning System [10:03]
Olimpiu Pop: You mentioned OpenSSF's work around AI. Previously, we expected software development to rely on human engineering skills built over decades. Now, there is a shift toward AI prompting and engineering assistance. How difficult is it to integrate these security frameworks into AI development harnesses?
How is it is to include all this tooling into harnesses because now all our experience transformed itself into harnesses.
Christopher Robinson: It is a fascinating space. LLMs and AI agents have invited a vast group of new stakeholders into software development. Someone with minimal formal software engineering background can now generate code using straightforward prompts. The key is ensuring these workflows incorporate proper security guardrails and harnesses.
While experienced engineers can leverage trained harnesses and best practices, the challenge lies in the influx of new non-developer contributors across accounting, marketing, and operational roles writing code. With frontier LLMs, there is immense excitement to adopt these powerful tools immediately.
In the rush to adopt AI capabilities, teams risk overlooking 50 years of established software engineering discipline and security practices. AI makes it easy to bypass those foundational controls if guardrails are not explicitly built in.
That has been OpenSSF's main focus this year. We brought in a dedicated AI Security Architect to lead the deployment of the Open Source Software Cyber Reasoning System. This framework acts as a modular harness where developers can plug in AI models, fine-tune their operation, and apply specific security skills and domain context.
Looking ahead, our goal is to build modular skills that integrate directly into these AI harnesses. Next year, we plan to release dedicated skills for Scorecard, SLSA, and Security Insights. These tools will enable automated agents to enforce proven security practices during code generation, ensuring more secure software outputs.
Olimpiu Pop: That is great to hear. Recently, when setting up a repository, I had to manually break down Scorecard recommendations and configure them step by step. With my engineering background, I knew how to implement them, but non-technical users focusing purely on product vision need automated triggers to enforce those standards seamlessly.
And those people don't know what's to be expected. And then it's easier for them if something just triggers that point.
Christopher Robinson: In the hands of an experienced senior engineer, LLMs can be transformative—boosting productivity and reinforcing guardrails. However, developers must actively configure and enable those security skills. I am cautiously optimistic, though real challenges remain.
Olimpiu Pop: I see strong enthusiasm at both ends of the spectrum. Senior engineers can move faster without being blocked, while non-engineering teams can build tools independently without navigating traditional engineering bottlenecks.
Is the EU’s CRA a Blueprint for the Rest of the World? [15:03]
You also brought up a major regulatory acronym in Europe: the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA).
Christopher Robinson: Yes, absolutely.
Olimpiu Pop: There is a common saying that Europe excels at regulation—as seen with GDPR, the AI Act, and now the CRA. At a recent panel you participated in, speakers discussed digital sovereignty alongside ecosystem fragmentation. In open source, we think globally, but regulations like the US Executive Orders and memory-safe language mandates introduced regional variations. What is your global outlook on cybersecurity regulation right now?
And in the open source ecosystem, we are talking about the global world, a global village. If we take a step upwards, because you're obviously looking at the whole global ecosystem, CRA is getting into force slowly, starting from this autumn. It has multiple stages. Then the US used to have at some point some executive order that started everything in terms of hardening software. And then from that point on, we discussed about memory save programming languages.
I know that Australia invests a lot of money. As you mentioned, you have an agenda for this year and for next year. Maybe you can give us a summary, where is the world from the perspective of the cybersecurity?
Christopher Robinson: Having spent decades as a practitioner starting in the heavily regulated banking sector, I appreciate the value of clear compliance frameworks. That perspective made me eager to see the EU CRA take shape.
While regulation brings implementation challenges, the CRA focuses on necessary, long-overdue principles. Like GDPR's emphasis on citizen data protection, the CRA prioritizes consumer protection against software vulnerabilities and unsafe products, which is a commendable objective.
Global jurisdictions are watching the EU CRA closely ahead of its full enforcement date on December 11, 2027. Countries including the UK, India, Japan, and Australia are observing the rollout as they draft their own cybersecurity approaches.
I anticipate other regions introducing CRA-aligned legislation in the coming years. As a practitioner who prefers efficiency over rework, my hope is that international bodies harmonize their standards rather than creating fragmented, conflicting regulatory requirements.
Fragmented rules would create significant friction. For instance, if Europe adopts established standards for Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) while another region mandates a proprietary 86-point criteria list, manufacturers and developers will face conflicting compliance burdens that hinder efficient delivery.
My goal is to see global regulatory efforts align with the core principles of the CRA—whether through formal legislation or executive frameworks—to maintain consistent expectations for developers worldwide.
Olimpiu Pop: That is a crucial point. A key strength of the CRA was the collaboration between regulators and industry leaders to reach consensus. The remaining question centers on implementation and ensuring fair execution across organizations of all sizes.
Recent high-profile security incidents have increased public and corporate awareness of cybersecurity risks. Beyond standard threats, the global context involves active cyber warfare, making robust software defense essential. Hopefully, regulatory and industry efforts continue moving in the right direction.
Christopher Robinson: To tie this back to digital sovereignty: open-source software provides the most reliable foundation for organizations to maintain autonomy and avoid vendor lock-in. Open source allows teams to inspect, fork, modify, and contribute code back to the community, rather than depending on a single commercial vendor.
This flexibility allows organizations to combine best-of-breed tools—such as pairing an open-weight LLM with European cloud hosting, US-developed web servers, or global components—while retaining full transparency and control over their technology stack.
Users are More Aware About Digital Sovereignty [22:04]
Olimpiu Pop: This aligns with the local-first software movement. Just as European regulation emphasizes user rights, local-first architecture prioritizes data ownership—ensuring users retain control over their data locally rather than relying entirely on centralized cloud providers.
Instead of receiving an unusable data export when a cloud service shuts down, local-first applications keep data accessible to the user long-term. Combining strong privacy regulations with local-first technical paradigms is a vital step forward for software design.
Christopher Robinson: Agreed.
Olimpiu Pop: Regardless of preference, AI tools are now a permanent part of the software landscape.
Christopher Robinson: They are certainly here to stay.
Olimpiu Pop: Some express concern that automated tools will diminish the human role in software creation. Where do you stand on this spectrum—are you optimistic, pessimistic, or somewhere in between?
Christopher Robinson: I consider myself an AI realist and use these tools daily in my work. AI acts as a helpful assistant that accelerates workflows, rather than a replacement for human engineering judgment. Like a fuzzer or a multimeter in electronics, AI is a tool, and the outcomes depend on how effectively it is applied.
It is important to understand what LLMs actually do: they perform statistical predictions based on context rather than reasoning magic, and they can produce incorrect outputs. Their primary strength lies in identifying patterns across vast datasets—a task where human processing is slower.
When applied thoughtfully, AI provides substantial benefits. However, using these tools without understanding underlying security principles risks exposing sensitive personal or corporate data to external models.
As an AI realist, my goal is to help developers maximize the advantages of AI while remaining aware of potential security risks.
Olimpiu Pop: Given the central role of AI in open source, communities are actively debating AI contribution policies. Some projects require strict human authorship, while leaders like Linus Torvalds view AI as another tool to be used with proper oversight. How do you view recommended AI contribution policies for open-source projects?
Use it cautiously, but you have to understand what's there. And so on, so forth. What's your perspective? How do you see the AI policy of ... I don't know, recommend it maybe?
Christopher Robinson: Policies cross open source remain varied. Maintainers face influxes of automated vulnerability reports and AI-generated contributions, leading to different approaches. While projects like the Linux kernel permit AI-assisted code contributions under developer review, smaller projects with fewer review resources may take a more restrictive stance.
AI usage in software development will continue to grow. The priority for open-source projects is to establish clear, explicit contribution guidelines defining their stance on AI tools. Transparent policies allow contributors to choose projects that align with their preferred workflows.
Olimpiu Pop: Thank you for sharing your insights today, Chris. It was a pleasure speaking with you.
Christopher Robinson: Thank you very much for having me. It was great talking with you.
Mentioned:
