articles.title: Redmi Watch 6 é bom? Testamos o relógio com tela AMOLED e GPS independente • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Redmi Watch 6 é bom? Testamos o relógio com tela AMOLED e GPS independente
Smartwatch da Xiaomi entrega tela AMOLED, GPS independente e boa autonomia de bateria a um custo mais acessível
O Redmi Watch 6 é um smartwatch intermediário com recursos interessantes, como tela AMOLED brilhante, GPS independente, boa autonomia de bateria e player de música que não depende de pareamento com o smartphone.
O dispositivo ainda monitora dados básicos de saúde e chega com mais de 150 modos de treino para atender a diferentes esportistas, apesar de não contar com mapas offline ou NFC para pagamentos por aproximação.
Mas será que no balanço geral ele vale a compra? Eu testei o Redmi Watch 6 por 20 dias e detalho toda minha experiência logo abaixo.
Aviso de ética
O Tecnoblog é um veículo jornalístico independente que ajuda as pessoas a tomarem sua próxima decisão de compra desde 2005.
Esta análise não têm intenção publicitária, e ressalta os pontos positivos e negativos do produto. Nenhuma empresa pagou, revisou ou teve acesso antecipado a este conteúdo.
O Redmi Watch 6 foi cedido por empréstimo pela Xiaomi e será devolvido após os testes. Para mais informações, acesse a nossa Política Editorial.
A embalagem do Redmi Watch 6 contém o relógio, um cabo para carregamento magnético e um manual de usuário que também inclui a certificação de garantia.
O único item essencial que não vem na caixa é o adaptador de tomada, o que é algo comum da indústria de relógios inteligentes.
A boa notícia é que praticamente qualquer fonte que você tenha em casa deve funcionar, devido à potência modesta exigida de 5 W (5 V e 1 A).
Talvez seja difícil perceber à primeira vista, mas o Redmi Watch 6 é ligeiramente menor e mais fino que seu antecessor, além de estar mais leve. A caixa retangular com cantos arredondados mede 46,45 mm de altura, 40,03 mm de largura e 9,94 mm de espessura, pesando 31 g (sem a pulseira).
O comparativo abaixo ajuda a mostrar as diferenças de dimensões e peso entre os modelos.
|  | Redmi Watch 6 | Redmi Watch 5 | 
|---|---|---|
| Dimensões (A x L x E) | 46,45 mm × 40,03 mm × 9,94 mm | 47,5 mm × 41,1 mm × 11,3 mm | 
| Peso | 31 g (sem a pulseira) | 33,5 g (sem a pulseira) | 
É um relógio grande, mas leve e bem confortável — caiu bem no meu pulso. As pulseiras de TPU também são macias e facilmente removíveis: um clique nos botões da traseira e elas se destacam do corpo.
Por falar em traseira, a parte interna da caixa abriga o sensor de frequência cardíaca, microfone, alto-falantes e os pontos de contato para carregamento.
A grande novidade de design, no entanto, está no botão inédito na lateral direita. Para que ele fosse incorporado, a Xiaomi precisou reposicionar a coroa giratória de aço inoxidável, agora posicionada mais acima. Isso liberou espaço para o botão, localizado logo abaixo.
O botão lateral facilita a navegação e oferece atalhos mais rápidos de uso. Um clique nele e acessamos a Central de Controle. Com três cliques, acionamos o contato de emergência — configurado no app Mi Fitness. E se pressionarmos o botão por alguns segundos, entramos no menu liga/desliga.
O modelo que recebi é a versão em preto obsidiano, que seria minha escolha natural se tivesse comprado o wearable. Mas você também pode encontrar o Redmi Watch 6 em prata cinza ou azul glacial.
Além de ser menor e mais leve que seu antecessor, o Redmi Watch 6 chega com promessa de maior resistência resistente. A caixa retangular mantém a construção em liga de alumínio, mas o material usado é 20% mais resistente e a resistência estrutural é 40% superior em relação ao Redmi Watch 5, segundo a Xiaomi.
No meu caso, foi difícil avaliar essa parte, já que o modelo que recebi havia sido testado por outras pessoas e estava com a lateral esquerda um pouco desgastada, com pequenos arranhões e notas de desbotamento.
Ainda falando de construção, o relógio tem resistência contra água de 5 ATM, equivalente a 50 metros de profundidade. Isso significa que você pode usá-lo para nadar em piscinas ou águas rasas perto da costa.
Por aqui, ele resistiu tranquilamente a algumas sessões de natação de 10 minutos na piscina do prédio. Depois de cada treino, o dispositivo expulsa a água automaticamente do relógio para evitar degradações.
E eu aproveito o espaço para falar sobre uma questão que vira e mexe recebemos no Tecnoblog. A resistência contra água não é sinal verde para usar o relógio durante banhos quentes. E a própria Xiaomi alerta contra a prática.
A resistência de 5 ATM não protege o dispositivo contra vapor e água quente, que podem oxidar componentes internos. Portanto, tire ele do pulso antes de entrar no chuveiro para não impactar sua durabilidade.
A tela AMOLED de 2,07 polegadas é um dos grandes destaques do Redmi Watch 6. É um display amplo com bordas ultrafinas de 2 mm, o que garante bom espaço para visualização de conteúdos, especialmente de caracteres menores.
E a taxa de atualização de 60 Hz proporciona a fluidez necessária de navegação e animações das watchfaces.
O pico de brilho de 2.000 nits também ajuda na visibilidade e permitiu que eu enxergasse tudo na tela, sem dificuldades, em ambientes internos ou externos. E deixo meu elogio ao brilho automático, que se adaptou bem aos diferentes níveis de luminosidade.
A tela traz o recurso de ativação ao levantar o braço e chega com o Always-on Display, que mantém a tela ativada com dados básicos mesmo que você não esteja olhando para ela, embora aumente o gasto de energia.
E lembra que eu comentei sobre a lateral desgastada no modelo recebido? Pois a tela também chegou com arranhões de usos anteriores e passou a impressão de que risca com facilidade. Por motivos de prevenção, eu recomendaria uma película para reforçar a proteção.
O smartwatch opera sob o sistema HyperOS 3 da Xiaomi, que é simples e bem intuitivo. Temos três opções de layout, widgets personalizáveis e várias watchfaces nativas. Inclusive, você pode encontrar diversos outros mostradores de relógio pelo app Mi Fitness, disponível para Android ou iPhone.
Mas o SO não conta com uma loja de apps e nem permite a instalação de apps de terceiros. Em outras palavras, você só vai conseguir usar as ferramentas que já chegam instaladas no smartwatch.
A exemplo do modelo antecessor, o Redmi Watch 6 traz apenas um sensor de frequência cardíaca com um sensor de saturação de oxigênio no sangue.
Você pode medir batimentos cardíacos, conferir o nível de oxigênio no sangue, analisar as métricas de sono e até índice de estresse.
Não tenho do que reclamar sobre os monitoramentos. Achei que o relógio fez um bom rastreamento do meu ciclo de sono e não notei nenhum dado de saúde discrepante o suficiente para eu me preocupar.
Só é importante entender as limitações de rastreamento: o monitoramento de saúde é básico e atende a usuários que não precisam de dados complexos. Funciona para o meu caso. Mas ele não cobre medições avançadas como eletrocardiograma — presente em smartwatches premium mais caros e completos.
Em compensação, o Redmi Watch oferece 161 modalidades esportivas, incluindo corrida, ciclismo, natação e até hipismo. E durante os treinos, uma olhada rápida no relógio te deixa a par da frequência cardíaca e gasto de energia em tempo real.
Uma grata surpresa é que a Xiaomi atualizou algoritmos e os dados de frequência cardíaca estão presentes nos treinos de natação.
Mas o meu destaque vai para o GPS independente, agora com antena L1 dupla. Nesta estrutura, o relógio seleciona a antena com sinal mais forte para entregar uma conexão mais estável e posicionamentos mais precisos.
Confesso que é libertador sair para caminhar sem precisar levar o celular, já que o relógio consegue, por si só, marcar meu trajeto. E os registros foram bem certeiros.
Infelizmente, não há mapas offline e nem navegação por rotas. No entanto, assim que cheguei em casa, sincronizei os dados com o Mi Fitness e pude ver todo o percurso pelo mapa do app.
Além dos monitoramentos de saúde e treino, temos uma porção de outros recursos que facilitam a vida no dia a dia.
O relógio pode receber notificações de apps, visualizar mensagens do WhatsApp, além de receber ou fazer ligações telefônicas usando o microfone e alto-falantes dele.
Também há ferramentas para localizar o celular vinculado e apps utilitários como gravador de voz, lanterna, alarme com resposta tátil e drenagem de água. Muitas das ferramentas só funcionam quando o Bluetooth 5.4 do relógio está ativado e pareado ao smartphone.
Curiosamente, uma das funções que mais gostei funciona sem pareamento: a reprodução de músicas de maneira independente. É verdade que você vai precisar do celular para passar as músicas para a memória interna de 512 MB do smartwatch. Mas depois disso, ele poderá tocar as faixas pelo alto-falante ou fones de ouvido mesmo sem estar pareado.
É uma função ótima para quem vai correr, treinar ou passear por aí apenas com o relógio no pulso. Mas o sistema não é perfeito e a transferência de músicas só funciona em smartphones Android. Se fosse minha noiva munida de seu iPhone, por exemplo, ela teria que me pedir esse favor.
Vale destacar ainda que o Redmi Watch não tem Wi-Fi e não suporta assistentes virtuais. E também não conta com NFC para pagamentos por aproximação.
O Redmi Watch 6 chega com uma bateria de 550 mAh, que é a mesma capacidade vista no Redmi Watch 5. A Xiaomi fala em uma autonomia de até 24 dias de uso leve, 12 dias de uso normal e 7 dias de uso intenso.
Nos meus testes, o relógio durou cerca de 6 dias e 21 horas. Lembro de ter tirado o smartwatch da tomada por volta das 15h de uma quarta-feira e ele só foi descarregar completamente na quarta-feira seguinte, lá pelo meio-dia.
Confesso que esperava uma autonomia maior. Até porque usei uma watchface de baixo gasto energético, mantive o AOD desligado, ativei o brilho automático e desliguei o Bluetooth na maior parte do tempo. Expectativas à parte, ele apresentou boa autonomia durando quase uma semana inteira.
Já o tempo de carregamento se manteve dentro dos padrões de smartwatches, levando aproximadamente 1 hora e 47 minutos na tomada.
O Redmi Watch 6 vale a compra se você está buscando um relógio de monitoramento básico e com ótimo custo-benefício. Atualmente, ele pode ser encontrado na faixa dos R$ 550 a R$ 590 em marketplaces. Um bom preço pelo que entrega, e bem distante dos quase R$ 1.300 cobrados na loja oficial da Xiaomi.
Mas ele não é o único modelo competitivo do segmento intermediário. O Amazfit Bip 6, por exemplo, oferece navegação por rotas e assistente de voz custando menos que R$ 500. E o Huawei Fit 5, apesar de estar mais caro, chega com 64 GB de memória interna e inclui detecção de quedas.
No fim, tudo vai depender do que você busca em um smartwatch e no orçamento disponível. Porém, digo tranquilo que o Redmi Watch 6 é uma escolha segura e com potencial para se tornar seu fiel companheiro de pulso.
Só fica a sugestão de conferir os Achados do TB antes de finalizar a compra. De repente, o Redmi Watch 6 ou algum de seus concorrentes pode surgir lá com preços melhores para dar uma aliviada no seu bolso.
No geral, eu gostei do Redmi Watch 6. Mas e o que você achou dele? Bora continuar o papo na Comunidade do Tecnoblog!

articles.title: Un arquitecto técnico experto en ahorro energético lo explica: "A una bomba de calor le va bien que le pidas poco, que sea una casa, que esté bien aislada"
articles.text:
Cambiar la caldera de gas por una bomba de calor parece la manera más rápida de pagar menos por la calefacción, pero puedes encontrarte con que apenas hay diferencia. Por eso, el arquitecto técnico Jordi Martí avisa en su canal de TikTok de que el aparato no garantiza por sí solo una factura mucho más baja, y lo ilustra de una forma bastante gráfica: “A una bomba de calor le va bien que le pidas poco, que sea una casa, que esté bien aislada”.
Lo que pide la bomba de calor. Las bombas de calor rinden mejor y ahorran más cuando no necesitan ir siempre al límite, que es cuando tu vivienda está bien aislada y conserva bien la temperatura. Por eso, se puede decir que el ahorro depende tanto del aparato como de la construcción de la vivienda, el sistema de calefacción que tiene e incluso tus ventanas. La OCU también apunta en esta dirección en su guía para preparar la casa, donde recuerda que el nivel de aislamiento influye en la eficiencia de la bomba de calor, y por eso simplemente cambiar la caldera dejando lo demás igual no es siempre suficiente.
La teoría y la factura. “En teoría debería dividir el consumo por tres o por cuatro, pero miras las facturas y eso no lo notas tanto. Y el confort, pues eso, que a veces no da”, señala el arquitecto. Eso sí, según Martí, si la casa tiene poco aislamiento, ventanas antiguas o muchas pérdidas, el aparato tiene que trabajar bastante más tiempo, y si los radiadores exigen temperaturas elevadas, la bomba pierde ventaja.
Kilian Jornet cargando pianos. Para explicarlo, Martí tira de un ejemplo con Kilian Jornet, el corredor de montaña catalán capaz de subir desniveles enormes como pocos: “Kilian Jornet te sube el Everest en un momento con una eficiencia brutal, pero si le pones a transportar pianos seguramente no destacará mucho”.
Con la bomba de calor pasa algo parecido. “Si tienes una vivienda mal aislada con radiadores normales y quieres cambiar la caldera por una bomba de calor será como hacerle transportar pianos”, explica. Vamos, que dos viviendas con el mismo equipo pueden acabar teniendo consumos muy diferentes.
El aislamiento manda. Para Martí, el aislamiento es uno de los factores que más influyen en el consumo, ya que una casa que retiene bien el calor necesita menos energía para calentarse, y permite que el equipo que tengas funcione a baja potencia durante más tiempo. “Lo que quiere la bomba de calor es ir tranquila, es cuando brilla. No le pidas mucha potencia”, explica. Las ventanas antiguas o con filtraciones provocan pérdidas constantes de calor, por lo que una de las primeras medidas para mejorarlo es cambiarlas por una de doble o triple acristalamiento.
Antes de cambiar la caldera. Por eso, antes de quitar la caldera conviene revisar el estado de la vivienda y valorar si toca mejorar el aislamiento o cambiar las ventanas más viejas, porque así se reduce la energía que tendrá que aportar la bomba. Y el tipo de emisor también cuenta, porque el suelo radiante funciona con agua a menos temperatura y se adapta bien a este sistema, mientras que los radiadores convencionales pueden necesitar temperaturas más altas.
La conclusión de Martí es sencilla: la bomba de calor puede consumir muy poco, pero necesita una vivienda que no la obligue a trabajar continuamente al límite, y cuanta menos energía pida la casa, mejores resultados dará.

articles.title: AWS Open-Sources Emulator for Local Testing of 200+ Services by Coding Agents
articles.text:
AWS has released AWS Emulator, a local program that serves an HTTPS endpoint for the public APIs of more than 200 AWS services. AWS Emulator lets developers and coding agents create resources, hit the same errors AWS would return, and iterate without provisioning cloud resources or incurring service charges for the operations it emulates.
Teams point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at it with environment variables such as AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, leaving application code unchanged. On Linux it installs as an RPM or Debian package for x86_64 or aarch64; on macOS and Windows, AWS documents a short Dockerfile and does not publish a prebuilt image. Rust tests can use an embedded mode that runs the emulator inside the test process and wires its HTTP client into the AWS SDK for Rust. An aws-emulator skill can start the emulator for coding agents and check a project against published fidelity tests. Written in Rust, it is generated from more than 400 Smithy API models AWS publishes for the SDKs, according to Swaminathan Sivasubramanian.
AWS says agents wrote and tested the code. Matthew Goldberg, a senior principal engineer at AWS, describes three teams: one writes fidelity tests from the public API models and verifies them against real AWS, one replays those tests and files issues, and one implements each fix. Every change must pass a merge gate that checks compilation, coding standards, security, and fidelity regressions. The work runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime Instances, AWS CodePipeline, and AWS CodeCommit.
How closely the emulator matches AWS varies by service. AWS publishes versioned fidelity tests and per-service scores with each release; a test passes only when every call matches AWS, including status codes, side effects, and exact errors. Unimplemented operations return HTTP 501 with the error code NotImplemented. AWS says fidelity is closest on control-plane APIs, while data-plane behavior and support for CloudFormation, Terraform, and the AWS CDK vary by service. Documented limits include no evaluation of IAM or resource-based policies, so it must not be used to test security; a single shared account and Region per process; in-memory state that disappears when the process stops; and no testing for long-running use or load. The evaluation suite includes tests the emulator does not yet pass.
Developers already have several local AWS stand-ins, including LocalStack, Floci, and moto. AWS Emulator is generated from AWS's own API models, ships official fidelity scores, and is dedicated to the public domain, but it is not a drop-in replacement for every workflow those tools cover, especially permission testing and infrastructure-as-code pipelines.
Developer Josh Builds wrote:
AWS just released a free local emulator of its APIs, made for coding agents and written entirely by agents. I counted its published fidelity tests: S3, DynamoDB and SQS pass about 2 in 3. CloudFormation passes under 1 in 5.
Yurii Serhiichuk compared it with existing emulators and published a container image and GitHub Action to cover a packaging gap:
AWS shipped AWS Emulator today - think LocalStack/Floci but native. Rust, built by agents (so hopefully it gets updated pretty fast). No public docker image though, and no GitHub action. So I filled that part.
AWS Emulator is generally available at no additional service fee. Source is on GitHub under the CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication, except third-party code in the vendor/ directory, which is under the Apache License 2.0. Setup details are in the user guide, and fidelity scores ship with each release.

articles.title: Old Bitly links hijacked in X posts from Trump, McDonald's, Burger King, and others
articles.text:
In context: Back when tweets were capped at 140 characters, brands and politicians ran most of their links through Bitly to shrink them down. That's why years of old posts on X are still full of tiny bit.ly addresses. Click one, and the service quietly forwards you to the full web page sitting behind it. Most people wouldn't think twice before doing that. Over the weekend, pranksters managed to take over some of those old links in posts from Donald Trump, McDonald's and Burger King.
CNN found that Trump's account was hit the hardest. At least a dozen of his posts now carry swapped links, including a 2013 complaint about wind turbines. Open it today, and you'll land on a Google site called "fortnite baby," complete with a photo of an infant.
Over at Burger King, a 2011 post meant to help people find nearby restaurants now leads to Wikipedia's list of Nazi concentration camps. McDonald's didn't escape either – one of its 2011 posts now opens a page about the September 11 attacks.
Bill Gates, former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau and Mike Pence all had old posts tampered with as well. Weirdly, the FBI's 2012 post about its "Ghost Clicks" case now just shows a photo of a seal.
In theory, none of this should be possible. Bitly's own help pages say the code at the end of a short link can never be reused, even after the account that created it gets deleted.
The company acknowledged the problem on Sunday, saying it had found an issue that let bad actors "repurpose certain old, inactive links." It has since suspended the accounts behind the changes and is working to disable the affected URLs.
Back in February 2025, crypto scammers used a Bitly bug to point some of Trump's old tweets at memecoin pages. The company patched it at the time, but this weekend's redirects seem to suggest a similar hole stayed open.
This time, most of the redirects look like plain trolling with no obvious money angle. Even so, Carnegie Mellon digital media professor Ari Lightman told CNN that this kind of tampering is risky. Plenty of old accounts go unmonitored, he noted, and a swapped link on one of them could expose the information of anyone who clicks it.
By comparison, when Google switched off its inactive goo.gl links last year, they simply started returning errors. A hijacked link is a different problem since it keeps working and quietly sends people somewhere new.

articles.title: Un aspirador en seco y húmedo que friega con vapor a 200 grados: este Dreame T16 Pro Steam te puede ahorrar mucho tiempo al limpiar
articles.text:
Con el poco tiempo que tenemos en nuestro día a día, cualquier dispositivo para ayudarnos a limpiar siempre es bien recibido. Obviando los robots aspiradores (que lo hacen casi todo solos), un buen aspirador en seco y húmedo nos puede venir genial, especialmente en hogares con mascotas y niños. Y precisamente ahora que estamos en Black Friday prácticamente, ha llegado la mejor oferta del Dreame T16 Pro Steam: es uno de los mejores que hay y su precio ha caído hasta los 529 euros.
DREAME T16 Pro Steam Aspirador en Seco y Húmedo, Vapor a 200 °C | Fregado a 90 °C, Alcance Ultrabajo de 9,85 cm, 30k Pa, Libre de Enredos, Lavado de Cepillo Con Agua Caliente y Vapor, App
Un aspirador eficaz hasta con las manchas más rebeldes
Este dispositivo de Dreame llegó a las tiendas en España en septiembre y, aunque ya ha tenido una pequeña rebaja en alguna ocasión, no tan grande como los 120 euros de descuento que tiene ahora mismo. El Dreame T16 Pro Steam es el aspirador en seco y húmedo tope de gama de este fabricante y, entre otras cosas, destaca por su sistema de vapor.
A la hora de fregar, el aspirador mezcla un sistema de agua caliente a 90 grados y vapor a 200 grados, por lo que es capaz de derretir las manchas más pegajosas y resistentes a la vez que desinfecta el suelo. Además, tiene una potencia de succión de 30.000 Pa, por lo que irá recogiendo líquidos y sólidos con buena fuerza.
Otro punto interesante de este aspirador Dreame es que tiene un diseño reclinable de 180 grados, por lo que se puede pasar bajo muebles y camas sin dificultad. Para terminar, su batería ofrece una autonomía de hasta 70 minutos por carga y cuenta con un sistema que combina también vapor y agua para limpiar tanto el cepillo como la base, evitando así posibles malos olores.

articles.title: ElecWave Debuts Foldable KF01 Keyboard
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
ElecWave Debuts Foldable KF01 Keyboard
ElecWave today announced its brand debut with the launch of its first product, the ElecWave KF01 foldable keyboard. Guided by its brand slogan, "Convenient, No Compromise," ElecWave believes that working from anywhere should not mean compromising on typing comfort or productivity. Backed by the group behind global brands including Tribit and Ohuhu, and drawing on 20 years of iClever keyboard engineering expertise, ElecWave brings that promise to life with the KF01, a travel-friendly foldable keyboard that combines a full-size typing layout, comfortable scissor-switch keys, multi-device connectivity, and long battery life
As working on the go becomes increasingly common, professionals need the flexibility to stay productive in offices, cafés, and while traveling. Although foldable phones and dual-screen devices offer more screen space, typing directly on them can still be slow and frustrating. Even laptops such as MacBooks lack a built-in numeric keypad, which can make spreadsheet work and data entry less efficient. The ElecWave KF01 addresses these challenges with a full-size, desktop-style typing experience in a compact, foldable design, turning a desk, airplane tray table, or café counter into a practical workspace."As someone who frequently works on the go, I was frustrated by the trade-off in foldable keyboards: if a keyboard was compact enough to travel with, it was usually too cramped for productive typing," said Sam, founder and CEO of ElecWave. "Today, the world is our workspace, whether you're finishing a report on a flight, answering emails at a local café, or extending a business trip for leisure. Working on the go shouldn't mean compromising on comfort or speed. We built ElecWave on a simple principle: to deliver full-size typing performance wherever life and work take you."
Foldable Portability, Uncompromised Typing
As ElecWave's debut keyboard, the KF01 combines full-size typing comfort with a travel-friendly foldable design. When folded, it measures just 7.48 × 4.91 × 0.91 inches, with a footprint comparable to that of an iPad mini, making it easy to carry in a work bag or backpack. Unfolded, it measures 14.63 × 4.91 × 0.47 inches and features a full-size layout, standard-size keycaps, and an integrated numeric keypad for more efficient typing and data entry. Low-profile scissor-switch keys provide responsive tactile feedback and a comfortable, quiet typing experience. Together, these features help users maintain familiar typing habits across different work environments.
Boosted Productivity, Lasting Power
Designed for multi-device workflows, the ElecWave KF01 can pair with up to three devices via Bluetooth, allowing users to switch between them as needed. With dedicated Mac and Windows key layouts and automatic operating system recognition, it supports familiar keyboard functions across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Dedicated screenshot and emoji shortcuts further streamline everyday tasks.
The KF01 features USB-C charging and is designed to minimize interruptions throughout the workday. Its battery supports up to 100 hours of continuous use, up to 180 days of standby time, or approximately two months of regular office typing between charges. To conserve power, an automatic sleep feature activates after two hours of inactivity; the keyboard wakes with a keystroke.
Pricing and Availability
The ElecWave KF01 is now available on Amazon, starting at $39.99.

articles.title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
articles.text:
Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania, one in New York, and one in Wisconsin.
Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania’s health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state’s seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County, but state health officials have not confirmed it.
For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania’s case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650.
Lost status
With outbreaks that have been smoldering and flaring since last year, the US has reportedly lost its measles elimination status—as medical and public health experts have widely expected it would. A panel of experts for the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a regional branch of the World Health Organization, convened last week to review US measles data and assess its elimination status. The PAHO is set to announce its conclusion and the review’s other findings on Tuesday, November 17. But sources broke the news to The Wall Street Journal on Friday that the panel had found that the US had indeed lost its status.

articles.title: Logitech boosts MX Master 4 mouse with stylish special editions
articles.text:
If you’ve been eyeing Logitech’s excellent MX Master 4 mouse, but aren’t thrilled by the boring colour options, the company finally has a solution.
The MX Master 4 now has two special edition options, both of which boast snazzy new visuals on top of the same excellent features. The MX Master 4 Special Edition comes in two options, ‘Creator’ and ‘Developer.’
Logitech launched the Creator variant (pictured above) alongside the Adobe Max event earlier this week, and it starts shipping today. While the Developer version launched last month alongside the GitHub Universe event last month.
The Creator Special Edition is my favourite of the two mice, sporting a wonderful red and white colourway. (Though maybe I just like it because it matches MobileSyrup…) I love all the subtle lines to popular creator software, like the keyframe graphics and calibration band.
And the timeline on the mouse sports a few easter eggs, including 4:21 (International Day of Innovation and Creativity), 4:27 (World Design Day), 8:19 (World Photography Day), and 10:27 (World Day of Audiovisual Heritage).
The Developer Special Edition mouse is also quite nice with its two-tone body and the lime-green accents. I appreciate the little details on it as well, like the ‘Hello, World’ text on the thumb rest.
Aside from style, the new Special Editions don’t add anything to the existing MX Master 4 formula. When I reviewed it earlier this year, I was a fan of the design and ergonomics, the vertical and horizontal scroll wheels, and useful software features like the Actions Ring. The support haptics are a nice addition as well, though they don’t add much to the experience.
Since the Special Editions only bring a surface-level visual upgrade, I appreciate that Logitech didn’t increase the price. Both the Creator and Developer editions cost $159.99 in Canada (though at the time of writing, the Developer edition was temporarily sold out).

articles.title: Trump Administration Moves to Block China From Indirect Access to American AI Technology
articles.text:
The Trump administration on Monday issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, marking the latest step to limit China’s abilities to use U.S. chips to train their best artificial intelligence models.
The rule also was issued days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid scrutiny of his ties to a Chinese executive who used to lead Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The company provides computing power to Chinese companies using chips housed in Southeast Asian data centers, including facilities in Malaysia.
“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries,” the Bureau of Industry and Security under the Commerce Department said in issuing the rule that took effect immediately.
Under the new rule, overseas data centers that serve companies in countries including China, Russia, Iran and Cuba are required to identify their end users. There also will be an additional, case-by-case licensing requirements for sales of chips for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil — countries that “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to unauthorized destinations, the rule says.
The U.S. bans sales of the country’s most advanced AI chips to China, seeking to maintain an edge in its rivalry with China for predominance in artificial intelligence. However, many lawmakers and policymakers believe the country’s export control rules are not tough enough and filled with loopholes such as cloud computing that allow China to rent processing power built on American technology.
Last year, U.S. Rep. Michael Lawler, a New York Republican, introduced a bill to broaden the U.S. export controls to include remote access. He told Congress “physical export controls” under current rules do not apply to remote access, allowing China to “access our tech through the cloud” and giving it “a real tool to sidestep” U.S. export restrictions. The bill has passed the House.

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (16/11/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta segunda-feira (16/11).
Pix completa 6 anos com mais de 1 bilhão de chaves cadastradas
Lançado pelo Banco Central em novembro de 2020, o Pix completa seis anos em 2026 ultrapassando a marca de 1 bilhão de chaves cadastradas no Brasil, cerca de 80 milhões a mais do que no fim de 2025. Apenas em setembro deste ano, o sistema registrou 7,1 bilhões de transações, movimentando aproximadamente R$ 3,2 trilhões. Ao longo dessa trajetória, a ferramenta incorporou novos recursos, permitindo agendar transferências, automatizar pagamentos, comprar por aproximação e até realizar saques em estabelecimentos comerciais.
Starship é recuperada no ar com sucesso pelos braços robóticos da SpaceX
Em um marco histórico para a exploração espacial, a espaçonave Starship, da SpaceX, orbitou a Terra e retornou ao planeta sendo capturada no ar pelos braços mecânicos da própria torre de lançamento, apelidados de chopsticks. O feito ocorreu ao final do 15º voo de teste, lançado na última sexta-feira (13).
Saída de CEO da Nvidia deixa dúvida no ar: e se Musk ou Zuckerberg caírem?
A saída de Jensen Huang do comando da Nvidia expôs um desafio de governança que também ronda outras gigantes da tecnologia: a ausência de planos claros de sucessão para seus fundadores. O cenário acende um alerta para empresas como Meta, Tesla e SpaceX, cujas estratégias e operações estão profundamente atreladas às figuras de Mark Zuckerberg e Elon Musk — sendo que, no caso de Musk, os próprios documentos financeiros das companhias já admitem os riscos ligados a uma eventual ausência do executivo.
Estados Unidos ampliam restrições a chips de IA e incluem o Brasil
O governo dos Estados Unidos anunciou nesta segunda-feira (16), durante viagem do presidente Donald Trump à Ásia, novas restrições à exportação de chips avançados de inteligência artificial para data centers fora do território americano. A medida, que busca evitar que empresas chinesas acessem componentes dos EUA por meio de terceiros para treinar seus modelos, passou a incluir o Brasil, além de Singapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia. Com a regra, companhias desses cinco países, apontados por Washington como destinos de alto risco para o desvio ilegal de tecnologia à China, precisarão solicitar licenças específicas ao governo americano para importar determinados processadores.
Beatriz Campos é jornalista formada pela Universidade São Judas Tadeu e jornalista do Olhar Digital.
André Milhomem integra a equipe de redes sociais do Olhar Digital e do programa Olhar Digital News.

articles.title: Island is a new screen-time app that turns staying off your phone into a game | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A new startup is taking a different approach to helping people manage their screen time. Instead of blocking apps or restricting the phone’s use after a set period, an app called Island encourages you to meet your screen time goals by way of a farming simulator game. Yes, a game! Island works by rewarding you when you’re disciplined enough to meet your goals with a “credit score” that increases your farm’s production, unlocking new crops, animals, and other content.
This carrot-instead-of-stick approach was dreamed up by entrepreneurs Ashish Selvaraj (CEO) and Ethan Pronev (CTO), who met while studying at the University of Waterloo, then went on to work at companies that included Jane Street, Citadel, Databricks, and Microsoft.
Later, they quit their jobs to join the startup accelerator Y Combinator, where they first tried out other ideas in areas like B2B and software-as-a-service, but weren’t finding the right fit.
Island ended up being their fifth pivot, and the first the founders actually found themselves enjoying.
“Once we were in YC, I think there’s a big mindset — I think in [San Francisco], in general — of, ‘selling shovels.’ Everyone wants to ‘sell shovels’ to other companies, and around us, that’s just what was going on,” explains Selvaraj, speaking about the concept that many successful startups sell the tools, infrastructure, or services to others following whatever the current market boom or trend may be.
“So all the ideas we had — we tried these things — but we found that we weren’t passionate about it. Like idea after idea seemed like ultimately the product was just a dashboard with some kind of different backend,” he added. “It felt like we quit our jobs … just to do something that was a variation of that.”
With Island, the team gets to tap into their creativity, having drawn the pixel art themselves.
“A lot of people do use [AI] models to generate the art, but we felt that it had a certain character when we drew it ourselves,” he told TechCrunch. “I feel like with Claude getting so good, there’s a tendency to give away every task to Claude. But ultimately it feels like there’s something else that comes out when you do it yourself, especially in something like art,” Selvaraj said.
What’s more, the app does appear to be successful in helping users meet their goals, the startup’s early data shows. After early testing and an October launch, the team says that the majority of its users (82%) will end their screen time right at the limit they’ve set. Many more are ending their screen time when they get the “15 minutes left” warning.
Island could appeal to those who have given up on other screen time apps out of frustration because the app doesn’t actually lock you out of apps or your phone. That’s something that can end up being more disruptive, especially when you’re in the middle of doing something, like posting, sharing, commenting, or chatting, among other things. Instead, Island taps into users’ own self-discipline and their desire to see their island flourish to encourage screen time breaks.
The idea to encourage users to keep their goals by offering some other type of in-app reward system isn’t entirely novel. Last year, Hank Green’s screen time app Focus Friend went viral for its experience, which involved a little friend that could only knit items that, in turn, allowed you to get points used to decorate your room when you were focused on your non-distracting apps.
Similar ideas have been used in self-care apps and habit-trackers like Finch, Amaru, Belly, Flora, Urso, and others. But Island expands this concept from being focused on helping out a virtual friend or pet to one that’s more of a game — and one where you can experience the consequences without “having to torture your pet,” notes Selvaraj.
Island also allows users to add friends and visit each other’s islands, compete in group challenges, and keep each other accountable by tying your island together with one friend of your choosing. In the latter scenario, if either friend goes over their limit, both of their islands will suffer.
The startup says Island has proven to be fairly “sticky” with a 51% daily active users-to-monthly active users ratio, and a day 30 retention rate of 49%, meaning 49% of users were still active on the app on the 30th day since the app was installed.
The app is currently free to use, with a $39.99 per year subscription that allows you to set individual limits on different apps, instead of just an overall daily screen time limit. The company hasn’t raised additional seed funding outside of YC, but plans to begin marketing the app on social media for the rest of the year.

articles.title: Fable 5.2 creates an underwater world in a browser in only 96 KB — 40-line prompt creates impressive demo that runs at 180 FPS
articles.text:
Fable 5.2 creates an underwater world in a browser in only 96 KB — 40-line prompt creates impressive demo that runs at 180 FPS
Elegant effort is reminiscent of both old- and new-school demoscene.
Claude Fable 5.2 was released recently to mostly rave reviews, with both users and analysis outlets ranking it nipping at the heels of the much pricier Opus 5.5. Perhaps as practical proof of that claim, front-end developer Maksymilian Dendura took inspiration from the demoscene and had Fable roll his own virtual underwater world, Abyssal Garden, in only 96 KB of Javascript/HTML — you can check it out here.
The demo's 3D space and textures are all procedurally generated, meaning they're the result of mathematical equations rather than prebuilt 3D meshes, and all calculated on load. Using actual meshes and images for textures would otherwise take up a significant amount of space.
Building structures procedurally is difficult and has limitations, but it's exceedingly effective when used properly. Some games employ this technique for repeated elements like trees and grass.
Likewise, all the visual effects and even some texturing are done with shaders, which are small programs that change how a mesh or texture appears — for example, to make parts of an object shiny. Games use them extensively, as many players are aware, thanks to endless "loading shaders" screens or Unreal Engine's st-tu-tutering.
The result is definitely impressive, especially but not only as it's purely browser-based, relying on WebGPU and WebGL. Both are rarely-mentioned technologies that have actually existed for a long while now. As their names imply, they let developers render 2D and 3D graphics in a manner similar to that of OpenGL, but in a browser, using JavaScript as the base language.
The demo's most impressive fact is the simplicity of the prompt that got Fable 5.2 to build it. It's only about 40 lines long with word wrapping, and clearly illustrates the degree of autonomy that contemporary agentic AI has when given a specific, yet exceedingly open-ended task like this one. It's reasonable enough to assume the author did a few rounds of tweaking (and he has excellent artistic taste too), but the agent's acumen is nevertheless impressive.
Comparing this demo to an actual game is inevitable, but the reality is that demos have but an atom-sized fraction of the content of a full game, and are limited to little or no interaction, logic, or physics.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Performance is decent for what is a great-looking but otherwise tiny and almost featureless space. The author says that he's getting 180 FPS at 1440p on an RTX 5070 Ti. Likewise, having this world in 97 KB sounds impressive, but it's actually gigantic for this type of demo, even if an X user further optimized it for 52 KB.
Regular computing users, including AI neophytes and acolytes, may not be aware that this kind of space-optimized programming for the purposes of visual/aural demonstrations is a discipline and art form that harkens back to the 1980s when 16-bit computers appeared — called the "demoscene."
By no means discounting the extraordinary fact that Fable did this nearly all by itself — which is the actual achievement here — code wizards have pulled off nearly impossible feats decades ago, including in browsers. The 2009 demo Elevatedn (17 years ago) has a comparable aesthetic, and includes music, in just under 4 KB (yes, four). There's even a browser version of it, taking up all of 4,777 bytes.
Hartverdrahtet (2012 — 14 years ago) has a highly complex 3D space, again in 4 KB. And old-timers in the audience will remember ".kkrieger", an FPS game prototype that fit in all of 96 KB, including meshes, textures, music, and sound effects... back in 2004.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Also follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

It gave my iGPU a workout but maintained 60 FPS at a 720p-ish resolution on the lowest detail setting. I expected worse but it worked quite well. Reply

articles.title: Google quietly purged 362 shady Russian Chrome VPN extensions following TechRadar investigation — but the Chrome Web Store’s ‘whack-a-mole’ continues
articles.text:
Google quietly purged 362 shady Russian Chrome VPN extensions following TechRadar investigation — but the Chrome Web Store’s ‘whack-a-mole’ continues
Copycats are still slipping past Chrome's defenses
Last month, TechRadar published an investigation highlighting 369 suspicious VPN extensions targeting Russian users. Since then, Google has removed all but seven of them.
Many of the purged extensions used throwaway, personal developer emails, had inadequate privacy policies and mimicked well-known brands, including ExpressVPN and Windscribe. Several had even been flagged in threat intelligence reports months before.
While the removal of these apps is a positive step, a quick look through the Web Store shows that there’s still work to be done.
Hundreds of shady VPN extensions removed
Our initial investigation flagged more than 350 extensions targeting Russian civilians, which had over 200,000 users combined.
VPNs have become a critical tool in Russia owing to heightened internet censorship and surveillance. Unfortunately, this also means they have become a prime target for groups looking to turn a quick profit.
We shared details of all the extensions included in our investigation with Google ahead of publication and, less than one month later, almost all of them have been removed from the Chrome Web Store.
Google did not respond to requests for comment to confirm whether the extensions were removed as a result of our investigation or as part of routine maintenance of the store.
Ongoing enforcement issues
Looking at the VPN and proxy Chrome extensions still live today, it's clear that many apps bearing all the same hallmarks of an untrustworthy operation remain.
These include a Russian extension using the Nord brand name, extensions with thousands of downloads managed from personal email addresses, and others hosting privacy policies on anonymous sites.google.com domains.
We also found three active VPN extensions linked to an email address previously flagged as belonging to a threat actor. We inspected the source code of one of these apps and found comments suggesting it is deliberately avoiding standard permissions to slip past Google’s Manifest V3 security rules.
In the extension's source code, the developer explicitly notes that they “intentionally avoid” requesting host_permissions, webRequest, and other standard functions to maintain a "safe MV3 install flow".
While a proxy or VPN extension doesn’t necessarily need those permissions, notes on its compliance in its source code suggest it may have been structured in a way to immediately pass Google’s automated checks.
Either way, it’s clear that cleaning up the Chrome Web Store is no easy feat. As Rebecca Rosenberg, Head of Growth at Windscribe, previously told TechRadar: “It’s pretty much a game of whack-a-mole now, [a] copycat is pulled and two more pop up.”
We’ve shared details of some of the live extensions referenced in this article with Google and asked for more details on how the company is protecting users of its extension store. The company did not respond by the time of publication.
Are VPN extensions really worth it?
Even as Google removes hundreds of shady VPN extensions, the Web Store still contains apps that you would be better off avoiding. And the issue runs deeper than bad actors.
In fact, VPN extensions are, by their very nature, not the best tool if you’re looking to protect your privacy online.
Speaking to TechRadar, a senior technical expert at Russian digital security group RKS Global said: “A Chrome extension is not a VPN in the technical sense. It does not create a tunnel; it uses the browser's API to configure a proxy: HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS. That is why it has limitations.”
This means that any other internet-connected activity on your device runs unencrypted and unprotected — including messaging apps, email apps, and anything else running outside your browser.
The RKS Global spokesperson also noted that “reliable anti-censorship protocols such as AmneziaWG, VLESS with Reality, or Shadowsocks cannot be implemented inside an extension”. So, choosing an extension to evade internet censorship in a highly monitored location such as Russia is rarely the best option.
That’s made worse by the fact that many of these shady extensions were, of course, never designed for censorship circumvention in the first place. Instead, they were built to turn a profit, with some actively harming your privacy rather than improving it.
The RKS Global spokesperson highlighted proxyware as one such example, where “a free ‘VPN’ extension turns the user's browser into an exit node of a residential proxy network”. In this scenario, a user’s home IP and bandwidth may be sold off to third parties for ad verification, web scraping and other unauthorized uses.
Open-source anti-censorship VPN provider AmneziaVPN told TechRadar that the number of extensions with “malicious functionality” had grown recently. The company said extensions that “steal VPN keys from various services” are “released every day” and that there are also “plugins that carry malicious code for surveillance or for stealing data”.
While it’s unclear whether the extensions recently purged by Google were capable of this, experts warn that aggressive censorship in Russia is pushing users directly into the path of scams.
“State policy in Russia, under which the genuine clients of circumvention apps have been purged from the stores and blocked while demand has remained, has provided the ground for the growth of fakes in the stores and of the murky schemes through which people have to install anti-censorship solutions,” RKS Global concluded.
For anyone looking to protect their traffic, the safest approach is to use a full, system-wide VPN. Or, if you need a standalone browser extension, avoid Chrome Web Store search results and download it via a direct link on a trusted provider's website.
While Google's latest purge shows it is willing to remove the worst offenders, sticking to verified sources is well worth the extra click.
Sam is VPN Managing Editor at TechRadar. He has worked in the VPN industry since 2018 and has previously written for CNN, Al Jazeera, WIRED, and Deutsche Welle as a freelance journalist. He focuses on VPNs and digital privacy, cybersecurity and internet freedom.
Before joining TechRadar, Sam carried out research on global digital rights issues at Top10VPN. His research has been cited by the United Nations and UK Parliament, as well as publications such as The Guardian, Washington Post and BBC.

articles.title: Usable Security at Luxury Hotels - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Usable Security at Luxury Hotels
Interesting case study from luxury hotels. Attackers used a fake booking request to gain access to a reservations inbox, where they copied genuine refund requests and got fraudulent ones approved.
This is a good illustration why “just don’t click on links” is bad advice. It can’t work when answering strangers’ emails is the job. Even worse, in this case the guest-first culture punishes hesitation. More interesting, the case study shows that splitting security between owner, operator, and brand leaves nobody accountable. And this is exactly the setting where blaming staff becomes the convenient answer.
TimH • November 16, 2026 7:22 AM
TFA: “We suspect a colleague opened the email and clicked the link, unknowingly giving the attackers access to the reservations shared inbox.”
So there was no front-end layer checking inbox content for such dubiosities? Or limiting access to specific computer MACs, or intranet IP ranges.
The ball is in the IT org’s court for not setting this up.
Same with IT who can’t set a limit of 5 CCs on emails to stop an email blast CCing every customer.

articles.title: Apple manquerait de temps pour corriger le principal défaut de l’iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Parmi les concessions qu’Apple a dû faire pour parvenir à mettre au point l’iPhone Duo, l’absence de Face ID est sans doute celle qui a été le plus regrettée par les utilisateurs (avec l’absence d’un téléobjectif). À la place d’un système de reconnaissance faciale, ils ont eu affaire au bon vieux Touch ID. Un comble pour un appareil qui se veut à la pointe de la technologie, tout en affichant des prix particulièrement élevés. Mais si l’entreprise à la pomme savait dès le départ que ce manquement allait être pointé du doigt, elle compte bien le combler sur les prochaines générations de l’appareil. Seulement voilà, les caractéristiques techniques de l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération doivent être finalisées maintenant, et Apple serait actuellement dans une véritable course contre la montre.
Une course contre la montre pour parvenir à intégrer Face ID à l’iPhone Duo 2
Selon le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple aurait pour objectif de lancer l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération à l’automne 2027. Mais cela ne veut pas dire que l’entreprise bénéficie d’encore un an pour mettre au point l’appareil. En réalité, les caractéristiques matérielles de ce dernier doivent être fixées dès maintenant, c’est-à-dire un an avant sa commercialisation.
En octobre dernier, Mark Gurman avait expliqué qu’Apple travaillait sur plusieurs prototypes d’iPhone Duo 2 intégrant Face ID. Sur ces appareils, le système de reconnaissance faciale d’Apple serait situé sous l’écran externe. Les prototypes existent donc, mais l’entreprise à la pomme parviendra-t-elle à en mettre au point un à temps ? Selon Gurman, Apple serait actuellement face à un calendrier très serré.
Apple n’aurait pas pu prendre en compte les retours des utilisateurs de l’iPhone Duo
Il faut également préciser qu’Apple n’aurait pas été en mesure de prendre en compte les retours des utilisateurs de l’iPhone Duo de première génération pour définir les principales caractéristiques matérielles de son successeur, celles-ci ayant été fixées depuis déjà un certain temps. Par conséquent, si l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération intègre bel et bien Face ID, cela ne sera pas en raison des contestations des utilisateurs. En réalité, Apple était conscient dès le départ de ce manquement, mais n’a pas eu d’autre choix que d’effectuer cette concession afin de mettre au point un écran d’une épaisseur de 5,2 mm lorsqu’il est déplié. Pour rappel, Face ID nécessite une certaine profondeur pour pouvoir fonctionner.
Il reste maintenant à voir si l’entreprise à la pomme parviendra à intégrer de justesse Face ID sur l’iPhone Duo de seconde génération. Dans le cas contraire, il faudra attendre la troisième génération. Dans tous les cas, il s’agit de la priorité d’Apple pour son iPhone pliant.

articles.title: Silicon Motherboard Integrates ICs and Passive Components - EE Times
articles.text:
Nisshinbo Micro Devices developed Silicon Motherboard (Si-MB), a novel 3D packaging technology. By mounting ICs and external components on both sides of a small silicon substrate and enclosing them in a single package, this technology significantly reduces the mounting area. This kind of innovative advancement is poised to significantly contribute to downsizing devices and systems.
● Increasing demand for smaller, higher density designs
The number of semiconductors deployed across a wide range of devices and systems, including automobiles, industrial equipment, and consumer electronics, continues to rise steadily. Concurrently, the overarching push to shrink overall device sizes has created increasingly stringent constraints on the available mounting area. As a result, manufacturers are now under immense pressure to achieve further miniaturization and higher integration of components, all while maintaining absolute reliability under harsh operating conditions. As the number of components increases, the supply chain becomes more complex, and procurement risks increase, making the reduction of the bill of materials (BOM) another critical objective.
To meet these demands, Nisshinbo Micro Devices developed Silicon Motherboard (Si-MB)*.
*“Si-MB” is a registered trademark of Nisshinbo Micro Devices.
● Mounting ICs and passive components on both sides of the substrate
Silicon Motherboard is a 3D packaging technology that integrates ICs and electronic components in which circuits are formed on both sides of a silicon substrate, and the entire assembly is enclosed within a single package.
Transistors, resistors, and capacitors are first formed inside the silicon substrate using a wafer fabrication process. Functional chips, such as operational amplifier ICs and power management ICs, are then mounted on the top surface of the substrate. External passive components that are difficult to integrate into an IC, such as chip resistors and chip capacitors, are then mounted on the printed wiring on the bottom (back) surface of the substrate. Finally, this silicon substrate is housed in commonly used packages of SOP, QFN, and SON. This approach allows for higher component density by consolidating components while using existing packages.
The most prominent feature of this setup is the mounting of external components on the bottom surface of the substrate. More specifically, a resin, which serves as an insulating film, is applied and cured on the back surface where a wiring layer for mounting components is then formed via printing. This makes it possible to integrate passive components, such as high-capacity capacitors of 1,000 pF or more, low-resistance resistors of 1 Ω or less, and inductors, onto the silicon substrate.
Yoshio Fujii, manager of the Package Development Department at Nisshinbo Micro Devices, emphasizes that this technology matters because the motherboard is made of silicon. Mr. Fujii says, “The use of silicon allows us to leverage the semiconductor wafer fabrication process to increase wiring density and mount functional chips. Components that cannot be processed using semiconductor methods can be mounted on the back surface. Since real estate (mounting area) is at a premium, this technology uses both the top and bottom surfaces, contributing to an overall reduction of costs.”
Another factor helping to reduce costs is the use of existing packages for Silicon Motherboard. Even when a specific technology can highly integrate and significantly downsize devices, if the technology then requires new evaluation equipment or mounting processes, customers may be reluctant to adopt it. “Our customers want to achieve miniaturization and higher performance right away,” explains Fujii. “Since we use existing packages with a proven market record of accomplishment, no new investment in evaluation equipment is required, which allows customers to start evaluations and prototyping immediately. A major advantage of Silicon Motherboards technology is that they enable high-density miniaturization within a short timeframe while maintaining quality.”
● Mounting passive components: a challenge for chiplet integration
As improvements in semiconductor performance through advances in front-end semiconductor manufacturing processes become increasingly difficult, 3D packaging technology is attracting significant attention as a cost-effective way to boost performance. One technology drawing particular attention is chiplet integration. While chiplet integration can significantly increase integration density, this packaging technology is specifically designed for ICs, making it difficult to integrate passive components as well. “In particular, mounting passive components on the back surface of the substrate is not realistic from a manufacturing process standpoint,” notes Fujii. Furthermore, bonding integrity at the connection points poses challenges that limit durability.
In contrast, both chips (packaged devices) and passive components can be mounted freely on a conventional printed circuit board (PCB) assembly. However, since the mounting area depends heavily on the placement pitch, achieving significant downsizing remains difficult.
Silicon Motherboard addresses the challenges associated with conventional component mounting and emerging chiplet integration and successfully delivers three key elements: the flexibility to mount diverse components, high-density packaging, and the durability required to operate stably in harsh environments.
● Reduction of 80% to 90% in mounting area
When Nisshinbo Micro Devices prototyped window comparator and current-sense amplifier circuits using Silicon Motherboard technology, the company successfully reduced the mounting area by 80% to 90% compared to a discrete circuit.
Two comparator ICs were mounted on a silicon substrate on the window comparator prototype, with resistors formed inside the substrate using a wafer fabrication process. On the bottom surface of the substrate, chip resistors were mounted onto the printed wiring. This resulted in an approximately 90% reduction in the mounting footprint compared to conventional configurations.
Current-sense amplifiers are used for motor current control and other purposes. In general, current passes through a low-resistance shunt resistor, and the resulting potential difference across it is amplified by an operational amplifier. When this configuration was implemented using Silicon Motherboard, the mounting area was successfully reduced by approximately 80%. According to Akihiko Matsunobu, manager of the Package Development Department at Nisshinbo Micro Devices, this prototype eliminates the need for a shunt resistor, which typically occupies a large area, by using the printed circuit traces on the back of Silicon Motherboard as the resistive element.
● Targeting automotive applications, industrial equipment, and AI servers
Nisshinbo Micro Devices plans to propose the use of Silicon Motherboard in automotive applications like electronic control units (ECUs), industrial robots and other equipment, and AI servers. ECUs and robots, in particular, feature a high ratio of analog semiconductors that demand high quality. While development cycles need to be shortened, keeping costs low is also essential. Nisshinbo Micro Devices believes Silicon Motherboard is well suited for such applications. The company is currently evaluating systems using Silicon Motherboard in collaboration with multiple manufacturers.
The company is also working to enhance heat dissipation properties. High-density packaging is plagued by thermal issues. Fujii notes that while there is still room for improvement even with Silicon Motherboard, silicon has high thermal conductivity, which makes it easier to achieve superior heat dissipation compared to organic substrates.
This new 3D mounting technology from Nisshinbo was initially developed using organic and ceramic substrates. However, organic substrates present the challenges of warping and contamination by dust and foreign particles. Since the substrates easily absorb moisture, problems of the components delaminating during the reflow soldering process also occurred. In contrast, silicon does not absorb water, offers high rigidity, and minimizes warping. “While silicon substrates have superior physical properties, organic substrates have the upper hand in terms of cost. Therefore, we leveraged our design and manufacturing expertise to reduce the area of the silicon substrate, thereby achieving high-density packaging while keeping costs down,” says Fujii.
Nisshinbo Micro Devices manufactures Silicon Motherboard-based devices using its own 5-inch and 6-inch wafer production lines. Although the company’s in-house factories can handle wafers up to 8 inches, Fujii explains, “We anticipate starting primarily with sample shipments and PoC (Proof of Concept) projects, so we plan to utilize the 5-inch and 6-inch lines, which allow for rapid production.”
● The key is an approach unique to an analog semiconductor IDM
Fujii says, “Silicon Motherboard is a technology that we were able to establish precisely because we are an IDM (integrated device manufacturer) specializing in analog semiconductors.”
Ultimately, an analog IC’s performance depends on its design and its integration with peripheral components such as resistors, capacitors, and inductors. Therefore, while the front-end process improves analog IC performance, back-end packaging technology that optimizes the IC and peripheral components as a single unit is crucial to ensure high performance and reliability in devices and systems.
“From the very beginning, our motivation was to incorporate peripheral components into a modular design to improve the performance and usability of analog ICs,” says Fujii. This approach, which is unique to an IDM specializing in analog semiconductors, led to the successful development of Silicon Motherboard.
“While we will thoroughly handle the packaging process for fabricating Silicon Motherboard-based devices, we believe that the functional ICs mounted onto it do not necessarily have to be Nisshinbo Micro Devices products,” says Fujii. “Because it offers a high degree of freedom in component placement, it is also easy to customize. Mixed-signal circuits (circuits combining digital and analog elements) can be implemented quickly. A major advantage that Silicon Motherboard offers customers is the ability to achieve flexible component mounting with short lead times without being limited to our own ICs,” he adds.
Born from an approach unique to an analog semiconductor IDM, Silicon Motherboard is poised to become a technology that meets the demand for further miniaturization of equipment and systems.

articles.title: GTA 6 donne un aperçu de sa météo particulièrement réaliste avec six nouvelles images
articles.text:
La sortie de GTA VI approche à grands pas. Attendu le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, le prochain jeu de Rockstar Games continue de faire parler de lui avec une nouvelle série d’images. Cette fois, le studio s’est associé à The Weather Channel pour présenter six captures de son monde ouvert sous différentes conditions météo.
Toujours dans l’idée de faire une communication un brin différente et décalée, ces nouvelles images sont présentées comme de véritables bulletins météorologiques par la chaîne de télévision américaine spécialisée. Des images, publiées sur le compte X de The Weather Channel ce 16 novembre 2026, et qui permettent surtout d’apprécier le travail réalisé sur les effets atmosphériques, la lumière, la pluie, le brouillard et les nuages.
Il faut dire qu’il y a de quoi faire : en situant son jeu à Leonida, l’État fictif inspiré de la Floride, Rockstar dispose d’un terrain idéal pour multiplier les phénomènes météorologiques, des fortes chaleurs et du grand soleil aux pluies torrentielles et aux violentes tempêtes, avec des conséquences visibles sur les paysages. Formation des nuages, brume, reflets sur les surfaces mouillées ou encore variations de luminosité, les amateurs de temps qui se détraque vont se régaler.
Six nouvelles images pour découvrir les caprices météo de Leonida
Les six captures mettent en scène des endroits différents de la carte. Chacune illustre un phénomène météorologique particulier, avec une attention évidente portée à la lumière, aux effets de l’eau et à la visibilité.
Au-delà de leur qualité graphique (admirez les nuages de la dernière image (bon sang), ces six nouvelles captures donnent un aperçu des ambitions de Rockstar Games. Dans GTA 6, les conditions météorologiques doivent être localisées, dynamiques et persistantes.
Les intempéries laisseront également des traces après leur passage, avec des flaques, des routes détrempées, de la brume et une visibilité réduite. Les nuages, le vent et l’état de la mer participeront eux aussi à cette météo évolutive. Reste à découvrir jusqu’où ces différents phénomènes influenceront concrètement la conduite et les activités des joueurs.
GTA VI sera disponible le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Sudanese fintech startup Cashi raises $660k from Proparco - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Sudanese fintech startup Cashi has raised US$660,000 in funding from Proparco, marking the French development finance institution’s first investment in Sudan.
Founded in 2022 by the team behind alsoug.com, which became Sudan’s leading online marketplace, Cashi is building a digital payments ecosystem for underserved markets, working around the limits of the country’s traditional payment infrastructure.
Users can deposit and withdraw cash, pay bills and transfer money through a network of local merchants, so they rely less on banks. Its MyCashi digital wallet has 2.2 million registered users, and it is especially popular with young people.
Network disruptions are common in Sudan, so Cashi has also built USSD, SMS, offline card and other non-app products. These keep transactions going and help aid organisations get humanitarian assistance to people in areas where connectivity is poor.
The funding from Proparco will support Cashi’s work in fragile markets, mainly its mission to provide reliable financial services in Sudan. The country is in a severe humanitarian and economic crisis, with limited access to banking, ongoing cash shortages and frequent outages of telecoms and payment systems.
“In Sudan today, being able to send, receive or withdraw money can decide how a family gets through the month, or whether a small shop stays open. When the banks were unavailable during the war, Cashi stayed open and available. We built it to keep working when cash runs short and the network drops,” said Nina Saeed, CEO of Cashi.
“Today, millions of consumers and merchants use Cashi. Millions more across Sudan still have no bank account and no ATM nearby. Where you live should not decide whether you can get paid, pay a bill or send money home. They are the people we are building for.”
The deal is part of Proparco’s wider push to back African businesses meeting critical development needs, especially in fragile and conflict-affected countries.
“In fragile contexts such as Sudan, access to reliable financial services is not only a driver of economic development, but also an essential means of supporting livelihoods and strengthening resilience,” said Guillaume Barberousse, global head of investment at Proparco.
“This first operation in Sudan reflects our commitment to supporting entrepreneurship and financial inclusion, including in the most challenging environments.”

articles.title: Yet another massive cyberattack hits Japan — city of Osaka latest to be hit, as more than a million email addresses exposed
articles.text:
Yet another massive cyberattack hits Japan — city of Osaka latest to be hit, as more than a million email addresses exposed
The Arara saga continues, now spilling into government entities
- Osaka City disclosed exposure of 1.08 million email addresses through the wider Arara email platform breach
- Stolen data included addresses used for government notifications, account activity, and administrative services
- Officials warned residents to watch for phishing emails impersonating Osaka City or related online systems
The Arara email exposure saga continues, as after Asoview, MOS Burger and Sega, we can now add the City of Osaka to the list of victims as well after it warned of losing more than a million emails and urged citizens to be wary of incoming phishing and other scam emails.
On November 13, Osaka City also disclosed being affected via a third-party service provider called TKC Corporation, a Japanese IT and software company that provides cloud-based technology services to businesses and government organizations, including accounting systems and public administration platforms.
The city said whoever received a notification between July 1 and October 31, 2026, has likely had their email address exposed to threat actors:
“Anyone who received an email from the System (sender address: info-osaka-online@city.osaka.lg.jp) between July 1, 2026 (Wednesday) and October 31, 2026 (Saturday) [is affected],” the machine-translated notice reads.
TKC Corporation struck
For Osaka City, TKC provided and operated the Osaka City Administrative Online System, a digital platform through which citizens can register accounts, log in, submit applications, and receive administrative notifications.
“The leaked information includes the email addresses to which the System sent messages in connection with user registration, changes to email addresses, password changes, logins, applications and other administrative procedures, changes in application processing status made by Osaka City, notifications and other announcements from the System.”
It is worth mentioning that these are the topics of the emails the city sent to affected individuals - passwords and logins were not exposed themselves.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Users of the System are asked to check their email histories to determine whether they received messages from the above sender address between July 1 and October 31, 2026,” Osaka concluded.
According to the notice, exactly 1,078,713 user email addresses were exposed. The city now urges those citizens to be wary of incoming emails:
“There is a possibility that suspicious emails related to this incident may be sent,” it said. “Even if an email claims to come from Osaka City or the System, do not open links or attachments in unexpected or unsolicited emails; enter your user ID, password, PIN, credit card details or other personal information, or respond to emails requesting payment.”
Arara affected again
The attack is the latest concerning Arara - a technology firm providing digital marketing and customer engagement services. One of its offerings is Arara Message, an email distribution platform that businesses can use to send newsletters and other communications to millions of people. Through it, Arara gets to manage contact information on behalf of those organizations - emails, names, phone numbers, and more.
In early November 2026, Arara reported its email distribution infrastructure was breached. Apparently, a combination of a web server vulnerability and “other system weaknesses” allowed unidentified threat actors to access 97 servers that stored data of up to 380 corporate customers. Obviously, Arara juggled a lot of clients, many of which now have to deal with email leakage.
Before Osaka City, multiple other companies confirmed being affected: Asoview reported approximately 15.82 million records, while electronics retailer Bic Camera reported 15.2 million. Fast-food chain MOS Burger disclosed the exposure of some 7.5 million email addresses, while cinema operator Shochiku Multiplex Theaters 3.3 million. Sega and its subsidiary Sega Fave disclosed approximately 2.2 million affected email addresses.
In total, the unidentified actors walked away with more than 81 million email addresses, together with other personally identifiable data. In a subsequent report, Arara added that the attackers compromised a separate environment containing additional 3.38 million email addresses and more than 400,000 customer records containing PII.
With 380 corporate customers at risk, it’s safe to assume this is not the last time we hear of the Arara breach.

articles.title: Cursor Supply Chain Attack Started at Fireworks AI
articles.text:
Credentials compromised in the hack of AI inference platform Fireworks AI allowed attackers to steal more secrets and push malicious Claude Code extension copies, Cursor says.
The supply chain attack was discovered on October 29 and resulted in threat actors making two modified versions of the anthropic.claude-code extension (2.1.312 and 2.1.313) available through the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace for roughly 11 hours.
Anthropic was never hacked, and all the malicious activity occurred in Cursor’s environment, the company explains.
Instead, Cursor was hit after Fireworks was hacked twice in October. First, internal Fireworks credentials were used to access Fireworks stored secrets and account and billing information. Then, a third-party cloud provider was compromised, Fireworks development machines were reached, and customer data was stolen.
A Cursor access key issued to Fireworks was compromised in one of these incidents and the attacker used it to copy data from a read-only storage bucket, including unredacted credentials that opened the door to SaaS tools used by Cursor.
“From these tools they accessed select archived non-production Cursor source code repositories (some containing business contact information), limited customer support data and email conversations, product usage metrics and contact details, summaries of some coding agent conversations, and some credentials users had sent to the Cursor support team,” Cursor explains.
While Cursor blocked the attacker’s access immediately after discovering the unauthorized activity, the attacker used secrets exfiltrated from the company’s internal systems to place “malicious, unauthorized copies of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension directly on the cache used to serve the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace.”
The malware was never present in the Open VSX marketplace source, but was served to the users who requested the cached versions of the extension. According to Cursor, at most 5,000 users were affected.
“If customers installed or updated to the tampered version Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 from the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace during the exposure window, we ask customers to follow the steps in our security notice. Uninstalling the extension alone may not be enough,” Cursor notes.
The company considers the incident contained, as it has not seen attacker activity in its environment since November 1.
Notion and Uber also disclosed data breaches stemming from the Fireworks compromise.
