articles.title: Black Friday : Amazon PULVÉRISE les prix des Echo, Ring et Fire TV, jusqu’à -83%
articles.text:
Amazon vient de lancer ses premières promos Black Friday sur ses propres appareils, à quelques jours du 27 novembre. Nous avons retenu 10 offres, des clés Fire TV aux enceintes Echo et aux caméras Ring et Blink, en précisant pour chacune si nous l’avons testée ou non.
Cette sélection s’ouvre sur le produit que nous avons testé, l’Echo Show 11, avant de passer à ceux que nous n’avons pas encore eus entre les mains. Elle couvre le streaming, les enceintes et écrans Echo, ainsi que les caméras et sonnettes Ring et Blink, avec des remises de 21 % à 83 % par rapport au prix conseillé. Le pack Blink Outdoor 4 avec sonnette concentre à la fois la plus forte économie en euros, 124,99 €, et la plus forte remise en pourcentage.
- Amazon Echo Show 11 à 199,99 € au lieu de 269,99 € (-26 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Stick HD à 23,99 € au lieu de 64,99 € (-63 %)
- Pack Blink Outdoor 4 + sonnette vidéo 2K+ à 24,99 € au lieu de 149,98 € (-83 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max à 52,99 € au lieu de 114,99 € (-54 %)
- Amazon Kindle 16go à 139,99€ au lieu de 174,99€ (-20%)
- Amazon Echo Spot (2024) à 59,99 € au lieu de 119,99 € (-50 %)
- Amazon Echo Studio à 189,99 € au lieu de 239,99 € (-21 %)
- Ring Caméra intérieure Plus, lot de 2 à 44,99 € au lieu de 119,98 € (-63 %)
- Amazon Echo Dot (nouvelle génération) à 78,99 € au lieu de 104,99 € (-25 %)
- Ring Battery Video Doorbell 2K à 49,99 € au lieu de 99,99 € (-50 %)
Echo Show 11 : noté 7/10 par notre rédaction, à 199,99 €
Notre test de l’Echo Show 11 lui a attribué 7/10. Son écran tactile Full HD de 11,95 pouces est jugé lumineux et précis, le son stéréo à 360° remplit une pièce d’environ 20 m² et Alexa se montre très réactive. Notre testeur a en revanche relevé des bugs tactiles et des latences dans l’interface.
✅ Points forts
- Un design plus élégant : l’écran semble flotter au-dessus d’une enceinte recouverte de tissu mesh, en blanc ou en graphite.
- Un son qui emplit la pièce : deux haut-parleurs stéréo à l’avant et un woofer pensé pour une diffusion à 360°.
- À savoir : notre test, publié en janvier 2026, relevait des bugs tactiles qui persistent et une saturation du son à haut volume.
Fire TV Stick HD : le streaming Full HD en Wi-Fi 6, à 23,99 €
Amazon le présente comme son lecteur HD en streaming le plus rapide à ce jour. Il offre une image Full HD, prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6 et donne accès à Prime Video, Netflix, YouTube, Disney+ ou encore TF1+. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une installation simplifiée : la clé est alimentée par le port USB de la TV grâce au câble USB-C fourni, sans adaptateur secteur.
- Un format ultra-portable : elle se branche directement sur le port HDMI sans bloquer les autres ports.
- À savoir : il se limite à la Full HD. Pour la 4K, voir le Fire TV Stick 4K Max, plus bas dans cette sélection.
Pack Blink Outdoor 4 et sonnette 2K+ : 124,99 € de remise, à 24,99 €
Ce pack réunit la caméra extérieure sans fil Blink Outdoor 4, une sonnette vidéo 2K+ et un module de synchronisation. La caméra embarque une détection de mouvements double zone, la sonnette filme en 2K avec vision nocturne infrarouge et audio bidirectionnel. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Deux appareils en un seul pack : surveillance de l’extérieur et sonnette vidéo, pilotables depuis la même application Blink.
- Une installation sans fil : l’ensemble se configure en quelques minutes, kits de montage inclus.
- À savoir : les notifications spécifiques aux personnes demandent un abonnement Blink, vendu séparément. Un essai gratuit de 30 jours est inclus.
Kindle : la liseuse plus fine et plus rapide, à 139,99 €
Cette nouvelle génération de Kindle passe à un boîtier plus fin et plus léger, avec un écran de 6 pouces antireflets à luminosité réglable. Amazon annonce une ouverture des livres 30 % plus rapide qu’avec son prédécesseur et jusqu’à 6 semaines d’autonomie avec une seule charge. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une autonomie annoncée de 6 semaines : l’écran ne consomme de la batterie que lorsque vous tournez la page ou utilisez l’éclairage avant.
- Une batterie remplaçable : le boîtier arrière s’ouvre pour changer la batterie, puis se clipse de nouveau.
- À savoir : c’est la remise la plus faible de la sélection, -20 %. La télécommande Kindle Click et l’étui en maille sont vendus séparément.
Fire TV Stick 4K Max : Dolby Vision, Wi-Fi 6E et 16 Go, à 52,99 €
C’est le stick le plus puissant de la gamme Fire TV selon Amazon. Il gère la 4K Ultra HD avec Dolby Vision, HDR10+ et le son Dolby Atmos, prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6E et propose une fonction Écran dynamique pour afficher des photos ou des œuvres d’art. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une image 4K complète : Dolby Vision, HDR et HDR10+ sont pris en charge, avec l’audio Dolby Atmos.
- Plus de place pour vos applications : 16 Go de stockage, soit le double du Fire TV Stick 4K et des autres sticks d’Amazon, selon le constructeur.
- À savoir : il coûte plus du double du Fire TV Stick HD : sans téléviseur 4K, l’écart ne se justifie pas.
Echo Spot : le réveil connecté avec Alexa, à moitié prix, à 59,99 €
L’Echo Spot est un réveil connecté qui affiche l’heure, la météo et le titre du morceau en cours, avec des cadrans et des thèmes de couleur personnalisables. Il diffuse de la musique et des podcasts via Alexa et sert aussi de commande pour les appareils connectés compatibles. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un réveil en douceur : une routine Alexa peut vous réveiller avec de la musique et un éclairage progressif.
- Un écran personnalisable : le style du cadran et le thème de couleur se choisissent depuis l’appareil.
- À savoir : pour un son plus ample, l’Echo Studio, présenté plus bas, passe en Dolby Atmos, mais à 189,99 €.
Echo Studio : Dolby Atmos et hub connecté intégré, à 189,99 €
L’Echo Studio mise sur l’audio 3D et le Dolby Atmos, avec des basses puissantes selon Amazon. Il analyse l’acoustique de la pièce pour ajuster la lecture en continu et intègre un hub pour piloter des appareils compatibles Alexa sans boîtier séparé. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un son 3D en Dolby Atmos : l’enceinte vise un rendu immersif, avec des voix limpides et des basses profondes.
- Un réglage automatique : il s’adapte à l’acoustique de la pièce, où qu’il soit placé.
- À savoir : c’est la remise la plus faible de la sélection, -21 %, pour un prix final de 189,99 €.
Ring Caméra intérieure Plus, lot de 2 : deux caméras 2K à 44,99 €
Cette caméra intérieure filme en 2K, propose un zoom jusqu’à 4x et conserve des couleurs fidèles dans la pénombre, avant de passer en noir et blanc dans l’obscurité totale. Le lot en comprend deux, à brancher sur une prise standard. Nous ne les avons pas testées.
✅ Points forts
- Une vidéo 2K avec zoom 4x : de quoi repérer des détails à distance, de jour comme en faible luminosité.
- Une confidentialité maîtrisée : un cache d’objectif manuel et des zones de confidentialité se règlent à la demande.
- À savoir : la sauvegarde des vidéos sur 180 jours et les alertes de détection de personnes exigent un abonnement Ring, vendu séparément.
Echo Dot nouvelle génération : un hub connecté intégré, à 78,99 €
Amazon présente cet Echo Dot comme le premier de la gamme à intégrer un hub connecté. Il promet 1,5 fois plus de basses et peut être jumelé à un second Echo Dot pour du son stéréo. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un hub intégré : il pilote lumières, stores et centaines d’appareils compatibles, sans hub séparé.
- Un son stéréo possible : deux Echo Dot se jumellent pour un rendu stéréo.
- À savoir : c’est l’une des remises les plus modestes de la sélection, -25 %, pour un prix final de 78,99 €.
Ring Battery Video Doorbell 2K : la sonnette sans fil à moitié prix, à 49,99 €
Cette sonnette sans fil filme en 2K avec un zoom jusqu’à 6x, propose l’audio bidirectionnel et se pose soi-même. Sa batterie intégrée se recharge en USB-C. Nous ne l’avons pas testée.
✅ Points forts
- Un zoom jusqu’à 6x : de quoi inspecter un visage ou un détail à distance.
- Une pose sans fil : la sonnette se détache avec l’outil fourni pour se recharger en USB-C.
- À savoir : la batterie n’est pas amovible, le câble USB-C n’est pas fourni et les vidéos conservées 180 jours passent par un abonnement Ring.
Black Friday 2026 : ce que change le calendrier d’Amazon
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30. Amazon affiche déjà la mention « Offre Pré-Black Friday » sur ces neuf produits. Les prix de cette sélection ont été relevés le 16 novembre 2026 et peuvent évoluer d’ici là, à la hausse comme à la baisse. Pour suivre l’ensemble des remises sans y passer vos soirées, notre page Black Friday réunit les offres retenues par la rédaction, chez Amazon comme chez les autres enseignes.
Comment savoir si une promo high-tech est vraiment intéressante ?
Regardez d’abord le prix de référence : sur la fiche Amazon, la mention « prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours » permet de vérifier que la baisse est récente, et elle correspond au prix conseillé pour la plupart des produits de cette sélection. Pensez ensuite au coût réel de l’usage : les caméras et sonnettes Ring ou Blink limitent certaines fonctions, comme les alertes de personnes ou la conservation des vidéos, à un abonnement vendu séparément. Vérifiez enfin ce que l’appareil sait faire avec votre équipement, car un Fire TV Stick 4K Max n’apporte rien sur un téléviseur Full HD, et une note obtenue en test vaut mieux qu’une promesse de fiche produit.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform
Imagine a batch job that has run every night for decades without failing, and the only person who understands its code is about to retire. We have seen this situation again and again while working with banking, insurance, and airline customers. Their Assembler programs still run critical business operations, but fewer people can read them each year. Rewriting them by hand takes years, risks breaking business rules nobody remembers writing, and still depends on the same experts who are leaving. Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform change that equation.
This post shows you a multi-stage transformation methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE (an AI-powered integrated development environment), and AWS Transform that can help reduce modernization time compared to manual approaches while maintaining business logic integrity through validation checkpoints. You will learn how to systematically extract business rules from Assembler code, convert them through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized applications as Java Spring Boot services on AWS.
Prerequisites
Before starting the modernization process, make sure you have:
- Active AWS account with least-privilege AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions for Amazon Bedrock, AWS Transform, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).
- Access to Amazon Q Developer or Kiro for AI-assisted code analysis.
- Access to AWS Transform for COBOL to Java conversion.
- Access to Amazon Bedrock with appropriate foundation models (FMs).
- An Amazon S3 bucket configured for source code and artifact storage, with encryption and Block Public Access enabled.
- Knowledge of the target business domain and application functionality.
- Availability of business and technical subject matter experts (SMEs) for validation sessions.
- Source Assembler code inventory with available documentation.
- Test data sets with expected outputs for functional equivalence testing.
Solution overview
You can transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications tightly bounded with COBOL into Java Spring Boot applications built for the AWS cloud through a systematic five-phase approach. This multi-stage methodology, converting Assembler to COBOL as an intermediate step before Java transformation, reduces risk and preserves business logic with greater reliability than direct Assembler-to-Java conversion. The intermediate COBOL stage provides a structured, human-readable format that subject matter experts (SMEs) can validate before final transformation. This makes sure that business rules remain intact throughout the modernization journey. The following sections describe both the current mainframe architecture and the target cloud-focused state.
Current state
Your current architecture represents a traditional mainframe environment where Assembler programs execute batch processes, connected with COBOL, interact with databases, and process files. At its core, JCL (Job Control Language) jobs trigger Assembler program execution at scheduled intervals. These programs read input from VSAM (Virtual Storage Access Method) and sequential files and perform operations against IBM Db2 for z/OS. Your business logic executes using low-level register operations (direct CPU register manipulation) and memory management. Output is written back to files or database tables, and job completion status is reported through JCL return codes. All of this runs on IBM z/OS mainframe infrastructure.
Target state
The modernization solution helps you transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications into Java applications built for the AWS cloud through a multi-phase, AI-powered workflow. The architecture uses Amazon Bedrock and Kiro IDE for AI-assisted code analysis and business rule extraction, and AWS Transform for automated COBOL-to-Java conversion.
If COBOL source code is already available, you follow the conventional approach and provide it directly to AWS Transform for conversion to Java Spring Boot applications.
With this solution, you can achieve:
- Reduced transformation time compared to manual approaches.
- Systematic business logic preservation through validation checkpoints.
- Human-in-the-loop validation at critical stages.
- Automated code conversion with functional equivalence testing.
You begin the transformation workflow by analyzing Assembler code to generate Business Rules Extraction (BRE) documentation. You then create detailed functional specifications with human-in-the-loop refinement. The validated specifications guide the Assembler-to-COBOL conversion, generating intermediate COBOL code that bridges the gap between low-level hardware instructions and business-oriented constructs. This COBOL code undergoes functional equivalence testing before AWS Transform converts it to Java, with validation checkpoints at each phase to reduce risk and verify business continuity.
Business rules extraction with AI
The quality of your Business Rules Extraction (BRE) directly impacts transformation accuracy, so focus carefully on this phase. Use Amazon Bedrock, through Kiro IDE or the Amazon Bedrock console, along with AWS Transform for mainframe to extract and document business rules from your Assembler source code.
You can use the prompts in this post directly in Amazon Bedrock through the Chat Playground, or within Kiro IDE using its built-in AI chat and Spec panel. Replace the placeholder values with your actual Assembler code and context before running.
Amazon Bedrock is the inference platform behind the first four phases: business rules extraction, specification creation, Assembler-to-COBOL conversion, and validation. Choose a foundation model with strong code reasoning and a large context window, because Assembler programs are long and dense. Set the temperature to 0 so you get consistent output across runs. To process many programs, call the same prompts through the Amazon Bedrock Converse API and store each output in your Amazon S3 bucket so it can feed the next phase. Amazon Bedrock doesn’t use your prompts or model outputs to train AWS models or share them with third parties. For details, see Data protection in Amazon Bedrock. Use sanitized test data instead of production data or personally identifiable information (PII).
The more context you provide to the AI, the better it understands the business intent behind the code. Include relevant documentation, data dictionaries, and available business context alongside the Assembler code when prompting.
Note: Save the output of each prompt as you go. You will need them as inputs in the next phase.
Example prompt for context-aware analysis:
You can customize this prompt by adding domain-specific terminology from your business context. When you run this prompt, you will see structured JSON output that you can use for automated validation and direct integration with downstream transformation tools. Data mapping accuracy directly affects conversion quality. Incomplete mappings can lead to lost or corrupted business logic.
Validate with SMEs
Treat AI-generated BRE documents as drafts, not final outputs. Have subject matter experts review and validate the extracted rules before moving forward. Document discrepancies in a validation log and update the BRE based on SME feedback before proceeding to specification creation.
To help SMEs validate the rules, supplement textual BRE documents with visual aids like flowcharts and data flow diagrams. Maintain a validation checklist covering business rule accuracy, data mapping correctness, edge case handling, and error condition completeness.
Extracting spec-driven data flow
After you validate business rules with SMEs, translate them into detailed functional specifications that will guide code conversion. This spec-driven approach confirms that business requirements are clearly documented and agreed upon before code transformation begins, reducing costly rework later.
Use the extracted BRE documents to create complete functional specifications that guide COBOL code generation. These specifications should include program overview, COBOL data structures, process flow design, and business rules coverage mapping.
Example prompt for functional specification generation:
You can adjust the data structure specifications based on your COBOL standards. When you run this prompt, you will receive a complete functional specification with full traceability from business rules to COBOL structures, ready for SME review and direct integration with Kiro for code generation.
Converting legacy Assembler to COBOL
With validated functional specifications in hand, the next phase uses these structured outputs to guide the Assembler-to-COBOL conversion. The intermediate COBOL step helps you bridge the gap between low-level hardware instructions and business-oriented constructs, which helps you verify that business logic is preserved before the final Java transformation.
Example prompt to guide the conversion:
You can modify the formatting requirements to match your organization’s COBOL standards. When you run this prompt, you will generate COBOL code designed to be syntactically correct, logically equivalent to the original Assembler, and fully traceable, with comments linking each code section back to specific business rules from the BRE document. Once generated, rigorously validate the COBOL code before proceeding to the final Java transformation.
Validating the transformation
You should treat testing as an ongoing activity throughout the transformation process, not only a final phase. Your functional equivalence validation between Assembler and COBOL code should employ a comprehensive testing framework that systematically evaluates syntax correctness, structural alignment, logic equivalence, data flow integrity, business rules coverage, and specification compliance.
Example prompt to guide the testing:
You can customize the validation thresholds based on your quality requirements. When you run this prompt, you will receive a comprehensive validation report with actionable recommendations for addressing gaps in program structure, conditional logic, data transformations, and traceability between the original Assembler instructions and the modernized COBOL implementation.
COBOL to Java transformation
In the final phase, you use AWS Transform to automatically convert validated COBOL code into Java Spring Boot applications. Generate production-ready Java code with the intelligent refactoring in AWS Transform. This refactoring preserves the business logic validated in previous phases while introducing modern design patterns, including dependency injection, repository patterns, and service layers.
You can deploy the resulting Java applications on AWS infrastructure to achieve cloud scalability and resilience while maintaining the same business functionality as your legacy mainframe systems. This cloud-focused approach replaces monolithic mainframe architecture with modular, maintainable code that can be independently deployed, monitored, and enhanced.
For detailed step-by-step instructions, refer to the AWS Transform Refactor Workshop.
Lessons learned
When you apply this methodology in practice, here are the key lessons that can shape your approach:
- Human-in-the-loop validation is essential for transformation quality. Amazon Bedrock and Kiro IDE can help improve business rule identification, but AI-generated documents should always be treated as drafts. SME review is essential at every critical stage, not only during extraction, to catch domain-specific logic, edge cases, and business context that AI tools may overlook. This human oversight can help reduce post-deployment defects compared to automated conversion without structured checkpoints.
- The intermediate COBOL step reduces risk. You will find the multi-stage approach (Assembler to COBOL to Java) with validation checkpoints at each phase more reliable than attempting direct conversion. The intermediate step helps you verify business logic preservation before committing to the final Java transformation.
- A spec-driven methodology helps you prevent rework. Creating detailed functional specifications before code conversion catches misunderstandings early. With structured JSON specifications, you can also automate validation and direct integration with transformation tools.
- Incremental validation helps you accelerate your overall timeline. Testing after each transformation stage, rather than waiting until the end, helps you detect issues early and reduces overall rework. Quality gates at each phase help confirm the output is ready for the next stage.
Conclusion and next steps
In this post, we walked through a systematic, AI-powered approach to transform legacy mainframe Assembler applications into Java applications built for the cloud on AWS. This approach combines Amazon Bedrock and Kiro IDE for intelligent business logic extraction with AWS Transform for automated COBOL-to-Java conversion. By following a multi-stage methodology with validation checkpoints at each phase, you can help accelerate modernization timelines while preserving critical business logic integrity.
To evaluate the full service landscape and understand how the components fit together, start with the AWS Mainframe Modernization documentation. When you’re ready to see the pipeline in action, the AWS Transform Refactor Workshop walks you through the end-to-end process with sample workloads you can run in your own environment. If you’d like to discuss how this approach applies to your specific environment, contact an AWS representative.
Tell us about your modernization journey and share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: “Todos los que importan en el sector tecnológico fuera de los laboratorios admiran a Jensen”: líderes piden regreso a Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk y más de 165.000 personas firmaron una carta abierta que exige a la junta directiva de Nvidia la reincorporación de Jensen Huang como consejero delegado, apenas días después de que el cofundador de la compañía renunciara al cargo tras conocerse que mantuvo una relación extramatrimonial con una presunta espía china.
La presión llega en un momento sensible: este martes Nvidia presentará sus resultados trimestrales, en medio de una investigación interna sobre la conducta de Huang y de un debate abierto sobre quién debería liderar la empresa de chips valuada en 4 billones de dólares.
Quiénes piden el regreso de Huang y por qué
La campaña para reinstalar a Huang se extendió durante el fin de semana. Además de Musk, firmaron la carta abierta Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, y Garry Tan, presidente de Y Combinator. Entre los firmantes también figura Travis Kalanick, cofundador de Uber, quien escribió que Huang “erró, sí, errar es humano, pero no creo que nada de lo que hizo alcance el umbral para separarlo de su compañía”.
Más de 7.500 firmantes se identificaron como empleados de Nvidia, equivalentes al 18% de la plantilla de la empresa.
En paralelo, un aliado de Huang confirmó a Financial Times que un grupo de ejecutivos de Silicon Valley armó un “cuartel de guerra” para presionar por su regreso y buscar apoyo en la Casa Blanca. “Todos los que importan en el sector tecnológico fuera de los laboratorios de vanguardia admiran a Jensen”, afirmó esa persona, que agregó que el propio Huang respalda estos esfuerzos.
Brad Gerstner, fundador de Altimeter Capital, y Gavin Baker, director de Atreides Management, ambos accionistas de Nvidia, publicaron el viernes una carta abierta en la que piden a la junta dejar “todas las opciones sobre la mesa, incluido el posible regreso de Jensen Huang”, y citaron “el éxito extraordinario” de su liderazgo como argumento.
Incluso entre sus aliados persisten las dudas sobre cómo rehabilitar su reputación. Una persona involucrada en los esfuerzos por su reincorporación reconoció que “tener una relación extramatrimonial con una subordinada es motivo de despido”.
Los obstáculos políticos y financieros para un regreso
El camino de regreso de Huang enfrenta resistencia en Washington. El secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, pidió el domingo una “reorganización drástica” en el liderazgo de Nvidia y sostuvo que la empresa debería buscar a su próximo CEO “afuera” de la compañía.
Bessent planteó que la prioridad no es la infidelidad de Huang, sino que Nvidia explique si permitió a sabiendas que sus chips de IA más avanzados llegaran a China. Estados Unidos prohíbe la venta a ese país de los semiconductores de punta como parte de su estrategia para mantener la delantera en la carrera por la inteligencia artificial: a fines de 2025, Trump autorizó la venta de los chips H200, pero no de los modelos superiores.
“Nada por encima de los H200 puede venderse a los chinos”, dijo Bessent, quien exigió respuestas de la investigación interna de Nvidia en un plazo de diez días.
No todos en el sector financiero respaldan la posibilidad de un regreso. El analista Dan Ives, de Yorkville Ives, calificó de “ridícula” la idea de reinstalar a Huang y definió la petición pública como “ruido y distracción”. Para Ives, el mejor camino para la empresa es un CEO externo o la confirmación permanente de Kress en el cargo.
Cómo fue la salida de Jensen Huang de Nvidia
Huang renunció el jueves pasado, después de 33 años al frente de la compañía que ayudó a fundar en 1993. Su salida se precipitó tras conocerse que mantuvo al menos dos relaciones extramatrimoniales: una con una subordinada y otra con Alice Huang, ejecutiva de la empresa singapurense Megaspeed, señalada como presunta espía para China.
La relación con Alice Huang disparó un escrutinio adicional sobre los controles de cumplimiento de Nvidia en sus ventas de chips de inteligencia artificial a clientes asiáticos con posibles vínculos con Pekín.
Megaspeed fue uno de los mayores clientes extranjeros de la compañía en los últimos tres años, con compras cercanas a los 5.000 millones de dólares en chips y hardware avanzado. El domingo, la firma se defendió calificándose como “un negocio legítimo y lícito”.
Jensen Huang acordó comparecer ante el comité selecto de la Cámara de Representantes sobre China, además de los comités de asuntos exteriores e inteligencia, aunque las fechas de esas audiencias, previsiblemente a puertas cerradas, no fueron confirmadas.

articles.title: 11,000 applied, 10 made the cut: Meet the UAE-India Start-up Series finalists
articles.text:
11,000 applied, 10 made the cut: Meet the UAE-India Start-up Series finalists
Ten start-ups in AI, climate, deep tech and digital assets, chosen from more than 11,000 applications, pitch in Bengaluru on 18 November for a place in Hub71’s Abu Dhabi programmes.
More than 11,000 Indian start-ups applied to the second edition of the UAE-India Start-up Series. Ten are left. On the afternoon of 18 November in Bengaluru, each will get seven minutes to argue that its business is ready for the UAE: three minutes to pitch and four to answer questions.
The UAE-India Start-up Series helps Indian start-ups enter and scale in the UAE market. It is anchored in the UAE-India Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), whose start-up provisions call for closer ties between incubators and accelerators in the two countries. Abu Dhabi's technology ecosystem Hub71 is the Series' cross-border partner. Its second edition, the UAE-India Start-up Series 2.0, ends with a two-day Final Pitch Event on 17 and 18 November.
The edition arrives as more Indian founders look to the Gulf for their next market. The UAE offers capital, a route into the wider region and a business culture many Indian companies already know. The harder question, and the one the final will test, is which companies can turn that interest into paying customers there.
From 11,000 applications to ten
The ten finalists come from four sectors: artificial intelligence (three start-ups), energy and climate (three), deep tech and robotics (three) and digital assets (one). They are based across the country, from Bengaluru, Chennai and Pune to Bhubaneswar and West Bengal.
Most are well past the idea stage. Several report revenue in the millions of dollars, and three already sell into the UAE:
- Onsite counts 59 UAE customers among its 1,591 paying customers.
- Flo Mobility has robots working on construction sites for ALEC in the UAE.
- XYMA Analytics has deployed its sensors with Emirates Steel.
The final pitches come after a day and a half of preparation. Finalists will meet investors one-on-one and take part in mentorship and pitch practice. That includes a session led by Hub71 on entering and scaling in the UAE.
The winners will be announced on the night of 18 November, when the Top 50 Investment Dossier will also be released.
The ten finalists
The finalists are listed below in the order they will pitch. Figures are as reported by the companies to the organisers.
What is at stake: a route into Abu Dhabi
The main prize is a place in Hub71's programmes in Abu Dhabi. Hub71 first announced its partnership with the Series in November 2025 and confirmed it for the second edition at its Impact Event in June 2026.
Hub71 Access Programme. Three start-ups will be shortlisted and one will be onboarded. That company gets up to AED 250,000 (about ₹65 lakh) in in-kind incentives and AED 250,000 (about ₹65 lakh) in cash through a SAFE note, an investment that converts into equity at a later funding round. It also receives mentorship, investor introductions, regulatory support and access to Hub71's corporate and government partners.
Hub71 Immersion Programme. Up to six start-ups will spend a week in virtual preparation on the Abu Dhabi and UAE ecosystem. They then spend a week at Hub71 in person, with sessions on market entry and introductions across its partner network. According to the Series website, the UAE leg for selected start-ups begins in March 2027.
What the first edition delivered
The first edition of the Series concluded in New Delhi in 2025, with twenty start-ups pitching in its final. Five of them moved on to Hub71. Endimension, an AI-first radiology platform, joined the Access Programme as part of Cohort 18. BioReform, Docket Run, Data Sutram and SBNRI entered the Immersion Programme.
The second edition has a smaller final and a field that is, on paper, further along. One question to watch is whether the jury backs start-ups that already have UAE customers or those with the most room to grow there. The longer test comes after the event: how many finalists build a lasting presence in the UAE.

articles.title: 7 Tips For Complying with CJIS Password and MFA Requirements
articles.text:
Compromised passwords and gaps in multi-factor authentication (MFA) remain common ways attackers gain access to sensitive systems. For law enforcement agencies handling criminal justice information (CJI), protecting against these threats is also a matter of CJIS compliance.
The FBI's latest CJIS Security Policy sets clear requirements for password management and MFA. these are Priority 1 (P1) controls, so must be implemented immediately to comply. But this can be challenging, particularly across the complex IT environments that are common in law enforcement.
This guide contains practical tips to help agencies meet the latest requirements, strengthen their defenses against credential-based attacks, and make ongoing compliance easier to manage.
1. Enforce Stronger Minimum Password Lengths
CJIS requires user-selected passwords to be at least eight characters long, or six characters if generated by a credential service provider or verifier using an approved random number generator. However, we recommend going beyond these minimums and encouraging passphrases of at least 15 characters.
Longer passwords are generally harder to crack, and passphrases can be easier to remember than shorter passwords with complex combinations of symbols and numbers.
CJIS doesn't require traditional complexity rules, so focus on length and strength rather than arbitrary character requirements.
2. Block Weak and Compromised Passwords
Agencies must maintain a list of commonly used, predictable, and compromised passwords. This should include passwords exposed in previous breaches, dictionary words, sequential characters, and context-specific terms such as usernames or agency names.
CJIS requires agencies to update this list at least quarterly, and whenever organizational passwords are suspected of being compromised.
Solutions like Specops Password Policy with Breached Password Protection can simplify this process with CJIS-aligned password policy templates. You can create an unlimited custom dictionary of blocked words unique to your agency, with granular controls for blocking weak constructions.
Importantly, the Breached Password Protection feature delivers continuous screening against a growing database of more than six billion compromised passwords.
Secure your Active Directory passwords with Specops Password Policy
Verizon’s Data Breach Investigation Report found stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches. 
Effortlessly secure Active Directory with compliant password policies, blocking 4+ billion compromised passwords, boosting security, and slashing support hassles!
3. Reset Passwords Quickly and Give Users Clear Feedback
Agencies must force a password change whenever there's evidence that a credential has been compromised. Don't rely solely on scheduled password changes to address exposed credentials.
You must also check existing passwords against the breach list at least quarterly. More regular checks can help identify compromised credentials earlier, giving IT teams an opportunity to respond before attackers exploit them.
CJIS also requires users to select a new password immediately whenever compromise is suspected.
When a user does need to create or reset a password, rather than displaying a generic error message, provide clear, real-time feedback that helps users understand what makes a password weak and how to improve it.
Specops Password Policy delivers that support, making it easier to create strong, memorable passwords while reducing frustration and unnecessary help desk requests.
4. Protect Passwords in Transit and At Rest
Password security doesn't end with enforcing strong credentials. CJIS also requires passwords to be transmitted over encrypted, authenticated channels to prevent interception and man-in-the-middle attacks.
When stored, passwords must be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function, making them more resistant to offline cracking if an authentication database is compromised.
Agencies should review how their applications and authentication systems handle credentials to ensure these protections are in place.
5. Require MFA For All Privileged and Non-Privileged Accounts
CJIS requires MFA for both privileged and non-privileged organizational accounts. Don't focus solely on administrator accounts. Standard user accounts can also give attackers access to sensitive data or provide a foothold for further attacks.
Review your accounts and access policies to identify where MFA is missing, including accounts belonging to employees and contractors.
6. Extend MFA Across All Relevant Access Methods
CJIS requires MFA for local, network, and remote access. Agencies should review authentication across their environment, ensuring that all systems that touch CJI are adequately protected.
Solutions such as Specops Secure Access helps agencies extend MFA to Windows logons, RDP, and VPN connections, with single sign-on (SSO) support for compatible SaaS applications through OIDC and SAML.
7. Make Sure Your MFA Methods Meet CJIS Requirements
CJIS specifies Authenticator Assurance Level 2 (AAL2), which requires two different authentication factors. This is a combination of something you know (like a password), something you have (like a smart card), or something you are (like a fingerprint).
Review your authentication methods to ensure they meet these requirements. Where possible, consider phishing-resistant MFA methods to provide stronger protection against credential phishing and adversary-in-the-middle attacks.
Keep Your Authentication Controls Effective
CJIS compliance doesn't end once you've implemented strong password policies and MFA. Regularly reviewing your authentication controls, checking for compromised credentials, and auditing Active Directory can help you identify security gaps before attackers exploit them.
As a starting point, Specops Password Auditor performs a free, read-only AD audit that checks for weak or compromised passwords and inactive privileged administrator accounts. You’ll get the results in an easy-to understand interactive report that highlights your current exposure.
By combining strong authentication controls with regular security assessments, agencies can reduce credential-related risks and make ongoing CJIS compliance easier to manage.

articles.title: ¡Es oficial! Robert Pattinson es el nuevo James Bond
articles.text:
Los rumores estaban en lo cierto. Amazon MGM Studios acaba de confirmar a Robert Pattinson como el nuevo James Bond. La estrella de The Batman, La Odisea, Tenet, Mickey 17 y la saga Crepúsculo es el elegido para reemplazar a Daniel Craig en el papel del agente 007. Su primer trabajo será en la nueva película que tendrá la dirección del canadiense Denis Villeneuve.
Los detalles sobre la contratación de Robert Pattinson como nuevo James Bond son escasos, por no decir prácticamente nulos. Además de la primera foto oficial del actor como 007, los responsables de la saga han compartido un breve vídeo en el que el intérprete aparece entre las sombras portando su pistola.
El pasado viernes, un reporte de Puck News generó revuelo al indicar a Robert Pattinson como el candidato número 1 de Amazon MGM Studios para ser el próximo James Bond. Hasta aquí, el actor no aparecía entre los candidatos al papel, lo cual provocaba gran sorpresa.
Con la noticia ya confirmada, es evidente que la información que manejaban los insiders no estaba para nada fuera de lugar. Al momento de redacción de este artículo, no se han dado a conocer los pormenores del acuerdo con Robert Pattinson como James Bond. No obstante, el primer rumor apuntaba a un contrato por tres películas. Esto aún no se ha confirmado públicamente.
"James Bond es uno de los personajes más legendarios del cine, y que se me confíe el papel de 007 es el honor de toda una vida. Estoy profundamente agradecido con Denis, Amy, David, Tanya y con todo el equipo de Amazon MGM Studios por haber confiado en mí. Decir que este papel es un sueño hecho realidad es quedarse corto. No podría estar más entusiasmado con esta colaboración y con el trabajo que tenemos por delante junto a este equipo fantástico", dijo Pattinson en un comunicado compartido con la prensa.
Robert Pattinson, el primer James Bond de la era Amazon
De esta manera, Robert Pattinson se convierte en el primer James Bond de la era Amazon. Recordemos que la compañía obtuvo el control creativo de la saga del agente 007 a principios de 2025, luego de décadas en manos de EON Productions. Esto se produjo en gran medida por el descontento de la firma de Jeff Bezos con las restricciones que imponía Barbara Broccoli cada vez que le acercaban alguna propuesta relacionada con la propiedad intelectual.
Si bien en un principio se rumoreó que Amazon MGM Studios pagó alrededor de 1.000 millones de dólares para el control total sobre James Bond, la realidad habría sido otra. A finales del año pasado se supo que el acuerdo se habría cerrado por apenas 20 millones de dólares. Los pormenores de la negociación nunca se revelaron públicamente.
Tras la confirmación de Robert Pattinson, Denis Villeneuve también se pronunció al respecto. "Antes que nada, quiero expresar mi profundo agradecimiento a los extraordinarios actores que nos acompañaron en este viaje. Contamos con un talento excepcional a nuestro alrededor, pero solo puede haber un 007. Me llena de alegría dar la bienvenida a Robert Pattinson como nuestro nuevo James Bond. Él posee el alma atemporal de 007 y aporta un espíritu totalmente novedoso. No veo la hora de empezar", remarcó el cineasta.
Además de Villeneuve como director y de Robert Pattinson como protagonista, la próxima película de James Bond tendrá a Steven Knight, el creador de Peaky Blinders, como guionista. Los productores serán Amy Pascal y David Heyman. Por lo pronto, la cinta no tiene fecha de estreno ni otros protagonistas confirmados. Se espera que Villeneuve se ponga manos a la obra cuando culmine la gira promocional de Dune: Parte tres, que se estrena en diciembre. En dicho filme ya trabajó con Pattinson, de modo que ya existe un antecedente entre ambos.

articles.title: Rockstar organiza conciertos, saca bandas sonoras y pone todo el peso en el sonido de GTA VI: ya funciona casi como una discográfica
articles.text:
Rockstar venderá su juego más esperado sin disco y, al mismo tiempo, pondrá su música en CD, en vinilo y en una edición limitada que cuesta más que el propio juego. La aparente contradicción tiene toda la lógica (aunque sea la del mercado): la saga nació dentro de una discográfica, y ahora Rockstar vuelve a funcionar como si fuera una. La presencia del audio en la franquicia es mucho más relevante de lo que parece.
Guest stars. Rockstar empezó detallando las seis primeras emisoras de 'GTA VI' y anunció que también habría un podcast bajo demanda disponible, algo inédito en la saga (y muy apropiado para reforzar su humor), además emisoras conversacionales cuando los personajes vayan a pie, gracias a auriculares conectados al móvil. Además, hay invitados especiales: Cocoteo FM, que Rockstar define como "la fiesta que nunca se apaga", y que en el juego presentan El Martillo y La Gata, que tiene detrás, según varios medios, a Bad Bunny y RaiNao. También Lana Del Rey podría estar tras la emisora de country Back Country Radio.
Como una discográfica. Alrededor de las emisoras, Rockstar ha montado un calendario de lanzamientos propio de un sello. 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album', con 34 temas originales, llega a las plataformas de streaming el 19 de noviembre, como el juego. Sus seis primeros sencillos reúnen a Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Morgan Wallen, Rauw Alejandro o el dúo argentino CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso. A ellos se suman Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa, Zara Larsson, Jennie, Arca o Justice. El álbum con la partitura de Justice, de 30 cortes más varios extras digitales, llega el 11 de diciembre. Es una decisión inesperada para una franquicia que casi siempre se ha limitado a licenciar canciones previas.
Historia de una partitura. Sam Houser, fundador de Rockstar, empezó su carrera en 1990 clasificando el correo en la sede londinense de la discográfica BMG. Era un trabajo de verano, pero en 1996 ya dirigía BMG Interactive, la rama de videojuegos de la empresa, y que en 1998 vendió a Take-Two la división con todos los derechos de 'GTA'. Antes, el primer 'GTA' de DMA Design cambiaba de emisora al cambiar de coche, con música compuesta en el propio estudio. Unos años después, en 2013, 'GTA V' incluyó la primera música ambiental dinámica original de la serie, y Rockstar publicó un volumen entero de canciones nuevas de Wavves, Twin Shadow o Tyler, The Creator.
El problema de alquilar canciones. El grueso de la radio de 'GTA' se ha ido construyendo a lo largo de los años con catálogos licenciados, un alquiler que tiene fecha de caducidad. Por ejemplo, en abril de 2018 Rockstar tuvo que retirar canciones de 'GTA IV' porque vencían licencias firmadas a diez años. Según la propia compañía, el recorte afectaba sobre todo a Vladivostok FM, la emisora de pop ruso, donde hubo que meter temas nuevos a modo de parche.
El poder prescriptivo de GTA. Es la cara que más interesa a las discográficas. Tras el primer tráiler de 'GTA VI', en diciembre de 2023, las escuchas de 'Love Is a Long Road', de Tom Petty, subieron un 36,97 % en Spotify respecto a la semana anterior. Era la canción del tráiler, y su tirón recuerda al que las canciones de 'FIFA' disfrutaron durante años. Por eso, la friolera de 34 temas encargados en exclusiva para esta nueva entrega es, más que un escaparate musical, un negocio redondo.
Cosas de discográficas. De un tiempo a esta parte, y con la limitadísima cantidad de lanzamientos en materia de videojuegos que tiene Rockstar, su actividad se ha centrado más en la música que en lo que los hizo famosos. En mayo de 2021, presentó CircoLoco Records, un sello creado junto a la marca de fiestas de Ibiza, con una frase que reconocía que "la música siempre ha sido una parte fundamental" de Rockstar Games. Ese mismo diciembre, 'GTA Online' estrenó MOTOMAMI Los Santos, una emisora presentada por Rosalía y Arca (que ahora firma un tema del álbum de 'GTA VI') y que adelantaba el primer sencillo del siguiente álbum de la catalana. Era parte de una trama que giraba alrededor a un móvil robado a Dr. Dre, cargado de temas inéditos que el jugador debía recuperar antes de que se filtraran.
El 21 de noviembre, dos días después de la salida del juego, Rockstar y PlayStation celebrarán en Miami, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, dos escenarios con Travis Scott, Cardi B, Metro Boomin, Rauw & Friends, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso y una sesión de Justice. Y es que uno de los principales socios de 'GTA VI' es una major discográfica. Atlantic Records forma parte de Atlantic Music Group, propiedad de Warner Music Group, que en enero creó dentro del grupo de sellos una presidencia para Kevin Weaver con competencias sobre bandas sonoras, sincronizaciones e iniciativas de videojuegos. Su historial incluye 'Barbie The Album' y 'F1 The Album', y sus proyectos suman más de 65.000 millones de reproducciones.
Un recordatorio más de que GTA VI puede ser un fenómeno pop, pero también un negocio cuyos tentáculos hacen palidecer a cualquier gran empresa tecnológica actual.

articles.title: Georgina Rodríguez: “Dejé el currículum en Inditex y empecé en Massimo Dutti, pero paseaba a veces por la Milla de Oro y me encantaba ver los escaparates. Cuando entraba a una boutique de lujo, para mí era como entrar en un museo”
articles.text:
En una entrevista, Georgina Rodríguez explicaba que había dejado el currículum en Inditex y había empezado en Massimo Dutti. Pero también paseaba por la Milla de Oro. Le gustaba mirar cómo eran los escaparates.
Así conseguía ir acercándose a las tiendas que realmente le interesaban. Cuando entraba en alguna boutique de lujo, se sentía como en un museo. Antes de llegar a Gucci, trabajó en un hotel y también estuvo en Inglaterra cuidando niños.
Vivía con su madre y su hermana antes de irse a Madrid. Según contaba, estuvieron muy unidas. Nunca les faltó lo básico. Hubo momentos mejores y peores. En algunos días comían mejor que en otros, e incluso hubo días en los que no había agua caliente.
Cuando tenía 18 años le ofrecieron un trabajo en un hotel de un pueblo cerca de Barbastro (a dos horas y media de Jaca). Entonces, su madre le dejó 100 euros para que pudiera irse del pueblo. Empezó a tener sueldo propio. Pagaba un alquiler y vivía de forma independiente.
De Massimo Dutti a Gucci, con Inglaterra en medio
Según contó, trabajó en el hotel de Graus. Es entonces cuando decide irse a Madrid. Quería estudiar Administración de Empresas. Dejó el currículum en Inditex y después empezó a trabajar en Massimo Dutti.
Tiempo más tarde se trasladó a trabajar a Inglaterra. Era niñera y aprovechaba para aprender inglés. Volvió a España y consiguió entrar en Gucci. Ahí es donde empezó a conocer el mundo de la moda desde dentro.
Su cambio de vida ha acompañado su carrera como modelo y creadora de contenido. También ha tenido proyectos empresariales. Además, es la pareja de Cristiano Ronaldo. Todo esto ha sido en paralelo.
Ese cambio de vida lo recogió el reality de Netflix “Soy Georgina”. Para promocionarlo se utilizó la frase “Antes vendía bolsos, ahora los colecciona”. Según explicaba en la entrevista, es un eslogan que viene de parte de todo lo que significó su vida anterior.
Cuando alguien le comentaba que era maravilloso pasar de vender bolsos de lujo a poder comprarlos, le parecía cierto. En aquella entrevista contaba que de su vida anterior echaba en falta poder salir a la calle sin que la reconocieran. También que no tuviera que preocuparse por quién podía sacarle una foto.

articles.title: Google corrige 83 nouvelles failles Chrome, dont 5 vulnérabilités critiques
articles.text:
Google a déployé une nouvelle version de Chrome. Disponible depuis ce mercredi 11 novembre sur Windows, macOS et Linux, la mise à jour corrige un total de 83 failles de sécurité. C’est la deuxième mise à jour de sécurité en une semaine. Deux jours plus tôt, Google avait déjà corrigé en urgence une faille zero day exploitée par des pirates. C’était la huitième faille zero day de l’année découverte sur le navigateur.
Cinq failles critiques dans la mémoire de Chrome
Parmi les 83 brèches, cinq ont été jugées « critiques », le niveau de gravité le plus élevé, par les ingénieurs de Google. Les 78 autres sont de sévérité « élevée ». Cette fois, Google n’a pas découvert de tentative d’exploitation des failles. Les cinq failles critiques concernent la gestion de la mémoire. Concrètement, Chrome libère une zone de la mémoire, mais continue ensuite de s’en servir. Un pirate peut alors glisser des données malveillantes dans cet espace. Les chercheurs de Malwarebytes soulignent que ce problème de mémoire peut provoquer des « plantages, des corruptions de données et des fuites d’informations ».
L’une des failles de sévérité a déjà retenu l’attention des cybercriminels. Située dans V8, le moteur qui exécute le code JavaScript des sites web, elle « permet à un attaquant distant d’exécuter du code arbitraire à l’intérieur du bac à sable de Chrome via une page HTML spécialement conçue », explique Google. Sur GitHub, un code de démonstration est apparu quelques jours plus tôt. Ce code peut faire gagner du temps aux pirates qui souhaiteraient exploiter la vulnérabilité. Le risque reste néanmoins limité. Même en exploitant la faille, un pirate risque de se retrouver coincé dans le « bac à sable », l’espace isolé dans lequel Chrome affiche une page web. Il faudrait trouver et exploiter une seconde faille pour lancer une cyberattaque efficace.
À lire aussi : Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d’internautes pendant 10 ans
C’est la troisième mise à jour de Chrome en un peu plus d’une semaine. Lancée début novembre, la version 157 corrigeait déjà 213 failles dans le code du navigateur. Cette cadence de mise à jour découle évidemment de l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle générative. Massivement utilisée par Google, elle permet de débusquer de plus en plus facilement des vulnérabilités.
La mise à jour est estampillée 157.0.8103.78 ou .79 sur Windows et macOS, et 157.0.8103.78 sur Linux. Pour l’installer sans attendre, cliquez sur les trois points en haut à droite de Chrome, puis allez dans « Aide » et « À propos de Google Chrome ». Le navigateur télécharge alors tout seul la dernière version. Cliquez ensuite sur « Relancer » pour installer les correctifs. Il suffit ensuite de relancer Chrome. On vous conseille d’activer les mises à jour automatiques pour rester protégé.

articles.title: Beijing now bans owning and storing drones, even if you never fly them
articles.text:
What just happened? Drone users who complain that rules related to UAVs are too tough should be thankful they don't live in Beijing. A law came into effect in the Chinese capital yesterday that makes owning and storing the devices illegal, meaning you can't even keep a drone that you never fly.
While many Chinese cities have no-fly zones in sensitive areas for civilian drones, Beijing is the only one to ban ownership.
The restrictions cover the entire municipality, including its rural areas, spanning around 16,400 square kilometers (6,332 square miles), around half the size of Belgium. Bringing drones or their components into Beijing is also forbidden, so leaving one packed away in your luggage won't get you around the rules.
Authorities announced the extreme measure in September, claiming it was a requirement to keep the city secure. Beijing had already banned drone sales in May, but registered owners were initially allowed to keep their devices if they registered them with authorities, a luxury that has now disappeared.
In June, a small plane crashed into Beijing's tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 people. It raised concerns about airspace safety and led to the current drone restrictions.
There are a handful of exemptions that allow drones to be owned and used, including activities involving law enforcement, counterterrorism, emergency relief, agriculture, and scientific research.
For ordinary owners, though, complying has meant selling their drones, sending them away, or handing them over for recycling. ABC News reported that some people using buyback sites were receiving less than a quarter of what they originally paid. Keeping a drone could result in confiscation and fines of up to 5,000 yuan ($749).
One Beijing aerial photographer, Matthew Zhang, moved his drone to his parents' home in nearby Tianjin and planned to travel there whenever he wanted to use it. Another owner sent his aircraft to his sister in Australia to keep it in the family.
Even toys appear to be off limits. ABC found that the rules appeared to extend to remote-controlled model aircraft and toy drones, while Taobao had blocked motorized flying products, including powered paper planes, from being sold to Beijing addresses.
It's somewhat ironic that Beijing now has some of the toughest drone restrictions in the world when China is home to DJI and dominates the consumer drone industry. Elsewhere in the country, drones are being used for deliveries, farming, and emergency work, while Beijing residents can't even keep them in their homes.
Some US cities have considered tougher restrictions on drones, but nothing approaching Beijing's. In August, Wheat Ridge, Colorado, was considering banning unauthorized drone flights over streets, parks, and other public spaces. However, the FAA says local authorities can restrict drone takeoffs and landings, rather than flights through the airspace above.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
- November 12, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Santa Barbara. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Pehuén Moure, Jacob Granley, Fabrizio Grani, Leili Soo, Antonio Lozano, Rocío López-Peco, Adrián Villamarín-Ortiz, Cristina Soto-Sánchez, Shih-Chii Liu, Michael Beyeler, Eduardo Fernández. Deep learning-based control of electrically evoked activity in human visual cortex. Neuron, 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2026.07.006

articles.title: AI agents were all over KubeCon. Production is another story
articles.text:
AI agents were all over KubeCon. Production is another story
AI agents are testing systems that were originally built for people, and Jonathan Bryce thinks the cloud-native community has a lot of work to do to help those systems keep up in this new era.
The New Stack sat down with Bryce, the executive director of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City to talk about the projects joining the foundation and how AI is changing its work.
Bryce tells The New Stack, “A lot of the existing systems in our world were built for human speed, and agent speed is a completely different type of usage pattern and scenario, and so these systems are just not scalable and resilient enough to handle the kind of workloads that agents are generating.”
Running training and inference workloads on Kubernetes is already a familiar job for this community, and Bryce argues that the financial services, healthcare, and transportation systems that agents interact with will also need the elasticity and observability that cloud-native technologies provide.
OpenShell and Agent Substrate
At KubeCon, Nvidia announced that it was contributing OpenShell to the CNCF. Google had also announced the donation of Agent Substrate ahead of the show. Both joined the CNCF as Sandbox projects, the foundation’s entry-level tier.
At its core, OpenShell enforces policies, including which files, networks, credentials, and model endpoints an agent can access. Agent Substrate tackles a related but different issue by providing isolated environments for agents on Kubernetes, with features like support for suspending idle sessions and resuming them when needed.
“We can make AI systems that have security and control architected into them from the infrastructure side,” Bryce says.
He sees this as a responsibility for the community, given the questions AI has raised about security and resource consumption. Moving a project like OpenShell into neutral governance also lets more companies contribute to it, he says.
Doing more with existing hardware
Agent workloads also aren’t as evenly distributed as those of more traditional enterprise applications.
“Your agent, even if it’s always waiting around to be at your beck and call, it’s not necessarily doing work 24/7,” Bryce says. “How do you spin it down and spin it up where it feels like it’s ready for you at any time? That’s going to be the user experience that people demand. How do you do that without just having it sit there and burn CPU cycles on nothing?”
Agent Substrate saves the agent’s state and frees up the compute it was using, then restores the session onto an available worker.
Bryce also highlighted llm-d, the distributed inference framework, as an example of software getting more out of existing hardware. While hardware is expensive, expensive to run, and (at least currently) in limited supply, software gives developers something they can work on now.
A flood of vulnerability reports
Zero-days and security also came up more at this KubeCon than in previous years.
As more people use AI tools to find and report vulnerabilities, Bryce says, open source maintainers have been flooded with duplicate and unverified reports that they still have to take seriously.
He thinks the pace may no longer be accelerating the way it was early this year, but he isn’t sure what 2027 will bring as the models keep getting better.
“Y2K didn’t end up being that big of a deal,” he says. “This is really a moment that could be a big deal if we don’t actually just all get together and work as quickly as we can.”
Agent adoption is still early
For all the talk about agents at the show, though, Bryce’s assessment of adoption is measured.
“Beyond software development, adoption is still quite low,” he says.
He sees production use in customer service and other areas with a well-defined, historical base of knowledge.
“We’re very, very, very early in the path to billions of agents that are taking action on our behalf on a constant basis,” Bryce says.
Companies remain cautious about what happens when they give an agent access and something goes wrong, which won’t come as a surprise if you’ve recently spent any time talking to big enterprises and their customers.
For now, Bryce sees this as a positive, because it may just allow the community enough time to harden projects like OpenShell and Agent Substrate before enterprises put agents to work more broadly.

articles.title: Hackers Probe Newly Disclosed Flaws in Copeland Refrigeration Controllers
articles.text:
Exploitation attempts against a vulnerability in Copeland’s XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers began less than two hours after the issue was made public last week, according to VulnCheck.
The security firm disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in XWEB EVO, a Dixell supervisory system now sold under the Copeland name. VulnCheck’s Valentin Lobstein said each flaw was shown to yield root privileges on test systems.
The product drew the researcher’s attention after the October 11-12 attack that triggered defrost cycles at roughly 700 French supermarkets. CERT-FR named Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers among the compromised products, and France has blamed Iran for the campaign.
Nine of the flaws disclosed by VulnCheck only affect firmware builds that predate a 2021 rewrite. They include unauthenticated command execution, a hardcoded administrator password, and command injection via the login page.
The other five vulnerabilities also impact the latest firmware. Four of them involve predictable credentials: the administrator’s daily password is generated from the device’s MAC address and the current date, and the MAC address is exposed to unauthenticated users.
An attacker can calculate the password offline, enable SSH, and log in as root, since the root password is built from the same daily code. The fifth flaw is a command injection issue that requires authentication.
These five issues will not be fixed. Copeland ended software support for the XWEB EVO family on March 16, 2026, and has advised customers to move to XWEB Pro models.
The CVE records were published on November 12, and VulnCheck’s sensors saw the first exploitation attempts within two hours. They targeted CVE-2026-124014, which allows unauthenticated attackers to write to the system configuration file.
A single IP address sent 125 requests overnight. On November 13, a second IP sent four probes aimed at CVE-2026-124010, the unauthenticated root command execution flaw. Both targeted flaws only affect the older firmware.
“Neither scanning source is evidence of the October refrigeration campaign that France attributed to Iran’s IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh: that was a targeted sabotage operation, while these are opportunistic hosts acting on fresh advisories,” Lobstein said.
Onyphe data cited by VulnCheck shows nearly 2,000 internet-exposed XWEB EVO hosts, compared with 108 for XWEB Pro.
“Operators who still run one should treat it as a device that must never touch the public internet, segment it behind a VPN, and plan the move to a supported platform,” the researcher added.

articles.title: Veterano do Linux reduz atividades no projeto por causa da IA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Veterano do Linux reduz atividades no projeto por causa da IA
Responsável por áreas de gerenciamento de memória no Linux, Lorenzo Stoakes decidiu reduzir sua participação no kernel por causa da sobrecarga oriunda da IA.
Meses atrás, quando Linus Torvalds sinalizou que a IA estava sobrecarregando os desenvolvedores do Linux, ele não estava exagerando. Prova disso é que, recentemente, Lorenzo Stoakes decidiu reduzir a sua presença no projeto. É uma decisão impactante. Estamos falando do responsável por cuidar de quatro áreas relacionadas ao gerenciamento de memória do kernel.
O problema não é a inteligência artificial por si só. O ponto de conflito está no uso de ferramentas que “caçam bugs” no Linux com auxílio da IA e, principalmente, nos códigos gerados por elas. Em linhas gerais, esses mecanismos têm produzido um volume muito grande de relatórios de falhas e sugestões de patches, a ponto de os desenvolvedores terem dificuldade para lidar com tudo isso.
Talvez a pior parte seja o fato de boa parte desses relatórios ou patches estarem relacionados a bugs com baixa de prioridade, que já estavam na fila de correção ou até que foram corrigidos recentemente.
Mas, sim, a IA também tem conseguido apontar problemas ou pontos de ajustes legítimos, mas em um ritmo com o qual os desenvolvedores do Linux não estavam habituados. Ao que tudo indica, foi isso que fez Stoakes reduzir a sua participação no projeto.
Lorenzo Stoakes não é tão conhecido quanto Linus Torvalds, mas está longe de ser um nome qualquer. Ele é um engenheiro de software britânico que atualmente trabalha na Arm e que tem um longo histórico de contribuições com o Linux.
Como já dito, a sua especialidade é gerenciamento de memória, tanto que Stoakes até lançou um livro sobre o assunto: The Linux Memory Manager (ainda sem versão em português).
Eis que, em 10 de novembro, Stoakes enviou uma mensagem à lista de discussão oficial do kernel com os seguintes dizeres:
Devido à atual demanda de código que chega ao kernel resultante das séries [de alterações] geradas por IA, infelizmente não tenho disponibilidade suficiente para oferecer revisões, exceto nas áreas em que me mantenho [como mantenedor].
(…) Peço desculpas por isso, mas, dadas as tendências atuais, gostaria de fazer algo para tornar minha caixa de entrada um pouco mais gerenciável.
Lorenzo Stoakes
Observe que este não é um abandono do projeto. Stoakes continuará atuando como mantenedor das quatro áreas de gerenciamento de memória com as quais trabalha há anos, mas, essencialmente, deixará de oferecer revisões ou códigos para subsistemas que não estão diretamente sob sua responsabilidade.
A principal causa para a decisão é, de fato, o aumento de demanda oriundo das revisões feitas por IA, como o engenheiro declarou ao The Register: “sim, a IA é parte do motivo; em geral, [o volume de notificações] passou de ‘uma vez por semana’ para ‘diariamente’ e agora para ‘metade do que vejo em revisão'”.
Curiosamente, o próprio Linus Torvalds deu a entender que algumas partes do kernel já estão “em equilíbrio” com IA. Mas, como o caso de Stoakes sugere, ainda há muito o que ser feito para que esse equilíbrio alcance outras partes do projeto.

articles.title: BDC leads investment in Saskatoon company modernizing railway logistics | BetaKit
articles.text:
Saskatoon’s Standard Rail Corporation has raised $1.85 million to scale its railway logistics platform, the company announced last week.
The news: Standard Rail announced the seed investment on Nov. 12, telling BetaKit that the funding was led by BDC’s Capital Seed Venture Fund, with additional participation from Waterloo’s Infiniq Ventures. Funding will go toward expanding the company’s logistics platform, SIDINGS, as well as growing its engineering and marketing teams.
From the source: “I spent years driving industrial roads looking for track, knocking on doors for storage and transload, and icing it together one site at a time,” said Standard Rail CEO Robert Skarzynski in a press release. “With BDC’s backing, we’re building the system this industry has always needed.”
The context: SIDINGS is designed as a digital platform connecting domestic and international shippers with rail capacity across North America. The platform is intended to replicate the ease-of-access logistics that has become commonplace in both the air and ocean freight industries but has remained largely disconnected in the broader rail transportation industry. The platform is an open network service connecting shippers, facilities, and rail service providers in a single online location. Shippers can search for more than 60,000 rail-served locations in Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The platform also allows users to book, bid, and request pricing online.
Standard Rail said that with BDC’s financing, it will look to onboard more rail service providers to the platform.
Final thought: Prior to launching SIDINGS, Standard Rail was involved in physical railcar maintenance, repair, and fleet services, including logistics planning, which gave the company’s team a frontline view of the rail transportation industry. It was that domain knowledge that Mark Smith, partner and team lead at BDC’s Seed Venture Fund, said clinched the bank’s decision to back Standard Rail, which has several competitors that also service the rail logistics space, including Commtrex and Canadian rival Freightera. Smith called Standard Rail’s hands-on involvement in the industry a strategic advantage as it seeks to scale.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
