articles.title: Ex-engenheiro da OpenAI contesta prisão e nega ligação com governo saudita
articles.text:
A defesa de Abdulrahman Alfozan, ex-engenheiro da OpenAI acusado de instalar dispositivo de gravação escondido em uma sala de reuniões da empresa, afirma que o governo dos Estados Unidos não apresentou provas de que ele atuasse como espião ou tivesse ligações com a Arábia Saudita. Em manifestação judicial apresentada nesta segunda-feira (16), os advogados contestaram a manutenção da prisão preventiva e disseram que o cliente está sendo detido ilegalmente, sem direito a fiança.
Alfozan, cidadão saudita de 35 anos, foi preso em outubro e responde a uma acusação de interceptação ilegal de comunicações. O caso ganhou dimensão de segurança nacional depois que autoridades estadunidenses relacionaram a investigação a possíveis tentativas de obtenção de informações confidenciais de uma das principais empresas de inteligência artificial (IA) do mundo.
Segundo os advogados, apesar de terem recebido documentos e participado de duas reuniões com os promotores, eles ainda não tiveram acesso a evidências que sustentem as alegações de ligação do engenheiro com o governo saudita ou de espionagem econômica.
“Em termos simples, o governo não pode manter o sr. Alfozan detido com base em alegações sobre suas ligações com a Arábia Saudita ou espionagem econômica, sem apresentar prontamente à defesa todas as evidências relevantes”, argumentaram os advogados na manifestação.
Entenda a acusação contra o ex-funcionário da OpenAI
- A investigação começou depois que funcionários da OpenAI encontraram um dispositivo de gravação escondido atrás de uma televisão em uma sala de reuniões executivas, na sede da empresa em São Francisco, na Califórnia (EUA);
- O equipamento estava conectado a uma entrada USB e havia sido escondido em papel higiênico. Segundo documentos apresentados pelo Departamento de Justiça, o dispositivo foi instalado por volta de 28 de setembro e descoberto em 30 de setembro de 2026;
- A sala era utilizada por executivos para reuniões sobre informações técnicas, comerciais e estratégicas da companhia. Os encontros também envolviam discussões sobre pesquisas proprietárias, planos de produtos, relações comerciais e compromissos com autoridades governamentais;
- De acordo com a denúncia, imagens de câmeras de segurança mostraram Alfozan circulando próximo ao espaço em diferentes ocasiões, embora não tivesse autorização para participar das reuniões realizadas ali;
- Os investigadores também apontaram consultas feitas por meio de ferramentas de produtividade sobre endereços dos prédios da OpenAI, salas de reunião e agendas de executivos;
- Outro elemento citado pelos promotores envolve uma conta do ChatGPT associada à esposa do engenheiro. Entre os registros estavam perguntas sobre como construir um gravador de áudio contínuo, adicionar conectividade Wi-Fi, criptografar cartões de memória e permitir acesso remoto ao equipamento.
O Departamento de Justiça também afirmou que, em 5 de outubro, Alfozan teria sido filmado verificando a parte traseira da televisão onde o primeiro dispositivo estava instalado. No mesmo dia, funcionários de segurança encontraram outro equipamento semelhante dentro de uma bolsa deixada pelo engenheiro em uma sala diferente do prédio.
Alfozan foi acusado de violar a Lei de Escutas Telefônicas dos Estados Unidos (Wiretap Act), que proíbe a interceptação ilegal de comunicações. Se condenado, poderá receber pena de até cinco anos de prisão.
Vale destacar que ele não foi formalmente acusado de espionagem. A suspeita de que poderia estar trabalhando em benefício de interesses estrangeiros aparece nas alegações dos investigadores e promotores, mas não constitui condenação ou acusação criminal específica de espionagem.
Leia mais:
- Você confia? Agente de IA da OpenAI, ChatGPT Wallet fará compras pelo usuário e promete segurança
- OpenAI anuncia punição para quem tentar sexualizar crianças no ChatGPT
- OpenAI é processada após agentes de IA invadirem sistemas de terceiros
Por que o juiz negou liberdade sob fiança?
Em outubro, um juiz federal decidiu manter Alfozan preso enquanto o processo avança. A decisão considerou que o engenheiro apresentava risco significativo de deixar os Estados Unidos e não retornar para responder às acusações.
Os promotores argumentaram que ele estava a poucos dias de viajar para a Arábia Saudita quando foi preso. Também mencionaram que sua esposa e seu filho pequeno deixaram os Estados Unidos no dia seguinte à detenção, em viagem para o exterior paga por um oficial militar saudita.
Outro ponto apresentado pela acusação foi a existência de contatos frequentes entre Alfozan e um integrante não identificado da família real saudita.
Segundo os promotores, essa pessoa tentou recrutá-lo para participar de uma iniciativa de IA no país. Em uma das mensagens citadas nos documentos judiciais, o integrante da família real teria escrito: “A Arábia Saudita precisa mais de você do que os EUA”. Alfozan teria respondido: “100”.
A defesa, por outro lado, argumentou que o engenheiro tinha vínculos importantes com os Estados Unidos. Ele vivia no país há aproximadamente 15 anos, possuía residência permanente desde 2020 e estudou no Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts (MIT) e na Universidade da Califórnia em Berkeley. Os advogados também afirmaram que Alfozan estava próximo de realizar uma entrevista para obter a cidadania americana.
Na audiência de outubro, o juiz ainda questionou uma oferta do Consulado Saudita para ajudar a pagar a fiança do acusado. A possibilidade de apoio financeiro de uma representação estrangeira foi considerada um fator relevante na avaliação do risco de fuga.
OpenAI acionou o FBI após encontrar equipamento
A OpenAI informou que descobriu o dispositivo de gravação em setembro e encaminhou o caso ao FBI. A companhia também demitiu Alfozan depois de sua prisão.
Segundo informações divulgadas pela Associated Press (AP), a empresa afirmou não ter encontrado indícios de que o ex-funcionário tenha acessado ou retirado pesos de modelos, código-fonte ou dados de clientes.
O episódio levantou preocupações sobre a proteção de informações estratégicas em empresas que desenvolvem IA avançada, especialmente diante da disputa internacional por tecnologias capazes de impulsionar a economia e a segurança nacional.
Por enquanto, o processo criminal continua concentrado na suposta interceptação ilegal de conversas. A defesa busca contestar a manutenção da prisão e questiona a ausência de evidências que sustentem as suspeitas de ligação com o governo saudita.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Was sind Zaps? Whatsapp arbeit an einer neuen Sendefunktion für Bilder und Videos
articles.text:
Whatsapp soll „Zaps“ bekommen: Welches Feature sich dahinter verbirgt
Whatsapp arbeitet derzeit an einer neuen Funktion, mit der Nutzer:innen Fotos und Videos teilen können, die nach dem Ansehen wieder verschwinden. Dieses Prinzip hat Snapchat bekannt gemacht, aber auch Instagram, das wie Whatsapp ebenfalls zum Meta-Konzern gehört, bietet mit Instants ein entsprechendes Feature. Der Messenger entwickelt diese Funktion jetzt weiter: Hier soll sie künftig Zaps heißen. WABetainfo hat einen Hinweis auf die Neuerung in der Beta-Version 2.26.46.2 für Android entdeckt, die im Google Play-Store verfügbar ist.
So sollen die neuen Zaps funktionieren
Um Zaps zu verschicken, sollen Nutzer:innen auf einen Button mit Blitzsymbol klicken können, der die Kamera öffnet. Wenn sie mit dieser „Instant-Kamera“ ein Foto oder Video aufnehmen, erstellen sie einen sogenannten Zap. Der Inhalt verschwindet wieder, sobald der oder die Empfänger:in ihn angesehen hat. Der Name Zap spiegele dabei die Kernidee der Funktion wider: Er suggeriert laut WABetainfo etwas Schnelles, Unmittelbares und Spontanes. Teilt ein:e Absender:in einen Zap, zeigt Whatsapp ihn direkt in der Chat-Oberfläche an. Empfänger sehen den Inhalt also direkt dort, wo auch andere Nachrichten erscheinen.
Mit der neuen Funktion erweitert Whatsapp auch den Kreis der Personen, die selbstlöschende Inhalte senden können. Bisher waren diese auf gegenseitige Kontakte beschränkt. Laut WABetainfo plant Meta mit diesem Update eine Erweiterung, damit Nutzer:innen Zaps an jeden Kontakt und jede Gruppe senden können. Ob sich diese auch in Kanälen teilen lassen werden, ist noch offen. Die Entwickler:innen geben an, dass als Zaps verschickten Fotos oder Videos wie reguläre Nachrichten Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt sein werden, sodass nur Absender:in und Empfänger:in sie sehen können.
Noch ist die neue Funktion nicht verfügbar
Teilt eine:r Absender:in mehr als einen Zap in derselben Unterhaltung, fasst Whatsapp diese zu einer Gruppe zusammen und zeigt die Gesamtanzahl an. Das soll für eine übersichtliche Unterhaltung sorgen. Öffnet ein:e Empfänger:in einen Zap, kann er oder sie mit beliebigen Emojis reagieren oder eine Nachricht in die Antwortleiste eingeben. Der Zap verschwindet, nachdem er angesehen wurde – für die absendende Person bleibt er aber dauerhaft im Chat sichtbar.
Whatsapp baut seinen Funktionsumfang stetig weiter aus. In Deutschland ist der Messenger besonders beliebt: Laut einer Statista-Umfrage nutzen ihn hier mehr als acht von zehn Erwachsenen, um mit Kolleg:innen, Freund:innen oder Verwandten in Kontakt zu bleiben. Laut WABetaInfo befindet sich die neue Zaps-Funktion derzeit noch in der Entwicklung. Ein konkretes Veröffentlichungsdatum ist bisher nicht bekannt, allerdings wird das Feature voraussichtlich mit einem kommenden Update zur Verfügung stehen.
) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Making a typo when trying to access AI could land you on a malware site
articles.text:
Making a typo when trying to access AI could land you on a malware site
Popular AI brands abused in a new typosquatting campaign
- Attackers registered hundreds of typo-squatted domains impersonating popular AI brands such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity
- Victims who mistyped URLs were redirected to malware, malicious browser extensions, or ClickFix-style attacks
- Researchers warn the campaign remains active, making bookmarks and careful URL verification essential defenses
Be careful when typing your favorite AI tool’s website into the address bar - one mistake and you might end up with malware on your computer.
This is the warning given out by security researchers Island, who recently uncovered a large-scale domain squatting campaign spoofing popular AI brands.
Users who want to open ChatGPT or Claude might misspell the name and end up on sites like chtgpt.com or cluade.ai. In a perfect world, these websites would return a 404 error (page not found) or would at least automatically redirect the visitor to the legitimate website. But we don’t live in a perfect world, but rather in one filled with malicious actors looking to benefit from even the tiniest of mistakes.
Benefitting from mistakes
In its report, Island said it found 186 typo-squatted domains impersonating 27 popular AI brands, among which are your usual household names - ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Midjourney, and Cursor.
What threat actors did, Island claims, is purchase 186 of these slightly erroneous domains and create websites which, depending on the visitor’s location, operating system and browser, would redirect them to different destinations. On these destinations, one of three things could happen: the victims would be shown a fake Cloudflare verification page, a fake security-check page, or instructions to download various browser extensions.
All three scenarios are malicious. The first one is a typical click-fix attack that instructs Windows users to copy and execute malicious PowerShell commands. These downloaded and executed additional scripts from attacker-controlled infrastructure but unfortunately, Island does not say what the final payload is or what it does.
The fake security-check pages offered a seemingly legitimate, Microsoft Store-signed application called Net Guard, which is actually able to hijack the victim’s browser. This one is particularly worrisome, since it was signed and distributed through a package matching the legitimate Microsoft Store listing, and could change default search engines, modify browser profiles, install extensions and execute JavaScript remotely.

The third attack instructed victims to download malicious extensions that hijacked their default search engine, which allows the attackers to generate profits through monetized searches, or by selling harvested search engine queries.
Are the domains still active?
Island says ChatGPT was the most popular company to spoof, with 25 identified lookalikes. It is followed by Claude (18 typosquatted domains), DeepSeek (16), and Runway (12). Perplexity, Lovable and Character.ai all have 11 each, it added.
It is worth mentioning that this was likely not done by a single actor, but rather numerous ones all using the same technique to target their victims. Also, Island stressed that the campaign likely extended beyond AI services - after examining shared infrastructure, the researchers connected the operation to 211 entry domains, including lookalikes of banks, insurers, telecom companies and enterprise software providers.
Security researchers usually publish these reports after helping minimize the risk which, in this case, would be seeing the domains seized and the malicious websites brought offline.
However, Island’s report does not discuss any takedowns, so it is safe to assume at least some of these domains are still active today. As a rule of thumb, make sure to carefully review the domain typed into the address bar before navigating anywhere. Alternatively, bookmarking your favorite tools is a good option, as well.
Malicious browser extensions did not get the same treatment, though. Of the 30 identified ones, 13 have already been removed from the Chrome Web Store, while 17 remained listed as of November 3, 2026. If not already, we can expect them to be removed in the coming days and weeks.

articles.title: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance
articles.text:
In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference.
NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power.
These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack, so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time.
NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1
AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights, advancing scientific research.
Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster.
MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy.
The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation.
NVIDIA also demonstrated performance at scale. On the DeepSeek-V3 benchmark, Vera Rubin NVL72 scaled from 256 to 1,024 GPUs with about 97% efficiency: quadrupling the GPUs cut time to train from 16 minutes to about four.
NVIDIA also ran the benchmark on 10,240 GPUs with GB300 systems, representing the largest scale in this round. Microsoft Azure matched that scale with 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 systems.
Results at this scale matter because adding GPUs only speeds up training if they can work together efficiently. NVIDIA NVLink scale-up networking connects the GPUs within each system so they act as one, while NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet scale-out networking link those systems across the data center. Combined with optimized software, this keeps thousands of GPUs working in concert, helping developers build more intelligent models while cutting training times.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Leads Agentic Inference on MLPerf Endpoints
An AI agent for travel that plans and books a whole trip — or an IT agent that finds and fixes a problem before anyone files a ticket — may reason, call tools and check its work many times to finish a single task.
Each of those steps generates tokens. Because AI data centers are limited by power, the more tokens a system can generate each second for every watt of power, the more agents it can serve and the more value it creates.
MLPerf Endpoints tests systems on real agentic coding and enterprise workflows, and checks that the agents still complete their tasks correctly. NVIDIA Vera Rubin leads across all of its agentic benchmarks.
For example, in a provisional result for Kimi K3, a large open model built for agentic workflows, Vera Rubin NVL72 systems deliver more than 10x the throughput per watt of NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 at the same response speed.
Every AI service has to balance serving many users at once against responding quickly to each one. Vera Rubin shifts that entire curve, serving more users while responding faster.
Leadership Across Benchmarks and Workloads
NVIDIA partners participated extensively in MLPerf Training, with submissions from 20 organizations: ASUS, Azure, Cisco, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Dell Technologies, Firmus, Giga Computing, Google Cloud, HPE, Inventec, Krai, Lambda, Nebius, Oracle, Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT), Supermicro, TTA and the University of Florida.
Their submissions show how NVIDIA’s programmable platform, with open source libraries and frameworks, lets a vast ecosystem of partners innovate and optimize AI training performance.
The lead extends beyond MLPerf.
Vera Rubin also delivers leading performance on independent benchmarks including SemiAnalysis AgentX and Artificial Analysis AgentPerf, showcasing how the same NVIDIA infrastructure can productively run everything from pretraining and post-training to agentic inference, as well as workloads beyond AI, such as the high-performance computing showcased at SC26 this week.
Dive deeper into the results in the MLPerf Training and MLPerf Endpoints technical blogs.

articles.title: Instagram now lets creators add Amazon affiliate links in reels and feed posts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Instagram announced on Monday that it’s launching an integration that will give creators a new way to earn by adding Amazon affiliate links directly in reels and feed posts. Creators can add up to 30 products per reel or 20 per feed post, which makes it possible for them to earn from multiple products through one piece of content.
While creators have long shared Amazon affiliate links through stories, DMs, and their bios, the new integration brings them to new parts of the app. The Meta-owned company told TechCrunch in an email that it has seen product links directly on creators’ reels and posts draw about twice as many clicks as the links in their bio.
By allowing creators to embed multiple product links directly in Reels and feed posts, the platform is expanding their opportunities to monetize content, while also giving them more flexibility in how they share recommendations. The change also strengthens the platform’s appeal to creators, as it continues to compete with rivals like TikTok and YouTube for their attention and content.
Instagram says adding products and affiliate links is free, and that it doesn’t take a commission on purchases or charge transaction fees.
Eligible creators can now connect their Instagram and Amazon Influencer accounts through the Monetization section of their Professional Dashboard. Once connected, Instagram automatically adds affiliate links when creators tag Amazon products in their content, with links directing viewers to the Amazon Shopping app. Connected affiliates also unlock image previews for their links, making it easier for viewers to recognize the products.
When creators connect their Amazon Associates account to Instagram, affiliate attribution is automatically applied to any Amazon product they add, even when they paste a regular product link, which wasn’t the case before, as they were required to add an affiliate URL.
Instagram says creators can also see each product’s estimated commission rate before adding it to a post or reel, with commissions continuing to be paid out by Amazon.
The new integration marks another step in Instagram’s efforts to expand its monetization tools while also making affiliate marketing more accessible for creators on its platform.

articles.title: Reducing High-Bandwidth Flash Latency In GPU Systems (Georgia Tech, Nvidia, Stanford)
articles.text:
Researchers at Georgia Tech, NVIDIA Research, and Stanford University published “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.”
Abstract Excerpt
“Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20μs, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering.
We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).”
Find the technical paper here. November 2026.
Saxena, Anish, Hritvik Taneja, Christos Kozyrakis, and Aamer Jaleel. “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.14776 (2026). License.

articles.title: Jensen Huang no tira la toalla: quiere volver a NVIDIA pocos días después de renunciar
articles.text:
Con su renuncia como CEO y presidente de NVIDIA todavía fresca, Jensen Huang no estaría dispuesto a darse por vencido al 100 %. Según un reporte de Financial Times, el ejecutivo ha comenzado a discutir con personas de confianza un posible regreso a la conducción de la empresa.
La idea llegaría de la mano de una movida por parte de colegas de Silicon Valley que pretenden hacer presión para que Jensen Huang pueda regresar a NVIDIA. Sus aliados buscarían generar el mayor ruido posible y para ello intentarían conseguir el apoyo de la Casa Blanca.
Por lo pronto, se desconoce si el regreso de Jensen Huang a NVIDIA es una opción real. El cofundador del gigante verde renunció a su cargo el pasado jueves, envuelto en un par de escándalos notorios. El primero, su relación extramatrimonial con Alice Huang, señalada como una supuesto espía china; el segundo, su amorío con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta del área de atención médica de la firma.
El presunto interés de Jensen Huang de volver a ser el CEO de NVIDIA se da en paralelo con una carta pública de empleados, exempleados, accionistas y socios reclamando su vuelta. La misma, titulada Stand with Jensen, cuenta con el aval de Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney (Epic Games) y varios otros ejecutivos tecnológicos de renombre.
Jensen Huang busca regresar como CEO de NVIDIA
Al momento de redacción de este artículo, la carta supera las 178.000 firmas, de las cuales más de 8.800 corresponderían a empleados actuales de NVIDIA. La veracidad de las rúbricas no se ha podido corroborar, pues en varios casos se han detectado nombres mal escritos que son parecidos a los de celebridades o personajes públicos.
Si Jensen Huang realmente regresa como CEO de NVIDIA, no será el primer caso de un movimiento de este tipo en el sector tecnológico. El caso más recordado es el de Sam Altman, destituido como jefe de OpenAI tras un motín gestado por sus principales laderos. Sin embargo, el empresario regresó a la startup de inteligencia artificial unos pocos días más tarde tras el reclamo de los empleados.
La carta abierta de la campaña Stand with Jensen plantea tres medidas a la junta directiva de NVIDIA. Por un lado, el regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO, pero también una investigación independiente y una audiencia justa, así como una explicación pública oportuna.
"Durante treinta y tres años, Jensen volcó todo su ser en la construcción de NVIDIA. Apostó por ideas que la mayor parte del sector descartó, mantuvo el rumbo durante años en los que tales apuestas parecían una insensatez, y permaneció el tiempo suficiente para ver cómo transformaban la forma en que el mundo procesa la información. Muchos de nosotros nos unimos a la empresa gracias a él. Muchos nos quedamos por la forma en que él abordaba el trabajo: como algo que merecía hacerse bien, en equipo, sin importar las horas que hicieran falta. Esta compañía es la obra de su vida. Eso merece algo más que gratitud a posteriori. Merece un trato justo, ahora mismo", dice el texto en favor del exjefe de NVIDIA.
Más allá del apoyo que está viendo Jensen Huang tras su renuncia, no todos están de acuerdo con un posible regreso como CEO de NVIDIA. Una de las fuentes de Financial Times indica que el romance del empresario con Kimberly Powell es causa suficiente de despido para cualquier ejecutivo. Esto, debido a las políticas de la empresa respecto de las relaciones entre directivos y subordinados.
Sea como sea, es evidente que el culebrón de Jensen Huang todavía tiene varios capítulos por escribir. Por lo pronto, Colette Kress continúa fungiendo como CEO interina mientras la empresa evalúa potenciales candidatos. Desde la junta han mencionado que todavía no se contactaron con ningún reemplazante, aunque los principales nombres apuntados serían los de Lisa Su, la CEO de AMD, y Rene Haas, CEO de ARM. Seguiremos atentos a las novedades.

articles.title: Windows 11 sur l'iPhone Duo : ce responsable Google a fait une petite prouesse avec Gemini
articles.text:
Ammaar Reshi dirige le produit et le design de Google AI Studio, et il a publié sur X une vidéo où Windows 11 tourne sur son iPhone Duo. Son projet WindowsiOS, en source ouverte sur GitHub, exécute la version ARM de Windows 11 24H2 dans une machine virtuelle à commandes tactiles. Le tout fonctionne en local sur la puce A20 Pro du pliable, sans diffusion depuis le cloud ni débridage de l’appareil.
 I used Gemini 4 Carbon to get Windows 11 running on my iPhone Duo! 💻
Unfold the screen and it’s a pocket PC, including Antigravity running coding agents on my phone.
This is the actual desktop ARM OS running locally with touch controls.
Demo + repo below! https://t.co/LVdeqvvOU1
— Ammaar Reshi (@ammaar) November 11, 2026
Un Mac obligatoire, l’antivirus au tapis et 12 Go de bagages
La prouesse repose sur une traduction logicielle du code ARM64, dite juste-à-temps, qui contourne le cadre de virtualisation matérielle verrouillé par Apple. Windows ne connaissant rien du matériel du téléphone, le projet lui fournit un adaptateur Ethernet virtuel et une sortie audio virtuelle. La couche Prism est même de la partie pour lancer des applications x86, sans garantie de compatibilité d’un logiciel à l’autre.
L’installation réclame un Mac Apple Silicon, les outils de développement d’Apple et une image de Windows 11 ARM, pour environ 12 Go occupés sur le téléphone. Le script d’optimisation fourni coupe la protection en temps réel de Microsoft Defender ainsi que des services de mise à jour en arrière-plan. Un Windows privé d’antivirus et de mises à jour automatiques se destine donc à la seule démonstration.
« J’ai utilisé Gemini 4 Carbon pour faire tourner Windows 11 sur mon iPhone Duo ! », s’enthousiasme l’intéressé, qui affirme avoir confié l’assemblage à des agents de Gemini 4 Carbon pendant deux heures. Il revendique une fluidité « quasi native », sans publier la moindre mesure, et la vidéo reste pour l’heure la seule preuve publique des performances annoncées. Gemini possède d’ailleurs sa propre application Windows depuis septembre. Avec WindowsiOS, l’assistant rend la politesse en sens inverse.
Sept ans après l’enterrement de Windows 10 Mobile, la revanche se paie 2 339 euros
Microsoft a débranché Windows 10 Mobile le 10 décembre 2019, en conseillant à ses derniers utilisateurs de migrer vers iOS ou Android. Les bidouilleurs ont pris le relais depuis. Le Français Gustave Monce a greffé Windows 11 sur le Surface Duo, le smartphone Android de Microsoft. En juillet 2024, l’émulateur UTM SE, validé par Apple après un premier refus, hissait une version allégée du système sur un iPhone 15 Pro : 20 minutes de démarrage, pour un résultat « terriblement lent ».
Cette lenteur tenait à l’absence de compilation juste-à-temps, qu’Apple a toujours bloquée hors de ses propres applications. Le DMA européen avait ouvert une brèche, entre boutiques alternatives comme AltStore et l’utilitaire StikDebug, qui active cette compilation sans ordinateur. iOS 26 l’a pourtant largement refermée en privant d’exécution la mémoire modifiable des applications tierces, et la plupart des émulateurs ont calé. La traduction maison de WindowsiOS prétend passer outre, promesse encore à vérifier.
Reste le prix du terrain de jeu : l’iPhone Duo se vend 2 339 euros en version 256 Go depuis le 23 octobre, et grimpe à 3 839 euros en 2 To. Son écran interne de 7,6 pouces offre au passage à Windows 11 la plus grande surface jamais vue sur un iPhone, et le projet se télécharge librement, à condition d’accepter le bricolage et ses risques.

articles.title: Los grandes centros de datos de EE UU ya consumen tanta energía como todo Chile
articles.text:
Los grandes centros de datos de EE UU ya consumen tanta energía como todo Chile
Un estudio publicado en Nature estima que estas infraestructuras acaparan el 1,8% de la electricidad del país y que las emisiones de carbono se han triplicado desde 2018
Los centros de datos son la columna vertebral de la era digital. En estas instalaciones repletas de procesadores se computan, almacenan y distribuyen ingentes cantidades de datos que hacen posible los servicios online o la inteligencia artificial (IA). Precisamente el boom de la IA ha provocado un frenesí constructor de centros de datos. Tenerlos en marcha día y noche requiere de muchísima energía, que se usa tanto para alimentar las propias máquinas como para refrigerarlas. Pero, ¿cuánta? ¿Y cuál es su huella de carbono?
La respuesta a estas preguntas solo las conocen las propias empresas que operan los centros de datos. No hay información pública y transparente al respecto. La opacidad de la industria hace que las cifras que se manejan sean estimaciones elaboradas por la comunidad científica. Un grupo de investigadores liderado por la Universidad de Harvard publica este lunes en la revista Nature los resultados de sus propias pesquisas, centradas en los hiperescalares (así se llama a los centros de datos más grandes). El estudio se fija en EE UU, el país del mundo que aglutina más centros de datos, en torno a la mitad del total.
Sus cifras son abultadas: los hiperescalares consumieron entre 68 y 99 teravatios-hora (TWh) de electricidad. Para poner esa cifra en contexto, la estimación más alta supera al consumo anual de un país como Chile (83,2 TWh), según datos de la agencia de estadística del Departamento de Energía (EIA), y se acerca a la de estados como Indiana, Míchigan o Tennessee. Eso equivale aproximadamente al 1,8% del consumo total de electricidad de EE UU. Los investigadores concluyen también que cuatro estados (Iowa, Ohio, Oregón y Virginia), concentran más de la mitad de todo el consumo energético detectado.
En cuanto a las emisiones, los cálculos de este equipo de Harvard las sitúan en unas 25,7 millones de toneladas métricas de CO₂, una cantidad entre dos y tres veces superior a una estimación anterior para 2018.
Lo interesante del estudio es la forma en que han construido su estimación. “Apenas hay datos públicos. El Departamento de Energía, por ejemplo, solo ofrece datos agregados de consumo energético para todo el país. Eso no sirve para saber cómo se comportan los centros de datos de forma particular”, apunta el autor principal del estudio, Gianluca Guidi, investigador postdoctoral fellow en el Departamento de Bioestadística. Como no hay registros públicos en los que chequear cuántas de estas instalaciones hay en EE UU y dónde, los investigadores optaron por una combinación de métodos. En primer lugar, trataron de conseguir información de los propios operadores, lo cual es una tarea farragosa (hay que ir empresa por empresa y estado por estado) y no siempre exitosa.
En segundo lugar, y aquí viene la novedad, contrastaron y ampliaron esa información con la observación directa: analizaron imágenes satelitales para detectar azoteas o parcelas típicas de hiperescalares, que tienen una arquitectura muy particular (parecen naves industriales, pero cuentan con sistemas de refrigeración fácilmente identificables y no suelen estar lejos de infraestructuras energéticas). La estimación de la potencia instalada de cada centro de datos la realizaron a partir de los metros cuadrados que ocupa la infraestructura.
Siguiendo este método, localizaron y situaron 403 hiperescalares en EE UU, con una potencia instalada media de 40 megavatios (MW) y una extensión promedio de unos 2.000 metros cuadrados. Los autores subrayan que esa cantidad se queda corta, ya que fue el fruto de la observación entre mayo de 2024 y abril de 2025. Los datos de consumo y emisiones, por tanto, también son necesariamente conservadores. “El boom de los centros de datos no se ha frenado desde abril de 2025. Se han construido nuevas instalaciones, se han ampliado los recintos ya existentes y la demanda de computación para IA sigue creciendo. Eso significa que el consumo eléctrico y la huella de carbono que estamos indicando podrían ser ya considerablemente mayores”, dice Guidi.
Estimaciones conservadoras
La estimación del volumen de los hiperescalares no tiene en cuenta la actividad a la que se dedican. Los procesos de entrenamiento e inferencia de IA, por ejemplo, consumen mucha más energía que el alojamiento de datos o la prestación de otros servicios en la nube. Es decir, un centro de datos más pequeño, pero dedicado a IA, puede consumir más que otro más grande que se ocupe de otras actividades. Como los promotores no suelen aclarar qué uso le dan a sus centros de datos, los investigadores salvaron este escollo dibujando tres posibles escenarios, relativos a un consumo bajo, moderado y alto.
El siguiente paso fue estimar su consumo energético, proceso que se hizo en función del tamaño de cada instalación, y sus emisiones, para lo que se tuvo en cuenta el mix energético empleado en cada localidad. Según señalan los autores, el consumo de energía aumentó considerablemente en los primeros años de la década de 2000, pero permaneció constante durante la de 2010, a pesar del crecimiento de la industria (lo que se puede explicar por las mejoras en la eficiencia del hardware y de los sistemas de refrigeración). La demanda ha vuelto a crecer en los últimos años de la mano de la computación necesaria para sostener los modelos comerciales de IA generativa.
El estudio también revela que aproximadamente el 54% de la electricidad que abasteció a los hiperescalares durante el periodo observado se generó a partir de combustibles fósiles, principalmente gas natural (38%) y carbón (15%), y que alrededor de una cuarta parte de la electricidad procedía de regiones con una red eléctrica más contaminante que la media.
Los investigadores observaron diferencias regionales sustanciales en las emisiones, que varían mucho debido a los distintos mixes energéticos usados. Muchas de las instalaciones se concentraban en zonas geográficas en las que la electricidad se genera en gran medida mediante centrales térmicas de carbón, lo que amplificaba su huella de carbono. “Las decisiones sobre la ubicación de los centros de datos y cómo se alimentan de energía son fundamentales para el medio ambiente y la salud pública, y deben tomarse basándose en datos fiables”, afirma una de las autoras del estudio, Francesca Dominici, catedrática Clarence James Gamble de Bioestadística, Población y Ciencia de Datos y directora de la Iniciativa de Ciencia de Datos de Harvard.
Eso cree también Shaolei Ren, que no ha participado en el estudio y que es profesor asociado de ingeniería eléctrica y computacional de la Universidad de California, Riverside y especialista en sostenibilidad de la IA. “El dibujo que traza este trabajo muestra por qué es importante en términos medioambientales dónde se ubican los centros de datos, a diferencia de otros análisis más agregados”, apunta. Ren ve las conclusiones de este estudio como el punto de partida para una investigación más detallada. “Si dispusiéramos de más información sobre cómo funcionan realmente las instalaciones concretas, podríamos comprender mejor dónde se encuentran las mayores oportunidades. En mi propio trabajo, me interesa especialmente relacionar la energía y las emisiones de carbono con el consumo de agua, la calidad del aire y los efectos sobre la salud”, subraya.
Aunque el método desarrollado por el equipo de Harvard es interesante, puede presentar algunas lagunas. “El artículo parte de la hipótesis de que todos los hiperescalares están conectados a la red eléctrica, cuando esto no es así”, señala Ana Valdivia, profesora de Inteligencia Artificial, Gobierno y Políticas de la Universidad de Oxford, cuya investigación más reciente se centra en evaluar el impacto ambiental de la IA. “Mi crítica a esta aproximación es que muchos centros de datos, como los de xAI en Tennessee, no están encontrando conexión a la red y están desarrollando su propia generación. Eso quiere decir que los resultados subestiman los datos reales, porque no se tiene en cuenta los que generan su propia energía”, añade la investigadora, que no ha participado en el artículo de Nature.

articles.title: James Bond : pourquoi Robert Pattinson est le meilleur choix possible pour 007
articles.text:
Amazon MGM Studios a officialisé le nouveau James Bond ce lundi 16 novembre 2026. L’annonce était très attendue, et elle a aussitôt relancé les débats habituels : trop célèbre, trop marqué par ses rôles passés, pas assez « traditionnel »… Comme à chaque passation de pouvoir depuis Sean Connery, le nouveau visage de James Bond suscite son lot de scepticisme.
Pourtant, en confiant le matricule 007 de James Bond à Robert Pattinson, Amazon MGM Studios et Denis Villeneuve ont peut-être réalisé le coup de maître nécessaire pour réinventer la franchise.
Une palette d’acteur taillée pour la complexité de James Bond
Réduire Robert Pattinson à la saga Twilight, qui l’a rendu célèbre, n’a plus de sens aujourd’hui. Depuis plus de 10 ans, le comédien londonien de 40 ans s’est imposé comme l’un des acteurs les plus exigeants et caméléons de sa génération. Des frères Safdie (Good Time) à Robert Eggers (The Lighthouse), en passant par David Cronenberg (Cosmopolis) ou Christopher Nolan (Tenet, dans lequel il est « presque » un James Bond), il a multiplié les rôles sombres, ambigus et nerveux.
Ce goût pour les personnages troubles fait de lui un candidat idéal pour James Bond. Dans les romans de Ian Fleming, 007 est un homme usé et cynique, capable d’une grande brutalité comme de moments de fragilité. Pattinson a déjà montré dans The Batman qu’il savait jouer un héros torturé, taiseux et physique, avec l’élégance britannique indispensable pour porter le smoking.
Pattinson tourne d’ailleurs en ce moment The Batman Part II, de Matt Reeves, précise le communiqué d’Amazon MGM Studios. Ce rôle chez DC a longtemps été présenté comme un obstacle à sa candidature, rappelle Variety. Le communiqué ne dit pas comment les deux calendriers vont s’articuler.
Le duo gagnant avec Denis Villeneuve
Denis Villeneuve est l’autre argument majeur en faveur de ce casting. Amazon MGM Studios a confié au réalisateur canadien la relance de la saga dès juin 2025, bien avant de choisir son interprète. Réputé pour son sens de la mise en scène monumentale et son approche réaliste de la tension dramatique (Sicario, Prisoners, Dune), Villeneuve aime travailler avec des acteurs capables de faire passer des émotions complexes par un simple regard.
Les deux hommes ont déjà travaillé ensemble : Pattinson joue Scytale, un assassin capable de changer d’apparence, dans Dune : Troisième partie, en salles le 16 décembre. Avoir déjà dirigé Pattinson sur un tournage de cette taille fait gagner du temps et de la confiance à Villeneuve. Plutôt que de devoir apprivoiser un jeune comédien inexpérimenté face à la pression d’un Bond, Villeneuve dispose d’un acteur qu’il a déjà dirigé.
Pattinson connaît aussi l’un des deux producteurs. David Heyman, qui produit ce Bond avec Amy Pascal, avait déjà produit Harry Potter et la Coupe de feu, le film qui a révélé l’acteur à 19 ans.
L’audace nécessaire pour ouvrir une nouvelle ère
Enfin, ce casting est la première grande décision d’Amazon MGM Studios depuis que le studio a pris, en mars 2025, le contrôle créatif de la saga, jusque-là détenu par Barbara Broccoli et Michael G. Wilson. Après cinq films menés par Daniel Craig qui ont profondément modernisé et humanisé l’espion britannique, un retour à un acteur plus classique aurait pu donner l’impression d’un surplace.
En misant sur une star mondiale qui continue de tourner pour le cinéma d’auteur, la production montre qu’elle ne veut pas d’un James Bond 26 nostalgique. Sa filmographie peut parler à la fois aux fidèles de la saga et aux cinéphiles plus exigeants. Pattinson aura passé la quarantaine à la sortie du film, attendue en 2028, alors que Deadline évoquait au départ un interprète de la fin de la vingtaine ou du début de la trentaine.

articles.title: Ola Electric hands the keys to dealers. What led to this shift in gears?
articles.text:
Ola Electric hands the keys to dealers. What led to this shift in gears?
For long, Ola Electric ran its own showrooms and sold directly to customers. Now it is shifting to a dealer-led model with plans to have 700 dealer outlets by March 2027. What prompted this reset and what should the company do for it to work?
On November 1, Ola Electric stopped taking orders at its own showrooms. Most of them will be shut by December, as Ola moves away from the direct-to-consumer model that defined the company and turns to a dealer-led business.
Ola has recorded this in its investor presentation filed with the NSE and BSE on November 12 under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The document covers the unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the second quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.
In its Q2 FY27 shareholders' letter, dated November 12, the company calls the move towards a dealer-led model a "reset". What prompted this 'reset'?
The numbers tell part of the story. Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 828 crore in Q1 FY26. It fell to Rs 690 crore in Q2, then Rs 470 crore in the next quarter, and bottomed out at Rs 265 crore in Q4 FY26.
Interestingly, the electric two-wheeler market has been growing in recent times. In Q2 FY27, industry volumes reached 5,99,317 units, up 82.7% year on year, and EV penetration in the two-wheeler market touched 11.2%. However, Ola's Q2 revenue fell 39% to Rs 421 crore in FY27.
The service record behind the reset
The shareholders' letter says little about why the direct model had to go, but public records give an indication.
The problems began with service. Between September 2023 and August 2024, the maker of electric two-wheelers received 10,644 complaints through the National Consumer Helpline. Of these, 3,389 concerned service delays and 1,899 were about delayed deliveries, according to media reports.
On October 7, 2024 the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) issued a show-cause notice giving the company 15 days to respond, and the complaints it cited included charges during the free service period, refusals or delays in warranty work, and unsatisfactory repairs.
Ola's response was that 99.1% of the complaints had been resolved to the customer's complete satisfaction. But the regulator reportedly found that 80% of those claimed resolutions had not been implemented, and the CCPA widened its inquiry.
Founder Bhavish Aggarwal promised the backlog would clear soon, and said the company would double its own service network to 1,000 centres by December 2024. Around the same time, a public spat erupted between Aggarwal and the comedian Kunal Kamra, who had taken up the customers' service complaints.
Subsequently, the company-owned store network ran into another problem. In March 2025, Bloomberg reported that only about 100 of Ola's roughly 3,400 showrooms displayed the trade certificate that the Motor Vehicles Act requires. Ola called the report misplaced and prejudiced.
Transport officials raided at least 26 stores in Maharashtra and six in Madhya Pradesh and impounded 60 scooters. Maharashtra's transport minister later said that of 432 stores inspected in April 2025, only 47 held valid certificates, and that the other 385 were shut.
The shareholders' letter does not connect any of this to the move towards a dealer network.
A new front end, built in eight weeks
The first set of dealer outlets became operational on September 4, on Janmashtami. By Diwali, on November 8, Ola says it had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 sales outlets. The company is planning about 450 outlets by December 2026 and 700 by March 2027.
Volumes through the new channel have climbed quickly. Wholesale orders were 3,955 vehicles in September and 13,505 in October. Ola expects 16,000 in November and 20,000 in December. Production is meant to keep pace, from 9,235 vehicles in August and 14,092 in October to about 25,000 in December.
The case Ola makes for dealers is financial as much as commercial. Under the old model, the company owned the stores, and carried the stock and the working capital. Now, it says, dealers pay for vehicles when they order them and hold the inventory in their own outlets.
Auto borrowings have fallen from Rs 2,422 crore in December 2024 to Rs 337 crore in September 2026, helped by a QIP and rights issue, and the company expects the auto business to generate free cash flow in the near term.
Operating expenses are meant to fall by a further Rs 50 crore as the company-owned stores close.
What the letter does not hide
The letter is candid in places. Inventory in the dealer channel built up through October and November, and registrations were a little slower in October. Ola puts channel inventory at about 15 days, and under a week in the earliest showrooms. It says that in markets where dealers opened early and have settled in, its market share is now well above pre-transition levels, though the company doe not give any figure.
There is also a supply problem. About 5,000 vehicles with paid orders in September were delayed by a week, running into October, because chargers were unavailable. The company says it is facing a paid order backlog and the constraint is its supply chain, not its plant, which it says can build well above the current output.
Hence the letter's headline claim: demand is no longer the constraint, supply is. The claim deserves attention. Wholesale figures count vehicles sent to dealers, not vehicles sold to riders, and the letter admits slower registrations in October.
The margin trade
Dealers do not come free. Ola says gross margin, which held at about 29.9% in Q2, will dip a little in Q3 and Q4 because of the dealer rollout, while operating margin should improve meaningfully. Excluding PLI incentives, Q2 gross margin was 26.5%. Gross margin per unit was roughly Rs 35,000, against an average selling price of about Rs 1,21,000, down from about Rs 1,68,000 in FY23.
The losses remain large. Operating EBITDA was a loss of Rs 218 crore in Q2FY27, wider than Rs 165 crore in Q1, and the loss after tax was Rs 362 crore. Consolidated free cash flow was negative Rs 371 crore, with the auto segment accounting for Rs 134 crore of that and the cell business most of the rest. Total borrowings are down from Rs 3,132 crore to Rs 1,819 crore.
The product roadmap
Going forward, Ola is betting on two things to win customers back: a cheaper scooter and its own batteries.
The cheaper scooter is the S1Z, which is expected to be delivered to customers by March 2027. It uses a battery type that Ola says costs less to build. The company plans to fit the same battery to its existing models. It also says that, as dealers open, demand will shift towards its premium scooters and motorcycles.
The batteries come from Ola’s own factory, which has reached its first 6 gigawatt-hours of capacity ahead of schedule. The government has extended a production incentive for the plant to 2031, and Ola expects the payments to kick in from January to March.
According to the company, making its own batteries costs the same as buying them, if about 70% of those made pass quality checks, and 10 to 15% less if 85% of them pass checks.
What to watch out for
A company not only owns its product but also owns every complaint that comes with it. While dealers will now share that responsibility, Ola cannot simply wish away all issues with a reset. It has to address the structural challenges that led to the bottlenecks and delays.
The success of the transition hinges on three major factors.
The first is sell-through: whether registrations keep pace with wholesale dispatches as the dealer network grows from 319 outlets to 700. The second is supply: whether production really reaches 25,000 a month, and whether suppliers and chargers keep up with it. The third test is margin: whether the cost savings from closing company showrooms outweigh the gross margin given up to dealers.
Ola has moved quickly, and the early numbers seem to be favourable. But they are the company's own, and they cover only a few weeks. The real proof will come in the Q3 results.
(Disclaimer: Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory, is an independent director at Ola Electric.)

articles.title: Google warns that fully-automated AI attacks are coming soon
articles.text:
Threat actors are now relying on agentic workflows powered by AI-based offensive frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, accelerating attacks to machine speed.
Although AI was initially used experimentally in the attack flow, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has observed its large-scale adoption by both financially motivated and state-sponsored threat groups.
A notable example is the use of CAIRN, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework, in an attack against the U.S. aerospace sector, and suspected North Korean hackers using Claude Code to deliver malware.
The researchers estimate that in the next three months threat actors will be able to launch unsophisticated attacks that require "little to no human interaction" and rely mostly on multiple AI agents.
Their projection is that "sophisticated, fully autonomous" agentic attacks are likely to emerge in the next six months.
In an advisory last week, the FBI warned that multiple threat actors started weaponizing the ARTEX AI pentesting framework since August and launched attacks against organizations in the financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
Using AI to find and exploit flaws
Google says attackers now systematically abuse open-source pentesting suites to run fully automated attacks, including ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and HexStrike AI.
Attackers used these frameworks to carry out adaptive attacks against internet-exposed endpoints vulnerable to low-complexity flaws for which large language models (LLMs) could easily build exploits.
In one example GTIG highlights in its AI Threat Tracker report, hackers used a multi-agent system called ‘exploit_agent’ to fully automate vulnerability finding and exploitation in attacks targeting French media, entertainment, and education websites.
“In the past quarter, GTIG identified threat actors using LLM frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop for the first time,” Google says.
“More specifically, GTIG identified an exposed staging server hosting a multi-agent vulnerability research and weaponization framework, dubbed exploit_agent, that integrates with multiple frontier and local LLMs.”
Google discovered this framework from the attacker’s exposed staging server, which also included stolen victim data, reconnaissance information, webshells, and brute-forcing scripts.
The system analyzes software updates on popular web apps to find signs of security flaws and automatically attempts to exploit them.
Google warns that the deployment of such frameworks in attacks has dramatically decreased the time defenders have to patch their systems, while it also produces false leads.
The researchers noted the recent example of PHP2Shell, where hundreds of purported proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits, mostly AI-generated, appeared shortly after PHP announced the two flaws. This added a significant burden on defenders, as they had to verify the code and develop protections.
Other AI usage trends
Beyond automated attacks, Google spotted multiple attacks from UNC6836, an activity cluster with suspected links to “Midnight Neptune,” targeting cryptocurrency firms in North America and Europe, using modified Claude Code.
After the initial compromise, the attackers modified the Claude Code app's settings so that at launch it triggered the download of the SOMBERMEME backdoor.
Google reports AI is now routinely used in influence operations by state-backed groups, commercial vendors, and political networks.
According to the researchers, LLMjacking has become a widespread problem, with attackers increasingly exploiting this new revenue stream at significant cost to affected organizations.
